s036e80097e.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
s036e80097e.description: arXiv:2611.26663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI has improved individual productivity, but whether adding a plurality of AI partners helps or hurts remains open. We crossed AI partnership (one versus two) with behavioral formation (calibrated to average human behavior versus customized by the participant) in a brainstorming experiment ($N$=168) with human-human dyads as reference. Two-AI rooms posted more ideas to the shared board, but human-authored ideas dropped substantially. With one AI partner, formation mattered: humans paired with an average-calibrated AI posted more than any other condition. With two, this effect vanished. Humans continued talking but converted fewer ideas into board posts. AI social talk predicted more human posts, while AI posting volume predicted fe
s036e80097e.summary: A study with 168 participants tested how the number and calibration of AI partners affect human-AI brainstorming, finding two-AI rooms posted more ideas but fewer human-authored ones.
s036e80097e.why: Suggests adding more AI collaborators can shift output toward AI-authored content, relevant to designing multi-agent team tools.

sd55ff3b0f9.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
sd55ff3b0f9.description: arXiv:2611.26717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Synthesizing relational training data such as knowledge graphs with a large language model typically emits structured objects one at a time, which keeps each object valid but leaves the relationships between them ungrounded. We study an alternative paradigm, generation by simulation: rather than describing a relational artifact, we simulate a process that produces it and take the artifact to be its causal record. Language-model agents propose intent and a deterministic referee resolves outcomes against an explicit world model, so a relation is emitted only when the event it represents occurs, making coherence a property of construction. We instantiate the paradigm for cyber threat intelligence knowledge graphs in the STIX 2.1 standard with th
sd55ff3b0f9.summary: Researchers propose generating knowledge graphs by simulating a process with language-model agents and a deterministic referee, rather than producing objects one at a time.
sd55ff3b0f9.why: Offers a method for keeping relationships between generated structured data coherent, though the text gives limited detail on practical results.

s7ccc51f7d5.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
s7ccc51f7d5.description: arXiv:2611.26722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To autonomously execute multi-step tasks, enterprise agents must reliably interact with tools, call APIs, or query databases, making tool-calling a fundamental capability of AI models. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) optimises for producing the correct call, but never contrasts it with a plausible incorrect one. In an environment where even a minor formatting error can invalidate a call and an incorrect decision can derail the interaction, direct preference optimisation (DPO) targets exactly this contrast. DPO, therefore, requires preference pairs rather than plain demonstrations. For tool-calling, such data, especially in realistic multi-turn settings, remains extremely scarce. To address this scarcity, we introduce TOUMAII, a large-scale tool-
s7ccc51f7d5.summary: Researchers released TOUMAII, a 4.5-million-pair tool-calling preference dataset for direct preference optimization, along with a source-agnostic generator.
s7ccc51f7d5.why: Provides a large preference dataset for training enterprise agents to make correct tool calls, useful for fine-tuning pipelines.

sd63805c1ed.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
sd63805c1ed.description: arXiv:2611.26782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulation resolves atomic-scale motion and predicts the structural, mechanical, and dynamic properties of materials, making it cen- tral to materials design and discovery. Yet an MD study requires an expert-driven workflow: designing the simulation, writing reliable input scripts, executing them, and analyzing the results with separate tools. Here we present ChatAtom, a multi-agent large language model system that translates a natural-language request into a complete MD workflow without the user writing input scripts or analysis code. Each agent has a defined responsibility within the workflow. An orchestrator plans the study; the LAMMPS and OVITO agents each use a generator-reviewer pair to prepare and review simulat
sd63805c1ed.summary: ChatAtom is a multi-agent LLM system that turns natural-language requests into complete molecular dynamics workflows, including writing input scripts and analysis.
sd63805c1ed.why: Shows LLM agents automating scientific simulation pipelines, a pattern relevant to engineers building domain-specific agent workflows.

se212b10205.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
se212b10205.description: arXiv:2611.26794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Readouts of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), such as CD8+ T-cell density, intra-epithelial infiltration and the Ki67 index, combine tissue architecture from H&E with cell phenotypes from multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) could automate these readouts with an explanation, but two gaps remain. Pathology MLLMs read H&E alone, while these readouts need the cell phenotypes that mIF measures. And their reasoning has no step-level truth to be checked against, so R1-style reinforcement learning rewards only the final answer and leaves the reasoning unverified. Same-section H&E and mIF provide what both gaps lack: mIF measures every cell without manual annotation, which gives cell-level ground truth
se212b10205.summary: Researchers propose interpretable tumor immune microenvironment reasoning by combining H&E tissue images with multiplex immunofluorescence cell phenotypes in multimodal LLMs.
se212b10205.why: Highlights the need for step-level verifiable reasoning in multimodal models, though the text offers limited detail on outcomes.

s7b900895fb.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
s7b900895fb.description: arXiv:2611.26797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models now write working code, produce realistic images, and hold long conversations, yet the mechanisms behind their intelligence still evade our understanding. This thesis explores that puzzle through Associative Memory (AM), in which patterns are stored as energy minima and retrieved through attractor dynamics. Beyond their capacity, AMs form new minima known as spurious states, long regarded as a failure of memory. We argue that this failure is where creativity begins, and that memorization and generalization can coexist as outcomes of one retrieval process. First, we show that diffusion models behave as AMs. With little data, a diffusion model forms a distinct basin of attraction around each training sample. As the data grows,
s7b900895fb.summary: A thesis argues that memorization and generalization can coexist in generative models, framing spurious states in associative memory as a source of creativity.

s392b2bf540.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
s392b2bf540.description: arXiv:2611.26870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, where they must distinguish between normative reasoning (what should happen) and descriptive reasoning (what is likely to happen). Most fairness benchmarks evaluate demographic discrimination under a single reasoning objective, and none we know of tests whether a model treats the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one. We introduce normative--descriptive calibration, the extent to which a model's differentiation between matched candidates depends on whether it is asked to predict or to decide, and measure it with the Normative--Descriptive Calibration Benchmark (NDCB): 697 matched-pair scenarios across six domains, eac
s392b2bf540.summary: Researchers introduce normative-descriptive calibration, a benchmark testing whether LLMs treat the same item differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one.
s392b2bf540.why: Adds a evaluation dimension beyond demographic fairness, relevant to teams deploying LLMs in socially consequential decisions.

sf9653447a3.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
sf9653447a3.description: arXiv:2611.26903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Partial-edit deepfake localization aims to identify manipulated regions within otherwise authentic speech. Recent systems report strong overall results, but aggregate scores do not reveal whether this performance holds across different editing conditions. In this work, we present an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization (SAL) using WavLM-Large and XLS-R representations on the VoiceCraft and SSR-Speech subsets of PartialEdit. We categorize edits along three transcript-derived axes, namely content, meaning change, and editing operation, and evaluate each generator separately. While both representations achieve strong overall performance, localization is noticeably weaker on SSR-Speech. From our experiments, we f
sf9653447a3.summary: Researchers analyze partial-edit deepfake localization for speech across edit and generator conditions, using WavLM-Large and XLS-R on PartialEdit subsets.
sf9653447a3.why: Shows aggregate detection scores can hide weaknesses across editing conditions, which matters for teams evaluating audio deepfake detectors.

s692a19875b.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
s692a19875b.description: arXiv:2611.26906v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) theorem solvers differ in both proving capability and inference cost. Applying an expensive solver to every subgoal wastes computation when cheaper models are sufficient, while always starting from the cheapest solver wastes attempts on subgoals that require stronger models. We present BudgetPV, an agentic budget-aware predict-and-verify system that allocates computation across unresolved subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers. BudgetPV uses a cross-solver predictor to guide solver selection for each subgoal and revises the allocation as verification feedback becomes available. The allocation problem changes as proving progresses. Early decisions mainly determine which solver should handle an untried subgoal, while
s692a19875b.summary: Researchers present BudgetPV, an agentic system that allocates compute across subgoals and heterogeneous LLM theorem solvers based on cost and capability.
s692a19875b.why: Demonstrates routing subtasks to cheaper or stronger models to balance inference cost against success, a pattern applicable to production model routing.

s0d97de254e.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
s0d97de254e.description: arXiv:2611.26910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are expected to improve themselves from their own experience across episodes, with fixed weights. Self-improvement in an embodied world cannot be read from one measure. Existing benchmarks measure task progress, world-knowledge question answering (QA), and episodic memory, but a correct answer does not show that the agent ever observed the evidence for it, and progress does not show what the agent learned. We introduce AstronautBench, which measures one agent's self-improvement through three views on the same run: what it knows, whether its own evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it gets in the world. It is built on the game Outer Wilds, where each episode is a 22-minute loop after which the world resets, only the agent's
s0d97de254e.summary: AstronautBench is a benchmark measuring LLM agent self-improvement across episodes through knowledge, evidence, and task progress views on the same run.
s0d97de254e.why: Argues that task success alone doesn't show learning, offering a multi-view evaluation approach for agent developers.

s5ab33db955.title: Self-Evolving Beyond Human-Crafted Experience for EDA Scripting
s5ab33db955.description: arXiv:2611.26912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing complexity of electronic systems demands efficient design flows, yet EDA scripting remains a bottleneck: proprietary APIs are sparsely documented, and errors often appear as silent failures or cryptic exceptions. Hand-crafted knowledge helps but is difficult to maintain as toolchains evolve. We present ZhuLong-SE (Self-Evolution), an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces. Building on ZhuLong, it enhances the task-level harness with API retrieval, documentation responses, isolated sandbox execution, and static checking, then adds governed cross-task self-evolution. Beyond solving individual tasks, ZhuLong-SE distills past execution traces into a three-tier memory store governed by ground
s5ab33db955.summary: ZhuLong-SE is an execution-grounded LLM agent that learns reusable knowledge from prior task traces to improve EDA scripting with API retrieval and sandbox execution.
s5ab33db955.why: Shows agents learning from past traces to handle sparsely documented proprietary APIs, relevant to hard-to-document toolchains.

s3433b5b74f.title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
s3433b5b74f.description: arXiv:2611.26935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop a theory for the organization of predictive information based on the scaling behavior of a family of information measures, and the theory predicts that if this organization has the same form at all me
s3433b5b74f.summary: Researchers study how predictive information is carried by preceding text and distributed along history, examining the self-similar organization of information in language.

sc8d198630f.title: CodeReviewBench: An Automated Benchmark for Evaluating the Software Factory
sc8d198630f.description: arXiv:2611.26942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI agents ship more code with minimal human oversight, code review becomes the critical quality-control checkpoint -- but one without a reliable, objective verifier: review quality is nuanced and ultimately a judgment call by the PR author. Existing benchmarks are structurally misaligned with this: annotators are third-party reviewers, like the bots they evaluate, not the PR authors who actually decide what to fix. They also rely on small, static issue sets that require full re-evaluation as tools update, limiting how frequently progress can be tracked. We introduce CodeReviewBench, built on a fundamentally different signal: revealed developer preferences -- if a developer acts on a bot's suggestion, we treat it as useful; if they ignore i
sc8d198630f.summary: CodeReviewBench is a proposed automated benchmark for evaluating AI code review, using PR authors rather than third-party reviewers as the judges of review quality.
sc8d198630f.why: Targets code review as a quality gate for AI-generated code, relevant to teams scaling agent-written pull requests.

s397a58d08f.title: Keep the Process, Change the Supplier: Runtime Governance for Tool-Using AI Agents
s397a58d08f.description: arXiv:2611.26966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using AI agents propose actions whose authorization and external effects cannot be inferred from generated text alone. We study an execution boundary that separates agent proposals from business-controlled authority, context disclosure, and supplier selection. The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) mediates capability calls and records uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without returning an acceptable reply. We evaluate this runtime with scripted requests and synthetic suppliers: 2,400 fault episodes across four policies, 60 process-termination/restart episodes, 19,000 timed calls across 19 configurations, five targeted mutations over 43 fixtures, and 160 substitution records. No language model or autonomous agent is evalua
s397a58d08f.summary: The Open Process Control Plane (OPCP) is a runtime that mediates tool-using agents' capability calls, recording uncertain outcomes when a supplier may have acted without replying.
s397a58d08f.why: Addresses authorization and audit of agent actions with external side effects, a key concern for production agent governance.

s967eeb51cb.title: Right Numbers, Wrong Story: When LLMs Narrate Financial Changes Beyond Their Inputs
s967eeb51cb.description: arXiv:2611.26968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A financial report drafted by an LLM can state every number correctly but still go beyond its input, adding judgments and causes that no one supplied. We call these additions unsupported framing and find them far more often in LLM drafts than in reports written by proInput facts Revenue +3% Higher prices 10-K filings Revenue increased 3% on higher prices. 10-K writer Revenue surged 3% on higher prices, due to strong demand. LLM Fits the size? Surged: Unusual for 3% In the input? In the input? Strong demand: Not in input Higher prices: Kept fessionals, and attempts to fix them by prompting with how each word is used instead make such judgments more frequent. We therefore propose FrameCheck, a plug-in that sits beFrameCheck Revenue increased 3%
s967eeb51cb.summary: Researchers show LLM-drafted financial reports can state every number correctly yet add unsupported judgments and causes, appearing far more often than in human-written 10-K filings.
s967eeb51cb.why: Accurate figures do not guarantee faithful financial narratives, so teams deploying LLM report drafting need checks beyond numeric accuracy.

s8140136569.title: Run One, Get Two: Near-Free Streaming Safety Checks for Local LLMs
s8140136569.description: arXiv:2611.26975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local LLM assistants decode for one user at a time, so decoding is bound by memory bandwidth and leaves compute idle. Streaming safety checks today trade accuracy against cost. A dedicated guard model is accurate but nearly doubles the latency per token, while a hidden-state probe is cheap but less accurate. We present ToRA, an adapter that runs a second model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing its weights and KV cache. Dual-row kernels read each weight once for both rows. On Qwen3-0.6B, ToRA matches or beats a dedicated streaming guard, with higher F1 on 12 of 17 benchmarks. It detects 11.8 points more unsafe responses than the probe at a similar cost, under 4% added latency per token.
s8140136569.summary: ToRA is an adapter that runs a second safety-check model as an extra row in the generator's decode step, sharing weights and KV cache for near-free streaming guardrails on local LLMs.
s8140136569.why: It offers guard-model accuracy for streaming safety checks without nearly doubling per-token latency on local assistants.

s7d212e2fba.title: MixFold: Sub-4-Bit Mixed-Precision LLM Inference via Output-Channel Grouping on Mobile NPUs
s7d212e2fba.description: arXiv:2611.26976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sub-4-bit quantization allows mobile devices to run larger LLMs, but its memory savings do not always translate into faster decoding on mobile NPUs. Their matrix units support only a few native integer datatypes, and converting unsupported weight formats on the vector unit can erase the gains from fewer bits. Mixed precision faces an additional constraint: each matrix-unit tile uses one datatype. MixFold executes 3-bit and perfectly symmetric 2-bit weights using native integer operations without expanding the weights to wider datatypes during decoding. MixFold then assigns datatypes to output-channel groups aligned with the matrix-unit tiles, enabling finer-than-layer assignment without disrupting matrix-unit execution. We compare MixFold wit
s7d212e2fba.summary: MixFold proposes executing sub-4-bit mixed-precision LLM weights with native integer operations on mobile NPUs, avoiding conversion to wider datatypes during decoding.
s7d212e2fba.why: Memory savings from low-bit quantization only speed up mobile decoding if conversion overhead is avoided, which this method targets.

sb051403af0.title: From Letter-of-Credit Requirements to Executable Specifications: Evaluating Verification Accuracy and Completeness
sb051403af0.description: arXiv:2611.26988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In letter-of-credit (LC) document examination, a correct final decision does not show that every requirement was examined. We therefore evaluate examination requirement by requirement and make each requirement executable. A language model converts the bill of lading (BL) and commercial invoice (IV) requirements of a credit into atomic conditions and logical structures, and a deterministic verifier retrieves the named evidence and computes each outcome, so every check can be compared with a gold encoding and traced to logged evidence. Because LC records are confidential, our on-premises 9B parser is fine-tuned only on synthetic pairs built from templates and human-reviewed public document values. On 345 real LC cases, final-decision accuracy p
sb051403af0.summary: Researchers propose converting letter-of-credit requirements into executable, atomic checks via a language model and deterministic verifier, evaluated requirement by requirement against gold encodings.
sb051403af0.why: Checking each requirement rather than only the final decision gives auditable, traceable verification for trade-finance document review.

s27117f410f.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
s27117f410f.description: arXiv:2611.26998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study reward fidelity in an adversarial reinforcement-learning loop for red-teaming financial-services language-model guardrails. Apparent wins can arise when an attack omits prescribed personally identifiable information (PII), or when a reward judge credits a response that did not break the targeted policy. On attacker-generated and public benchmark examples, TypeSafe Jev checks whether the prescribed PII is present. For outcome scoring, we compare the decision models TypeSafe Jev, Laya (pretrained and post-trained), and pretrained CLM-8B with logged Opus 4.8 judgements from a replay corpus. Post-training markedly improves Laya's agreement with the judge. A separate author-reviewed off-target set establishes that Opus can award false win
s27117f410f.summary: The paper studies reward fidelity in adversarial RL for red-teaming financial-services LLM guardrails, finding apparent attack wins can come from missing PII or lenient reward judges.
s27117f410f.why: Reward judges that credit non-successful attacks can mislead guardrail evaluation, so reward signals need verification before trusting results.

s17169dd0c7.title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
s17169dd0c7.description: arXiv:2611.27007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rigorously evaluating medical artificial intelligence (AI) requires testing open-ended clinical management across diverse presentations and stages of care. However, existing benchmarks rely on manual expert authoring, limiting coverage across conditions, conditional care pathways, and evolving guidelines. We develop an automated pipeline that extracts and verifies structured clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations to generate scenarios spanning the care continuum, including nuanced presentations and practice variations across regions and guideline editions. Applied to 436 BMJ Best Practice clinical monographs (354 US, 82 International), this yields 3,200 scenarios spanning differential diagnosis, investiga
s17169dd0c7.summary: Researchers describe an automated pipeline that extracts clinical criteria and decision trees from practice recommendations to generate medical AI test scenarios across the care continuum.
s17169dd0c7.why: Automatically generated, guideline-grounded scenarios could scale evaluation of medical AI beyond costly manual expert benchmark authoring.

sb4c5575ce5.title: Many Plans at Once: Diverse Top-Quality Planning in Continuous Time
sb4c5575ce5.description: arXiv:2611.27012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Planners for physical systems usually return a single trajectory, which leaves no alternative when an unmodeled constraint invalidates the chosen route or downstream preferences change. A set of plans computed in advance provides ready-made alternatives and warm-starts for fast adaptation, but only if the plans are both low-cost and mutually distinct. Discrete planning addresses this with top-quality and diverse planning, but these ideas do not transfer to continuous time, where every valid trajectory has infinitely many valid near-copies, and existing trajectory planners converge to one or a few solutions. We present Many Plans at Once (MPAO), which treats every plan it finds as a reason to search elsewhere: it samples untrained neural netwo
sb4c5575ce5.summary: Researchers present methods for computing diverse, top-quality plans in continuous time, giving alternative trajectories for physical systems when constraints change.
sb4c5575ce5.why: Precomputed diverse plans offer ready alternatives and warm starts for robotics and physical planners facing unmodeled constraints.

scb843bf8d5.title: Same Facts, Different Decision: Fact-Invariant Manipulation and Provenance-Based Defense in Typed Decision Models
scb843bf8d5.description: arXiv:2611.27016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Typed decision models such as TypeSafe's Jev answer only with a probability, an option, or a score, so software can act on them directly. Their inputs, however, often include text from outsiders. Prior attacks test this risk poorly. Injected instructions rarely work on these models, and added facts can make a changed decision correct. We show that outside comments can persuade these models to make a wrong decision without adding any fact. We propose LEVER, an attack that writes such comments with four levers from argumentation theory, uses a separate verifier to discard any comment that adds a fact, and searches for effective comments guided by the model's output probabilities. We further propose the Provenance Gate, a defense that accepts a
scb843bf8d5.summary: The paper introduces LEVER, an attack that uses argumentation-based outside comments to push typed decision models into wrong decisions without adding any new facts, and proposes a provenance-based defense.
scb843bf8d5.why: Decision models that consume third-party text can be steered by persuasive comments alone, so input provenance matters for security.

s94f914119f.title: Integral Multipliers and Arithmetic Obstructions for Two-Hidden-Layer ReLU Maxima
s94f914119f.description: arXiv:2611.27018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study exact representations of maximum functions by ReLU networks with two hidden layers and integer parameters. The least positive output multiplier is two for the six-input maximum, and either two or six for the seven-input maximum. We obtain these bounds from integral cubical fillings and a coefficient-preserving passage from polytope identities to networks. For the coordinate-facet complex of the six-simplex, we compute a coning index of six over the integers and three after inverting two, allowing arbitrary integral directions within each facet. A class in the homology of the unrestricted kernel complex characterizes the remaining seven-input problem; its vanishing is equivalent to an integral filling of a fixed target. We also constr
s94f914119f.summary: The paper derives integer-parameter bounds on the least positive output multiplier for exact representations of six- and seven-input maximum functions by two-hidden-layer ReLU networks.

sced64c19e2.title: Disentangling Verbalized Evaluation Awareness and Refusal through Neuron-Level Intervention
sced64c19e2.description: arXiv:2611.27032v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large reasoning models (LRMs) become more capable, reliable evaluation becomes essential. LRMs can sometimes recognize that they are being evaluated, a phenomenon known as \emph{evaluation awareness}. This phenomenon raises concerns about whether safety behavior, particularly refusal behavior, generalizes from evaluation to deployment. Prior work manipulates \emph{verbalized evaluation awareness (VEA)} through activation steering and observes higher refusal rates when VEA is present, but the mechanisms underlying this connection remain poorly understood. We identify \emph{VEA neurons} by contrasting their activations in VEA and non-VEA reasoning segments. Intervening on 5,000 VEA neurons reduces the VEA rate from 12.6--51.8\% to at most 1.
sced64c19e2.summary: Researchers use neuron-level intervention to separate verbalized evaluation awareness from refusal behavior in large reasoning models.
sced64c19e2.why: Understanding whether evaluation awareness drives refusals bears on whether safety tests generalize to deployment behavior.

sf0701cace4.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Stateful Privacy Sniffing of LLM Agents via Behavioral Covert Channels in Web Interactions
sf0701cace4.description: arXiv:2611.27046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on Web interaction, issuing searches, following links, and reading pages, to complete complex user tasks. Since each action is driven by the agent's private context, including the user's prompt, dialogue history, memory, and connected data, it also opens a new privacy exposure surface. Prior attacks either passively analyze network traffic, which yields only coarse correlations, or hijack the agent through indirect prompt injection, which must place sensitive content in an outgoing field and is blocked by content-level defenses. Whether an attacker can actively recover fine-grained private context without any explicit transmission thus remains insufficiently understood. Our insight is that an agent's benign Web de
sf0701cace4.summary: The paper presents a stateful privacy attack in which LLM agents leak private context through behavioral covert channels in their web actions such as searches and link-following.
sf0701cace4.why: Agent actions on the web can reveal private user context even when content filters block direct leakage, expanding the privacy attack surface.

sb1d173c8f8.title: A Continuous Relaxation of Quantization-Aware Training
sb1d173c8f8.description: arXiv:2611.27056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantization is a critical piece of the deployment pipeline in the era of large generative models. Low-bit quantization, particularly 2-bits or sub-2-bits, is a notoriously difficult problem, particularly when using a channelwise quantization scheme which has been shown as a leading candidate for hardware-efficiency. The key challenges with low-bit quantization range from limited quantization levels to saddle points or flat regions in the loss surface. In this paper, we look at the problem of flat quantization loss surfaces through a lens of dynamically changing bitwidth. Unlike existing techniques which either change the bit-precision abruptly or keep it fixed, we propose to gradually alter the bitwidth as the model trains. To this end, we p
sb1d173c8f8.summary: Researchers propose a continuous relaxation of quantization-aware training to address flat, saddle-point-laden loss surfaces in low-bit, channelwise quantization of large models.
sb1d173c8f8.why: Sub-2-bit channelwise quantization is hard to train, and a better optimization approach could make hardware-efficient deployment more practical.

s7f5fd3cd46.title: Dynamic Token Merging for Efficient Vision-Language Models
s7f5fd3cd46.description: arXiv:2611.27064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) represent each image with hundreds of visual tokens, which can make inference costly even when a prompt depends on only part of the image. Dynamic Token Merging (DTM), introduced in MrT5 for byte-level text encoders, learns which tokens to remove: a lightweight delete gate scores contextualized hidden states, acts as a differentiable attention bias during training, and physically removes tokens at inference. We argue that DTM is a general token deletion framework rather than a byte-level technique, and extend it to the vision modality and to decoder-only models. Applying DTM to T5Gemma 2 and Gemma 3 yields V-MrT5Gemma2, which deletes visual tokens inside a bidirectional multimodal encoder, and V-MrGemma3, which c
s7f5fd3cd46.summary: The authors extend Dynamic Token Merging, a learned token deletion method, to vision-language models so they can drop visual tokens at inference and reduce cost.
s7f5fd3cd46.why: Removing unneeded visual tokens could cut VLM inference costs when prompts depend on only part of an image.

s9fd887eb66.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models
s9fd887eb66.description: arXiv:2611.27068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) from verifiable outcomes gives a language agent one reward per episode: every step is credited alike, and nothing about the task is learned when all rollouts fail. The last mile, step-level credit, usually requires step labels, a learned critic, costly LLM judges or hand-written rules. We introduce DM-PRM, which turns a general-purpose decision model -- one answering yes/no questions with probabilities -- into a general-purpose process reward model (PRM), zero-shot: no step labels, no fine-tuning, no critic. DM-PRM asks one question per step and adds the standardised answers to the advantage. It plugs into any policy-gradient method; one model, with one question text per environment, serves household tasks, web sho
s9fd887eb66.summary: DM-PRM converts a general-purpose yes/no decision model into a zero-shot process reward model that gives step-level credit without step labels, fine-tuning, or a critic.
s9fd887eb66.why: Step-level rewards without labels or critics could simplify RL training for language agents on multi-step tasks.

s8112ef1cde.title: Writing Weights or Training Them? Spatial Reasoning through Weight-Space Programming and Low-Rank Adaptation
s8112ef1cde.description: arXiv:2611.27089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Weight-space programming lets a language model inspect and edit another model's weights, offering an alternative to gradient-based adaptation. We evaluated both approaches using Qwen3.5-0.8B on a fixed reference-frame task (128 items), StepGame (200 items), and two untrained distance-comparison tasks. With thinking enabled, the public patch (p50c) raised mean accuracy from 0.0% to 22.1% on the reference-frame task and from 19.2% to 33.7% on StepGame across three sampling seeds. Randomly permuting its weight change removed the gain. Further closed-form edits did not improve on p50c, whereas a rank-1 LoRA adapter trained on worked solutions reached 100% and 98.8%, respectively, with 0.09% trainable parameters. Removing the worked solutions from
s8112ef1cde.summary: Researchers compare weight-space programming, where one model edits another's weights, with LoRA fine-tuning on spatial reasoning tasks using Qwen3.5-0.8B.
s8112ef1cde.why: It compares a gradient-free adaptation method with LoRA on small-model reasoning benchmarks, though the reported gains are modest and task-specific.

s9e4c319f67.title: Reasoning in Two Dimensions: Quantifying Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness and Efficiency
s9e4c319f67.description: arXiv:2611.27100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning exposes intermediate steps, but a correct answer does not establish that an LLM relies on the dependence expressed by those steps or reasons efficiently. We operationalize CoT faithfulness and efficiency within a common framework. Specifically, we represent a CoT as a semantic reasoning graph and decompose the model's predictive dependence along two complementary axes: dependence explained by semantic support versus additional reasoning history, and dependence allocated to answer-reaching versus off-path reasoning. This decomposition yields global and step-level measures of unfaithfulness and inefficiency. Controlled interventions show that the proposed metrics respond to hidden dependence and induced off-path
s9e4c319f67.summary: Researchers propose a framework that represents chain-of-thought as a semantic reasoning graph to measure its faithfulness and efficiency.
s9e4c319f67.why: Correct answers alone don't show a model uses its stated reasoning, so this offers a way to audit reasoning traces.

sb9a327b243.title: CoEvoBench: Can LLMs Drive Recursive Co-Evolution of Agentic Systems?
sb9a327b243.description: arXiv:2611.27116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The performance of an LLM agent depends on both its model and its harness, the code that mediates its interaction with tools and environments. Can LLM researchers drive this co-evolution as a recursive improvement process, deciding round after round which component to change when each change alters the value of the other? Existing benchmarks evaluate post-training or data research with the harness out of scope, or harness optimization with the model fixed, leaving this joint decision unmeasured. We introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs as researchers co-evolving the model and harness of a target agent across five agentic domains. Researchers start from a common base model and initial harness, train and revise within a 24-hour
sb9a327b243.summary: Researchers introduce CoEvoBench, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can decide which component of an agent system, model or harness, to change in recursive co-evolution.
sb9a327b243.why: Agent performance depends on both model and harness, so this benchmark targets a joint decision that existing benchmarks leave unmeasured.

s71b5734548.title: Portable Active Recovery under Timed and Position-Dependent Visual Outages
s71b5734548.description: arXiv:2611.27121v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a camera blackout depends on physical position rather than elapsed time, stable hovering prevents visual recovery and mission completion. On stereo visual-inertial quadrotors without external localization, an exogenous timed blackout and an endogenous position-dependent dark zone appear identical at loss onset yet require opposite responses: hover-and-wait completes 93/96 timed blackouts but 0/96 spatial outages (13 hard failures), whereas blind continuation traverses many spatial zones yet fails heavily during timed blackouts. We formulate visual-outage recovery as a worst-condition active-observability problem and introduce a portable recovery module at the reference interface of an unchanged host controller with zero retraining. Using
s71b5734548.summary: Researchers study quadrotor recovery during camera blackouts, finding hover-and-wait works for timed outages but fails for position-dependent dark zones, which need different responses.
s71b5734548.why: Drone teams relying on visual navigation without external localization need recovery strategies that distinguish timed from location-based outages.

sa8d6b2426a.title: When Students Fail to Learn from Teachers: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
sa8d6b2426a.description: arXiv:2611.27125v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has become a core technique for post-training large language models, enabling students to learn from dense token-level supervision on their own generations. However, even with a capable teacher, OPD training can be unstable, leading to excessive response length, repetitive generation, and severe performance degradation. One example is \textit{spurious agreement}, where the student maintains high overlap with the teacher at the states visited but produces repetitive generations. Although such failures have been observed, the mechanisms behind these failures remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we investigate OPD through the lens of learning dynamics, tracing three mechanisms from local analysis to subsequ
sa8d6b2426a.summary: Researchers analyze why on-policy distillation for LLM post-training can be unstable, including a failure mode called spurious agreement that causes repetitive generation.
sa8d6b2426a.why: Teams using on-policy distillation to post-train LLMs may see length blowups and degradation, so understanding these dynamics matters for training stability.

s6065d7aa1b.title: MAPES: Multi-Value Alignment Pipeline via Expert Specialization
s6065d7aa1b.description: arXiv:2611.27133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human preferences requires simultaneously satisfying multiple, often competing values. Existing preference optimization methods collapse these into a single implicit signal, and even multi-objective extensions optimize within a shared parameter space, leaving cross-value conflicts unresolved. We propose MAPES, a multi-value alignment paradigm in which conflict resolution is a first-class concern at every pipeline stage: it first decomposes supervision into value-specific experts trained in isolated parameter subspaces, then recomposes them via preference-aware value merging and a lightweight harmonization stage that aligns the merged model with the expert ensemble. Across five preference alignment be
s6065d7aa1b.summary: Researchers propose MAPES, a multi-value LLM alignment pipeline that trains value-specific experts in isolated parameter spaces before resolving conflicts.
s6065d7aa1b.why: Single-signal preference methods can hide conflicts between values, so this approach targets alignment tradeoffs explicitly.

s5b7b28b8b6.title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
s5b7b28b8b6.description: arXiv:2611.27138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Language models fuse reports in retrieval, multi-agent consensus and agent memory, where treating shared-source reports as independent can double count evidence. A common remedy is an instruction to count each source once. Its value depends on the receiver's raw baseline. Pricing it needs an exact reference. We build the graded-dependence exact reference: binary worlds with single-report reliability 0.65 and four dependence levels, whose disclosed parameters give every world an exact posterior and every rule a target risk. The paired gain protocol scores raw and instructed answers of four configurations on 2,976 worlds. Agreement and gain separate in both directions. At $\delta$ = 0, claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6.1-sol agreed with the rule within
s5b7b28b8b6.summary: Researchers show LLMs can double count shared-source evidence in fusion tasks and build an exact posterior reference to separate rule compliance from real posterior gain.
s5b7b28b8b6.why: Retrieval, multi-agent consensus, and memory systems can overcount correlated reports, so teams need measurable checks on evidence fusion.

s58fa5bdce9.title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout
s58fa5bdce9.description: arXiv:2611.27149v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predictive world models learn to forecast observations, but accurate short-term predictions do not necessarily produce physically coherent behavior over longer horizons. We investigate how incorporating physical structure can strengthen world models while retaining their underlying predictive objectives. Across token-based models of planetary motion and JEPA-style visual models of mechanical systems, we study conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry-aware representations, temporal consistency, and learned structured dynamics. In planetary motion, angular-momentum supervision improves autonomous next-token forecasting, while the benefits of temporal regularization depend on the accompanying physical objective and representation. In visual mode
s58fa5bdce9.summary: Researchers study how adding physical structure, such as conserved quantities and symmetries, to predictive world models affects long-horizon physical coherence.
s58fa5bdce9.why: Accurate short-term forecasts don't guarantee physically coherent rollouts, which matters for anyone building world models for planning.

s3e35b02037.title: From Acting to Learning: Experience Selection toward Continually Learning Agents
s3e35b02037.description: arXiv:2611.27159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Successful agent interactions provide training data, but success alone does not determine which records a student should learn from. We examine experience selection for a 4B language agent as a component of continual agent learning. Nine selectors are compared across two fixed experience pools, eight initialization seeds, and two sampling seeds, yielding 288 trained students. Each student is evaluated on 128 development task groups with a common executor. With equal global selection freedom, 256 distinct contents, and 768 training presentations, optimizer-aware gradient selection reaches 81.45\% and 73.19\% success in the two pools. Its gains over global random selection are 8.25 and 5.96 percentage points; gains over global high-NLL selectio
s3e35b02037.summary: Researchers compare nine experience selectors for training a 4B language agent across many seeds and pools to study continual agent learning.
s3e35b02037.why: Choosing which agent experiences to train on affects continual learning results, a practical design decision for agent builders.

sa32ba8ef01.title: Learning Adaptive Defense Strategies: Fine-Tuned LLMs for Network Security Games under Network Mobility
sa32ba8ef01.description: arXiv:2611.27180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models(LLM) show promise for strategic reasoning, yet their ability to compute game-theoretic equilibria under dynamic conditions remains largely unexplored. This work investigates whether fine-tuned LLMs can serve as solver-free surrogates for online equilibrium computation in honeypot allocation, a setting in which network mobility continuously reshapes the underlying attack graph and forces repeated re-solving of a two-player zero-sum game. We construct a dataset of 270 security games on networks of 8--25 nodes with solver-grounded equilibrium labels, and evaluate four classes of predictor over 1{,}524 held-out mobility events: non-learned baselines, six open-weight architectures evaluated zero-shot, the same six after LoRA
sa32ba8ef01.summary: Researchers fine-tune LLMs to act as solver-free surrogates for computing equilibria in honeypot allocation games on networks with changing topology.
sa32ba8ef01.why: Fine-tuned models could approximate repeated game-theoretic re-solving in security settings, though the abstract gives limited evidence of production readiness.

s0b24363beb.title: What Does Matching a Human Intervention Effect Establish? Benchmark Checks for LLM Simulations
s0b24363beb.description: arXiv:2611.27186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM simulations are validated by equivalence with human effects, yet a zero reference passes whenever the human 90 percent interval lies inside the margin, as the human benchmark shows before simulation. When the zero reference fails, planned precision gives independent simulations the margin up to which passing is a 5 percent test of response. In an exploratory 70-experiment reanalysis, 72 percent of GPT-4's $\pm$0.20 SD passes were zero-reference passes; GPT-4 passed 16 contrasts the zero reference failed (1.58 expected without response). In a preregistered audit, Claude Sonnet 5.5 passed three intention targets, all zero-reference passes, and the registered belief-gradient control; norm beliefs changed 0.065 SD against humans' 0.351 (zero-
s0b24363beb.summary: Researchers argue that matching a human intervention effect in LLM simulations does not establish validity, using a reanalysis of 70 experiments with GPT-4.
s0b24363beb.why: Teams using LLM simulations as stand-ins for human studies may be overstating validation if they rely on zero-reference equivalence tests.

s5cb0308074.title: EDAGoat: An EDA-Aware Agent for Project-Level GPU Optimization
s5cb0308074.description: arXiv:2611.27196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GPU acceleration has transformed electronic design automation (EDA), yet further improving expert-engineered GPU tools still demands substantial manual effort. Automating this work calls for coding agents that can trace bottlenecks across host and device code while preserving correctness and design quality. We introduce EDAGoat, to our knowledge the first EDA-aware GPU optimization agent for this task. Its optimization enhancement (OE) mode guides edits with four cross-project GPU optimization patterns. Its mandatory validation (MV) mode requires the agent to test the edited program against the EDA constraints its changes could affect. Our benchmark covers five GPU EDA projects across four task families and 55 circuit inputs, measuring comple
s5cb0308074.summary: Researchers introduce EDAGoat, an EDA-aware coding agent that optimizes project-level GPU code with optimization patterns and mandatory validation.
s5cb0308074.why: Automating GPU optimization in EDA tools with validation could reduce manual engineering effort while preserving correctness.

s65d8d4e046.title: Bel: Step-Level Policy Improvement of Visual Agents Without Training
s65d8d4e046.description: arXiv:2611.27222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A visual agent acts on what it sees: it taps and types on a screen, or points on a camera image to show a robot where to act. One wrong step can fail its task, yet the right action is often among its own samples, passed over by its greedy decode. Choosing it is a visual judgment, since an action is best judged where it acts, not by its text or coordinates alone: as text, a tap is two numbers; drawn on the screen, it is the Post button of an empty draft. We find that this is decisive: given the screenshot and a tap's coordinates, a decision model chooses among GUI-R1-3B's samples significantly worse on average than when the tap is drawn where it lands. Bel turns this finding into a method that trains nothing and needs only a frozen policy's sa
s65d8d4e046.summary: Researchers present Bel, a training-free method that improves visual agent steps by choosing among the agent's own sampled actions using a visual judgment model.
s65d8d4e046.why: Teams building screen or robot visual agents may improve step accuracy without retraining, though the abstract gives few benchmark details.

s6672e5bff7.title: LiDAR Signals for Robot Locomotion: Spherical Range Images Enable Robust Sim-to-Real Transfer
s6672e5bff7.description: arXiv:2611.27223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing legged-locomotion systems commonly rely on depth images or online elevation maps. However, depth-based policies suffer from perceptual sim-to-real discrepancies due to imperfect depth sensor modeling, while map-based approaches are vulnerable to drift and misalignment. LiDAR offers direct measurements of the surrounding geometry, but raw LiDAR scans lack a compact, structured representation for high-frequency control. We propose a LiDAR perception pipeline that maintains perceptual consistency across simulation and reality through sensing- and representation-level alignment. At the sensor level, we recover frame-wise angular sampling patterns from the physical LiDAR and replay them in simulation with GPU ray casting. At the represent
s6672e5bff7.summary: Researchers propose a LiDAR perception pipeline using spherical range images to improve sim-to-real transfer for legged robot locomotion.
s6672e5bff7.why: Depth-image and elevation-map approaches suffer sim-to-real gaps, so a LiDAR representation could make locomotion policies more robust on hardware.

s1b398c5722.title: No Perfect Guardrail & No Perfect Guard: On the Decidability of Output Policies for Large Language Models
s1b398c5722.description: arXiv:2611.27260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expecting guardrails to provide a general guarantee of safety fails to recognize the limits of computational enforcement and policy specification. We argue that promising such perfection is an ethical failure of precision, and that invoking it to abdicate responsibility is a moral failure. Guardrails can support responsible action, but cannot relieve researchers, developers, policymakers, or users of their obligations to examine what they claim, permit, and prevent. We establish a precise computational boundary. If every finite string is a possible output of a language model, a computable guard that blocks every forbidden output and passes every permitted one exists if and only if the policy is decidable. For an undecidable policy, every guar
s1b398c5722.summary: Authors argue LLM output guardrails cannot guarantee safety and present a computational boundary on deciding output policies.
s1b398c5722.why: Teams relying on guardrails as complete safety guarantees should note theoretical limits and keep human responsibility and testing in place.

sc2dfcaf92f.title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
sc2dfcaf92f.description: arXiv:2611.27283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dermatologists describe lesions with a standardized morphological lexicon, which makes concept-based models attractive for interpretable skin disease diagnosis. How much diagnostic information these concepts actually carry, however, is rarely quantified. We present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the expert-annotated SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k (3,230 images, 48 concepts, 113 diseases). DermKG has 3,452 nodes of 8 types and 19,365 edges of 11 relation types, and encodes disease concept profiles, concept co-occurrence, a three-level diagnostic hierarchy, and 20 clinical morphology rules, all of which are supported by the training data (15 strong, 5 moderate). An information-ceiling analysis shows that the 3,230 lesions
sc2dfcaf92f.summary: Researchers present DermKG, a concept-centric knowledge graph built on the SkinCon subset of Fitzpatrick17k for interpretable skin disease diagnosis.

scd268a271b.title: Belief-State Management Meets Rubric Rewards for Agentic Forecasting
scd268a271b.description: arXiv:2611.27286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current large language model (LLM) agents still struggle to forecast real-world events. This stems from two primary limitations: i) standard ReAct harness accumulates reasoning and evidence within one growing context, and ii) outcome-based rewards in forecasting lead to a slow and noisy signal that cannot distinguish sound reasoning from lucky guesses. To address these, we introduce a forecasting training framework including harness design and post-training. For the harness side, we propose Proactive Belief-State Management (PBM), equipping agents with a fold tool to compress lengthy context into compact belief states and reset the context for subsequent exploration. For the training side, we develop SEIPH, a five-dimensional, outcome-blind r
scd268a271b.summary: Researchers propose a forecasting training framework for LLM agents, combining Proactive Belief-State Management in the harness with rubric-based rewards in post-training.
scd268a271b.why: It targets two known weaknesses of agentic forecasting: context bloat in ReAct loops and slow, noisy outcome-only rewards.

s56f47ff6a1.title: HookEvo: A Framework for Coordinated Plugin Evolution on Hook-Enabled Agent Runtimes
s56f47ff6a1.description: arXiv:2611.27294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repairing failures in tool-using agents can require coordinated changes to how the harness interprets tool receipts, assembles context, and checks actions. We introduce HookEvo, a framework that uses an existing agent runtime's lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses. We instantiate HookEvo on DeepSeek Harness. In each round, a separate improver diagnoses failures from execution traces and proposes a candidate. HookEvo evaluates the candidate against the current harness on matched tasks and carries the retained version into the next round. A single candidate can jointly edit executable plugin handlers and the state they share within a task, allowing a tool receipt to inform context and control a later action. Using a frozen Qwen3-4B
s56f47ff6a1.summary: HookEvo is a framework that uses agent runtime lifecycle hooks to evolve task-specific harnesses, with an improver proposing candidates that are evaluated against the current harness.
s56f47ff6a1.why: It offers a method for automatically repairing tool-using agent failures by coordinating changes to tool receipts, context assembly, and action checks.

s74a9dcadb0.title: $\gamma$-Scape: An Agent-Centric World for Mobile Embodied Intelligence
s74a9dcadb0.description: arXiv:2611.27306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent embodied agents construct and adapt robot behavior through executable programs, tool use, and interaction feedback. Studying these systems in mobile manipulation calls for physical worlds that connect agent-directed execution with its physical consequences and reusable interaction experience. We introduce $\gamma$-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform for mobile embodied intelligence. Agents compose motion tools and learned skills to carry out complete tasks that combine navigation and manipulation in a persistent physical world. BenchForge grounds structured objectives in physical task instances with instructions, reference programs, and goal evaluators, defining task goals while preserving agents' choice of valid
s74a9dcadb0.summary: Researchers introduce γ-Scape, an agent-centric simulation and benchmark platform where agents compose motion tools and learned skills for mobile manipulation tasks.
s74a9dcadb0.why: It provides a persistent physical simulation benchmark for evaluating embodied agents that combine navigation and manipulation.

sd6efc31d2a.title: H-MSAE: Hierarchical Sparse Concept Coverage for Efficient and Diverse Instruction Data Selection
sd6efc31d2a.description: arXiv:2611.27329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large instruction-tuning corpora contain substantial semantic redundancy, motivating the selection of compact subsets that preserve useful supervision while reducing training cost. Existing diversity-aware selectors often rely on generated semantic tags and explicit graph structures, introducing considerable annotation and preprocessing overhead. We introduce H-MSAE, a hierarchical sparse instruction selection framework that organizes multi-resolution concepts learned by a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder into a coarse-to-fine hierarchy. Quality-weighted, diminishing-return coverage with ancestor propagation promotes high-quality and non-redundant semantic coverage, while pool-relative length constraints regulate subset composition. We motivate
sd6efc31d2a.summary: H-MSAE is a hierarchical sparse instruction selection method that organizes concepts from a Matryoshka sparse autoencoder to pick diverse, compact instruction-tuning subsets.
sd6efc31d2a.why: It aims to cut instruction-tuning costs by removing semantic redundancy without the annotation overhead of existing diversity selectors.

s3a75be3aed.title: GGDriver: Glance at What Is Shared, Gaze at What Differs for Perception-Free Planning
s3a75be3aed.description: arXiv:2611.27330v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A planner deciding whether to turn left or continue straight needs to inspect different parts of the scene for each maneuver. Yet many end-to-end driving planners evaluate every candidate trajectory against the same compressed scene representation. We let each candidate select the visual evidence used to refine and score it. A global glance first produces trajectory hypotheses from shared scene features. We then project a corridor around each trajectory into the camera views and use the resulting mask to attend to patch features at the backbone's native resolution. After refinement, the scorer projects each final proposal again and ranks it using evidence along its own path. This geometric selection requires only the predicted trajectory and
s3a75be3aed.summary: GGDriver is an end-to-end driving planner in which each candidate trajectory selects its own visual evidence from camera features to refine and score itself.
s3a75be3aed.why: It proposes a per-trajectory attention mechanism for planning, relevant to autonomous driving stack design.

sb2c44c249e.title: EcomWriteBench: A Real-World Benchmark for E-commerce Writing Tasks
sb2c44c249e.description: arXiv:2611.27349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used throughout e-commerce workflows to generate content that informs purchasing decisions and supports customer interactions. Evaluating these systems requires accounting for user needs, product evidence, structural constraints, and business requirements that are not fully captured by general-purpose writing benchmarks. We introduce EcomWriteBench, a real-world benchmark containing 3,861 queries from 69 e-commerce writing tasks across 13 categories and five languages. Through task-level extraction, cross-task consolidation, and refinement guided by human feedback, EcomWriteBench constructs a shared pool of 37 abilities and identifies the subset applicable to each task. Ability-wise scoring enable
sb2c44c249e.summary: EcomWriteBench is a benchmark of 3,861 queries across 69 e-commerce writing tasks, 13 categories and five languages, for evaluating LLMs on commerce content.
sb2c44c249e.why: It offers a domain-specific evaluation set for teams deploying LLMs in e-commerce content and customer workflows.

sc15a9d5ce0.title: GRACE: Controlled Evidence Interventions for Diagnosing and Improving Knowledge Integration in GraphRAG
sc15a9d5ce0.description: arXiv:2611.27350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GraphRAG combines a language model's parametric knowledge with retrieved graph evidence, yet aggregate accuracy cannot show whether failures stem from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge. We introduce GRACE, a benchmark built by executing LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata and applying four controlled interventions to each evidence subgraph: severing a support path, adding type-compatible distractors, attaching high-degree hubs, and replacing the supported answer with a counterfactual entity. Questions and option positions remain fixed across the five states. The validated benchmark contains 4,028 questions and 20,140 question-graph pairs. These comparisons reveal that question-only routing cannot distinguish evidence
sc15a9d5ce0.summary: GRACE is a GraphRAG benchmark built from LC-QuAD 2.0 queries over Wikidata, applying controlled evidence interventions to diagnose knowledge integration failures.
sc15a9d5ce0.why: It helps teams tell whether GraphRAG failures come from missing paths, distractors, or conflicts with model knowledge.

s1f40527b0d.title: WePM: Hierarchical Conflict Reconciliation for Unified MLLMs
s1f40527b0d.description: arXiv:2611.27365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bringing multimodal intelligence from the cloud to users' devices keeps sensitive data local and reduces inference cost, but deploying a specialized model per capability duplicates vision-language capacity under tight memory and compute budgets. We formalize heterogeneous capability density (HCD), measuring how broadly and effectively a model serves heterogeneous task families per unit of resident inference memory. High HCD across representation, generation, and decision raises two challenges: these capabilities need visual evidence at different spatial granularities under a fixed token budget, and separately collected task corpora yield conflicting updates to shared parameters, while cross-task paired supervision is costly and ambiguous for
s1f40527b0d.summary: WePM proposes hierarchical conflict reconciliation for unified multimodal LLMs, aiming to serve multiple vision-language capabilities within limited on-device memory.
s1f40527b0d.why: It addresses running several multimodal capabilities in one model under tight memory and compute budgets on user devices.

sb9e9d87c99.title: AMARIS: Merging Generalist and Specialist LLMs via Adaptive Subspace Inheritance
sb9e9d87c99.description: arXiv:2611.27369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Domain specialization of large language models (LLMs) often improves target-domain performance but degrades broad capabilities. Model merging is an attractive training-free alternative, yet common parameter-space strategies (for example, interpolation and sparsified averaging) provide limited control over task-specific interference. We introduce Adaptive Model Alignment via Ranked Inherited Subspaces (AMARIS), a covariance-driven framework that transfers specialist updates only along selected activation directions. AMARIS formulates merging as budgeted subspace inheritance: it seeks high specialist activation capture under a regularized base-output perturbation budget, then builds a low-rank projection gate from ranked generalized eigendirect
sb9e9d87c99.summary: AMARIS is a training-free model merging method that transfers specialist LLM updates only along selected activation directions to limit interference with general capabilities.
sb9e9d87c99.why: It offers a training-free alternative to fine-tuning that may preserve broad model abilities when adding domain specialization.

s600ed65a73.title: ReActWAM: Action-Consistent Caching for Efficient World-Action Models
s600ed65a73.description: arXiv:2611.27372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World-action models (WAMs) often generate future visual states alongside robot actions, introducing substantial computational overhead during inference. During closed-loop execution, consecutive inference cycles often predict similar action sequences, leading to redundant computation. However, reducing this redundancy requires distinguishing consistent actions from changes that demand fresh computation. To address these challenges, we propose ReActWAM, a training-free framework that combines action-intent-guided prefix skipping with inner-chunk prediction reuse. A coarse-to-fine assessment evaluates motion changes, visual consistency, and action prediction conflicts. For eligible chunks, we draw on first-step differences to adapt the cached l
s600ed65a73.summary: ReActWAM is a training-free framework that caches and skips redundant computation in world-action models during consecutive robot inference cycles.
s600ed65a73.why: It could reduce inference overhead for robot policies that generate future visual states alongside actions.

se2054f5cfa.title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
se2054f5cfa.description: arXiv:2611.27390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. We propose training-free decision-point evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier sequential triage protocol. Masking reasoning and diagnosis, the same 4B model scores sufficiency from objective evidence via prior-debiased probabilities over five ordered levels. Calibration freezes a nominal top-50% threshold, selecting single-run, five-run consistency, or full-deferral tiers by whether the one-sided 95% Wilson lower confidence bound of pass rate among accepted cases meets the 95% clinical target
se2054f5cfa.summary: Researchers propose training-free evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier triage protocol so an on-premise 4B clinical agent can auto-accept confident diagnoses and defer others.
se2054f5cfa.why: It offers a lower-compute way to decide which clinical AI outputs need human review, versus costly repeated-run consistency checks.

s7a2bf0a96f.title: Beyond Linear Decodability: Understanding and Improving Instruction Following in World Action Models
s7a2bf0a96f.description: arXiv:2611.27401v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World action models (WAMs) exhibit strong manipulation capabilities yet often fail to follow test-time language instructions. Prior work shows that non-following (NF) WAMs encode information about the instructed target, but this information does not control their behavior. By comparing NF WAM with its instruction-following (IF) counterpart, we find that target information is substantially more linearly decodable in IF WAMs, despite being encoded in both. Motivated by this observation, we introduce linear decodability supervision (LDS), a simple yet effective auxiliary training objective that promotes the linear decodability of the instructed target information. On LIBERO-CF, InternW0-$\Delta$ with LDS achieves a success rate of 74.6% and a gr
s7a2bf0a96f.summary: Researchers propose linear decodability supervision to improve instruction following in world action models, which often encode target information without acting on it.
s7a2bf0a96f.why: It identifies why robot policies ignore instructions despite encoding the target, and offers a simple training fix.

s830195f89c.title: Jagged Robustness: Uneven Safety Transfer and Emerging Vulnerabilities under LLM Quantization
s830195f89c.description: arXiv:2611.27424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantization enables efficient inference in language models through model parameter compression. This work audits the impact of quantization on capability and safety domains including model safeguards, instruction-following, ethics and bias. Through benchmarks, we find that model safeguards and bias can degrade under quantization, while other capabilities such as truthfulness remain more stable in Qwen3-4B. We define this uneven transfer of LLM capabilities under quantization as Jagged Robustness. We find multiple factors driving Jagged Robustness: task complexity, evaluation method and generation coherence. Moreover, we verify the degradation of model safeguards by observing increased compliance with unsafe requests under quantization, and d
s830195f89c.summary: A study of Qwen3-4B finds that quantization degrades safeguards and bias behavior while truthfulness stays stable, an uneven pattern the authors call Jagged Robustness.
s830195f89c.why: Teams deploying quantized models should not assume safety behavior transfers evenly; safeguards and bias may degrade.

s1431d3eec6.title: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy: A judgment-aggregation perspective
s1431d3eec6.description: arXiv:2611.27463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy is based on the idea that some sentences, or predicates within them, have multiple competing interpretations or specifications. A sentence is deemed determinately true if and only if it is true according to all specifications; and determinately false if and only if it is false according to all specifications. In all other cases, the sentence is assigned no determinate truth-value. Supervaluationism, however, is only one way of taking into account the verdicts of different specifications -- in technical terms, "aggregating" those verdicts. In this paper, we introduce insights from the theory of judgment aggregation to study a broad class of different aggregation functions. This allows us to o
s1431d3eec6.summary: A philosophy paper examines supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy through the lens of judgment aggregation.

s10b9bbb2d3.title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation
s10b9bbb2d3.description: arXiv:2611.27483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). We introduce GenAI4SimPy, a multi-agent framework powered by Qwen 3.6 (27B), an open-weight large language model, that automates end-to-end DES generation from manufacturing event logs to executable SimPy models through tool-augmented reasoning and human-in-the-loop validation. Evaluated on three execution blocks from a public smart factory dataset, the framework achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 7.9\% and coverage of failure rate for all three blocks and of throughput for two of three. A fidelity paradox was observed: accurate process-level parameters did not ensure system-level behavioral fidelity, with flow-time and
s10b9bbb2d3.summary: GenAI4SimPy is a multi-agent framework using the open-weight Qwen 3.6 (27B) model to generate executable SimPy discrete-event simulations from manufacturing event logs, with human validation.
s10b9bbb2d3.why: It shows an open-weight, agent-based route for giving small manufacturers simulation capability without specialized expertise.

se5e8375acb.title: Efficient Natural Language to Temporal Logic Translation for Real-Time Physical AI
se5e8375acb.description: arXiv:2611.27489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Robots can be controlled to perform tasks with guaranteed correctness when the task instructions are stated in a formal language. Large language models (LLMs) have been widely used to allow users to provide such instructions in natural language (NL), by translating NL into formal language. When deploying such translators on a robot, however, we face limited computing and energy resources, while offloading computation or data to the cloud may be infeasible or undesirable. Yet an LLM is a general-purpose text generator, whereas a formula in a fixed formal language fragment follows a well-defined syntax. We therefore ask whether text generation is needed at all. For the formal language of linear temporal logic (LTL), we show that this translatio
se5e8375acb.summary: Researchers study translating natural language into temporal logic for robots using compact models instead of large LLMs, given limited on-device compute and energy.
se5e8375acb.why: Shows how robots could run instruction-to-formal-spec translation on-device, avoiding cloud offloading under tight compute and energy budgets.

s47609eed3e.title: Trained on Harm, Still Refusing: A Training-Time Defense for Code Generation
s47609eed3e.description: arXiv:2611.27495v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning enables safety-aligned code language models to adapt to diverse downstream tasks. However, training on untrusted data can severely undermine their ability to refuse harmful requests. Notably, we find that models comply with harmful requests even though harmfulness information remains highly decodable from their internal representations. Moreover, an initial preference for refusal does not necessarily translate into sustained refusal behavior throughout generation. Together, these findings reveal a critical gap between recognizing harmful requests and consistently refusing to fulfill them. To address this gap, we introduce SAFEHOLD, a novel provider-enforced defense framework that preserves safety alignment during harmful fine-tuni
s47609eed3e.summary: Researchers find fine-tuning on untrusted data can erode code models' refusal of harmful requests, and propose a training-time defense to restore refusal.
s47609eed3e.why: Fine-tuning on untrusted data can silently weaken safety in code models, so teams deploying fine-tuned models need training-time safeguards.

s9c3ba71680.title: Altair-Nidhogg: Which Model-Merging Theories Hold for a One-Pass Decision Encoder? Soups, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE Against Joint Training and Prediction Ensembling
s9c3ba71680.description: arXiv:2611.27550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laya is a small model that answers a multiple-choice question in one pass: each option has a name and a written description. A new skill costs a training run, so we test whether published recipes for merging fine-tuned models (weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES, DARE) work for it, and whether the theories behind them hold. All 156 models start from one released checkpoint: four plain fine-tunes, five specialists (each adds one kind of training row), joint fine-tunes on all rows, and prediction ensembles. Items are held-out, synthetic and LLM-labelled. In-family, each skill is scored on new items of its own kind, and "kept" is the share of a specialist's gain over the plain fine-tune. Averaging four specialists keeps 52% [38, 64] with +1.
s9c3ba71680.summary: Researchers test whether model-merging methods like weight averaging, task arithmetic, TIES and DARE work for a small one-pass multiple-choice decision model across 156 models.
s9c3ba71680.why: Tests whether cheap model merging can replace retraining for adding skills, which matters for maintaining small specialized models.

s86d158aa7c.title: Vega-Fafnir: Is Greedy Decoding the Same Decoding? Where Rounding Noise in Speculative Verification Comes From and What Removing It Costs
s86d158aa7c.description: arXiv:2611.27554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Serving engines treat the ways of running a greedy language model as interchangeable: cached or not, padded or not, alone or batched, one token or several verified at once (speculative decoding). In finite precision they round differently. We measure how often the greedy text of Qwen3-0.6B (bfloat16, 128 new tokens, GSM8K and ARC prompts) differs from a reference that decodes one token per pass. Verifying 4 guessed tokens per pass changes 60% of 150 prompts and padding changes 68%; every first divergence has a top-1 minus top-2 logit gap of 0.375 or less. A split of the noise shows that cache entries written by multi-token passes are about as noisy as the multi-token pass itself. A margin gate (fall back to one token when the gap is below a b
s86d158aa7c.summary: Researchers show that greedy decoding outputs can differ across serving configurations such as batching, padding and speculative decoding due to finite-precision rounding noise.
s86d158aa7c.why: Serving optimizations like speculative decoding and padding can change greedy outputs, which matters for reproducibility and evaluation consistency.

s87e00e1f86.title: Can Language Models See the Circuit in Pixelated RFIC Passives?
s87e00e1f86.description: arXiv:2611.27559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The emergence of inverse-designed, pixelated passives for microwave and millimeter-wave applications has been a major development in the field of RFIC design. These devices, which appear to be QR-code-like in structure, exist in a generalizable, high-dimensional design space that includes conventional passive topologies. However, these structures are naturally unintuitive for designers, and failures or deviations in performance are difficult to debug.
