sa25e27fc12.title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
sa25e27fc12.description: arXiv:2611.27079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate that weight-space programming and edits guided by sparse autoencoders can remove unwanted aspects of a particle-physics foundation model through direct edits to its weights. In a foundation model trained on jets, we observe that adding a single soft neutral particle causes large changes in jet classification, violating infrared safety. We locate the responsible attention heads with mechanistic analysis and trace the flaw's origin to pretraining on datasets with different reconstruction thresholds. We then propose two targeted approaches to repair the flaw: by removing three latent directions identified with sparse autoencoders, and by letting language-model agents edit the weights directly, without gradients and with only 50
sa25e27fc12.summary: Researchers use sparse autoencoders and mechanistic analysis to edit weights of a particle-physics foundation model, fixing an infrared safety violation caused by pretraining data.
sa25e27fc12.why: Demonstrates targeted weight edits and mechanistic interpretability as a way to correct specific flaws in a foundation model.

scd64341212.title: Fooling the Mind Twice: Human Detection of Audiovisual Deepfakes Under Repeated Exposure and Corrective Feedback
scd64341212.description: arXiv:2611.27080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Human deepfake detection remains unreliable, and whether reassessment with corrective feedback improves subsequent judgments remains unclear. This study examined differences between initial and repeated deepfake assessments among 110 participants using audiovisual stimuli from the FakeAVCeleb and Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC) datasets. Participants evaluated 40 videos from each dataset in phase 1 (PhaseI) and reassessed the same videos in phase 2 (PhaseII) under a procedure combining repeated presentation and corrective feedback. For the FakeAVCeleb dataset, the participants' mean accuracy increased by 4.68 percentage points from 63.30 in PhaseI to 67.98 in PhaseII (t(109)=5.61, p<.001, d_z=0.54). A judgment-level logistic regression
scd64341212.summary: A study of 110 participants finds human audiovisual deepfake detection is unreliable and examines whether repeated exposure with corrective feedback improves judgments.
scd64341212.why: Shows humans remain unreliable deepfake detectors, which matters for designing verification workflows that rely on human review.

s94757dab97.title: Exercised, Rarely Recovered: What Public Reports Say About Recovery in 50 AI Agent Harnesses and Runtimes
s94757dab97.description: arXiv:2611.27090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When an AI coding agent deletes the wrong files or a long agent run crashes, users fall back on recovery mechanisms: resume from a checkpoint, undo, ask for approval, read the log. Research runtimes promise stronger guarantees, such as saga-style compensation and transactional rollback. We ask what public evidence shows about whether either kind works in real use. Under a protocol frozen before data collection, we graded 12 persistent agent runtimes, 26 coding-agent harnesses and 12 research runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, from not found to exercised in a real run, with two blind coding passes, adjudication and re-verification against archived sources. Recovery is exercised almost everywhere in practice: 11 of 12 runtimes and 25 of 2
s94757dab97.summary: A study grades 50 AI agent harnesses and runtimes on eight recovery mechanisms, based on public reports about how agents recover from wrong deletions or crashes.
s94757dab97.why: Suggests recovery mechanisms like checkpoints and rollback are rarely evident in real agent tools, a concern for anyone running coding agents.

s906d302ef4.title: Separating Automation Gains from Agent Contributions in AI-Assisted Model Validation
s906d302ef4.description: arXiv:2611.27094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents are being proposed for bank model validation, yet evaluations that compare agent-assisted work with manual practice credit the agent with gains that come from digitized evidence and deterministic tests. We propose a staged architecture in which an LLM-free controlled workflow (P1) is both the fallback and the control arm for individually authorized agent tasks (P2), and an attribution protocol that credits an agent only for faults P1 does not already report. The protocol charges decoy false alarms, unnecessary actions and endorsed developer assertions, counts invalid outputs as misses, folds newly automatable findings back into P1 with discovery credit, and fixes safety bounds and a break-even cost gate in advance. On a synthetic
s906d302ef4.summary: A paper proposes an attribution protocol for LLM agents in bank model validation that credits agents only for faults a deterministic LLM-free workflow does not already find.
s906d302ef4.why: Offers a method to measure true agent contribution versus gains from automation in regulated model validation workflows.

s6d4a57c91a.title: Epistemic Guard: Out-of-Process MCP Receipt Proxying, Post-Turn Prose Supervision, and Provenance-Gated Memory for Tool-Using Autonomous Agents
s6d4a57c91a.description: arXiv:2611.27095v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language-model agents using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) face three runtime verification gaps: (i) action fabrication, where post-tool prose narrates side effects that failed, timed out, or never ran; (ii) provenance collapse, where unverified model prose or web text enters durable memory alongside executed tool outputs; and (iii) syndicated echo amplification, where mirrored web pages satisfy multi-source corroboration from one origin. Existing MCP firewalls inspect wire calls before execution, while LLM-judge guardrails require multi-gigabyte VRAM without binding prose to receipts. We present epistemic-guard (v0.5.2), an open-source Python library and out-of-process stdio MCP receipt proxy (15 modules, 0 MiB GPU VRAM). epistemic-guard
s6d4a57c91a.summary: Epistemic Guard proposes runtime verification for MCP tool-using agents, addressing action fabrication, provenance collapse in memory, and syndicated echo amplification.
s6d4a57c91a.why: Targets concrete runtime gaps in MCP agents, such as prose narrating failed side effects and unverified content entering durable memory.

se05939eff2.title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology
se05939eff2.description: arXiv:2611.27102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A synoptic pathology report is a checklist of questions with fixed answer sets, many composed from others. Pathology foundation models answer them accurately with one classifier trained with labels for each, and frontier language models, which compose freely, cannot fit a slide of fourteen thousand tiles in their context. On 189 breast report questions, frontier models that read a written description of the slide or look at a thumbnail and tiles of it answer at 0.50 to 0.66, below the majority class at 0.67. A description is written before the question is known, and a look covers a handful of tiles. We present Opsis, which lets the model ask instead: a typed question interface on a frozen pathology encoder. A slide is encoded once, a questi
se05939eff2.summary: Opsis pairs a frontier model with typed pathology classifiers, reporting that frontier models reading slide descriptions or thumbnails underperform the majority-class baseline on 189 breast report questions.
se05939eff2.why: Shows frontier models alone underperform on structured pathology questions, pointing to hybrid designs that combine specialist classifiers with LLMs.

s43ae79ddd3.title: Schema-Validated LLM Workflows: A Benchmark Protocol and Comparative Evaluation Across Six Python Implementations
s43ae79ddd3.description: arXiv:2611.27106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to extract records, generate SQL, summarize reports, answer policy questions, and route operational work. At these software boundaries, parseable output is necessary but does not establish task correctness. We present a reproducible benchmark protocol, a public executable artifact, and a confirmatory live API evaluation that separate structural validity from task-specific correctness across five business workflow tasks and six Python implementation conditions: PydanticAI, LangGraph, DSPy, CrewAI, Agno, and a framework-free SDK reference. We hypothesize that (H1) schema validity and task quality are separable, (H2) structured-output binding paths are heterogeneous under a shared model and lowest-co
s43ae79ddd3.summary: A paper proposes a reproducible benchmark protocol and public artifact comparing six Python LLM workflow frameworks on schema-valid output and task correctness across five business tasks.
s43ae79ddd3.why: It separates structurally valid LLM output from correct results, helping teams choose frameworks and test LLM outputs at software boundaries.

scc0dedbb4f.title: Do Senior Agents Do Their Job? Measuring Role Integrity in How LLM Agents Use Subordinate Material
scc0dedbb4f.description: arXiv:2611.27139v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly divide long tasks among subagents whose reports a senior agent turns into the final answer. Such a division of labor pays off only if each agent, and above all the senior agent, carries out the duties of its role. Current evaluations, however, mostly score the final answer, and a fluent, well-cited answer cannot show whether the senior agent weighed its subagents' reports or merely aggregated them. To assess whether a senior agent meets its assigned responsibilities, we define role integrity as the preservation of an agent's functional responsibilities when it acts on its subordinates' material. To measure it, we introduce RI-Bench, a behavioral benchmark grounded in the structures and public records of
scc0dedbb4f.summary: Researchers define role integrity and propose measuring whether senior LLM agents truly weigh subordinate agents' reports rather than merely aggregating them.
scc0dedbb4f.why: Final-answer scores can hide whether a multi-agent orchestrator actually does its job, so teams need process-level evaluation.

sa1d86b49f0.title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer
sa1d86b49f0.description: arXiv:2611.27142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Promptable segmentation foundation models are increasingly used in specialized domains, but it remains unclear how SAM-3 should be fine-tuned when adapting it beyond its original training distribution. We study this question by comparing five adaptation families --LoRA, HiRA, KRAdapter, QuanTA, and Full Fine-Tuning-- across five segmentation datasets spanning medical imaging, remote sensing, and dense material segmentation. Across these datasets, compact parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods often match or approach Full Fine-Tuning in DSC and IoU, suggesting that strong in-domain adaptation does not always require updating the full model. However, this performance cannot be explained by nominal adapter rank or trainable parameter count al
sa1d86b49f0.summary: A study compares five fine-tuning methods for adapting SAM-3 segmentation to medical imaging, remote sensing, and material segmentation datasets.
sa1d86b49f0.why: Parameter-efficient methods often approach full fine-tuning here, suggesting cheaper adaptation options for specialized vision domains.

sd7549dbebf.title: Structure Over Scale: Rethinking Adaptation for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
sd7549dbebf.description: arXiv:2611.27148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) is often framed as a choice between the expressivity of Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) and the efficiency of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). We find that this framing misses an important variable: the geometry of the update. Under a common cold-start GRPO protocol, LoRA exhibits rank collapse: performance remains broadly stable at low rank, then fails abruptly as rank increases. On DeepMath-Hard, for example, accuracy drops from 73.1% at r=64 to 4.7% at r=128. In contrast, Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation (DoRA) and Quantum-Informed Tensor Adaptation (QuanTA) remain stable over a wider tested optimization region and are competitive with FFT while updating less than 0.6% of the model parameters.
sd7549dbebf.summary: Researchers report that LoRA suffers rank collapse under GRPO reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, while a weight-decomposed variant avoids the failure.
sd7549dbebf.why: Adapter rank choice can abruptly break RL fine-tuning, so teams using LoRA for RLVR should validate rank settings carefully.

s9be6c68a69.title: Co-Evolving Behavioral Agents and Detectors for Adaptive Information Operations
s9be6c68a69.description: arXiv:2611.27156v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Detectors of state-sponsored information operations (IOs) are trained on campaigns that platforms have already taken down. They lose much of their accuracy on an actor they have not seen, even though no operator in the archived data is trying to avoid them. A real operator wants two things, to reach an audience and to avoid being caught. We present IO-AI, a framework that gives simulated agents these two capabilities, engagement and evasion, and tests what each one does to detection. The agents are built from the posting behavior of real campaigns and choose the emotion, type, and timing of each post. An agent and a detector then train against each other in turn. We rank the trained agents by how hard they are to detect and train one detect
s9be6c68a69.summary: IO-AI is a framework that gives simulated information-operation agents engagement and evasion capabilities to test how these affect detector accuracy.
s9be6c68a69.why: It offers a way to stress-test detectors against adaptive adversaries rather than only archived, already-removed campaigns.

s253a177be9.title: Felid: A Flexible and Efficient Design for Transformer Fine-Tuning over Encrypted Data
s253a177be9.description: arXiv:2611.27175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables non-interactive, privacy-preserving transformer fine-tuning, protecting highly sensitive data as inputs to large language models. Prior work has predominantly pursued efficiency gains through architectural refinements, yet overall performance remains bounded by the substantial cost inherent in encrypted computation. To address these issues, we target the bottleneck at the ciphertext operation level. Concretely, we propose a novel packing strategy that supports batching over a flexible number of inputs, making it well-suited for fine-tuning workloads. In addition, we design operation-specific matrix evaluation algorithms that significantly reduce (i) the number of ciphertext rotations and relineariz
s253a177be9.summary: Felid proposes a new ciphertext packing strategy to speed up transformer fine-tuning over fully homomorphic encrypted data.
s253a177be9.why: Lowering encrypted computation cost could make privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning on sensitive data more practical.

s673e102a3c.title: GEG-SAM: Gaze Exploration-Guided Segment Anything Model for Weakly Supervised Polyp Segmentation
s673e102a3c.description: arXiv:2611.27183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Endoscopist gaze offers an unobtrusively acquired record of lesion-oriented visual exploration during routine clinical inspection, providing relevant supervision for tasks. However, existing methods treat fixations as isolated spatial prompts directly associated with the target, overlooking the fact that natural gaze records a continuous visual search process in which fixations are temporally connected, spatially organized, and coupled with the visual content. Interpreting each fixation independently based only on its local visual content overlooks the temporal evolution and spatial organization of the gaze trajectory, whereas modeling relations among fixations alone cannot reveal the visual semantics of the regions they attend to. To this
s673e102a3c.summary: GEG-SAM uses temporally connected endoscopist gaze fixations to guide the Segment Anything Model for weakly supervised polyp segmentation.

s83325b18b5.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI
s83325b18b5.description: arXiv:2611.27189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: India's AI debate often swings between two insufficient options: replicating the compute-intensive, capital-heavy foundation-model programmes of the United States or China, or remaining a downstream adopter of foreign AI with localised interfaces and safeguards. Neither serves a country that must deliver AI to a very large, diverse population across uneven infrastructure and within constrained budgets. This white paper from the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI), IIT Madras, proposes a third path: Responsible Frugal AI, which applies principle-based frugal engineering alongside Responsible AI. Responsible Frugal AI is right-sized AI: it fixes the functional requirement first, asks whether AI is needed at all, and then chooses the smallest su
s83325b18b5.summary: An IIT Madras CeRAI white paper proposes Responsible Frugal AI as a third path for India, favoring right-sized AI over replicating large foundation-model programmes.
s83325b18b5.why: It offers a policy and design perspective on building AI under tight compute and budget constraints for large, diverse populations.

s61299b2edb.title: DepthMSA: Combinatorial Training and Budget-Aware Depth Allocation for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
s61299b2edb.description: arXiv:2611.27198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: State-of-the-art multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) models rely on large pretrained encoders, yet typically process every modality to its full depth, regardless of its computational cost or predictive contribution. This raises a fundamental question: how should limited computation be allocated across modalities to preserve predictive performance? We reveal a substantial mismatch between the computational cost of modality encoders and the predictive benefit of processing them more deeply, suggesting that different modalities require different encoding depths. However, enabling heterogeneous depths introduces a key challenge: representations extracted at different depths must still be effectively fused. To address this, we propose $\textbf{D
s61299b2edb.summary: DepthMSA proposes combinatorial training and budget-aware depth allocation so multimodal sentiment models process each modality to different depths.
s61299b2edb.why: Allocating compute per modality by predictive benefit could cut inference cost in multimodal models without losing accuracy.

s7ee87e7987.title: LingSante-Pulse: Unified Physiological Pretraining through Random-Feature Prediction and Cross-Modal Alignment
s7ee87e7987.description: arXiv:2611.27206v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clinical monitoring and wearable devices capture complementary physiological signals, but their partially overlapping modality coverage makes within-signal information and cross-modal relationships difficult to exploit jointly. We introduce LingSante-Pulse, a unified, general-purpose and flexible physiological representation framework that learns from these heterogeneous recordings. A shared, signal-conditioned encoder processes each physical channel independently and supports different numbers and combinations of signals for multimodal assessment and single-sensor inference. Pairwise cross-modal alignment, structured random-feature prediction (RFP) and masked waveform reconstruction jointly learn physiological relationships and preserve in
s7ee87e7987.summary: LingSante-Pulse is a unified physiological representation framework that pretrains a shared encoder on heterogeneous clinical and wearable signals.

sbcf622f91e.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Qwen3-VL for Handwritten Mathematical Expression Recognition
sbcf622f91e.description: arXiv:2611.27208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Handwritten mathematical expression recognition (HMER) requires joint recovery of symbol identity and two-dimensional syntax, so a locally plausible transcription may still be structurally wrong. We study whether a compact vision-language model can be adapted to generate linearized Symbol Label Graphs (SLGs) under limited computing resources. Starting from a 4-bit Qwen3-VL-4B checkpoint, we apply rank-16 Low-Rank Adaptation to the vision, language, attention, and MLP modules and train with instruction-formatted CROHME 2019 examples. We compare this model with an internally implemented ViT-Transformer baseline, a zero-shot Qwen3-VL configuration, and additional internally evaluated alternatives. On the 1,198 valid CROHME test examples, the C
sbcf622f91e.summary: A study applies rank-16 LoRA to a 4-bit Qwen3-VL-4B model to recognize handwritten math expressions by generating symbol label graphs.
sbcf622f91e.why: It shows a compact vision-language model can be adapted to structured recognition tasks under limited compute.

s0263b6cc99.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
s0263b6cc99.description: arXiv:2611.27211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user's past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user's patterns, quoted evidence, and habits to avoid, then drafts from the user's samples and revises the draft twice against this profile, guided by its own style scores. On the three long-form tasks of LongLaMP with three LLMs, SP-Refine outperforms LongLaMP's retrieval-au
s0263b6cc99.summary: StylePrism defines 28 stylistic aspects and SP-Refine makes style extraction an explicit inference-time step for personalized long-form text generation.
s0263b6cc99.why: Explicit style extraction offers an alternative to leaving retrieved user texts for the model to interpret implicitly.

s74af93fbd3.title: EAF-TTS: Rethinking Codec-Latent Coordinates for Flow TTS
s74af93fbd3.description: arXiv:2611.27214v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent text-to-speech (TTS) systems generate codec latents decoded by a frozen decoder, but good reconstruction does not ensure geometry suitable for Flow generation from isotropic Gaussian noise. We present Embedded Acoustic Flow TTS (EAF-TTS), an acoustic-latent adaptation of ELF with phone- and duration-conditioned generation, shared-network terminal correction, and frozen WaveVAE decoding. EAF-TTS supports a fixed ZCA interface estimated from training data and adding no learned parameters. The codec, conditioning modules, Flow backbone, and 20-call inference are shared. The intervention is the full ZCA coordinate protocol---training and sampling coordinates, induced loss metric, and terminal perturbation---not an inference-only transfor
s74af93fbd3.summary: EAF-TTS adapts codec latents for flow-based text-to-speech, adding a fixed ZCA interface estimated from training data without learned parameters.

s4b07141410.title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard
s4b07141410.description: arXiv:2611.27215v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Commercial detectors of AI-generated audio are usually promoted with results on internal test sets that buyers cannot inspect. Independent benchmarks with private labels give a more reliable comparison. We report the results of Neural Defend's ARCAS foundation models on the Podonos audio deepfake detection benchmark, an independent leaderboard that scores commercial detection APIs and open-source detectors on one held-out set of real speech and speech from current text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems, delivered in six file formats, against labels that only Podonos holds. In the release of 29 October 2026, which covers 28 systems from 16 commercial vendors and the leading open models, ARCAS 290M and the smaller ARCAS 90M share first plac
s4b07141410.summary: Neural Defend reports its ARCAS models ranked first on the independent Podonos audio deepfake detection leaderboard against commercial and open-source detectors.
s4b07141410.why: Independent, privately labeled benchmarks offer a more reliable comparison than vendor-internal test results for detection tools.

s35e015cb88.title: Correct Precedents Induce Policy Violations in On-Device LLM Agents
s35e015cb88.description: arXiv:2611.27216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Local-cloud agent systems pair a cloud model with a small on-device agent that acts on private data, often as the last check before an irreversible action. We identify, for the first time, a failure in which such an agent is led into a violation by its own correct decisions within a session. After it correctly releases an item whose restriction was lifted, it becomes more likely to release the next item that is still restricted. Because the trigger is a correct decision, a history with no faulty step can still end in a violation. We call this failure correct-precedent generalization and find it in 13 open-weight models from nine developers. A single correct precedent can cut the safe rate of the most affected agent roughly in half, and the
s35e015cb88.summary: Researchers identify a failure where an on-device LLM agent's earlier correct release decisions make it more likely to release a later restricted item, causing violations.
s35e015cb88.why: Local-cloud agents acting as final checks can violate policy even with no faulty steps, so session-level safeguards are needed before irreversible actions.

s0e8705ea4a.title: NavTTT: Adaptive Parametric Memory via Hierarchical Test-Time Training for Vision-and-Language Navigation
s0e8705ea4a.description: arXiv:2611.27219v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) demands that agents accumulate and reason over streaming visual observations throughout long navigation episodes. Existing approaches struggle to maintain long-term history, constrained by the finite context capacity of transformer architectures. To solve the problem, fast-weight test-time training (TTT) provides a mechanism for encoding streaming observations into an evolving parameter state. However, existing TTT does not distinguish informative observations from repetitive visual content, allowing redundant tokens to interfere with the retention of information needed for subsequent decisions. We propose Navigation-Conditioned Test-Time Training (NavTTT), which introduces adaptive memory formation and
s0e8705ea4a.summary: Researchers propose NavTTT, a hierarchical test-time training method that gives vision-and-language navigation agents adaptive parametric memory over long streaming observations.
s0e8705ea4a.why: It targets the finite context limit of transformers for long-horizon embodied agents, a practical bottleneck for navigation systems.

s207cc22d6a.title: CreditFilter: Calibrated Token Weights over the Within-Response Entropy Rank for RLVR
s207cc22d6a.description: arXiv:2611.27227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Critic-free reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) typically assigns a uniform advantage to every token. Token-reweighting heuristics like the 80/20 mask favor high-entropy tokens, but fail to measure a token's actual impact on the outcome. We formalize this impact as the forking value: the variance of the success probability over the policy's next-token choices. The expected forking values along a response sum exactly to the reward variance. Token credit is thus, in expectation over a prompt's responses, a fixed budget spent at the forks. This motivates weights that redistribute credit within a response. The forking value factorizes into a fork consequence, which requires costly continuations to estimate, and a fork probabil
s207cc22d6a.summary: Researchers introduce CreditFilter, which assigns calibrated per-token weights based on a forking value measuring each token's actual impact on outcome in RLVR training.
s207cc22d6a.why: It offers a principled alternative to entropy-based token reweighting heuristics when post-training LLMs with verifiable rewards.

sba03b3f0d6.title: Proactive Defense Benchmark against Deepfake Generation
sba03b3f0d6.description: arXiv:2611.27253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Despite the proliferation of proactive defenses against deepfakes, the lack of a unified evaluation protocol precludes fair comparison and masks critical vulnerabilities. To bridge this gap, we present the first comprehensive benchmark that systematically assesses disruption, robustness, and transferability encompassing pixel, perceptual, and identity metrics. Our extensive analysis reveals that fidelity and identity metrics capture orthogonal performance axes, often leading to conflicting interpretations when relied upon individually. Furthermore, we identify a fundamental trade-off where peak white-box performance signals overfitting, and we introduce a calibrated evaluation to correct generator-induced identity bias. By exposing these bl
sba03b3f0d6.summary: Researchers present the first unified benchmark for evaluating proactive defenses against deepfake generation across disruption, robustness, and transferability.
sba03b3f0d6.why: It shows fidelity and identity metrics can conflict, so teams evaluating deepfake defenses should not rely on one metric alone.

s50b2bd1a5e.title: EAGLE: Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding
s50b2bd1a5e.description: arXiv:2611.27264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) still struggle with fine-grained understanding of high-resolution images: attention heads vary in their reliability for grounding target entities and their attributes, while localized details are often disconnected from the broader scene context. We propose EAGLE (Entity-Aware Grounding with Layered Evidence for High-Resolution Image Understanding), a plug-in framework that jointly selects grounding signals and organizes hierarchical visual evidence. EAGLE employs a fine-grained dataset to screen visually-grounded attention heads, followed by entity-aware grounding to extract target-specific regions. It then integrates hierarchical evidence construction and question-guided routing to select optimal v
s50b2bd1a5e.summary: Researchers propose EAGLE, a plug-in framework that improves multimodal LLMs' grounding of entities in high-resolution images by selecting reliable signals and layering visual evidence.
s50b2bd1a5e.why: It addresses fine-grained high-resolution image understanding, a known weakness of current multimodal models.

s8fb84deae6.title: Preserving Pretrained CFG Structure in RL for Diffusion Models with Conditional Contrast Regularization
s8fb84deae6.description: arXiv:2611.27288v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has become an important component in the post-training of diffusion models. In practice, however, standard RL often improves the target reward without reliably preserving holistic generation quality, leading to unstable reward-quality trade-offs that we view as a form of reward hacking. Since Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is known to improve visual clarity, prompt alignment, and perceptual quality in generation, we investigate whether its underlying structure can serve as a useful prior during RL. We present a unified geometric view that interprets both CFG and RL as correction vectors in a common prediction space, and identify the projection of the RL-induced correction onto the pretrained CFG correction as a u
s8fb84deae6.summary: Researchers propose conditional contrast regularization to preserve pretrained classifier-free guidance structure during reinforcement learning post-training of diffusion models.
s8fb84deae6.why: It aims to stop reward gains from degrading overall generation quality, a reward-hacking failure mode in diffusion RL.

s7cedc9f283.title: EgoLAM: Learning Latent Actions from Hand and Head Motion
s7cedc9f283.description: arXiv:2611.27290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent action models let a robot policy learn from video by turning the change between two frames into a training target. In egocentric video, a cup can move across the image because a hand pushes it or because the wearer turns. Both changes help predict the next frame, but only the first describes manipulation. During training, EgoLAM supervises the action code with measured wrist motion and supplies camera motion separately to the forward model. Even when the wearer turns while pushing a cup, the training target still describes how the hand pushed it. The action encoder pools object slots around each hand, and wrist translation and rotation can be decoded from the code in a common reference frame. Extracting a code then requires only two
s7cedc9f283.summary: Researchers present EgoLAM, which learns latent actions from egocentric video by supervising with measured wrist motion and modeling camera motion separately.
s7cedc9f283.why: Separating hand motion from head motion could improve robot policies learned from human video demonstrations.

s659f780bc0.title: Can Reasoning and Image Description Enhance Yes/No Visual Mathematical Understanding?
s659f780bc0.description: arXiv:2611.27302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on general visual tasks, yet their ability to understand mathematical images remains limited. This paper investigates whether explicit reasoning and textual image descriptions can enhance VLMs' performance on binary yes/no visual mathematical questions. To achieve this, we curated a paired evaluation set to benchmark prominent open-source VLMs under varying prompt and input conditions. In particular, we leverage Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting and use textual descriptions, either replacing or augmenting visual inputs, to isolate and evaluate mathematical comprehension. Our results show that explicit reasoning improves performance, especially in paired consistency accuracy
s659f780bc0.summary: Researchers study whether chain-of-thought reasoning and textual image descriptions improve open-source vision-language models on yes/no visual math questions.
s659f780bc0.why: It gives evidence on when prompting and description aids help VLMs with mathematical images, though the summary offers limited detail on results.

sfa59326541.title: A Framework for AI-Ready Data in Earth and Environmental Science
sfa59326541.description: arXiv:2611.27313v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), specifically machine learning (ML), is increasingly integral to Earth and environmental research, yet the suitability of current research data infrastructures for supporting AI workflows remains poorly defined. While the FAIR principles provide a foundation for scientific data management, they do not explicitly address several requirements arising when datasets are used for training, evaluating, and deploying AI models. This article presents a practically motivated framework for assessing and improving AI-readiness of research data within distributed Earth and environmental data infrastructures. The framework was developed through a structured, community-driven process, beginning with a review of existing liter
sfa59326541.summary: Researchers present a framework for assessing and improving the AI-readiness of Earth and environmental science datasets, extending FAIR principles to training and deployment needs.
sfa59326541.why: Teams building ML pipelines on scientific data can use it to check whether datasets meet training and evaluation requirements.

s5e8196d15f.title: Do Language Models Know Which Words Steer Their Reasoning?
s5e8196d15f.description: arXiv:2611.27317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits intermediate reasoning steps from language models, it is unclear which words in the context actually steer the CoT. We identify Phantom Context Influence (PCI): language models are disproportionately steered by semantically irrelevant context words, even as the same models deny those words' relevance when asked. To localize PCI, we introduce Leave-One-Out Word JSD analysis, which removes one context word at a time from the otherwise intact context to isolate its marginal effect on the next-token distribution; words whose removal flips the prediction (pivot words) are passed to the same LLM to self-judge whether it recognizes this predictive dependence. Across four models and three benchmarks, l
s5e8196d15f.summary: Researchers identify Phantom Context Influence, where language models are steered by semantically irrelevant context words and deny their relevance when asked.
s5e8196d15f.why: Irrelevant prompt content can silently skew reasoning, which matters for reliability and auditing of LLM applications.

s43df8b8d1d.title: Reasoning in Fewer Tokens: Concept-Normalized Multilingual Scratchpads and Reversible Model-Adaptive Reasoning Codes
s43df8b8d1d.description: arXiv:2611.27326v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) but incurs high inference costs due to lengthy autoregressive decoding. While previous efficiency approaches reduce costs by discarding tokens or utilizing continuous latent representations, these lossy methods fundamentally sacrifice interpretability and auditability. In this work, we introduce a novel compression framework for intermediate reasoning. We apply Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) to reasoning corpora to learn a compressed vocabulary of Private Use Area (PUA) tokens, each representing frequent semantic spans. After expanding the LLM's vocabulary, we fine-tune the model via strictly 1:1, our method is lossless. We evaluate our ap
s43df8b8d1d.summary: Researchers propose a compression framework that applies Byte-Pair Encoding to reasoning corpora to shorten chain-of-thought traces while keeping them interpretable.
s43df8b8d1d.why: Shorter reasoning traces could cut inference costs without the lossy trade-offs of discarding tokens or using latent representations.

sd2b85a4b68.title: Unimodal Shortcuts and Joint Scene-Intent Dependence in Vision-Language Safety Representations
sd2b85a4b68.description: arXiv:2611.27339v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The safety of a request to a vision-language model often depends on the image: asking how to serve a dish is harmless for fresh food and harmful for spoiled food. High accuracy on situational safety benchmarks does not tell us whether a model's safety representation encodes both the scene and the user's intent, because a benchmark can often be solved from one modality alone. Studying frozen vision-language safety representations, we audit five public situational benchmarks and find that each admits a unimodal shortcut: images alone predict the labels, and on same-image prompt pairs a probe that never sees the photograph reaches 0.9645 AUROC. We therefore build a controlled evaluation that crosses safe and hazardous scenes with observation a
sd2b85a4b68.summary: Researchers audit five public vision-language safety benchmarks and find each admits a unimodal shortcut, so high scores may not reflect joint scene-intent understanding.
sd2b85a4b68.why: Benchmark scores can overstate a model's safety reasoning, so teams should check for single-modality shortcuts before trusting results.

see744d37e7.title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models
see744d37e7.description: arXiv:2611.27344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and vide
see744d37e7.summary: Researchers introduce motion-region guidance to make robotic action-conditioned video world models focus on interaction-relevant regions rather than global reconstruction error.
see744d37e7.why: Better local interaction fidelity could make video world models more useful for robot policy evaluation and simulation.

s9da4b7ef1a.title: PAVE: A Harness for Geometrically Consistent Road Network Modeling with Vision-Language Models
s9da4b7ef1a.description: arXiv:2611.27352v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transportation models, whether they simulate traffic or support planning, are only as reliable as the road networks they run on, down to the lanes and turns at each intersection. Practitioners still take such a network from GIS files and supply its junction and movement data by hand, a task that recurs with each new base year and design alternative, or they generate it from open map data. OpenStreetMap's lane tags give the correct layout for only 13 of the 44 approaches we test; open map data are often incomplete or inaccurate. Satellite and street-level imagery, in contrast, cover all 44 and show their lanes as painted. Vision-language models (VLMs) can read such imagery, but asked directly they lose geometric consistency when the same lan
s9da4b7ef1a.summary: Researchers present PAVE, a harness using vision-language models to build geometrically consistent road network models, reporting OpenStreetMap lane tags correct for only 13 of 44 approaches tested.
s9da4b7ef1a.why: Transportation teams spend significant manual effort building road networks, and automated, consistent alternatives could reduce that work.

s01872c4203.title: WaXup: Weight Averaging of Experts as Data Augmentation for Robust Introspection
s01872c4203.description: arXiv:2611.27353v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As the capabilities of large language models keep improving, traditional mechanistic interpretability methods struggle to keep pace. In contrast, trainable introspection methods emerge as a promising alternative; they repurpose the model itself as a self-diagnostic tool, trained to verbalize what it has learned during finetuning in natural language. While training on datasets of finetuned experts achieves encouraging results, it currently lacks robustness and generalization. Building on the data augmentation framework of MiXup, we introduce WaXup, a method that augments the introspection training set through linear interpolation in the weight space. This is motivated by the linear mode connectivity property: weight averaged experts interpol
s01872c4203.summary: Researchers introduce WaXup, which applies weight averaging of finetuned experts as data augmentation to make trainable LLM introspection methods more robust.
s01872c4203.why: More robust introspection could offer a practical self-diagnostic tool for understanding what finetuning taught a model.

s19fc8427b0.title: Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
s19fc8427b0.description: arXiv:2611.27368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep parallel cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (CMARL)} trains multiple agents that all act at every time step to optimize a common objective. Like single-agent RL, CMARL can produce unsafe behaviors that violate implicit safety requirements not captured by the reward, and these behaviors are hard to explain. However, testing CMARL policies for safety has received less attention than the safety testing of single-agent RL policies. In this paper, we propose DisQ, a test case selection method that identifies failure-revealing states in value-based CMARL by exploiting a signal specific to trained Q-learning agents. The signal is the Q-value gap, an explainable metric that flags a state when the agents' estimates of the achievable
s19fc8427b0.summary: Researchers propose DisQ, a test case selection method that finds failure-revealing states to test cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning policies for safety violations.
s19fc8427b0.why: Multi-agent RL policies can violate safety requirements not captured by reward, and DisQ offers a way to surface those failures.

sbe4691731e.title: VMSA: Video Memory Skill Agent for Long Video Understanding
sbe4691731e.description: arXiv:2611.27381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-video question answering requires retrieving and integrating relevant evidence from videos spanning hours or even days. Recent agentic approaches organize video information into external memories and iteratively retrieve evidence to answer questions. However, effective retrieval and reasoning remain challenging, as agents must determine what information to search for, which memory sources to access, and how to connect evidence across distant temporal intervals. To address these challenges, we propose Video Memory Skill Agent (VMSA), a framework that jointly designs structured video memories and memory skills for long-video understanding. VMSA constructs three complementary memory components. Segment Caption Memory and Entity Event Memo
sbe4691731e.summary: Researchers introduce VMSA, a Video Memory Skill Agent that organizes video into external memories and iteratively retrieves evidence for long-video question answering.
sbe4691731e.why: Shows an agentic memory-and-retrieval pattern for reasoning over hours-long video, relevant to teams building long-context multimodal systems.

sdce75dc3d0.title: PanoUAV-Track: Full-Spherical UAV Visual Tracking in the Wild
sdce75dc3d0.description: arXiv:2611.27383v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing UAV tracking benchmarks predominantly rely on perspective cameras with limited fields of view. Omnidirectional cameras enable full-spherical observation, yet tracking from moving UAV platforms remains largely unexplored. Unlike ground-level panoramic tracking, UAV-mounted omnidirectional cameras observe targets across both azimuth and elevation, introducing geometric challenges under equirectangular projection (ERP). To investigate this setting, we capture approximately \textbf{40 hours of real-world 8K panoramic UAV video} and construct \textbf{PanoUAV-Track} through temporal clip extraction, target annotation, and the integration of simulated sequences. The resulting benchmark comprises 1,895 sequences, 507,961 frames, and 2,872
sdce75dc3d0.summary: Researchers present PanoUAV-Track, a benchmark of about 40 hours of 8K panoramic drone video for full-spherical visual object tracking from moving UAVs.
sdce75dc3d0.why: Provides a new benchmark for omnidirectional drone tracking, highlighting equirectangular projection challenges that standard perspective-camera benchmarks miss.

sdbc6e8f8b8.title: Taking Apart and Putting Together: Tracking Objects Through Physical Transformations
sdbc6e8f8b8.description: arXiv:2611.27398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending video object tracking to environments where objects undergo physical assemblies and disassemblies. TTU requires continuously tracking objects through transformations, identifying new entities, maintaining a state graph of their relationships, and assigning semantic labels to transformations. While foundation models (e.g., SAM 2/3) maintain tracklets through appearance changes, they cannot update semantic identities as objects physically evolve. Prior work addresses only disassemblies, relying on expensive searches triggered only when tracking fails. We propose Tracking Instances via Proposals and Overlaps (TIPO), a training-free framework that continuously infers transf
sdbc6e8f8b8.summary: Researchers introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending object tracking to objects that physically assemble and disassemble, maintaining a state graph of relationships.
sdbc6e8f8b8.why: Current foundation trackers like SAM 2/3 cannot update semantic identities as objects change physically, a gap relevant to robotics and video perception work.

s382af47d8c.title: Detecting Word-Substitution Poisoning of a RAG Knowledge Base with Relative Entropy and Runtime Verification
s382af47d8c.description: arXiv:2611.27410v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system answers questions using passages it retrieves from a knowledge base, so users must trust that knowledge base. We study an attacker who quietly edits existing passages by swapping words for synonyms (PWWS, TextFooler) in a cybersecurity RAG system built from MITRE ATT&CK and CAPEC. Using a reviewed 44-question benchmark, repeated paired runs and a control corpus in which only the layout changes, we find that poisoning lowers judged answer correctness from 0.714 to 0.555. The damage comes mostly from lost evidence and refusals, not from false statements. To find the edited passages, we use relative entropy. Comparing a whole passage with normal text is a weak signal. Still, one term of the relativ
s382af47d8c.summary: Researchers show synonym-swap poisoning of a RAG knowledge base lowers answer correctness from 0.714 to 0.555 and study detection using relative entropy and runtime verification.
s382af47d8c.why: Demonstrates a subtle data-integrity threat to RAG systems and a detection approach teams can evaluate for knowledge base monitoring.

sa89348b2dc.title: ADEPT: Adaptive Monocular Depth Estimation via Model-In-The-Loop Photometric Tuning with Capture Risk Prediction
sa89348b2dc.description: arXiv:2611.27423v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Exposure and gain determine the visual evidence available to monocular depth estimation (MDE), particularly when robot motion creates a tradeoff between light collection and motion blur. We present ADEPT, a framework that adapts these settings using learned feedback from a frozen depth model. During training, ground-truth depth identifies the lowest-error reference within a group of physically evaluated camera settings. A compact predictor learns reference-relative disagreement (RRD) between each candidate's depth prediction and the reference prediction using regression and ranking losses. At deployment, it scores observed captures using frozen-model features and camera, motion, and illumination context, without ground truth or reference im
sa89348b2dc.summary: ADEPT adapts camera exposure and gain for monocular depth estimation using feedback from a frozen depth model and a learned capture-risk predictor.
sa89348b2dc.why: Offers a method to tune camera settings for depth estimation on robots, trading light collection against motion blur.

sabb9f28457.title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
sabb9f28457.description: arXiv:2611.27425v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can reason directly about the weights of other neural networks. Given only a natural-language objective, an LLM can inspect a model's weights, understand what they compute, and edit them directly without gradient-based optimization. This capability, termed weight-space programming (WSP), has been used to improve model performance on math reasoning, medical QA and other benchmarks. We propose TrojanMaxxing, a novel strategy to backdoor vision-language models (VLMs), by reframing it as a WSP task. We use Claude Opus 5.5 and Mythos 5.2 agents to backdoor VLMs without any optimization or training methods. The agents inspect the model weights, apply targeted edits, and co-design an imperceptibl
sabb9f28457.summary: TrojanMaxxing proposes backdooring vision-language models by using an LLM to directly edit model weights from a natural-language objective, without gradient-based optimization.
sabb9f28457.why: Shows weight-space programming can be misused to implant backdoors in VLMs, a supply-chain security concern for teams deploying third-party models.

s64bfada739.title: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs
s64bfada739.description: arXiv:2611.27426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-weight Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely downloaded for their strong coding and reasoning capabilities and deployed locally beyond the provider's control. To prevent misuse, developers embed safety guardrails into these models before release. However, we find that these guardrails rely on the residual writing weights to trigger refusals. Based on this insight, we propose Cleave, a training-free attack that directly edits these weights to remove safety restrictions while preserving general capabilities. With Cleave, malicious users can either remove all guardrails or selectively lift only cybersecurity restrictions. Because this selective removal retains up to a 99% refusal rate on other harmful requests and avoids weight rank col
s64bfada739.summary: Cleave is a training-free attack that edits residual writing weights in open-weight LLMs to remove safety guardrails while preserving general capabilities.
s64bfada739.why: Shows safety refusals in open-weight models can be stripped via weight edits, so teams relying on embedded guardrails for local deployments face real risk.

s1c89671c16.title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning
s1c89671c16.description: arXiv:2611.27427v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and heterogeneous, often incomplete multimodal observations. Existing multimodal models can integrate imaging and clinical measurements but often overlook disease-specific evidence patterns and pairwise relations among competing diagnoses. We therefore propose Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning (KnowSR), which aligns multimodal patient representations with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes, signed evidence directions, and pairwise diagnostic relations. Specifically, in KnowSR, patient-specific knowledge alignment and target-aware pooling inject structured disease evidence, while anchored
s1c89671c16.summary: KnowSR aligns multimodal patient data with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes to improve differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders.

s4cfcc90159.title: No Audio, No Transcripts, No Problem: LLM-based ASR Adaptation Using Only Domain Documents
s4cfcc90159.description: arXiv:2611.27434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a speech recognizer be adapted to a new domain with no target audio and no transcripts, using only written documentation? This is the realistic onboarding setting: a new customer hands over raw documentation, not the transcripts that text-only adaptation normally assumes. We turn a domain's documents into adaptation text in two ways, directly as written sentences or rendered by a large language model (LLM) into synthetic spoken dialogs, and feed them to a recently proposed denoising-based text-only adaptation method. We show that, across in-domain, out-of-domain, and cross-domain settings on two corpora, document-only adaptation can match or closely approach real transcriptions; whether written or conversational rendering is best depend
s4cfcc90159.summary: Researchers show a speech recognizer can be adapted to a new domain using only written documents, converted directly or into synthetic spoken dialogs by an LLM, with no audio or transcripts.
s4cfcc90159.why: Suggests a low-cost onboarding path for domain-specific ASR when a customer provides only documentation rather than recordings.

s91303d70a2.title: THRIFTY: Cost-Constrained Reasoning-Data Synthesis for Small Language Models
s91303d70a2.description: arXiv:2611.27436v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for efficient, specialized deployment, and are typically trained on reasoning trajectories distilled from a larger teacher LLM. Generating this synthetic data is a major cost of the pipeline, especially when the teacher is a frontier model. Existing collection methods, however, are largely cost-unaware, or at best spread a fixed sampling budget uniformly across queries. Such allocation ignores the wide variation in problem difficulty and the strategic over- or under-sampling it invites. Thus, we propose THRIFTY, a Thompson-sampling bandit controller that spends a fixed generation-token budget to collect diverse correct reasoning trajectories, casting the task as a bandits-with-knapsac
s91303d70a2.summary: THRIFTY proposes cost-constrained synthesis of reasoning data for small language models, allocating teacher-model sampling budget according to query difficulty.
s91303d70a2.why: Targets the major cost of distilling reasoning trajectories from frontier teachers, relevant to teams training small models on a budget.

s83ab0639ce.title: Learning When to Ask: Advisor-Aware Post-Training for SLM Agents
s83ab0639ce.description: arXiv:2611.27443v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly attractive for cheap, high-throughput agentic deployment, but they remain weak at multi-step reasoning and tool use that long-horizon tasks demand. We study how to post-train an SLM to seek advice from a stronger model and act on that advice itself, following an advisor-executor pattern. Out of the box, this pattern fails across open- and closed-source small-model families: wiring an SLM to an advisor is a harness-design matter that is not enough on its own. A post-training recipe is needed to teach the model when to ask, in a cost-aware fashion, and how to follow advice across steps. Our method, ADAPT (ADvisor-Aware Post-Training), is a multi-stage recipe that instills this behavior, learning e
s83ab0639ce.summary: Researchers post-train small language models to seek advice from a stronger advisor model and act on it, addressing weak multi-step reasoning and tool use in SLM agents.
s83ab0639ce.why: Offers a post-training recipe for advisor-executor agent patterns that could make cheap small-model agents more reliable.

s92251e20bc.title: Mechanism Parity for Simulation-Based Validation of Autonomous-Driving Perception
s92251e20bc.description: arXiv:2611.27447v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulation is central to intelligent-vehicle validation, but visual realism or output agreement between a real scene and its synthetic counterpart does not prove that a perception system used the same evidence in both domains. This paper addresses that mechanism-parity gap for paired real-synthetic autonomous-driving perception. It unifies Decisive-Feature Fidelity, which compares decisive evidence maps in a frozen system under test (SUT), with Concept-Decisive Feature Fidelity, which projects decisive evidence into semantic scene concepts for diagnosis. The framework is a validation diagnostic rather than a standalone safety certificate: it asks whether output-consistent simulation also preserves the mechanism by which the perception model
s92251e20bc.summary: The paper proposes mechanism-parity validation, comparing decisive evidence in perception systems across real and synthetic driving scenes to check they use the same evidence.
s92251e20bc.why: Visual realism alone does not show a perception model relies on the same evidence in simulation, a key validity concern for AV testing pipelines.

s4049585b08.title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act
s4049585b08.description: arXiv:2611.27462v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) imposes detailed obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems but offers limited operational guidance, particularly when these systems integrate third-party General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models. This paper introduces a toolkit that fosters the development of legal-by-design AI-assisted recruitment systems by translating the core legal obligations of the AI Act's conformity assessment---specifically Articles 9--15 and Annex IV---into techno-normative requirements and corresponding guiding questions. While recruitment pipelines may involve components with varying technical complexity and differing levels of algorithmic transparency, this paper focuses on the most challenging case: the integration of
s4049585b08.summary: The paper presents a toolkit translating EU AI Act obligations for high-risk systems (Articles 9–15, Annex IV) into technical requirements and guiding questions for AI recruitment tools using LLMs.
s4049585b08.why: Gives engineering teams building LLM-based hiring tools concrete compliance questions to design against AI Act conformity requirements.

sa3e723e504.title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition
sa3e723e504.description: arXiv:2611.27465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing an editable music score requires musical events, sung text and the instructions that organise them on the page. Existing recognition targets often omit part of this information, while direct MusicXML prediction repeats substantial structural markup. We introduce Cecilia, a compact representation of canonicalised MusicXML that retains musical content, lyric attachments and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts this representation through metadata and measure-bounded music segments from shared visual memory. A learned count head determines the number of output segments. Across paired complete scores under a common tokeniser, the ratio of mean MusicXML to Cecilia sequence lengths is 27.73. Cecilia-OMR outperforms Legato 2 on
sa3e723e504.summary: Cecilia introduces a compact representation of MusicXML retaining musical content, lyrics, and layout, and a model that predicts it for optical music recognition.

s18975e3f59.title: ROSWORLD: When Digital Task Competence Meets Physical Execution
s18975e3f59.description: arXiv:2611.27467v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computer-use agents now solve most desktop tasks through direct software input, but a robot using the same computer must turn GUI knowledge into physical contact with a keyboard and mouse. We introduce ROSWorld, a benchmark that couples a physically simulated robot workstation to a live OSWorld desktop, so that a robot and a desktop agent pursue the same goals under the same official evaluators. The evaluated model receives observations only from the workstation camera views and operates the peripherals through either a single-arm rigid probe or dual-arm dexterous hands. Across five frontier models and 40 tasks in ten applications, models that complete 31-39 tasks on the desktop complete at most 23 with the probe and 28 with the hands. Pair
s18975e3f59.summary: ROSWorld couples a physically simulated robot workstation to a live OSWorld desktop so a robot and a desktop agent pursue the same tasks under official evaluators.
s18975e3f59.why: Benchmarks whether GUI competence transfers to physical keyboard and mouse execution by robots, relevant to embodied computer-use agents.

s5300ba10ae.title: Alignment without Transfer: Tokenization Impacts Cross-lingual Representations during Multilingual Language Model Pretraining
s5300ba10ae.description: arXiv:2611.27491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tokenization represents one of the most crucial steps in mulilingual NLP pipelines. Yet, tokenizers routinely under-allocate vocabulary to low-resource languages. While improved allocation leads to better performance, it remains poorly understood how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations and transfer during pretraining. To address this, we pretrain 39 mono- and bilingual 1B decoder-only models on FineWeb2-HQ across English, German, French, Arabic and Chinese, varying only the tokenizer. Our results demonstrate that improved vocabulary allocation (i) substantially raises cross-lingual representation alignment in early-to-mid layers, an effect that prior work measuring only the output layer could not observe, (ii) increases cross-
s5300ba10ae.summary: Researchers pretrained 39 mono- and bilingual 1B models across five languages, varying only the tokenizer, to study how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations.
s5300ba10ae.why: Shows tokenizer vocabulary allocation affects cross-lingual transfer, a design choice engineers building multilingual models should weigh.

s8eb1efdcaf.title: Learning Unknown Oscillators From Bandit Feedback
s8eb1efdcaf.description: arXiv:2611.27492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study semi-bandits driven by unknown oscillators. Each round, a learner selects two of four reward channels and observes their individual rewards. Frequency errors change future reward rankings and the resulting measurements. We show when committing to one fitted oscillator lets its greedy choices expose prediction errors. Our controller bounds reward loss (regret) over a continuous confidence set and holds the longest block within budget. An online regression policy gathers observations when the check fails. Regret grows at a square-root rate, up to logarithmic factors, across all frequencies and extends to two competing oscillators. On 96 fresh synthetic instances, checked commitment uses 49 fits instead of 1,023, with 1.5% higher mean
s8eb1efdcaf.summary: The paper studies semi-bandit learning with unknown oscillators, where a learner picks two of four reward channels and bounds regret using a confidence-set controller.

sf8b736ad0d.title: Turnout: Adaptive Attention Switching for Efficient Reasoning
sf8b736ad0d.description: arXiv:2611.27500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-hoc transformer linearization replaces the key-value cache of full attention, which grows linearly with generation length, with a fixed size state. This change reduces memory consumption but often hurts accuracy. In reasoning tasks, which require long generations, this effect is especially pronounced. In this work we introduce Turnout, a method that mitigates accuracy loss as a result of linearization, while maintaining its memory-reduction benefits. We apply post-hoc linearization to a pretrained full-attention model, training a linear path through distillation while leaving the original full-attention path unchanged. During response generation, the resulting hybrid model retains both paths and uses a learned policy to control when ea
sf8b736ad0d.summary: Turnout is a method that applies post-hoc linearization to pretrained full-attention models, aiming to recover the accuracy lost on long reasoning tasks while keeping memory savings.
sf8b736ad0d.why: Targets the accuracy cost of replacing growing KV caches with fixed-size states, relevant to teams serving long-generation reasoning workloads.

s5eed1aed48.title: The Assistant Persona Differs Across Languages in Activation Space
s5eed1aed48.description: arXiv:2611.27504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models behave differently across languages, and are noticeably less safe in lower-resource languages. This gap is well established behaviorally, but not mechanistically. Directions in activation space, including the assistant persona direction, are almost always extracted from English and assumed to generalize across languages. We extract the assistant persona direction in 31 languages in Qwen3-32B, and find that the resulting axes differ substantially: their cosine similarity to the English axis ranges from 0.378 to 0.911. Moreover, each language's assistant persona direction and its magnitude are correlated with the language's resource level. We also find that the model's default assistant state is farther from the helpful
s5eed1aed48.summary: Researchers extracted the assistant persona direction in 31 languages for Qwen3-32B and found it differs substantially from the English axis, with cosine similarity from 0.378 to 0.911.
s5eed1aed48.why: Suggests safety steering vectors extracted from English may not transfer to other languages, a concern for multilingual deployments.

se0fd9495a9.title: Self-Supervised Continuous-Time Depth Learning and Ego-Motion Estimation from Asynchronous Events
se0fd9495a9.description: arXiv:2611.27509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Event cameras register brightness changes pixel by pixel with microsecond precision, whereas the dense depth that could supervise them is costly to acquire and exists only at isolated instants. Condensing the stream into frames eases learning, but at the expense of the very timing that sets event sensing apart. We propose a self-supervised approach in which each event is assigned its own depth in continuous time, and the camera motion is recovered from the same observations. Supervision arises from geometry: lifted into 3D by its predicted depth and displaced by the camera motion at the instant it fired, an event should coincide with others produced by the same edge, so any misalignment exposes an error in depth or motion. Differentiable re
se0fd9495a9.summary: The paper proposes self-supervised continuous-time depth and ego-motion estimation from asynchronous event camera data, assigning each event its own depth.

s1c913deeed.title: PhiJEPA: Denoising Latent Predictions for Visual Representation Learning
s1c913deeed.description: arXiv:2611.27516v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a predictor trained to infer hidden image regions still help a world model plan when part of an object disappears from view and the visible context is blurred? We introduce PhiJEPA, a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts PhiNet's two-stage prediction to masked Transformers. From sparse, photometrically corrupted context, a Transformer block predicts hidden tokens of an independently corrupted teacher view. A token-wise MLP then maps these predictions to clean teacher tokens. Controlled ablations show that the combined objective improves dense features over the tested one-stage alternatives. Pre-trained on ImageNet-1K with $5.6\times10^{19}$ training FLOPs, PhiJEPA achieves 69.3 mIoU on linear PASCAL VOC segmentation, exce
s1c913deeed.summary: PhiJEPA is a joint-embedding predictive architecture that adapts two-stage prediction to masked Transformers for visual representation learning from corrupted context.

sc28adffe24.title: PaMuk-Bench: A Parallel Multilingual Multitask Benchmark for Vision-Language Tasks
sc28adffe24.description: arXiv:2611.27521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While vision-language models (VLMs) currently obtain notable results for highly-studied languages, e.g. English, they exhibit significant performance drops in certain low-resource languages, especially due to the lack of annotated datasets. To this end, we propose PaMuk-Bench, a novel parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks. Our benchmark includes a set of over 10K curated English prompts that are translated into six languages: Arabic, Danish, French, Hindi, Italian, Romanian. Parallel translations, which are obtained via a semi-automatic process, along with accompanying generated and retrieved images enable the comparative development and evaluation of VLMs across a wide range of tasks: text-to-image generation,
sc28adffe24.summary: PaMuk-Bench is a parallel multilingual multitask benchmark for vision-language tasks, with over 10K English prompts translated into six languages.
sc28adffe24.why: Provides a parallel evaluation set for measuring VLM performance gaps in lower-resource languages.

sf9a782a95a.title: Fix Where It Fails: Root-Cause-Guided Agentic Harness Optimization for Scene Graph Generation
sf9a782a95a.description: arXiv:2611.27529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scene graph generation (SGG) aims to detect objects in an image and predict the relationships between them. The standard PredCls, SGCls, and SGDet settings show how much performance drops without ground-truth boxes and labels, but not where or why a model fails. Knowing this would allow fixing a model where it fails, without retraining. We propose RoHa-SGG (Root-cause-guided Harness optimization for SGG), which extends agentic harness optimization to SGG. It optimizes the harness, the inference code around a frozen SGG model. RoHa-SGG has two main LLM agents. A root-cause analysis (RCA) agent finds the components where the model fails and diagnoses why, and a proposer agent searches for a harness that fixes these causes. We evaluate RoHa-SG
sf9a782a95a.summary: RoHa-SGG optimizes the inference harness around a frozen scene graph generation model using root-cause analysis to fix failures without retraining.
sf9a782a95a.why: Demonstrates harness-level optimization as a way to improve model performance without retraining, applicable to other agentic pipelines.

sc43d7b48ab.title: On the Limits of Observability for Evaluating Coverage in Machine Unlearning
sc43d7b48ab.description: arXiv:2611.27543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine unlearning aims to remove the influence of any requested subset of training data while preserving utility on the remaining data. Empirical evaluations measure predictive accuracy and infer training-set membership (MIAs) from model outputs or intermediate activations. However, by focusing on selected forget sets, these evaluations can overlook Coverage, the range of requests a method can fulfill. To assess this coverage, we first conduct a stress test of observability with 502 retrained models, finding that hidden embeddings reveal known deletions missed in predictions. To characterize capacity limits on coverage, we show that distinguishing all $n$ singleton deletions with linear scores can require a shared representation of rank $\
sc43d7b48ab.summary: The paper examines the limits of observability-based evaluation in machine unlearning, using a stress test with 502 retrained models to assess coverage of forget requests.
sc43d7b48ab.why: Suggests common unlearning evaluations may miss whether a method can fulfill the full range of removal requests.

s4e30510cbd.title: Bringing AI Assistance to the Beznau Nuclear Power Plant: A Hierarchical System of LLM Agents for Reactor Monitoring
s4e30510cbd.description: arXiv:2611.27556v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beznau Unit 1 in Switzerland, in operation since 1969, is the most experienced nuclear reactor still running worldwide. Five decades of incremental modernization have left its monitoring systems, alarm logs, variable catalogs, technical specifications and investigation reports in separate silos that were never designed to be queried together. As a result, investigating a core instrumentation anomaly means slow, manual gathering of knowledge scattered across databases, documents, and experienced colleagues. We present a hierarchical multi-agent assistant built on large language models (LLMs) to support these investigations and reduce the need for tedious manual searches in SAP systems. An orchestrating agent breaks down an engineer's questio
s4e30510cbd.summary: Researchers present a hierarchical multi-agent LLM system to help investigate instrumentation anomalies at Switzerland's Beznau Unit 1 nuclear reactor by unifying siloed data.
s4e30510cbd.why: Illustrates a multi-agent LLM deployment in a safety-critical industrial setting with fragmented legacy data sources.

se16bb75db1.title: Unlocking Heterogeneous Accelerator Flexibility in AI Data Centers: Sizing and Workload Allocation
se16bb75db1.description: arXiv:2611.27576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI data centers are an emerging electricity demand, but limited local grid capacity could delay their connection and expansion. While existing operational strategies consider spatio-temporal workload flexibility, few studies address the strategic sizing and allocation of diverse accelerator archetypes with different capital and energy-efficiency trade-offs. This paper unlocks the flexibility potential of heterogeneous accelerators by jointly sizing and allocating different AI workloads (training, delay-tolerant batch work, and online inference requests) across sites and hours to meet the time-varying grid constraint at minimum cost. Workload-specific throughput and energy coefficients link these decisions to facility power. In a representat
se16bb75db1.summary: The paper proposes jointly sizing and allocating heterogeneous AI accelerators and workloads, such as training, batch, and inference, under limited local grid capacity.
se16bb75db1.why: Frames data center capacity planning around grid constraints and accelerator mix, relevant to infrastructure leads.

s040aa12518.title: PromptTTSD: Controllable Text to Spoken Dialogue Synthesis with Open-Ended Text Descriptions
s040aa12518.description: arXiv:2611.27601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spoken dialogue synthesis aims to generate multi-turn conversational speech from dialogue scripts while maintaining speaker consistency and contextual appropriateness. However, existing models largely lack fine-grained controllability, which is critical for capturing the dynamic, context-dependent style shifts in natural conversations. While prompt-based TTS has enabled such control for single-speaker speech, existing datasets heavily rely on predefined tags, which fundamentally limits their capacity to capture open-ended styles. To address this gap, we propose a scalable pipeline for extracting conversational speech from multi-narrator audiobooks, featuring an improved two-stage alignment algorithm to preserve dialogue continuity, paired w
s040aa12518.summary: PromptTTSD is a controllable text-to-spoken-dialogue synthesis method that uses open-ended text descriptions rather than predefined style tags.

s7e2e1a3564.title: Potential emergence in LLM agents: a statistical physics perspective
s7e2e1a3564.description: arXiv:2611.27618v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There has been significant recent interest in understanding the behaviour of LLM agents from the perspective of human preferences or corpus statistics. In this paper we propose agent states as intermediate variables through which post-training can be measured and predicted. From a statistical physics perspective, we study the emergence of a global potential which governs the transition of state in LLM agent reasoning. We introduce a partition function to model the ideal KL-regularised transition distribution and track potential structure, mean reward and state entropy. We demonstrate our approach in two Qwen3.5-9B tasks: safety-test selection and physics-reasoning auditing. We observe that the potential structure strengthens during post-tra
s7e2e1a3564.summary: The paper uses a statistical physics framework, with agent states and a partition function, to study emergence of a global potential governing LLM agent reasoning transitions.

s43d5eb8e2d.title: Hy-MT3: More Accurate, Robust and Practical Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild
