s31262d5f30.why: It tests whether autonomous ML engineering agents work beyond benchmarks in production-scale recommendation pipelines.

sf41c486401.title: When Figures Disagree with Text: Evaluating Autonomous Visual Evidence Verification in Scientific Papers
sf41c486401.description: arXiv:2611.24353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scientific figures carry evidence for the claims that cite them, so reviewing a paper means checking that a figure agrees with the text, and not only describing what the figure shows. Benchmarks of figure-text verification typically hand the model the figure, the claim, or the knowledge that an inconsistency exists, which leaves untested whether a model can find the figure worth checking in a complete paper, relate a visual element to the claim it conflicts with, and recognize the conflict. We study this autonomous setting on 31 full manuscripts, each carrying a reviewer-documented figure-text inconsistency from PRISMM-Bench that is hidden from the model. Six multimodal models review each PDF under a neutral prompt, and we then add one in
sf41c486401.summary: A study introduces an evaluation of autonomous visual evidence verification, testing whether models can find and check figures against text claims across 31 full scientific manuscripts.
sf41c486401.why: It shows how well models catch figure-text inconsistencies in complete papers, a gap that matters for automated review tools.

sc9cf37a5ed.title: Can an LLM Repair a Language Model in Weight Space Without Gradient Training?
sc9cf37a5ed.description: arXiv:2611.25613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although an external language model can select and test repairs to another model's weights, behavior can also be recovered through fixed numerical edits. We assessed the value of interactive selection in a controlled study of Transformer repair. After inspecting predictions, activation summaries, and weight statistics, the editor selects projection recipes to apply to the target without gradient updates. We analyzed 20 recorded sessions involving five masked and causal language models, comparing the selected edits with fixed projections, scripted and matched-budget black-box search, and low-rank adaptation. Under the core two-layer fault, live selection matches black-box search on SmolLM2 and Qwen2.5. For Pythia, live selection achieves 6
sc9cf37a5ed.summary: A study examines whether an LLM can repair another language model by selecting fixed numerical weight edits without gradient training, across 20 sessions on five models.
sc9cf37a5ed.why: It explores gradient-free model repair, though the abstract gives limited detail on how well the approach works in practice.

s8c220fcdc7.title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
s8c220fcdc7.description: arXiv:2611.26538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent attributes would predict. Without such a baseline, many existing audits flag a subgroup when it exceeds each attribute alone, a condition that attributes acting independently already satisfy. We test this standard criterion on 150 synthetic datasets built with no interaction. With the shuffle null, it flags 66.1 false subgroups per dataset on average, and at least one in every dataset. When we plant interactions of known size into
s8c220fcdc7.summary: LLM GerryMandering proposes separating interaction effects from additive effects when auditing intersectional bias, arguing a common audit criterion is already met by independent attributes.
s8c220fcdc7.why: Engineers auditing bias should note that a standard subgroup flagging rule can trigger from attributes acting independently, so baselines matter.

s84ca102539.title: OpinionGPT: Modelling Explicit Biases in Instruction-Tuned LLMs
s84ca102539.description: arXiv:2309.03876v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Instruction-tuned Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently showcased remarkable ability to generate fitting responses to natural language instructions. However, an open research question concerns the inherent biases of trained models and their responses. For instance, if the data used to tune an LLM is dominantly written by persons with a specific political bias, we might expect generated answers to share this bias. Current research work seeks to de-bias such models, or suppress potentially biased answers. With this demonstration, we take a different view on biases in instruction-tuning: Rather than aiming to suppress them, we aim to make them explicit and transparent. To this end, we present OpinionGPT, a web demo in which users
s84ca102539.summary: OpinionGPT is a demonstration of modelling explicit biases in instruction-tuned LLMs, so that responses reflect particular viewpoints rather than being suppressed.

sc0ad3a715a.title: Automatic Detection of LLM-Generated Code: A Comparative Case Study of Contemporary Models Across Function and Class Granularities
sc0ad3a715a.description: arXiv:2409.01382v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) for code generation risks incorporating vulnerable code into software systems. Existing detectors face two critical limitations: a lack of systematic cross-model validation and opaque "black box" operation. We address this through a comparative study of code generated by four distinct LLMs: GPT-3.5, Claude 3 Haiku, Claude Haiku 4.5, and GPT-OSS. Analyzing 14,485 Python functions and 11,913 classes from the CodeSearchNet dataset, we generated corresponding code with all four LLMs. Using interpretable software metrics, we trained CatBoost classifiers for each configuration. Our analysis reveals that granularity effects dominate model differences by a factor of 8.6, with negligible feature o
sc0ad3a715a.summary: A comparative study analyzes code generated by four LLMs across 14,485 functions and 11,913 classes to assess automatic detection of LLM-generated code.
sc0ad3a715a.why: Detecting AI-generated code matters for security review and provenance, and the study compares detectors across several models.

s3453989ced.title: A context-adaptive policy framework for robust and reactive robotic manipulation via uncertainty-aware imitation learning
s3453989ced.description: arXiv:2410.24035v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating robust and reactive manipulation strategies that can adapt to changing context information is a challenging task in robotics. Over the years, Learning from Demonstration (LfD) has emerged as an intuitive and effective solution for generating reactive policies, particularly by following dynamical-system(DS)-based approaches. However, most state-of-the-art DS-based approaches focus on addressing the robustness limitations, overlooking the modulation of policies in response to the environment. As a result, they tend to be inflexible with respect to parameterization by task-dependent variables. In this work, we build on existing work on policy fusion and uncertainty quantification to propose a context-adaptive policy framewor
s3453989ced.summary: A paper proposes a context-adaptive, uncertainty-aware imitation learning framework for robotic manipulation that modulates dynamical-system policies in response to environment context.

s521855672a.title: Causality can systematically address the monsters under the bench(marks)
s521855672a.description: arXiv:2502.05085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Effective and reliable evaluation is essential for advancing empirical machine learning. However, the increasing accessibility of generalist models and the progress towards ever more complex, high-level tasks make systematic evaluation more challenging. Benchmarks are plagued by various biases, artifacts, or leakage, while models may behave unreliably due to poorly explored failure modes. Haphazard treatments and inconsistent formulations of such "monsters" leads to a duplication of efforts, a lack of trust in results, and unsupported inferences. In this position paper, we argue causality offers an ideal framework to systematically address these challenges. By making causal assumptions in an approach explicit, we can faithfully mode
s521855672a.summary: A position paper argues causal methods can systematically address biases, artifacts, and leakage that undermine machine learning benchmarks and evaluation.
s521855672a.why: Benchmark leakage and artifacts can produce misleading results, so causal framing may improve how teams evaluate models.

s1583de5061.title: LoopNav: Benchmarking Spatial Consistency in World Models
s1583de5061.description: arXiv:2505.22976v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ability to simulate the world in a spatially consistent manner is a crucial requirement for effective world models. Such a model enables high-quality visual generation, and also ensures the reliability of world models for downstream tasks such as simulation and planning. It must not only retain long-horizon observational information, but also enables the construction of explicit or implicit internal spatial representations. However, existing datasets do not explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints, limiting both the ability to systematically evaluate this capability and to learn it through data-driven approaches. Furthermore, most existing benchmarks primarily emphasize visual coherence or generation quality, neglectin
s1583de5061.summary: LoopNav is a benchmark that tests spatial consistency in world models, using datasets that explicitly enforce spatial consistency constraints.
s1583de5061.why: Spatial consistency is a requirement for world models used in simulation and planning, and existing datasets do not enforce it explicitly.

sba09e6ff18.title: Fine-Tuning Next-Scale Visual Autoregressive Models with Group Relative Policy Optimization
sba09e6ff18.description: arXiv:2505.23331v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-tuning pre-trained generative models with Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as an effective approach for aligning outputs more closely with nuanced human preferences. In this paper, we investigate the application of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to fine-tune next-scale visual autoregressive (VAR) models. Our empirical results demonstrate that this approach enables alignment to intricate reward signals derived from aesthetic predictors and CLIP embeddings, significantly enhancing image quality and enabling precise control over the generation style. Interestingly, by leveraging CLIP, our method can help VAR models generalize beyond their initial ImageNet distribution: through RL-driven exploration, these models
sba09e6ff18.summary: Researchers apply Group Relative Policy Optimization to fine-tune next-scale visual autoregressive image models using aesthetic and CLIP-based reward signals.
sba09e6ff18.why: It shows an RL fine-tuning recipe for autoregressive image generators that improves image quality under preference-based rewards.

s3d0c961a3c.title: Beyond Output Faithfulness: Diagnosing and Mitigating Pathway Rerouting in Feature Attribution
s3d0c961a3c.description: arXiv:2509.04588v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Insertion and deletion are standard metrics for evaluating feature attributions by progressively adding or removing pixels. While they test whether attributed features control a model output, they do not verify whether they do so through the computation that supports the clean prediction. We study this distinction with Ensemble Quantile Optimization (EQO), a differentiable method that directly optimizes the insertion sequence. On CNNs, Unconstrained EQO attains the highest insertion scores while departing from clean representations and retaining its insertion score after channels supporting the clean prediction are ablated. Together, these results reveal pathway rerouting that output-only metrics cannot detect. On a Vision Transform
s3d0c961a3c.summary: A paper studies pathway rerouting in feature attribution, showing that insertion and deletion metrics can be satisfied by methods that depart from the clean model computation.
s3d0c961a3c.why: Engineers relying on attribution metrics for interpretability should know that high insertion scores may not reflect the computation actually used.

s51c250ece2.title: Reconstruction Alignment Improves Unified Multimodal Models
s51c250ece2.description: arXiv:2509.07295v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discover a simple but effective way for visual understanding to help visual generation in a unified model. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) unify visual understanding and generation within a single architecture. However, conventional training relies on image-text pairs (or sequences) whose captions are typically sparse and miss fine-grained visual details, even when they use hundreds of words to describe a simple image. We introduce Reconstruction Alignment (RecA), a resource-efficient post-training method that leverages visual understanding encoder embeddings as dense "text prompts," providing rich supervision without captions. Concretely, RecA conditions a UMM on its own visual understanding embeddings and optimizes it to recon
s51c250ece2.summary: Reconstruction Alignment (RecA) is a post-training method that uses visual understanding to improve visual generation in unified multimodal models, using dense visual signals instead of sparse captions.
s51c250ece2.why: It offers a resource-efficient post-training technique to improve generation in unified multimodal models.

sedf40d2f7b.title: Rhythm-TTS: High-Fidelity Shortcut Latent Modeling and Probabilistic Rhythm Generation for Zero-Shot Text-to-Speech
sedf40d2f7b.description: arXiv:2510.02848v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) systems are commonly built on either discrete codec tokens or continuous acoustic representations. Discrete-token models benefit from stable sequence modeling and explicit speech factorization, but they ultimately synthesize speech through codebook lookup and codeword composition, which can accumulate errors and impose a quality ceiling on naturalness and speaker similarity. Continuous-representation models can generate fine-grained speech latents directly, but often require heavier in-context modeling and less explicit alignment. This paper presents Rhythm-TTS, a shortcut zero-shot TTS framework that combines the factorizability of discrete codec tokens with the fidelity of continuous latent generatio
sedf40d2f7b.summary: Rhythm-TTS proposes shortcut latent modeling and probabilistic rhythm generation for zero-shot text-to-speech, combining aspects of discrete and continuous speech representations.

s4272e65904.title: Improving Consistency in Retrieval-Augmented Systems with Group Similarity Rewards
s4272e65904.description: arXiv:2510.04392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes domains where users expect outputs to be consistent across semantically equivalent queries. However, existing systems often exhibit significant inconsistencies due to variability in both the retriever and generator, undermining trust and reliability. In this work, we focus on information consistency, i.e., the requirement that generated outputs convey the same core content across semantically equivalent inputs. We introduce a principled evaluation framework that decomposes RAG consistency into retriever-level, generator-level, and end-to-end components, enabling systematic identification of inconsistency sources. To improve consistency, we propose
s4272e65904.summary: Researchers introduce an evaluation framework and group similarity rewards to improve output consistency across semantically equivalent queries in retrieval-augmented generation systems.
s4272e65904.why: Inconsistent answers to equivalent queries undermine trust in RAG deployments in high-stakes domains, so measurable consistency methods matter for production teams.

s661fecc82c.title: RAG Makes Guardrails Brittle? Investigating Robustness of Guardrails under RAG-style Contexts
s661fecc82c.description: arXiv:2510.05310v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the increasing adoption of large language models (LLMs), ensuring the safety of LLM systems has become a pressing concern. External LLM-based guardrail models have emerged as a popular solution to screen unsafe inputs and outputs, but they are themselves fine-tuned or prompt-engineered LLMs vulnerable to data distribution shifts. In this paper, taking Retrieval Augmentation Generation (RAG) as a case study, we investigate how robust LLM-based guardrails are against additional information embedded in the context. Through a systematic evaluation of 3 Llama Guards and 2 GPT-oss models, we find that inserting benign retrieved documents flips the judgments of input and output guardrails in around 11% and 8% of cases respectively, wi
s661fecc82c.summary: A study examines whether LLM-based safety guardrails remain robust when RAG-style retrieved context adds extra information to inputs.
s661fecc82c.why: Guardrails that fail under retrieved context could let unsafe content through in RAG pipelines, a risk for teams relying on them.

s2a1263ce92.title: Learning to Assimilate: Amortized Control for Autoregressive Diffusion
s2a1263ce92.description: arXiv:2510.06637v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autoregressive diffusion models (ARDMs) offer expressive priors for forecasting chaotic dynamics. However, maintaining consistency with sparse observations over long rollouts can require substantial test-time computation. We introduce Control-Augmented Data Assimilation (CADA), which trains a lightweight controller on top of a frozen ARDM to steer predictions toward future observations. Using a KL-regularized stochastic optimal control objective, the controller learns from short autoregressive rollouts to anticipate observations while staying close to the pretrained dynamics. At inference, it injects corrections at each denoising step without per-forecast optimization. Across two chaotic PDE benchmarks, CADA improves long-horizon ac
s2a1263ce92.summary: Researchers propose Control-Augmented Data Assimilation, which trains a lightweight controller on a frozen autoregressive diffusion model to steer forecasts toward sparse observations.

s4ca8ac309a.title: Provable Selective Auto-labeling with Reliability Guarantees
s4ca8ac309a.description: arXiv:2510.14581v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Auto-labeling has emerged as a popular, cost-effective alternative to manual annotation. However, its performance is often highly inconsistent across different tasks, underscoring the importance of selective strategies. Despite this, existing heuristic methods for selective auto-labeling still rely heavily on model confidence scores and offer no reliable guarantee on the trustworthiness of the selected examples. To address this, we propose \textbf{Conformal Labeling}, a novel method that selects a subset of auto-generated labels with a provably controlled false labeling rate (FLR). Our key idea is to formulate selective auto-labeling as a multiple-hypothesis testing problem, where each hypothesis indicates whether to accept the auto
s4ca8ac309a.summary: Researchers propose Conformal Labeling, a method that selects auto-generated labels with reliability guarantees rather than relying on heuristic model confidence scores.
s4ca8ac309a.why: Offers statistically grounded guarantees on auto-labeled data quality, which could help teams cut annotation costs without sacrificing trustworthiness.

se90d693a63.title: Generalizing Test-time Compute-optimal Scaling as an Optimizable Graph
se90d693a63.description: arXiv:2511.00086v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Test-Time Scaling (TTS) improves large language models (LLMs) by allocating additional computation during inference, typically through parallel, sequential, or hybrid scaling. However, prior studies often assume fixed collaboration architectures (e.g., topologies) and single-model usage, overlooking that optimal architectures and model combinations can vary across tasks. Therefore, we study the novel problem of searching for compute-optimal model combinations and architectures in TTS under a fixed budget. We formalize it as a multi-LLM collaboration graph, where nodes encode roles and LLM model assignments, and edges capture information flow. This problem is challenging because (i) the combinatorial search space is prohibitively lar
se90d693a63.summary: Researchers formulate a search for compute-optimal model combinations and architectures for test-time scaling of LLMs under a fixed budget, rather than assuming fixed topologies.
se90d693a63.why: Suggests that choosing model mixes and collaboration structures per task, not a fixed setup, may improve inference efficiency.

s8f87b1ab62.title: Object-Centric World Models for Causality-Aware Reinforcement Learning
s8f87b1ab62.description: arXiv:2511.14262v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: World models have been developed to support sample-efficient deep reinforcement learning agents. However, it remains challenging for world models to accurately replicate environments that are high-dimensional, non-stationary, and composed of multiple objects with rich interactions since most world models learn holistic representations of all environmental components. By contrast, humans perceive the environment by decomposing it into discrete objects, facilitating efficient decision-making. Motivated by this insight, we propose \emph{Slot Transformer Imagination with CAusality-aware reinforcement learning} (STICA), a unified framework in which object-centric Transformers serve as the world model and causality-aware policy and value
s8f87b1ab62.summary: Researchers propose Slot-based object-centric world models to help reinforcement learning agents handle multi-object, high-dimensional, non-stationary environments.

s0bc761fe9c.title: Verify Before You Generate: Sketch-Guided Efficient Motion-Planning for Video Generation
s0bc761fe9c.description: arXiv:2511.17450v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent video generation approaches increasingly rely on planning intermediate control signals like object trajectories to improve temporal coherence and motion fidelity. However, these methods mostly employ single-shot plans that are typically limited to simple motion instructions, leading to suboptimal motion quality, or iterative refinement which requires multiple calls to the video generator and incurs high computational cost. To address this trade-off, we propose SketchVerify, a training-free framework whose key insight is to verify motion plans using lightweight video sketches before invoking the expensive video generator. This lightweight planning space enables efficient comparison of multiple candidate trajectories and bounde
s0bc761fe9c.summary: SketchVerify is a training-free framework that verifies object-trajectory plans before generating video, aiming to improve motion quality with less computation.
s0bc761fe9c.why: Verifying motion plans before calling the video generator could reduce costly iterative refinement passes for video generation pipelines.

s5276137fbf.title: Learning and Comparing Local Traces for Weakly Supervised Image Manipulation Localization
s5276137fbf.description: arXiv:2601.06222v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Image manipulation localization identifies edited regions and provides spatial evidence for assessing image reliability, but fully supervised methods require costly pixel-level annotations. Weakly supervised methods reduce this cost using image-level labels, but classification can rely on a few salient cues without ensuring accurate or complete localization. This difficulty is pronounced when manipulation traces are weak and unevenly distributed and authentic and manipulated regions share similar appearance. We propose a CLIP-based framework that integrates Trace-Oriented Vision--Language Adaptation (TOVA) and Relation-Aware Trace Discrimination (RATD). TOVA adapts the visual encoder and uses global visual context to aggregate edge-
s5276137fbf.summary: Researchers propose a CLIP-based framework for weakly supervised image manipulation localization that learns from image-level labels instead of pixel-level annotations.
s5276137fbf.why: Reducing reliance on costly pixel-level annotations could make image forgery localization cheaper to build and deploy.

s5482d41bc2.title: SAME: Stabilized Mixture-of-Experts for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
s5482d41bc2.description: arXiv:2602.01990v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, but real-world deployment requires them to continually expand their capabilities, making Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) essential. Recent methods leverage sparse expert routing to promote task specialization, but we find that the expert routing process suffers from drift as the data distribution evolves. For example, a grounding query that previously activated localization experts may instead be routed to irrelevant experts after learning OCR tasks. Meanwhile, the grounding-related experts can be overwritten by new tasks and lose their original functionality. Such failure reflects two problems: router drift, where expert s
s5482d41bc2.summary: Researchers present SAME, a stabilized mixture-of-experts method that addresses expert routing drift in multimodal continual instruction tuning of MLLMs.
s5482d41bc2.why: Routing drift during continual tuning can erode earlier capabilities, a practical concern for teams updating multimodal models over time.

sfc4ae9976e.title: TabularMath: Evaluating Computational Extrapolation in Tabular Learning via Program-Verified Synthesis
sfc4ae9976e.description: arXiv:2602.02523v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Standard tabular benchmarks reward interpolation: predicting values inside the data manifold, where local statistical smoothing works. However, much high-value tabular data, from pricing and financial rules to physical simulation, is produced by deterministic computations rather than noisy relationships. Can tabular models move from statistical interpolation to computational extrapolation, returning exact answers even beyond the range seen in training? We introduce TabularMath, a benchmark of 114 deterministic computations (233,472 rows) compiled from GSM8K and AIME problems into verified programs. We evaluate nine tabular methods, closed-form and symbolic regression baselines, and in-context learning with GPT-OSS-120B. On regressio
sfc4ae9976e.summary: TabularMath is a benchmark of 114 deterministic computations testing whether tabular models can extrapolate exact answers beyond their training range.
sfc4ae9976e.why: Shows that standard tabular models interpolate rather than compute, a caveat for using them on rule-based pricing or simulation data.

s5d6f02ab80.title: EMA Policy Gradient: Taming Reinforcement Learning for LLMs with EMA Anchor and Top-k KL
s5d6f02ab80.description: arXiv:2602.04417v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has enabled Large Language Models (LLMs) to acquire increasingly complex reasoning and agentic behaviors. In this work, we propose two simple techniques to improve policy gradient algorithms for LLMs. First, we replace the fixed anchor policy during RL with an Exponential Moving Average (EMA), similar to a target network in deep Q-learning. Second, we introduce Top-$k$ KL estimator, which allows for flexible interpolation between exact KL and sampled KL. We derive the stability conditions for using EMA anchor; moreover, we show that our Top-$k$ KL estimator yields both unbiased KL values and unbiased gradients at any $k$, while bringing the benefits of exact KL. When combined with GRPO, the two techniques
s5d6f02ab80.summary: Researchers propose replacing the fixed anchor policy in LLM reinforcement learning with an exponential moving average and introduce a Top-k KL estimator to improve stability.
s5d6f02ab80.why: Offers practical stabilization tweaks for policy gradient training of LLMs on reasoning and agentic tasks.

s8de9bec328.title: The Landscape of Generative AI in Information Systems: A Synthesis of Secondary Reviews and Research Agendas
s8de9bec328.description: arXiv:2603.11842v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The post-ChatGPT surge has rapidly reframed IS research and practice. As organizations and society grapple with GenAI adoption, a body of secondary studies and research agendas has emerged to synthesize early evidence and chart directions for future inquiry. This study reviews secondary and roadmap papers to synthesize the state of knowledge on GenAI's benefits and challenges in IS, and to identify future research directions. We performed a systematic search across Scopus, WoS, and eAIS for publications from 2023 onwards. Following a rigorous, multi-stage screening process, we selected a final set of 28 papers for analysis using bibliometric mapping and thematic analysis. We also conducted a quality assessment of all sources to gaug
s8de9bec328.summary: A review synthesizes secondary studies and research agendas on generative AI in information systems, covering benefits, challenges and future research directions from 2023 onward.

s7b1b2c4a0a.title: Delightful Policy Gradient under Distributed Friction
s7b1b2c4a0a.description: arXiv:2603.20521v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Distributed reinforcement learning trains on data from stale, buggy, or mismatched actors, whose actions often have high surprisal (negative log-probability) under the learner's policy. Supervised fine-tuning learns stably from such logged data, while policy gradient often does not. We trace the difference to negative learning from surprising data: rare failures can dominate finite-batch updates, while rare successes carry information the current policy would otherwise miss. The Delightful Policy Gradient (DG) separates the two by gating each term with delight, the product of advantage and surprisal, and needs no behavior probabilities. In a contaminated bandit, DG suppresses the perpendicular noise of rare failures by a factor that
s7b1b2c4a0a.summary: Researchers propose the Delightful Policy Gradient to handle learning from stale or mismatched distributed actors by gating surprising samples.
s7b1b2c4a0a.why: Addresses instability in distributed RL training on logged or off-policy data, relevant to teams running large-scale RL pipelines.

s14769caf59.title: Does This Gradient Spark Joy?
s14769caf59.description: arXiv:2603.20526v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Policy gradient computes a backward pass for every sample, although the backward pass is expensive and most samples carry little learning value. The Delightful Policy Gradient (DG) scores learning value in the forward pass with \emph{delight}, the product of advantage and surprisal (negative log-probability). We introduce the \emph{Kondo gate}, which compares delight against a compute price and pays for a backward pass only when the sample is worth it; sweeping the price traces a quality--cost trade-off. On MNIST, keeping 3\% of gradient terms learns faster than standard policy gradient even when backward passes are free, and nearly matches full DG. In bandits, zero-price gating preserves the expected gradient direction and removes
s14769caf59.summary: Researchers introduce the Kondo gate, which decides per sample whether a costly backward pass is worth computing in policy gradient training, trading quality against cost.
s14769caf59.why: Could cut backward-pass compute in RL training by skipping low-value samples, with a tunable quality-cost tradeoff.

s0423bb48f3.title: TopoPilot: Reliable Conversational Workflow Automation for Topological Data Analysis and Visualization
s0423bb48f3.description: arXiv:2603.25063v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent agentic systems demonstrate that large language models can generate complex codebases from natural language prompts. Despite this progress, they present reliability concerns for scientific visualization due to invalid operations, subtle errors, and failure to resolve underspecified inputs. In this work, we introduce TopoPilot, a reliable and extensible agentic framework for automating complex scientific visualization workflows. We focus on topological data analysis and visualization as a primary use case, while designing the framework to generalize to broader visualization domains. TopoPilot employs a two-agent architecture: an orchestrator translates user prompts into workflows composed of atomic backend actions, while a ver
s0423bb48f3.summary: TopoPilot is an agentic framework that automates topological data analysis and scientific visualization workflows from conversational prompts, aiming for reliable operations.
s0423bb48f3.why: Shows agentic LLM tooling being designed with guardrails for scientific workflows where invalid operations and subtle errors are costly.

s29700aa9c3.title: The Projector Forgets Too: Joint Merging for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
s29700aa9c3.description: arXiv:2604.14016v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT) is essential for sequential task adaptation of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) but is severely restricted by catastrophic forgetting. While existing literature focuses on the reasoning language backbone, in this work, we find that forgetting can arise from changes in both the cross-modal projector and the language model's LoRA adapters. In component restoration experiments, restoring an earlier task's LoRA adapter while retaining the final-task projector can leave an accuracy gap relative to restoring both components. To address these two sources of forgetting, we present \textbf{JoMe} (\textbf{Jo}int \textbf{Me}rging), which combines \textbf{C}ross-modal \textbf{P}rojection \t
s29700aa9c3.summary: Researchers find catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning stems from both the cross-modal projector and LoRA adapters, not only the language backbone.
s29700aa9c3.why: It suggests merging or restoring only language adapters is insufficient when adapting multimodal models sequentially, so teams need to track projector changes too.

s725da7b3f3.title: A Scale-Adaptive Framework for Joint Spatiotemporal Super-Resolution with Diffusion Models
s725da7b3f3.description: arXiv:2604.21903v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep-learning video super-resolution has progressed rapidly, but climate applications typically super-resolve (increase resolution) either space or time, and joint spatiotemporal models are often designed for a single pair of super-resolution (SR) factors (upscaling spatial and temporal ratio between the low-resolution sequence and the high-resolution sequence), limiting transfer across spatial resolutions and temporal cadences (frame rates). We present a scale-adaptive framework that reuses the same architecture across factors by decomposing spatiotemporal SR into a deterministic prediction of the conditional mean, with attention, and a residual conditional diffusion model, with an optional mass-conservation (same precipitation amo
s725da7b3f3.summary: Researchers propose a diffusion-based joint spatiotemporal super-resolution framework for climate data that reuses one architecture across different spatial and temporal upscaling factors.

s875390a671.title: When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on $\ell_1$-norm Lower Bounds
s875390a671.description: arXiv:2605.06615v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sign-based optimization algorithms, such as SignSGD and Muon, have garnered significant attention for their remarkable performance in training large foundation models. Despite this empirical success, we still lack a theoretical understanding of when and why these sign-based methods outperform vanilla SGD. The core obstacle is that under standard smoothness and finite variance conditions, SGD is known to be minimax optimal for finding stationary points measured by $\ell_2$-norms, thereby fundamentally precluding any complexity gains for sign-based methods in standard settings. To overcome this barrier, we analyze sign-based optimizers leveraging $\ell_1$-norm stationarity, $\ell_\infty$-smoothness, and a separable noise model, which
s875390a671.summary: A theoretical study examines when SignSGD and related sign-based optimizers outperform SGD, using l1-norm lower bounds to explain their advantage.
s875390a671.why: It gives engineers a theoretical basis for choosing sign-based optimizers like Muon over SGD when training large models.

s71588ff850.title: Mosaic: Efficient CPU-GPU Coordinated Block-Sparse Attention
s71588ff850.description: arXiv:2605.07719v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long-context LLM serving increasingly relies on CPU-resident context KV cache, driven by KV offloading and disaggregated prefill--decode execution. Although block-sparse attention reduces KV access, existing designs remain inefficient: GPU-centralized execution fetches selected KV blocks from CPU memory at each decoding step, making it PCIe-bound, while CPU--GPU partitioned execution places CPU-side sparse attention on the critical path, leaving substantial GPU time idle. This paper presents Mosaic, a CPU--GPU coordinated block-sparse attention system for efficient long-context decoding with CPU-resident context KV. Mosaic builds on three key insights: output-contribution-aware KV budgeting, head-specific and granularity-aware spars
s71588ff850.summary: Mosaic proposes a CPU-GPU coordinated block-sparse attention design to speed up long-context LLM serving that uses CPU-resident KV cache.
s71588ff850.why: It targets PCIe bottlenecks and idle GPU time in KV offloading, which affects the cost and latency of long-context inference serving.

s4630be0ac2.title: NoiseRater: Meta-Learned Noise Valuation for Diffusion Model Training
s4630be0ac2.description: arXiv:2605.08144v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Training a diffusion model involves two sources of randomness for each data sample: the timestep and the Gaussian noise realization. The timestep has been studied extensively through scheduling and weighting, whereas the impact of the noise realization at a given timestep is still underexplored. In this work, we examine whether different noise instances are equally informative. We introduce NoiseRater, a network that scores an individual noise instance conditioned on the data sample and timestep. The rater is learned through bilevel optimization, where its scores reweight the diffusion loss in the inner loop, and it is updated to reduce validation loss after the inner-loop updates. Using the trained rater to select training noise, w
s4630be0ac2.summary: NoiseRater is a meta-learned network that scores individual noise realizations for diffusion model training, learned via bilevel optimization.
s4630be0ac2.why: It challenges the assumption that all Gaussian noise samples are equally informative, which could affect diffusion training efficiency.

sc845e47ad3.title: Comment and Control: Hijacking Agentic Workflows via Context-Grounded Evolution
sc845e47ad3.description: arXiv:2605.11229v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Automation platforms such as GitHub Actions and n8n are increasingly adopting so-called agentic workflows, which integrate Large Language Model (LLM) agents for tasks such as code review and data synchronization. While bringing convenience for developers, this integration exposes a new risk: An adversary may control and craft certain inputs, such as GitHub issue comments, to manipulate the LLM agent for unwanted actions, such as credential exfiltration and arbitrary command execution. To our knowledge, no prior academic work has studied such a risk in agentic workflows. In this paper, we design the first detection and exploitation framework, called JAW, to hijack agentic workflows hosted on automation platforms via a novel approach
sc845e47ad3.summary: Researchers study how adversarial GitHub issue comments can hijack LLM agents in agentic workflows on platforms like GitHub Actions and n8n, enabling credential exfiltration.
sc845e47ad3.why: Teams running LLM agents in CI or automation pipelines face prompt-injection risks that can lead to credential theft and arbitrary command execution.

s7d89ac99d2.title: PhyMotion: Structured 3D Motion Reward for Physics-Grounded Human Video Generation
s7d89ac99d2.description: arXiv:2605.14269v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating realistic human motion is a central yet unsolved challenge in video generation. While reinforcement learning (RL)-based post-training has driven recent gains in general video quality, extending it to human motion remains bottlenecked by a reward signal that cannot reliably score motion realism. Existing video rewards primarily rely on 2D perceptual signals, without explicitly modeling the 3D body state, contact, and dynamics underlying articulated human motion, and often assign high scores to videos with floating bodies or physically implausible movements. To address this, we propose PhyMotion, a structured, fine-grained motion reward that grounds recovered 3D human trajectories in a physics simulator and evaluates motion
s7d89ac99d2.summary: PhyMotion proposes a structured 3D motion reward for reinforcement learning post-training to produce physically plausible human videos, addressing floating bodies and physics violations.

s322840ddec.title: StreamPro: Reinforcement Learning with Multi-Grained Rewards for Proactive Streaming Video Understanding
s322840ddec.description: arXiv:2605.16381v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Proactive streaming video understanding requires models to continuously monitor evolving video streams and decide whether, when, and what to respond. However, training models with such proactive capabilities remains challenging. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) suffers from severe imbalance between silence and response signals, while reinforcement learning (RL) faces sparse response-level rewards and difficulties in optimizing interdependent response sequences. To address these challenges, we propose StreamPro, a two-stage training framework. We first introduce CB-Stream Loss to alleviate supervision imbalance during SFT. We then employ Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with two complementary rewards: a refined Response-Matching
s322840ddec.summary: StreamPro is a two-stage reinforcement learning framework with multi-grained rewards for models that proactively decide when and what to respond to streaming video.

s32a789c9a7.title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Ophthalmic VQA via Spatially-Grounded Lesion Evidence
s32a789c9a7.description: arXiv:2605.22414v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Visual Question Answering (VQA) holds great promise for clinical support, particularly in ophthalmology, where retinal fundus photography is essential for diagnosis. However, ophthalmic VQA benchmarks primarily emphasize answer accuracy, neglecting the explicit visual evidence necessary for clinical interpretability. In this work, we introduce FundusGround, a new benchmark for clinically interpretable ophthalmic VQA with spatially-grounded lesion evidence. Specifically, we propose a three-stage pipeline that collects 10,719 fundus images with 15,595 image-level meticulously annotated lesions. To ensure anatomical consistency and clinical validity, all lesions are spatially localized using the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Stu
s32a789c9a7.summary: FundusGround is a new benchmark of 10,719 fundus images for ophthalmic visual question answering that requires spatially grounded lesion evidence.

s9b122fda8f.title: AutoDFT: A Closed-Loop Multi-Agent Framework for Autonomous DFT Calculations
s9b122fda8f.description: arXiv:2605.26179v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) serves as the basis for computational discovery in materials science and chemistry, yet each calculation demands extensive human effort: adjusting algorithms when convergence stalls, revising plans when unexpected physics emerges, and inserting steps as intermediate results reshape the problem. Existing LLM-based agents automate only the initial planning stage, producing a full execution plan upfront and leaving all subsequent adaptation to hand-crafted rules. As a result, these workflows remain fragile, do not generalize well beyond pre-planned scenarios, and often require expert intervention when failures or unexpected intermediate results require changes to the calculation path. Here, we introduce
s9b122fda8f.summary: AutoDFT is a closed-loop multi-agent framework that adapts DFT calculations during execution rather than relying on a fixed upfront plan.
s9b122fda8f.why: It shows LLM agents extending beyond initial planning to runtime adaptation in scientific computing workflows.

s908d199ebd.title: Trust Region Q Adjoint Matching
s908d199ebd.description: arXiv:2605.27079v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Off-policy reinforcement learning of pretrained flow policies remains challenging due to the instability of optimization arising from the multi-step sampling process. Recently, Q-learning with Adjoint Matching (QAM) addressed this by recasting policy improvement as a stochastic optimal control (SOC) problem guided by a learned critic. However, QAM inherits a fundamental fragility of critic-guided improvement, since small critic errors can be exponentially amplified and often lead to performance collapse. This paper introduces Trust Region Q Adjoint Matching (TRQAM), a stable off-policy fine-tuning algorithm that adaptively controls the path-space KL between the fine-tuned and pretrained policies through projected dual descent. Speci
s908d199ebd.summary: Trust Region Q Adjoint Matching is a method that adds trust-region constraints to Q-learning with adjoint matching to stabilize off-policy RL of pretrained flow policies.

sbce560a7e2.title: BioELX: Context-Aware Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking without Task-Specific Supervision
sbce560a7e2.description: arXiv:2605.27380v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cross-lingual biomedical entity linking (BEL) maps mentions in any language to unique identifiers in a biomedical knowledge base, supporting clinical and biomedical NLP applications. We identify two issues affecting current systems. First, the UMLS (Bodenreider,2004) aliases used to train cross-lingual BEL retrievers are heavily skewed toward English, so retrievers generalize poorly to non-English mentions. Second, although context is often necessary for disambiguation, naively injecting context into retrievers trained only to align aliases severely degrades retrieval. We propose BioELX, a retrieve-rerank framework that addresses both issues. For retrieval, we continue training SapBERT_multi (Liu et al., 2021b) using Wikidata-derive
sbce560a7e2.summary: BioELX is a context-aware cross-lingual biomedical entity linking method that works without task-specific supervision, addressing English-skewed UMLS aliases.

sc2b25e6092.title: Redefining Instance Matching: A Unified Framework for Part-Aware Matching in Panoptic Segmentation Evaluation
sc2b25e6092.description: arXiv:2605.31094v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Panoptic Quality metric is the standard for jointly evaluating instance and semantic segmentation. Its original definition matches predicted and ground truth segments only if their intersection over union exceeds 0.5, a threshold that guarantees a One-to-One matching that is both optimal and unique. Below this threshold, the uniqueness guarantee is lost and multiple matching strategies emerge in a poorly explored problem space. We systematically elucidate this space by recasting segment matching as a constrained bipartite assignment problem. sc2b25e6092.summary: Researchers formalize instance matching for panoptic quality below the IoU 0.5 threshold as a constrained bipartite assignment problem, exploring multiple matching strategies.

scb63c66b57.title: Moment-Video: Diagnosing Temporal Fidelity of Video MLLMs on Momentary Visual Events
scb63c66b57.description: arXiv:2606.02522v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Video multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general and long-form video understanding, yet their ability to capture and use brief, answer-critical visual evidence remains underexplored. Momentary actions or state transitions may determine an answer while occupying only a small fraction of the video. Performance on broad video understanding tasks alone does not establish whether models can reliably identify and use this temporally localized evidence. We introduce Moment-Video, a benchmark for evaluating temporal fidelity through momentary visual event understanding. Questions are constructed around visually observable events or event sequences, requiring models to notice, count, describe, or reason abou
scb63c66b57.summary: Moment-Video is a benchmark for testing whether video MLLMs can identify and use brief, answer-critical visual events in videos.
scb63c66b57.why: It exposes a gap in video MLLMs' temporal fidelity that general video benchmarks may not reveal.

se973d8d292.title: EssentialGIN: a new approach for gene essentiality prediction based on graph isomorphism neural networks
se973d8d292.description: arXiv:2606.07700v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Background: Prediction of essential genes (proteins), is a basic and challenging problem but at the same time very costly and time-consuming in wet-lab experiments. Predicting essential genes, only based on computational methods (to introduce wet-lab candidates) using centrality measures are not accurate and result in large number of false positives; therefore, more complex models such as deep learning and also integration of biological information are used in recent research to identify essential genes. se973d8d292.summary: EssentialGIN applies graph isomorphism neural networks to predict essential genes, aiming to reduce false positives from centrality-based methods.

s588f7b0a1e.why: Shows Google expanding personal data use across its ecosystem, relevant to privacy and enterprise data-governance decisions.

s49ef9cf508.title: Claude AI can review pull requests and ship fixes on its own now
s49ef9cf508.description: Anthropic is launching some new Claude AI features to help software engineers ship code. As part of a new Claude Ship product being announced today, Claude now can review, fix, and approve pull requests. Engineers have already been able to take advantage of Claude's code review capabilities thanks to the Code Review feature, which was […]

related.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes

s49ef9cf508.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Ship, letting Claude review, fix, and approve pull requests, extending its earlier Code Review feature.
s49ef9cf508.why: Engineering teams may soon delegate pull request review and fixes to Claude, changing code review workflows and approval controls.

s0cd17937bd.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
s0cd17937bd.description: The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It's a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday. Each year, attendees […]
s0cd17937bd.summary: The UN COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey ended chaotically, with delegates grappling with power-hungry AI data centers straining clean energy goals.
s0cd17937bd.why: Highlights growing energy demand from data centers as a policy constraint on infrastructure planning.

s1d0c151fef.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
s1d0c151fef.description: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux. It helps teams protect running systems while they roll out patches.
s1d0c151fef.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux that helps teams protect running systems during patch rollouts.
s1d0c151fef.why: Gives ops teams an open-source tool to keep live Linux systems protected while patching them.

s388f4aa5f2.title: Supertake raises $20M to let AI agents turn your market predictions into stock portfolios
s388f4aa5f2.description: Think you know where the market is headed? A startup called Supertake lets you put money behind your ideas without having to pick the stocks yourself.
s388f4aa5f2.summary: Supertake raised $20M to let users back market views with money through AI agents that turn predictions into stock portfolios.
s388f4aa5f2.why: Shows agent-driven investing products attracting funding, though the description gives few technical details for engineers.

sf527f13aec.title: SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets
sf527f13aec.description: arXiv:2611.28185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is usually benchmarked by one heart rate per video, a figure that hides the short windows in which a tele-consultation would actually read the pulse. We present SAMA, a training-free estimator that (i) forms a quality-weighted consensus of POS and CHROM chrominance spectra, (ii) discounts frequencies occupied by pulse-free references derived from the same frames (frame motion, skin-mask geometry and background brightness), (iii) follows the heart rate through time with a Viterbi ridge under a random-walk prior, and (iv) returns a track-filtered, amplitude-normalised waveform with a per-window confidence. No parameter is learned and no dataset-specific tuning is used. On 218 recordings from 111 participants i
sf527f13aec.summary: Researchers introduced SAMA, a training-free method for camera-based heart rate estimation, evaluated on five public datasets with short-window tracking.
sf527f13aec.why: Engineers building remote health monitoring can see a benchmark focused on short windows, which matters for tele-consultation use; the text gives few further specifics.

se01f40ad46.title: torchtsetlin: Fast, Interpretable Tsetlin Machines for PyTorch
se01f40ad46.description: arXiv:2611.28195v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Tsetlin machine learns propositional rules with teams of Tsetlin automata that are driven by reward and penalty rather than gradients, so its models are interpretable by construction and cheap to evaluate. Its software, however, consists of C and CUDA kernels behind scikit-learn-style wrappers that sit outside the deep learning ecosystem. torchtsetlin implements the Tsetlin machine family as ordinary PyTorch modules: vanilla and weighted, coalesced, regression, convolutional over sequences, images and volumes, and dense per-pixel segmentation. The automata are a tensor buffer, so a model moves with .to(device), is saved with state_dict() and learns from a mini-batch with one update(x,y) call. Its core technique is a batched formulation of
se01f40ad46.summary: Researchers released torchtsetlin, a PyTorch implementation of Tsetlin machines covering several variants, including convolutional and segmentation models.
se01f40ad46.why: Teams wanting interpretable rule-based models could use these as standard PyTorch modules instead of separate C and CUDA wrappers.

se7b239a8ed.title: From Point Clouds to Engineering Models: Benchmarking Agentic 3D Reconstruction in the Built Environment
se7b239a8ed.description: arXiv:2611.28197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can translate 3D measurements into CAD geometry, but reconstructing engineering models for the built environment demands semantic interpretation and consistent construction constraints beyond surface fitting. We formulate scene-level Scan-to-BIM (Building Information Modeling) as an agentic 3D coding task and introduce S2Bench, comprising public and proprietary scans of 128 real-world scenes across five domains, paired with expert-curated reference models spanning diverse spatial scales. A shared framework lets agents measure scans in Python, build class-labeled components in a live CAD/BIM kernel, and iteratively refine their code. We also propose parallel asynchronous collaboration, where a lead delegates versioned tasks, cont
se7b239a8ed.summary: Researchers introduced S2Bench, a benchmark of 128 real-world scenes for agentic scan-to-BIM 3D reconstruction of built environments.
se7b239a8ed.why: Engineers working on agents that turn scans into CAD or BIM models get a benchmark with expert reference models, though the text gives limited results.

s50bbe0428a.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
s50bbe0428a.description: arXiv:2611.28202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Bench,
s50bbe0428a.summary: Researchers proposed AutoPILOT, a visual agent harness that lets a model issue primitive actions or start ongoing operations, aiming at real-time gameplay.
s50bbe0428a.why: The harness design targets a gap where models fail when games keep running, which is relevant to building real-time agents; the text offers few results.

s0d29f7892d.title: FinEvo: Recursive Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Financial Modeling
s0d29f7892d.description: arXiv:2611.28239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have expanded their role in high-value productivity tasks, including financial analysis and modeling, while enabling models to play an increasingly active role in their own improvement. This motivates two complementary lines of inquiry: can financial modeling capabilities provide a foundation for model self-evolution, and can self-evolution, in turn, advance financial capabilities? We introduce FinEvo, a self-evolution framework that integrates autonomous experience construction with financial capability improvement. FinEvo prepares financial models, iteratively evolves challenges through self-play, and learns from the resulting interactions using executable rewards, relying on the same model throughou
s0d29f7892d.summary: Researchers introduced FinEvo, a self-evolution framework that aims to improve LLMs' long-horizon financial modeling through autonomous experience construction.
s0d29f7892d.why: Teams building financial AI may find the self-improvement loop relevant, but the text does not report outcomes.

s5c13a8ad0e.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
s5c13a8ad0e.description: arXiv:2611.28244v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. However, existing agents rely on harnesses that combine multiple mechanisms, making it difficult to determine how individual components contribute to performance. We systematically study harness design for long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents along two dimensions: context management, which determines what an agent retains from its past attempts, and skill management, which governs how it stores and reuses lessons from those attempts. Across MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna, and gpt-6-sol, we isolate the effects of individual harness design choices by evaluating each a
s5c13a8ad0e.summary: Researchers studied how context and skill management in harnesses affect self-evolving autoresearch agents that design and run experiments.
s5c13a8ad0e.why: Engineers building long-running research agents get a systematic look at which harness components actually drive performance.

s68c9e6e251.title: A Nepali-Accented English Evaluation Dataset for Automatic Speech Recognition
s68c9e6e251.description: arXiv:2611.28263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems perform strongly on native-English benchmarks, yet their accuracy degrades sharply when the input speech comes from under represented non-native accents. Nepali-accented English is particularly under-served: existing resources either focus on native Nepali speech, cover broader multi-accent settings without dedicated Nepali evaluation, or provide only limited Nepali-accent coverage. This paper presents a Nepali-accented English evaluation dataset designed to support robust ASR benchmarking under accent mismatch. The corpus was collected through a web-based platform that did not collect directly identifying metadata and contains recordings from 57 speakers. Each session follows a fixed 22-prompt proto
s68c9e6e251.summary: Researchers released a Nepali-accented English evaluation dataset for benchmarking automatic speech recognition under accent mismatch.
s68c9e6e251.why: Teams deploying ASR for South Asian users can use this dataset to measure accuracy on an under-served accent.

sd83a64ae22.title: Temporal Logic Tensor Networks: Foundations of Temporal Reasoning in Neural Networks
sd83a64ae22.description: arXiv:2611.28277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In dynamic scenes---football matches, traffic streams, surgery, or assembly---actions unfold at fundamentally different time scales: in football, a kick happens in milliseconds, a possession lasts seconds, and complex events such as a successful pass followed by a goal combine multiple atomic actions over extended durations. Models trained solely on visual data struggle to learn effectively across different time scales, lacking a principled way of reasoning across fine-grained instants and broader intervals. Neither point-wise nor purely interval semantics suffices: the former fragments events into frame-level snapshots lacking overall event identification; the latter treats intervals as atomic truth-values, ignoring state trajectories. We in
sd83a64ae22.summary: Researchers presented Temporal Logic Tensor Networks, a neural approach for reasoning over events at different time scales in dynamic scenes.
sd83a64ae22.why: The text is mostly framing; it offers little concrete detail for engineers beyond the motivation.

s266d401c6d.title: Specialized Large Language Models for Markovian Reasoning: Structural Cache Compression, Transition Pretraining, and Dual-Loop Transformers
s266d401c6d.description: arXiv:2611.28285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard autoregressive large language models attend to the growing history of generated tokens, making the key-value (KV) cache a central memory and throughput bottleneck in long-chain reasoning and multi-branch sampling. Yet an important class of reasoning problems is naturally first-order Markovian: the next step depends on a sufficient representation of the current state, rather than on the raw sequence of all earlier steps. We develop a unified design paradigm for Markovian-reasoning specialized large language models. At the cache level, the Markovian state interface transforms history-dependent KV storage into constant-size state transfer with respect to the number of reasoning steps. At the learning level, we reformulate long-chain pre
s266d401c6d.summary: Researchers proposed specialized Markovian-reasoning LLMs using structural KV cache compression, transition pretraining, and dual-loop transformers.
s266d401c6d.why: Reducing KV cache memory and throughput bottlenecks in long-chain reasoning is directly relevant to inference cost, though results are not given here.

s3fc6176696.title: Feedback-Driven Prompt Refinement for Educational AI: Affective Trajectory Estimation and Bloom's Taxonomy Classification
s3fc6176696.description: arXiv:2611.28293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contribution: This study has shown that a shared prompt-refinement procedure, guided by distinct affective and cognitive feedback signals, can improve held-out reference agreement and multi-label classification while reducing affective-generation variability without executor parameter updates. Background: Industry 4.0 has increased demand for personalized technical education across interconnected computing and engineering domains, while prompt sensitivity and generation variability have complicated dependable interpretation of instructional dialogue and learning outcomes. Research Questions: The study has examined whether task-specific feedback can improve affective-reference agreement, generation consistency, and cognitive classification wit
s3fc6176696.summary: Researchers showed that feedback-driven prompt refinement with affective and cognitive signals improves educational AI classification without updating model parameters.
s3fc6176696.why: Teams building educational tools can improve reliability through prompt refinement alone, without fine-tuning the executor model.

sb985c3ea07.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
sb985c3ea07.description: arXiv:2611.28295v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific information extraction (IE) is a fundamental component of AI for Science, transforming experimental knowledge embedded in scientific literature into structured and traceable data for evidence synthesis, scientific database construction, and data-driven discovery. However, critical experimental details are often distributed across text, tables, figures, captions, and surrounding discussion, making them difficult to recover using conventional text-only extraction. Existing LLM-based and multimodal RAG pipelines typically rely on full-document context or coarse page-level retrieval, introducing substantial irrelevant evidence and high textual and visual token costs. We propose GERF, a Graph-based Evidence Retrieval Framework for token
sb985c3ea07.summary: Researchers introduced GERF, a token-efficient multimodal retrieval framework for schema-guided extraction of experimental details from scientific papers.
sb985c3ea07.why: Pipelines extracting data from text, tables, and figures may benefit from its token-efficient retrieval, though the text gives no benchmark figures.

s61971d01de.title: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration
s61971d01de.description: arXiv:2611.28314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Abliteration is a widely used white-box attack against the safety alignment of large language models (LLMs). It elicits harmful behavior by estimating a refusal direction in the model's activation space and projecting that direction out of the residual-stream write-out matrices. We propose INSEP, a defense that fine-tunes the model to reduce the separability of harmful and benign activations along the refusal direction. Abliteration estimates this direction as a difference in class means and projects it out. Reducing separability weakens the signal the attack relies on. An adversarial eigendecomposition selects the most separable prompt subsets. A low-rank adapter reduces their separation along that direction. Behavioral losses preserve the b
s61971d01de.summary: Researchers proposed INSEP, a defense against abliteration attacks that fine-tunes LLMs to reduce separability of harmful and benign activations along the refusal direction.
s61971d01de.why: Teams hardening open-weight LLMs against safety-removal attacks get a candidate defense, though its effectiveness is not detailed here.

s754802fb82.title: Selection Policies for Equal-Byte Mixed-Precision Quantization of Small Language Models
s754802fb82.description: arXiv:2611.28318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can changing which matrices receive 2, 4, or 8 bits improve a small language model without increasing its parameter storage? I compare two parent-selection rules in the same genetic algorithm: a binary-tournament variant and an Alternis-inspired rule. A separate baseline samples repaired random allocations without crossover or mutation. All three use the same MLX affine quantizer, byte ceiling, initialization and candidate allowance within each study. An exploratory study on Qwen3.5-2B evaluates 90 allocations per run. The main study on Qwen3-1.7B evaluates 500 distinct allocations per run over 10 paired seeds. Against uniform four-bit, tournament reduces held-out next-token negative log-likelihood (NLL) by 0.0616 on AG News and 0.0152 on IMD
s754802fb82.summary: Researchers compared parent-selection rules in a genetic algorithm for allocating 2, 4, or 8 bits across matrices in small language models under equal byte budgets.
s754802fb82.why: Engineers compressing small models on fixed storage budgets get a comparison of mixed-precision allocation search strategies.

sa4d6e5a3e1.title: MatHarness: Towards Long-Horizon Open-ended AutoResearch for Computational Materials Science
sa4d6e5a3e1.description: arXiv:2611.28324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Materials science research is a non-linear, long-horizon process. Existing scientific agents, however, largely rely on specific task execution or predefined workflows, rendering them brittle in open-ended settings. To bridge this gap, we present MatHarness, an agent harness designed for open-ended, long-horizon computational materials research spanning the complete lifecycle from initial ideation to manuscript writing. MatHarness couples three mechanisms: execution robustness through pre-flight verification, expert-distilled skills, and just-in-time auditing; epistemic adaptability through persistent research artifacts and an evolving scientific mental model; and collective intelligence through a heterogeneous multi-agent round table under ta
sa4d6e5a3e1.summary: Researchers introduced MatHarness, an agent harness for open-ended, long-horizon computational materials research from ideation to manuscript writing.
sa4d6e5a3e1.why: Teams building research agents for scientific domains can study its pre-flight verification and skill-distillation design, though results are not in the text.

s99dfb34c8f.title: Decision models for UAVBench and the viability of edge deployment
s99dfb34c8f.description: arXiv:2611.28331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models are often proposed for reasoning onboard a drone. However, a good benchmark score does not tell us whether a model will actually run, and run usefully, on an edge computer. In this paper we study three related questions using the UAV decision benchmark, UAVBench. First, are small structured decision models good candidates for these tasks? Second, can an ordinary local machine (a Mac) screen candidate models before we test them on physical devices? Third, what software and resource limits govern deployment? Our main Mac evaluation covers 24 model configurations on the same 2,000 validated multiple-choice questions from UAVBench. These include 20 size-and-precision configurations of 11 generative models, plus four open-wei
s99dfb34c8f.summary: Researchers study whether small structured decision models can run on drone edge computers, using the UAVBench benchmark and a Mac for initial screening.
s99dfb34c8f.why: It addresses whether benchmark scores predict real onboard deployment, relevant to engineers planning edge AI on resource-limited hardware.

sb01ac4be12.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents
sb01ac4be12.description: arXiv:2611.28341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using LLM agents must recover when a tool call fails, by retrying, switching tools, or revising their plan. We study how agents fail when tools fail, using RetryRealistic, a sandboxed yet realistic testbed for controlled fault injection in which agents operate on a real OS filesystem with genuine permission enforcement, SQLite databases, a deterministic local HTTP server, and a constrained shell, across 8 tools, 9 fault types with controlled persistence, and 30 multi-step tasks. Evaluating four agents over 2,100 faulted runs against ground truth, we find that recovery is unreliable (19-68% correct) and frequently silent: 6-26% of runs end in a confident fabrication, a wrong answer asserted as fact. The failure mode is governed more by th
sb01ac4be12.summary: Researchers test how LLM agents fail when tools break, across 2,100 fault-injected runs, finding agents may fabricate results instead of reporting failures.
sb01ac4be12.why: Silent fabrication after tool failures is a reliability risk for anyone deploying tool-using agents, pointing to verification-first oversight.

s1e0c12cd1e.title: SMAD: A Semantics-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Unsupervised Time-Series Anomaly Detection
s1e0c12cd1e.description: arXiv:2611.28348v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Time-series anomaly detection (TSAD) lacks a one-size-fits-all detector for heterogeneous data and anomaly types. Existing automation is limited by implicit objectives, potentially unreliable historical knowledge, or high computational costs. More fundamentally, it selects how to detect anomalies without explicitly defining what to detect. We propose SMAD, an LLM-based multi-agent framework that translates anomaly intent into executable, testable detection pipelines. Rather than selecting detectors against an implicit target, SMAD establishes a natural-language semantic contract grounded in measurable time-series properties, specifying target event patterns, expected score responses, and validation questions. This contract governs both detect
s1e0c12cd1e.summary: SMAD is an LLM-based multi-agent framework that turns anomaly intent into executable time-series anomaly detection pipelines without supervision.

s17e2ca2217.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
s17e2ca2217.description: arXiv:2611.28356v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can now tune neural networks, yet without cross-session memory they spend costly trials rediscovering known lessons. Reuse is difficult because production models differ in architecture, training setup and inference budget. We present Engram, a memory system that links past trial outcomes with the hypotheses and rationale behind them and assesses whether this evidence applies to the current model. An online agent curates evidence at the decision points where it is needed: Initial Guidance supplies validated lessons at the start, Session Retrieval supplies related past sessions before each batch of hypotheses is generated, and Trial Candidate Review checks each trial candidate against matching past trials. Betw
s17e2ca2217.summary: Engram is a memory system that lets LLM agents reuse past neural network tuning trial outcomes across sessions and heterogeneous models.
s17e2ca2217.why: Cross-session memory could cut costly repeated trials when agents tune production models, though the text gives limited detail on results.

see35a818d0.title: Schedule, Rank, Profile: Continuous Evaluation of LLM Agents in Games
see35a818d0.description: arXiv:2611.28368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Games are a robust test for large language model agents: they require sequential decisions, adversarial or cooperative interaction, state tracking, reasoning under uncertainty, and long-horizon planning. However, a one-time game benchmark can go stale as models, prompts, environment implementations, and evaluation policies change, and refreshing it is costly: full round-robin evaluation scales poorly in the number of model pairs, and the resulting outcomes live on incompatible per-game scales. We present a framework for continuous evaluation of LLM agents in game settings, organized around three coupled components. First, an adaptive scheduler that maps pairwise Bradley-Terry uncertainty to reduced per-pair match targets, concentrating budget
see35a818d0.summary: Researchers propose a framework for continuous evaluation of LLM agents in games, scheduling matchups and ranking models to avoid costly full round-robin testing.
see35a818d0.why: Continuous, scalable agent evaluation helps teams keep benchmarks current as models and prompts change.

s1ddbfcfd2a.title: CausalNTP: A World-Model Recipe for Causal Next-Token Prediction under Noisy Training-data
s1ddbfcfd2a.description: arXiv:2611.28369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper shows that transformer networks trained with next-token prediction (NTP) and gradient descent do not learn to make predictions using only causally-relevant tokens in the left context, irrespective of the causal ordering of tokens during training, and identifies the learning deficiencies responsible. We introduce a causal world-model setup, for which, we characterize the Bayes-optimal predictor under the causal view of the data. We then prove that, a function that distills its predictions to non-causal views of data, when realized under Occam's Razor, recovers the true causal predictor.
