s1ddbfcfd2a.summary: The paper shows transformers trained with next-token prediction fail to rely only on causally relevant left-context tokens, and proposes a causal world-model recipe to fix this.
s1ddbfcfd2a.why: It identifies a training deficiency in next-token prediction that could affect reliability of models trained on noisy data.

s2af7e61379.title: The Effect of Security-Focused Prompts on Reported Findings: A Controlled Experiment on 400 AI-Generated Web Applications
s2af7e61379.description: arXiv:2611.28408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic coding tools turn a specification into a running web application, so their defaults for authentication, sessions, input validation, and dependencies become its security posture. This study asks whether appending a fixed block of OWASP-aligned security requirements to the prompt changes what such tools produce, by how much, and with what side effects. Each of 100 frozen specifications was realized four times: two agentic tools (Claude Code, Codex CLI) crossed with two prompts sharing a byte-identical functional core, without (A) and with (B) the security block. A fixed static and dynamic pipeline scanned the 400 applications, yielding 6,721 triaged findings, analyzed with count and logistic mixed models and with a dependency diff. The
s2af7e61379.summary: A controlled experiment on 400 AI-generated web apps compares security outcomes when OWASP-aligned security prompts are appended, across Claude Code and Codex CLI.
s2af7e61379.why: Agentic coding tools' default security posture matters for teams shipping generated apps, and prompt-level security requirements may change it.

s3553a7b73b.title: Diversity over Scale: Recursive Self-Improvement with Ensembles of Small Open-Weight Models
s3553a7b73b.description: arXiv:2611.28420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The advancement of large language models (LLMs) has significantly enhanced the capabilities of agents across various tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) loops, in which a language model repeatedly rewrites a program and builds on its previous version, now perform well in machine-learning tasks, but they rely on frontier models and hundreds of calls per run. Small open-weight models are far cheaper, yet when used alone, their programs often crash and their improvements stall. We propose DiVE (diverse models evolve), an ensemble method for RSI that aims to improve creativity and diversity of generated solutions. DiVE uses three components: a shared memory, a failure log, and best-idea-wins rounds. This allows models to write candidate solut
s3553a7b73b.summary: DiVE is an ensemble method for recursive self-improvement that uses diverse small open-weight models to rewrite programs instead of relying on frontier models.
s3553a7b73b.why: Using cheaper small open-weight model ensembles could make self-improvement loops less expensive and less prone to stalling.

s08b39e4286.title: Human-in-the-Loop Runbook Improvement with Agentic Support Automation
s08b39e4286.description: arXiv:2611.28441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operational support is an important component of production software services. Support requests are often emergent and can come in many forms such as customer escalations or unplanned service interruption. Engineers across organizations have been successful in implementing automation to help streamline support processes but many solutions remain in the hands of human operators. A successful strategy to improve operator response times is to maintain up-to-date runbooks which are documents enumerating triage steps and remediation procedures in the face of identified incidents. This paper is an investigation into an operational system which incorporates Agentic AI into a runbook based incident resolution pattern. The bot uses information in the
s08b39e4286.summary: Researchers present an agentic support automation approach that keeps operational runbooks improved with human-in-the-loop review for production service support.
s08b39e4286.why: Keeping runbooks current with agent help could reduce operator response times for production software teams.

sf7c331f90f.title: ESM-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Whether AI Agents Understand Earth System Model Physics and Code
sf7c331f90f.description: arXiv:2611.28477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents that modify Earth System Model (ESM) code must preserve both software interfaces and the physical assumptions encoded in them. We introduce ESM-Bench, a benchmark of 60 developer-commit tasks from 6 repositories: Noah-MP, CLM5, SUMMA, ParFlow, MOM6, and VIC. The v5 corpus contains 17 physics-based bug fixes, 16 process-representation modifications, 13 parameterization-scheme selections, and 14 parameter-optimization tasks. Each task includes a scientific objective, parent-commit source files, a reference diff, and three stored prompt variants. An artifact audit confirms that all 60 reference diffs apply to their supplied starting files. We define an eight-item patch-review rubric and audit five archived patch fixtures against
sf7c331f90f.summary: ESM-Bench introduces 60 developer-commit tasks from six Earth System Model repositories to test whether AI coding agents preserve physical assumptions in code.
sf7c331f90f.why: Agents editing scientific code must keep both software interfaces and physics intact, and this benchmark tests that directly.

s9fbe9699e8.title: Walks2Maps: Learning Indoor Geometry from Crowdsourced Wi-Fi RTT and Motion Trajectories
s9fbe9699e8.description: arXiv:2611.28532v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Everyday smartphone walks offer a scalable source of indoor geometry, but their motion traces drift and their radio measurements are distorted by multipath. We present Walks2Maps, a physics-guided framework that reconstructs a shared metric map from Wi-Fi round-trip-time (RTT) and motion observations, without a floor plan, surveyed access-point (AP) coordinates, or position labels. Walks2Maps jointly estimates pedestrian trajectories, AP locations, and per-trajectory stride scales, then recovers the pathway layout from the reconstructed paths. Shared AP observations connect walks recorded in different local frames, while metric ranges constrain their relative geometry and scale. s9fbe9699e8.summary: Walks2Maps reconstructs indoor floor-plan geometry from crowdsourced smartphone walks and Wi-Fi round-trip-time measurements, without surveyed access-point coordinates.
s9fbe9699e8.why: Crowdsourced indoor mapping without floor plans or surveyed positions could lower the cost of building indoor location maps.

s2bacbba9bb.title: X-AQA: Unifying Action Quality Assessment with Multimodal Large Language Models and Multi-Domain Learning
s2bacbba9bb.description: arXiv:2611.28548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Action Quality Assessment (AQA) aims to evaluate the quality of human actions, yet existing methods are predominantly developed and evaluated on individual datasets with different task formulations and assessment criteria. We introduce X-AQA, the first unified training and evaluation framework for general-purpose AQA with multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We construct X-AQA-40K, a training corpus comprising 40,163 samples from 22 data sources across four domains: competitive sports, fitness exercises, rehabilitation, and general skills. We convert heterogeneous annotations into a unified question-answering format, incorporating dataset-specific annotation guidelines and official scoring rules when available. Using this corpus, we fine
s2bacbba9bb.summary: X-AQA is a unified training and evaluation framework for action quality assessment using multimodal LLMs, trained on a 40,163-sample corpus across four domains.

sfab265feb4.title: From atomic events to material degradation across metre and year scales
sfab265feb4.description: arXiv:2611.28559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Material degradation emerges from microscopic events whose consequences accumulate over years, yet mechanism-resolved simulations remain confined below engineering timescales. The challenge is not just the sheer number of events: atomistic evolution is dominated by recurrent local motion, with only a tiny fraction driving lasting structural change. This distinction is not encoded in an instantaneous atomic configuration. Locally indistinguishable states can exhibit different event competition, escape times, and long-horizon outcomes, revealing missing kinetic context as a critical information bottleneck. This context spans space and time: the future consequence of a local transition depends on its surrounding defect environment and the kineti
sfab265feb4.summary: Researchers propose a method linking atomic-scale events to material degradation over metre and year scales, beyond what engineering simulations usually reach.

s5c84226f05.title: Beyond Unit Tests: Path-Aware Rubric-Guided LLM Autograding of Notebooks
s5c84226f05.description: arXiv:2611.28565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jupyter notebooks support open-ended, multi-step assessments in which students build one logical flow across interdependent steps, combining code, written analysis, and generated outputs such as plots. These reflect authentic scientific practice but are hard to grade consistently, since students may make different yet equally valid choices at each step, so a later answer can only be judged in light of the choices a student made earlier. We present an LLM-based autograder for such flow-structured notebook questions. It generates a rubric from a reference solution, then applies a softening pass that relaxes criteria tied to the reference so legitimate alternative paths are not penalized. Each question group is graded in a single model call, so
s5c84226f05.summary: An LLM-based autograder generates rubrics that evaluate multi-step Jupyter notebook assessments by considering the path a student took through interdependent steps.
s5c84226f05.why: Path-aware LLM grading offers a way to assess open-ended, flow-structured work that unit tests cannot judge.

sbf95f4cb73.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
sbf95f4cb73.description: arXiv:2611.28574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. The program retains images and computes directly on pixels, and its operations decide how this evidence is used in each task. During memory evolution, the same model traces failures in its visual trajectories to the operations that lost or misused evidence and revises them. It also rewrites the note
sbf95f4cb73.summary: EvoViM is a self-evolving framework where a frozen multimodal model converts its interaction experience into a visual program that retains images and computes on pixels.
sbf95f4cb73.why: Storing visual evidence and computing on pixels for deferred queries could inform how teams design memory for multimodal agents.

sbd5507d18a.title: Agent Money Benchmark: Can AI Agents Be Trusted to Spend Money?
sbd5507d18a.description: arXiv:2611.28610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Giving an AI agent a wallet lets it buy data and services on a client's behalf. Trust then depends on how it spends money and what that spending achieves. We introduce Agent Money Benchmark (AMB) to test whether agents spend a client's money well, starting with purchases of information for financial decisions. We link seller quotes and payments to final answers, evaluating 12 models on 80 payment tasks with simulated sellers and 76 research questions using live data. Purchases settled in USDC on Solana mainnet via x402, a protocol for paying per web request. Three of the 12 models passed 79 of 80 payment tasks without payment or budget errors. Nine fell for a seller's trap at least once; repeat charges and above-list quotes accounted for 79%
sbd5507d18a.summary: Researchers introduced Agent Money Benchmark, testing 12 models on whether AI agents spend a client's money well on information purchases paid in USDC via x402.
sbd5507d18a.why: Agents with wallets buying data raise spending-control and trust questions that engineers deploying payment-enabled agents must measure.

s73e5efabc1.title: Internalized Experience: How Training Data Shapes Memory Formation in LLMs
s73e5efabc1.description: arXiv:2611.28613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric memory enables large language models (LLMs) to retain information from past experience and reuse it in subsequent tasks. Yet how training data supports the internalization of reusable task rules remains unclear. We introduce FSMem (Finite-State Machine Memory), a state-transition framework for constructing training data and studying how data content and organization shape memory formation. We evaluate rule reuse across synthetic worlds, classical planning, and code execution through valid-action identification and execution-outcome prediction, complemented by next-operation prediction in code. Our experiments reveal several systematic learning patterns. Under matched training conditions, even unchanged task rules become harder to i
s73e5efabc1.summary: Researchers introduced FSMem, a state-transition framework for building training data and studying how data shapes LLM parametric memory of reusable task rules.
s73e5efabc1.why: It suggests training data organization affects whether models internalize reusable rules, relevant to teams designing fine-tuning datasets.

s4604f4e2f1.title: VeriLadder: A Multi-Agent Specification Refinement System for Tool-Verified Verilog Datasets
s4604f4e2f1.description: arXiv:2611.28617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training data is a bottleneck in AI, especially for large language models (LLMs) that write Verilog, because register-transfer-level (RTL) code is rarely published and existing datasets mostly check code for syntax, not instruction correctness. This paper presents VeriLadder, a five-level Verilog dataset, and the multi-agent framework that builds it, in which LLM agents write and revise specifications, and EDA tools (a synthesizer and a formal equivalence checker) decide what is accepted. Its levels follow an engineer's checks. Level 1 labels designs from two large Verilog corpora, namely RTLCoder and PyraNet, with synthesis results, failure causes, critical warnings and post-synthesis metrics. 28% of RTLCoder designs fail synthesis and are k
s4604f4e2f1.summary: VeriLadder is a five-level Verilog dataset built by a multi-agent framework where LLM agents write specifications and EDA tools decide acceptance.
s4604f4e2f1.why: Tool-verified dataset generation addresses the scarcity of correct RTL training data for LLMs writing hardware code.

se7976616db.title: Distilling Visual Agents from Limited Interaction Experience
se7976616db.description: arXiv:2611.28618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How much interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent? We study learning from few tasks and recorded interaction histories. Our framework selects representative trajectories using skill-context coverage and ordered visual-decision similarity. On-policy distillation (OPD) learns through fresh interaction on selected tasks or fresh student responses at fixed histories. Across Navigation, Sokoban, and spatial mapping, even one online training task supports transfer to other tasks. Four fixed trajectories raise a 4B student's success from 49.17% to 82.08% on standard Navigation and from 60.16% to 85.55% on Sokoban, recovering over 90% of the measured gap to a 27B teacher on these panels. On an independent Navigation panel, r
se7976616db.summary: Researchers study how little interaction experience is needed to distill a capable visual agent, using selected trajectories and on-policy distillation across Navigation and Sokoban.
se7976616db.why: Findings suggest a small number of trajectories can transfer, which may lower data costs for training visual agents.

sa1f296b111.title: Mitigating Backdoors in Masked Diffusion Language Models
sa1f296b111.description: arXiv:2611.28640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models because they can predict multiple tokens in parallel rather than generating tokens sequentially. However, recent studies have shown that MDLMs are vulnerable to backdoor attacks: when an input contains an attacker-chosen trigger, a backdoored model generates a targeted output, such as malicious code, while otherwise behaving normally. Despite this threat, backdoor defenses for MDLMs remain largely underexplored. We present UNMASK, the first defense framework for MDLMs that detects trigger-containing inputs, localizes the trigger tokens, and removes the backdoor from the compromised model. UNMASK exploits two fundamental properties of back
sa1f296b111.summary: Researchers present UNMASK, described as the first defense against backdoor attacks on masked diffusion language models, which are vulnerable to trigger-based malicious outputs.
sa1f296b111.why: Teams adopting diffusion language models need defenses against backdoors that cause targeted malicious generation.

s357ef653c4.title: Unlearning Model Identity: Ablating LoRA Weights from Question-Based Identity Tuning
s357ef653c4.description: arXiv:2611.28650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models are trained on diverse corpora containing outputs from proprietary teacher models and provider-curated sources. Models subsequently inherit embedded self-identity traits, persistently asserting specific proprietary names. Service providers of open-weight models frequently require the removal of model identity for downstream applications, such as custom interfaces, without exposing provider affiliations to end-users. Effective identity modification is therefore critical for customized model alignment and deployment. This study proposes a method to localize parameter-level representations of self-identity within low-rank adaptation modules to perform targeted weight ablation. By generating probing questions designed to eli
s357ef653c4.summary: Researchers study removing proprietary model identity from open-weight LLMs by ablating LoRA weights tied to question-based identity tuning.
s357ef653c4.why: Providers customizing open-weight models for downstream products need reliable ways to remove inherited vendor identity traits.

s6169742fcf.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus
s6169742fcf.description: arXiv:2611.28660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems for collective decision-making, such as multi-agent debate and consensus games, in which agents exchange messages and update their answers over multiple rounds and a resolution mechanism aggregates them into a final outcome. Most multi-agent LLM frameworks assume that every participant shares the system objective. In practice, however, a malicious agent can join as a legitimate member of the group and persuade the other agents toward a hidden adversarial goal. We formalize such attacks as a sequential decision-making problem in which the insider seeks to degrade the utility of the collective outcome. We propose a model-based insider attack that learns to persuade a
s6169742fcf.summary: Researchers study model-based insider attacks where a malicious agent joins a multi-agent LLM debate or consensus and persuades others toward a hidden goal.
s6169742fcf.why: Multi-agent systems that assume all participants share objectives may be vulnerable to covert persuasion, a risk for collective-decision deployments.

s413e2ebca9.title: Improving the Improver: Semantic PID Control for Medical Agent Self-Improvement
s413e2ebca9.description: arXiv:2611.28680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-stakes vertical medical tasks, such as postoperative pathological staging and long-term survival prediction, demand multi-step clinical reasoning over heterogeneous evidence under weak supervision and high outcome uncertainty. While we first orchestrate CliAgent, a domain-tailored clinical agent workflow that systematically grounds predictions in multi-modal patient evidence, manually designed medical agents remain constrained by static, brittle rules. Moreover, existing recursive self-improvement (RSI) methods suffer from feedback ambiguity and severe development-set overfitting when evolving agents in high-noise medical domains. Focusing on improving the improver, we propose Semantic PID-RSI, an evidence-guided control-theoretic framew
s413e2ebca9.summary: Researchers propose semantic PID control to improve recursive self-improvement of medical agents, applied to CliAgent for pathological staging and survival prediction tasks.

s298f996d6b.title: DeCo: Decoupled Traffic State Modeling with Cross-Variable Coordination
s298f996d6b.description: arXiv:2611.28685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate forecasts of traffic flow, occupancy, and speed are essential for congestion management and travel planning. These variables exhibit distinct spatiotemporal patterns, and their coupled dynamics characterize the evolution of traffic conditions, such as the onset and dissipation of congestion. Existing methods often either neglect this coupling or struggle to capture the distinct dynamics of all three variables within a unified model. In this paper, we propose DeCo, a decoupled traffic state modeling framework with cross-variable coordination for forecasting flow, occupancy, and speed. Specifically, DeCo first trains a dedicated forecaster for each variable to specialize in its unique spatiotemporal dynamics. It then estimates a residu
s298f996d6b.summary: DeCo is a decoupled traffic state modeling framework that forecasts traffic flow, occupancy, and speed with cross-variable coordination.

s29a1de3b43.title: Can Your AI Twin Meet People for You? It Can Hold a Conversation. But What Does It Need to Judge Like You?
s29a1de3b43.description: arXiv:2611.28692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Should your AI twin go meet people on your behalf? We built LLM twins of 710 real people from their other conversations in the CANDOR corpus, sent them to meet each other in 5,680 simulated first conversations, and checked every rehearsal against what the real people said after meeting for real (355 held-out, participant-disjoint pairs, against baselines that include each person's rating history). The rehearsals work: a twin's conversation predicts real liking ($\rho$=0.277), carries information that questionnaires and rating history do not have (partial $\rho$=0.16 [0.05, 0.26]), and recovers most of what the same reader gets from the real conversation (0.321). Swap controls show that this signal travels through the conversation, not through
s29a1de3b43.summary: Researchers built LLM twins of 710 CANDOR participants and tested whether simulated first conversations predict real liking, reporting a correlation of 0.277.
s29a1de3b43.why: Simulated persona rehearsals showing predictive signal could inform how agents act on users' behalf, though the reported effect is modest.

s29bc5b7499.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG
s29bc5b7499.description: arXiv:2611.28748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is known to reduce training-data leakage in single-turn interactions, but whether this protection persists over multi-turn conversations is unclear. We introduce CRELT (Conversational RAG Extraction Leakage Trajectory), a reusable framework that tracks, turn by turn, the real contact details from the training data that a RAG system discloses. CRELT separates retrieval, conversation history, and attack strategy through a full-factorial design, uses a retrieval corpus verified to contain none of the target PII, and counts an item as leaked only when it is absent from the model input at the turn it is produced. In our main experiment, this criterion excludes 29-53% of raw matches that were already present in
s29bc5b7499.summary: Researchers introduce CRELT, a framework that tracks turn-by-turn leakage of real contact details from training data in conversational RAG systems.
s29bc5b7499.why: Multi-turn conversations may leak personal data even when single-turn RAG appears protected, a concern for privacy-sensitive deployments.

s1b521bf600.title: DiscernBench: Evaluating Cooperative Discernment of LLM Agents in Institutional Settings
s1b521bf600.description: arXiv:2611.28787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deployment of large language models in operational settings demands evaluation of judgment under institutional constraint. We introduce DiscernBench, a benchmark for evaluating cooperative discernment: the ability of an agent to determine whether to comply with, refuse, or escalate a request in an institutional setting. DiscernBench comprises scenarios derived from real-world incident reports across domains such as aviation, law enforcement, and emergency management. We evaluate eight LLMs across three decision-making configurations and analyze both final decisions and the intermediate judgments produced during multi-agent deliberation. Under disagreement, Final Responders exhibit model- and role-dependent aggregation patterns in which a
s1b521bf600.summary: Researchers introduce DiscernBench, evaluating eight LLMs on whether agents comply with, refuse, or escalate requests in institutional scenarios drawn from real incident reports.
s1b521bf600.why: Agents operating under institutional constraints need judgment about refusal and escalation, which this benchmark tests across eight models.

s741abd01fc.title: When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?
s741abd01fc.description: arXiv:2611.28808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Looped transformers do not acquire new knowledge during a forward pass. Prior work shows that they store as many bits in their weights as non-looped models. It remains unclear how recurrence makes this knowledge available during inference. We study this question using synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning, measuring depth-resolved readable information in bits with native readouts and tuned lenses. Under final-loop supervision, single-hop facts become readable progressively: heavier memorization loads delay retrieval despite comparable final readable information. Untied baselines of equal unrolled depth concentrate retrieval near the end of their stacks, whereas looped models expose facts earlier. This delay is not intrinsic to the
s741abd01fc.summary: Researchers study how depth-resolved factual information becomes readable in looped transformers across synthetic factual recall and multi-hop reasoning tasks.
s741abd01fc.why: Understanding when stored facts surface in looped architectures informs design choices for recurrent-depth models.

sd71709ea22.title: Improving semantic equivalence in research-level math formalization
sd71709ea22.description: arXiv:2611.28819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formalizing mathematics in Lean is never a word-for-word translation of a paper: a Lean formalization changes definitions, strengthens hypotheses, splits arguments, and adds lemmas the paper never mentions. It stands to reason that a model that is good at autoformalization must be a good predictor of how a natural language source must differ from its faithful Lean formalization. With that in mind, we collect 4{,}076 audited examples of such changes from 832 Lean projects that formalize research-level mathematics, and use them to ask a practical question: how well can a model \emph{write} Lean inside a real research-level project that may contain tens of thousands of lines of code, and does training on discrepancies between natural language so
sd71709ea22.summary: Researchers collected 4,076 audited examples of changes between natural-language math and Lean formalizations to study semantic equivalence in autoformalization.
sd71709ea22.why: Training on documented formalization changes could improve tools that translate research mathematics into verified Lean code.

sb88a2ff303.title: Does a Frontier Large Language Model Know What It Can Solve? A 100-Conjecture Calibration Study
sb88a2ff303.description: arXiv:2611.28827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How does confidence correlate with actual performance in large language models, when attacking open research-level math problems? We address this question by studying the performance of ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra on a set of 100 open conjectures in geometric analysis. By construction, the model first selected open problems in geometric analysis that it assessed that it had at least a 50\% chance of proving or disproving, and then assigned a probability of success to each question. 13 questions were then excluded after an audit, and the model was asked to resolve the remaining 87 problems. Its mean stated resolution probability was $0.617$, versus an observed rate of $0.103$ (Brier score $0.351$, ECE $0.513$), thereby demonstrating that the model w
sb88a2ff303.summary: A study reports ChatGPT 5.6 Sol Ultra's confidence calibration on 100 open conjectures in geometric analysis, after 13 questions were excluded following an audit.
sb88a2ff303.why: Calibration results on open research problems show how far model self-assessed success probabilities can be trusted.

sfba9499570.title: EA-Bench: Measuring information and action efficiency under imperfect instructions
sfba9499570.description: arXiv:2611.28846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personal agents help users complete everyday work across digital applications. Many standard benchmarks assume that users provide sufficient information to solve a task. However, agents often encounter incomplete, distracting, or inconsistent information in practice. To systematically study agent inefficiency under such imperfect information, we introduce Efficient Action (EA)-Bench, which evaluates both tool calls and user interactions in work-related tasks. To our knowledge, it is the first benchmark to jointly evaluate tool-call efficiency and user-interaction efficiency under controlled missing, redundant, and conflicting information. We construct 63 base-task instances adapted from existing work-related benchmarks. To guide perturbation
sfba9499570.summary: Researchers introduced EA-Bench, a benchmark measuring how efficiently personal agents make tool calls and user interactions when instructions are incomplete or distracting.
sfba9499570.why: It targets a real gap: agents waste tool calls and user turns on imperfect instructions, which matters for cost and UX in deployed agents.

s0402aa1857.title: Guarding with Judgment: Learning to Intervene for Multimodal Safety
s0402aa1857.description: arXiv:2611.28849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. Choosing how to help requires distinguishing an established hazard from a condition that still needs verification, a distinction that binary safety labels leave unspecified. We formulate this decision through four actions: allow, warn, review, and refuse. To ground these decisions in verifiable evidence, we build a corpus of 20,126 training audits and the JudiBench benchmark, connecting each action to diagnostic judgments, source evidence, and controlled context changes. Our guard, JudiAct, separately states what the source establishes, what condition governs the help, and how the rules apply. It then checks these t
s0402aa1857.summary: Researchers propose a multimodal safety approach letting models allow, warn, review, or refuse, plus a 20,126-audit corpus and the JudiBench benchmark.
s0402aa1857.why: Replacing binary refusals with graded actions could reduce unnecessary blocking while still handling visually unsafe requests.

s406e1449c4.title: FormaFin: Verifiable Financial Analysis with Solver-Guided Reinforcement Learning
s406e1449c4.description: arXiv:2611.28881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Formally verifying financial analyses generated by large language models (LLMs) remains challenging as financial rules are largely expressed in natural language and rarely have corresponding formal specifications. Training language models to formalize these rules is hindered by the scarcity of labeled data and reliable training signals, while confidential financial data favor small models that run locally. We introduce FormaFin, a framework that trains small open language models to translate financial rules into reusable SMT formulas. FormaFin integrates teacher distillation with reinforcement learning using an SMT solver to compute rewards from numerical thresholds stated in financial rules. We evaluate FormaFin on corporate loan monitoring,
s406e1449c4.summary: FormaFin trains small open language models to translate financial rules into SMT formulas, enabling formal verification of LLM-generated financial analyses.
s406e1449c4.why: Small local models that verify financial reasoning could suit confidential data where cloud models are not an option.

s0b5ef5aab8.title: StudioBench: Benchmarking Agentic Multimodal Large Language Models for Productive Audiovisual Creation
s0b5ef5aab8.description: arXiv:2611.28902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video generators can now render convincing short clips, yet complete audiovisual works require coordinating visuals, sound, and editing across multiple stages. Existing benchmarks focus on individual generators or video agents under narrower production settings, leaving end-to-end creation by general multimodal large language models (MLLMs) underexplored. We introduce StudioBench, a benchmark comprising 160 tasks across eight video genres and five task types, spanning diverse audiovisual production requirements. Models produce minutes of finished audiovisual content using 33 atomic generation, editing, and inspection tools, without shell access or workflow templates. We evaluate the delivered films, while analyzing reconstructed workflow grap
s0b5ef5aab8.summary: StudioBench is a 160-task benchmark testing general multimodal LLMs on end-to-end audiovisual creation spanning visuals, sound, and editing.
s0b5ef5aab8.why: It measures whether general models can produce finished multi-stage video works, a capability gap relevant to creative tooling decisions.

sef6a3540e8.title: STRIDE: Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-Guided Skill Disclosure and Evolution for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
sef6a3540e8.description: arXiv:2611.28907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill-augmented reinforcement learning enables LLM agents to reuse task-solving knowledge across episodes, but existing systems typically expose agents to a flat skill pool and update skills only from coarse, episode-level outcomes. This conflates two distinct uses of experience: a stable strategy that should frame the whole episode, and tactical know-how that should be retrieved only when the agent reaches a local execution gap. We propose STRIDE (Strategy-to-Tactics Retrieval-guided skIll Disclosure and Evolution), a framework that brings progressive skill disclosure into agentic reinforcement learning. STRIDE keeps the selected strategy visible as episode context, exposes a compact tactic menu, and loads full tactic content only after an e
sef6a3540e8.summary: STRIDE proposes separating stable strategies from tactical skills in skill-augmented reinforcement learning for LLM agents, retrieving tactics only at execution gaps.
sef6a3540e8.why: Structured skill retrieval may improve how RL-trained agents reuse experience across episodes.

se06f1c4391.title: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning
se06f1c4391.description: arXiv:2611.28919v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual world models enable goal-conditioned planning by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions in latent space. However, planning depends on how well a model ranks candidates, whereas training optimizes how accurately it predicts each one. We identify the Decision-Relevant Residual (DRR), the part of the cost error that can reorder candidates, and show that the more training reduces the DRR, the more it improves selection (Spearman $\rho = 0.82$, vs. $0.61$ for prediction error). Building on this insight, we introduce Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in selection rule that scores candidates by the standardized consensus of several independently trained checkpoints, which averages out their checkpoint-specific residuals. Across t
se06f1c4391.summary: The paper finds that reducing decision-relevant residual error in visual world models improves action selection more than reducing raw prediction error, and proposes a decision-aligned selection method.
se06f1c4391.why: Training objectives that target ranking quality rather than prediction accuracy may yield better planning for robotics and agents.

s4173cd43a0.title: OmniDecisionBench: Evaluating and Benchmarking the Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
s4173cd43a0.description: arXiv:2611.28924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal System One models answer visual tasks with typed decisions and native probabilities, yet no holistic evaluation compares them with general VLMs or maps either class's capability boundaries. We introduce OmniDecisionBench, a holistic benchmark of multimodal System One models. Its main evaluation assigns 45 datasets (192,975 records) to five capability families and twelve primary angles across four typed interfaces, scoring accuracy and candidate-probability calibration. A validation layer adds three single-factor diagnostics varying visual presentation, textual evidence sufficiency, and target dataset. Across three System One models and two general VLMs, three regularities emerge. First, strengths depend on angle and metric: System
s4173cd43a0.summary: OmniDecisionBench is a holistic benchmark comparing multimodal System One decision models with general VLMs across 45 datasets and five capability families.
s4173cd43a0.why: It offers a structured comparison of decision-style multimodal models against general VLMs, useful when choosing models for visual classification tasks.

s1eec3125fd.title: STEdgeFormer: MCU and NPU Deployable Transformer Architecture
s1eec3125fd.description: arXiv:2611.28935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Transformer-based sequence models have achieved strong performance in language and time-series modeling, but self-attention remains computationally and memory intensive for deployment on resource-constrained edge accelerators. We propose STEdgeFormer, a lightweight, hardware-aware sequence architecture designed for efficient execution on embedded neural accelerators. STEdgeFormer combines polynomial mixture layers and DyT normalization with an accelerator-aware causal memory block, replacing pairwise self-attention with compact causal aggregation. On TinyStories, the fully NPU-supported STEdgeFormer (MW) achieves a perplexity of 7.39 with 4.12M parameters and 6.51 MB RAM, with an end-to-end latency of 40 ms. In comparison, the standard 4.12M-
s1eec3125fd.summary: STEdgeFormer is a transformer variant replacing self-attention with polynomial mixing and causal memory blocks, designed to run on MCU and NPU edge accelerators.
s1eec3125fd.why: It addresses running sequence models on constrained edge hardware where standard self-attention is too memory-intensive.

sb0beb2876b.title: PruneNAS: Constraint Aware Neural Architecture Search based Pruning
sb0beb2876b.description: arXiv:2611.28964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has achieved state-of-the-art performance across diverse tasks, but its high computational cost remains a major barrier. We introduce PruneNAS, a novel framework that integrates structured pruning into NAS to efficiently explore high-performing architectures while leveraging pretrained models. Unlike conventional NAS methods that train each candidate from scratch, PruneNAS generates a candidate pool by pruning pretrained networks at multiple granularity levels and formulates the selection as a global optimization problem using training-free importance metrics. This approach enables rapid evaluation of candidate architectures under strict resource constraints, dramatically reducing search time from hundreds of
sb0beb2876b.summary: PruneNAS integrates structured pruning into neural architecture search, generating candidates by pruning pretrained networks instead of training each from scratch.
sb0beb2876b.why: Reusing pretrained weights could cut the high compute cost of architecture search for teams deploying models.

sb11abae1ba.title: When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners
sb11abae1ba.description: arXiv:2611.28971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a recurrent reasoner returns a wrong answer, is its computation finished or merely stopped? We test this on a trained Hierarchical Reasoning Model (HRM; 27M parameters, Sudoku-Extreme) by running the recurrence for one more inference budget and comparing with an unperturbed control. Solved answers persist (0.95 of 512 endpoints). Wrong answers mostly do not: 0.42 of near-miss answers (n=170) and 0.18 of all 512 wrong endpoints keep their answer. Perturbations from 0.05x to 20x the terminal-update scale barely change these rates, so the measurement reflects continued recurrence, not noise sensitivity. The solved-above-wrong ordering also holds in five further settings (a second seed, TRM, Maze, GRAM-guided TRM, N-Queens), but a fixed 1/2
sb11abae1ba.summary: A study of a trained Hierarchical Reasoning Model finds wrong answers mostly remain unsettled under extra computation, while solved answers persist.
sb11abae1ba.why: Findings on recurrent reasoner failure dynamics inform how inference budgets and stopping criteria are set, though the scope is a single small model on Sudoku.

s50795a978d.title: Learning from Another Angle: Rotation-Based Test-Time Training for Multimodal Large Language Models
s50795a978d.description: arXiv:2611.28972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance on vision-language tasks but often remain vulnerable to distribution shifts due to their fixed parameters during inference. While Test-Time Training (TTT) offers a pathway for dynamic adaptation, existing approaches suffer from prohibitive computational overhead due to multiple sampling and the risk of error reinforcement from biased self-generated supervision. In light of this view, we propose RoTTT (Rotation-based Test-Time Training), a simple and efficient TTT approach that enables instance-specific refinement at inference time. For each test instance, RoTTT performs a small number of gradient updates by predicting the rotation angle of the input image. The known rotation
s50795a978d.summary: RoTTT proposes rotation-based test-time training for multimodal LLMs to adapt to distribution shifts with less overhead than multi-sample approaches.
s50795a978d.why: Cheaper test-time adaptation could make MLLMs more robust to shifted inputs without heavy inference costs.

s6da6790fbf.title: Do You Even Know What I Want? Improving LLMs Ability to Detect Hidden User Intent
s6da6790fbf.description: arXiv:2611.29028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As with conventional AI agents, a common source of misalignment between Large Language Models (LLMs) and their human users is misspecified goals. Often, this happens when the human has skewed beliefs about the system's model and provides it with information that causes behavior different from what they expected, with potentially unwanted side effects. To ensure goal alignment, one solution would be for the LLM to ask the human questions about their objectives. However, it has been well-documented that LLMs most often provide default responses to user requests rather than try and ask questions to clarify their true intent. In this paper, we address these challenges by adapting a novel formulation for the objective misspecification problem to w
s6da6790fbf.summary: The paper examines why LLMs fail to detect hidden user intent and seeks ways to improve their willingness to ask clarifying questions about objectives.
s6da6790fbf.why: Misspecified goals cause agent misalignment and side effects, so better clarification behavior matters for agent reliability.

sbd09f19e38.title: The Retry Tax: Why Static Same-Task Retries Can Cost More per Completion
sbd09f19e38.description: arXiv:2611.29133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrying an agent after failure can complete more tasks while increasing the cost per completion. We study a static policy that stops at verified success or an attempt cap and otherwise resets the original prompt and workspace without passing feedback to the next request. Under stationary task success probabilities, independent attempts conditional on the task, and a common attempt cost, easier tasks tend to succeed earlier. When task success probabilities differ, the unresolved mix shifts toward harder tasks. Specializing classical survivor selection, we show that cost per completion is at least as high as in one-shot serving and that marginal cost per additional completion is nondecreasing wherever the completion increments are positive. Th
sbd09f19e38.summary: The paper analyzes static same-task retry policies for agents, showing retries can increase cost per completion as unresolved tasks skew toward harder ones.
sbd09f19e38.why: Naive retry logic can quietly raise per-task costs, so teams running agents should model retry economics before adding attempts.

s8de4a61d6d.title: MVAgent: Per-Video Agents under Global Coordination for Multi-Video Understanding
s8de4a61d6d.description: arXiv:2611.29154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-video understanding requires systems to combine evidence from different videos for cross-video reasoning. Answering such questions involves two kinds of decisions. Observation decisions must adapt to each video's content, whereas cross-video judgments require relating evidence from different videos based on the question. Most existing agents make both kinds of decisions in one controller, whose context accumulates observations from every video. We separate them in MVAgent, a training-free Multi-Video Understanding Agent framework with one LocalAgent per video. Each LocalAgent plans observations of its own video and keeps a private observation history. A GlobalAgent coordinates cross-video reasoning by instructing the LocalAgents and com
s8de4a61d6d.summary: MVAgent separates per-video observation decisions from cross-video reasoning using a training-free multi-video understanding agent framework.
s8de4a61d6d.why: Splitting controllers keeps context from growing with every video, a design pattern relevant to long multi-input agent systems.

s2892c57139.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
s2892c57139.description: arXiv:2611.29238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-driven game development holds the potential to transform diverse human inspirations into interactive experiences. However, existing systems and benchmarks primarily focus on explicit development specifications, with limited support for adapting multimodal references and evaluating actual gameplay experiences. We introduce GameAnything, an open-source agentic platform that transforms multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. GameAnything integrates coding agents with an independent playtesting critic, persistent development state, and reusable experience memory to support continuous refinement. We further present GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark spanning diverse reference modalities, ga
s2892c57139.summary: GameAnything is an open-source agentic platform that turns multimodal inspirations into playable game extensions, integrating coding agents with an automated playtester.
s2892c57139.why: It shows coding agents combined with automated playtesting for game development, though the text gives little on evaluation results.

s5a443f6a01.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?
s5a443f6a01.description: arXiv:2611.29255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the growing demand for large language model (LLM) services, optimizing LLM serving systems is becoming increasingly complex, and the bottleneck is no longer predicting how a given configuration will perform. The harder problem is deciding what to investigate: which mechanisms matter for a workload, which configurations are worth testing, and what evidence a decision still needs. In this work, we present NoeVera, an agentic Second Brain that goes beyond just one-shot retrieval by turning papers, code, benchmarks, and experimental results into a persistent, provenance-preserving knowledge base with three planes: source evidence, reusable synthesis, and agent memory. Decision-aware retrieval assembles compact evidence packs, role-specific a
s5a443f6a01.summary: NoeVera is an agentic system that turns papers, code, benchmarks, and experiment results into a knowledge base to guide LLM serving optimization experiments.
s5a443f6a01.why: It targets the harder problem of choosing which LLM serving configurations and mechanisms to test, not just predicting their performance.

s4e0e1ec458.title: Neural Agent Compiler: Learning to Schedule Soft Dependencies
s4e0e1ec458.description: arXiv:2611.29262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents accomplish complex tasks by coordinating multiple reasoning steps and tool operations, which form dependencies among their operations. Existing orchestration methods primarily consider hard dependencies that determine when an operation can legally begin, but overlook soft dependencies, i.e., information that is not required for execution but may improve an already executable operation. We identify soft-dependency scheduling as an important problem in agent execution. To this end, we introduce Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a learned scheduler that predicts the task-quality and resource consequences of three execution modes and selects the highest-utility legal mode at a scheduling boundary. NAC represents the executa
s4e0e1ec458.summary: Researchers introduce Neural Agent Compiler (NAC), a method for scheduling soft dependencies, which are non-required information that can improve already executable LLM agent operations.
s4e0e1ec458.why: Current agent orchestration only handles hard dependencies, so this could improve how engineers schedule multi-step agent tool calls.

sfc0d947707.title: MetaSkill: Reusable Problem-Solving Methods for Adaptive Skill Orchestration in LLM Agents
sfc0d947707.description: arXiv:2611.29274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusable skills provide specialized procedures, but large language model (LLM) agents must still determine how to organize and adapt their use. We introduce MetaSkill, a two-layer framework for reusing problem-solving methods across tasks and domains. The method layer selects from 26 curated methods and binds abstract roles to task objects. The execution layer uses the instantiated method to identify intermediate objectives, coordinate native skills, and guide repair or method reselection. On 89 SkillsBench tasks and 995 ToolHop examples, MetaSkill outperforms the evaluated baselines in all six configurations, with accuracy gains of 3.51-13.48% over the strongest baseline. Ablations support explicit method-guided orchestration beyond direct m
sfc0d947707.summary: MetaSkill is a two-layer framework that lets LLM agents reuse problem-solving methods across tasks, selecting from 26 curated methods and binding roles to task objects.
sfc0d947707.why: It addresses how agents organize and adapt reusable skills, which matters for building more reliable agent workflows.

sc3220e9a5b.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
sc3220e9a5b.description: arXiv:2611.29306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-evolving agents improve by retaining feedback as reusable memories or skills, but every mistaken approval can shape many future behaviors. Two updates can provide exactly the same evidence to a verifier yet produce opposite safety outcomes, so the verifier cannot distinguish them from that evidence alone. We introduce DoppelVet, a verification framework that checks proposed updates before they enter an agent's persistent state. Without access to safety labels, DoppelVet constructs an alternative that matches every signal used by the existing verifier. It replays both updates from the same state and directly compares their behaviors in both presentation orders before deciding whether to retain the candidate. We evaluate DoppelVet on Doppe
sc3220e9a5b.summary: DoppelVet is a verification framework that checks proposed updates to self-evolving agents before they enter persistent memory or skill state.
sc3220e9a5b.why: Two updates can look identical to a verifier yet have opposite safety outcomes, so update checks need more than the evidence alone.

sfd82a9298e.title: EMIP: Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform
sfd82a9298e.description: arXiv:2611.29333v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Experimental platforms that enable multiple participants to engage in spoken dialogue and perform physical actions concurrently in a shared environment are important for studying cooperation between humans and embodied AI agents. In this paper, we propose EMIP (Embodied Multi-Party Interaction Platform), a virtual environment platform built on Minecraft. Through an Internet-based client-server architecture, EMIP connects multiple humans and multiple AI agents to the same virtual environment and supports full-duplex speech communication and simultaneous physical interaction. It provides interfaces based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) for environmental observation, physical action execution, and audio input and output, enabling researchers
sfd82a9298e.summary: EMIP is a Minecraft-based virtual platform connecting multiple humans and AI agents for full-duplex speech and simultaneous physical actions in a shared environment.
sfd82a9298e.why: It offers a testbed for studying human-AI cooperation in embodied settings, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sc6017948eb.title: SAE-Audit: Clinical-Trial Prediction via Inference-Time Optimization of Black-Box LLMs Audited by Sparse Autoencoder Evidence
sc6017948eb.description: arXiv:2611.29368v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical trials are costly and often take years to complete, making early outcome prediction valuable for trial planning. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to forecast clinical-trial outcomes, yet their predictions remain unreliable and their rationales may not faithfully reflect the evidence underlying their answers. On tasks such as predicting whether a registered clinical trial will complete or terminate early, frontier LLMs perform only modestly above chance in our experiments. We introduce SAE-Audit, which optimizes a black-box LLM at inference time with evidence obtained from a deployable open model. A frozen sparse autoencoder (SAE) on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is converted into a vocabulary of clinical concepts. Sparse pr
sc6017948eb.summary: SAE-Audit optimizes black-box LLMs at inference time for clinical-trial outcome prediction, audited using sparse autoencoder evidence, after finding frontier LLMs only modestly above chance.
sc6017948eb.why: It highlights that LLM predictions in high-stakes domains can be unreliable and their rationales may not reflect underlying evidence.

s7db283e3aa.title: Emotion-Aware and Context-Grounded Dialogue Agents for Personalized Video Game Interactions
s7db283e3aa.description: arXiv:2611.29372v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ChatNPC, a game companion that dynamically personalizes its responses in real time based on players' emotional shifts to enhance user immersion. The model integrates sequential data, leveraging the dynamic nature of streams to benefit from player information, spoken lines, and in-game context. We leverage recent progress in LLMs' tool-calling capabilities to extract vital information from memory and recognize potential constraints for accurate reasoning, thereby tackling the complexity of NPC conversation scenarios. The task is divided into a game sentinel-guided agent (SeGent), a memory capability, and a chat planning tool for reasoning instantiation. The approach uses a lightweight game template as an information framework, with
s7db283e3aa.summary: ChatNPC is a game companion that personalizes dialogue in real time based on players' emotional shifts, using LLM tool-calling to retrieve memory and in-game context.
s7db283e3aa.why: It shows how LLM tool-calling and memory can make game NPC dialogue more context-aware, though the text gives few evaluation details.

sf6c61b2d2a.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
sf6c61b2d2a.description: arXiv:2611.29519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent frameworks typically orchestrate language models through prompt-and-response interfaces. We propose a harness design that exposes intermediate model states and layer-level execution controls to the agent runtime. By connecting state collection, policy fitting, and execution, the design enables policies to allocate computation within and across models based on intermediate states. We demonstrate the approach with a prototype that learns stitching bridges and state-conditioned execution policies from paired model states, then applies them during inference to select among continue, exit, and stitch. For dispatcher supervision, we select the least-computation action whose full-vocabulary next-token prediction matches the source model's full
sf6c61b2d2a.summary: Researchers propose a harness design exposing intermediate model layer states and execution controls to agent runtimes, demonstrated with a prototype that learns state-conditioned execution policies.
sf6c61b2d2a.why: It suggests agent runtimes could allocate computation within and across models using internal states, not just prompt-response interfaces.

s0a3bb47246.title: Scalar Tuned Lens Summaries Offer Limited Incremental Value for Mid-Generation Abstention
s0a3bb47246.description: arXiv:2611.29589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mid-generation abstention aims to stop an unpromising response before spending its remaining computation budget. Intermediate transformer states may help predict eventual correctness, but whether scalar summaries of their vocabulary predictions add useful evidence is less clear. We compare Tuned Lens entropy and divergence features with final-state and raw intermediate-state probes under matched, causal evaluation. Across eight instruction-tuned models on MATH-500, raw intermediate states improve ranking, whereas scalar-only probes usually trail the final-state baseline. Scalar hybrids have positive exceptions, but their advantage over position-matched permutation controls is small. Cross-fitted residual comparisons further show that gains ov
s0a3bb47246.summary: A study finds scalar Tuned Lens summaries add limited value for mid-generation abstention, while raw intermediate-state probes improve ranking on MATH-500 across eight models.
s0a3bb47246.why: It suggests engineers aiming to stop unpromising generations early should rely on raw intermediate states rather than scalar summaries.

sa657ed1908.title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity
sa657ed1908.description: arXiv:2611.29592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As medical VLMs are increasingly evaluated for clinical decision-support scenarios, knowing when to trust their predictions is critical. Closed-ended medical VQA has become a common benchmark format because it enables automated scoring. Yet, systematic investigation into whether this format changes the reliability problem remains scarce. We identify a failure mode that we call stable wrongness: models can produce incorrect yes/no answers that remain confident and repeatable even when patient-specific visual evidence is removed or mismatched. This failure violates the premise behind sampling-stability uncertainty methods, including recent hallucination-aware calibration (HAC) variants: disagreement is informative only when errors are unstable.
sa657ed1908.summary: The paper identifies 'stable wrongness' in medical vision-language models, where incorrect yes/no answers stay confident and repeatable even when visual evidence is removed or mismatched.
sa657ed1908.why: Closed-ended benchmarks may hide reliability failures, so clinical deployments need counterfactual testing beyond accuracy scores.

sbd07cb7f0e.title: Similarity-Constrained Reweighting for Complex Query Answering on Knowledge Graphs
sbd07cb7f0e.description: arXiv:2611.29596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning models for Complex Query Answering (CQA) on knowledge graphs estimate the likelihood of answers that are not reachable via direct traversal. Recent work has proposed extending such queries with soft entity constraints, which require the target variable to be similar or dissimilar to specified sets of entities. We study a more general formulation where similarity constraints are specified on an arbitrary variable in a query, and introduce SCORE: a computationally efficient and interpretable method for incorporating similarity constraints on an arbitrary variable of a query. SCORE is based on a lightweight and interpretable score adjustment function that only requires tuning two hyperparameters on a validation set. Our experime
sbd07cb7f0e.summary: SCORE is a method for complex query answering on knowledge graphs that applies similarity constraints to arbitrary query variables, not only target variables.
sbd07cb7f0e.why: It offers a more general and interpretable way to incorporate similarity constraints into knowledge graph reasoning queries.

s8fc05b0f26.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
s8fc05b0f26.description: arXiv:2611.29619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most LLM agent frameworks build a crew that runs a task and exits. Physical environments (e.g., homes, labs, factory floors) need agents that stay up for months, survive their own bugs, and run on whatever hardware is already next to the sensors. We present Wactorz, an open-source runtime in which LLM-generated agents are long-lived, supervised actors: a planner turns a chat request into Python, compiles it into a new actor at runtime, and a supervisor restarts that actor alone, with its state intact, when it crashes. All coordination rides on MQTT, so agents can be spawned on, and live-migrated between, edge nodes such as a Raspberry Pi, and every internal event is a topic external systems can subscribe to. The recorded demo builds a camera-
s8fc05b0f26.summary: Wactorz is an open-source runtime where LLM-generated agents run as long-lived supervised actors that compile from chat requests and restart individually after crashes with state intact.
s8fc05b0f26.why: It targets agents that must run for months on edge hardware near sensors, a need most agent frameworks do not address.

s5c1c5cf12b.title: Fin-RSI: A Unified Library of Financial Skills, Checks, and Self-Improvement for LLM Agents
s5c1c5cf12b.description: arXiv:2611.29716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) become more capable, financial agents need tools they can readily discover and use. Yet financial software is fragmented across libraries with different interfaces and conventions, making it difficult to build reliable agent workflows. We present Fin-RSI, a unified Python library of financial skills, checks, and self-improvement designed for LLM agents. It brings together tools for market analysis, forecasting, portfolio construction, and trading research through shared interfaces across models and agent frameworks. Agents can find suitable tools from natural-language requests, reuse tested implementations, and improve generated programs through checking and feedback. Developers can extend the library with new
s5c1c5cf12b.summary: Fin-RSI is an open Python library of financial skills, checks, and self-improvement tools for LLM agents, with shared interfaces across models and agent frameworks.
s5c1c5cf12b.why: It offers a unified interface for financial tooling that engineers can plug into LLM agent workflows across frameworks.

sc2712471d9.title: Reinforcement Learning from LLM-Generated (Suboptimal) Demonstrations
sc2712471d9.description: arXiv:2611.29732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved substantial progress across many domains, but training an agent \textit{tabula rasa} remains highly sample-inefficient. A common remedy is to initialize the agent using a neural network pretrained on demonstrations. However, collecting demonstrations is expensive, and the demonstrations themselves can be suboptimal. In this work, we use a large language model (LLM) to generate an advice policy that produces demonstration data with effectively no human cost. We use this data to warmstart a DQN agent, and use the advice policy itself to guide exploration during training. Because LLM-generated advice is often suboptimal, we further introduce a value warmstart method that initializes the agent to recognize
sc2712471d9.summary: Researchers use an LLM to generate a suboptimal advice policy that produces demonstration data at effectively no human cost, then use it to warmstart a DQN reinforcement learning agent.
sc2712471d9.why: It suggests LLM-generated demonstrations could reduce the cost and sample inefficiency of training RL agents from scratch.

se1afb59d9f.title: Who Sent It or How It Moved? Sender Shortcuts in Cryptocurrency Anti-Money-Laundering Benchmarks, Audited on Elliptic2 and Elliptic++
se1afb59d9f.description: arXiv:2611.29744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two public benchmarks dominate graph-based anti-money-laundering (AML) research on Bitcoin: the transaction-level Elliptic dataset, extended as Elliptic++, and the subgraph-level Elliptic2. In both, a label is assigned according to the entity that sends the funds. We ask whether models trained on these benchmarks learn how laundering moves or merely who sent the money, and we propose a diagnostic protocol to tell the two apart: a sender lookup baseline, a novelty baseline, a sender-disjoint split with a leakage check, and a decomposition of performance into sender, receiver and intrinsic signal. On Elliptic2 the task largely reduces to classifying the sender. Under the standard random split, a no-learning lookup of sender history reaches a PR
se1afb59d9f.summary: A paper audits Bitcoin anti-money-laundering benchmarks Elliptic, Elliptic++, and Elliptic2, testing whether models learn laundering patterns or merely identify senders.
se1afb59d9f.why: It suggests reported performance on popular AML graph benchmarks may reflect sender shortcuts rather than detection of laundering behavior.

s73bea022a8.title: Dimension Is Free, Horizon Is Not: When Evolution Strategies Rival Policy Gradients for LLM Fine-Tuning
s73bea022a8.description: arXiv:2611.29795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Policy gradient (PG) methods such as GRPO dominate LLM fine-tuning, yet recent work showed that Evolution Strategies (ES) also scale to fine-tuning models with billions of parameters. Which method needs fewer samples, and on which tasks, remains unclear. We view the two methods as estimators of the same gradient that differ in where they explore. Because ES perturbs parameters, its noise grows with the number of parameters, and because PG samples actions, its noise grows with the number of generated tokens. Only noise along the directions that change the reward slows learning. The cost of ES then depends on the effective dimension, the number of independent skills a task requires rather than its parameter count, while the cost of PG depends o
s73bea022a8.summary: Researchers analyze when Evolution Strategies match policy gradient methods like GRPO for fine-tuning LLMs, framing both as estimators of the same gradient differing in exploration.
s73bea022a8.why: Clarifies sample-efficiency tradeoffs between ES and PG for LLM fine-tuning, informing choice of training method at scale.

s980785df16.title: Latent-Predisposition Personas for Heterogeneous and Reliable LLM Survey Simulation
s980785df16.description: arXiv:2611.29805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM personas are used to simulate survey publics, which should reproduce not only answer distributions but also within-person coherence and stability. Drawing on mass belief systems research, we show that persona-conditioned LLMs produce over-constrained publics. Across three model families and three U.S. surveys, opinions on unrelated issues are 1.6-4.6 times as correlated as among humans, and party identification explains 2.5-7.6 times as much answer variance. Common remedies (temperature, diversity instructions, backstories) weaken these correlations by making answers more random. On Qwen, their ten-day test-retest reliability falls to 33-59% of the human level, and when made consistent they lose correlation fit. We propose Latent-Predispo
s980785df16.summary: Researchers find LLM persona-based survey simulations produce overly correlated opinions and inflated party-identification effects compared with humans, and test remedies for these issues.
s980785df16.why: Teams using LLM personas for survey or opinion simulation should know their outputs can be over-constrained and unrealistically coherent.

seb0600db7c.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
seb0600db7c.description: arXiv:2611.29807v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents can write programs that carry out a task without calling a model at every step, so the task runs fast and its logic stays open to inspection. Agents improve these programs by running them, studying their failures, and revising the code, a form of recursive self-improvement (RSI). We ask whether this process also yields runtime checks that can be trusted. In five task domains, with up to seven author models, agents bring their programs to high scores. Yet when the environment changes, the checks they were told to write stay silent on half or more of the resulting failures in four domains. These failures can be detected and repaired: a monitor built from records of normal runs catches most of them in three domains, and the same agents
seb0600db7c.summary: A study finds self-improving AI agents that write runtime checks for their programs produce checks that stay silent when the environment changes, despite high task scores.
seb0600db7c.why: Runtime validation written by self-improving agents may not catch failures, so engineers should not trust agent-generated checks without testing.

s363309f57e.title: Memphis: A Case Study in Seeding an Agent Task from a Model's Real-World Attempt
s363309f57e.description: arXiv:2611.29824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent benchmarks are usually made harder by scaling up the data their tasks are built from, yet models that do well on them still fail at real work. We propose building simulated tasks from a model's own attempt at an open-ended task in the real world, so that the model's failures in the simulation resemble its failures in reality. As a case study, we had GPT-6.1 Sol manage two human workers in Cairo over chat for five shifts, with a budget of 7,000 Egyptian pounds, to build as many USB desk lamps as it could. It built two. From the real-world attempt's transcript, we build Memphis, an evaluation in a model-simulated world. Memphis is hard: GPT-6.1 Sol delivers 1.0 lamp per trial on average and repeats its real-world mistakes, buying too few
s363309f57e.summary: Researchers propose seeding agent benchmark tasks from a model's own real-world attempt, using a case study where GPT-6.1 Sol managed human workers building desk lamps.
s363309f57e.why: Suggests a method for building benchmarks that better reflect real-world failure modes of agents rather than just scaling up data.

s92254a86cf.title: Who Makes the Decision? Auditing an Agentic LLM Pipeline for Illicit Cryptocurrency Transaction Monitoring
s92254a86cf.description: arXiv:2611.29829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic pipelines that combine graph detectors, deterministic rules, retrieval-augmented generation and an LLM judge are being proposed to monitor illicit cryptocurrency flows and to write regulation-citing justifications for analysts. They are evaluated on end-to-end accuracy or on the quality of those justifications, and neither shows which component made a decision. We audit such a pipeline on the Elliptic++ Bitcoin dataset with decision-source attribution, a trace-level protocol with three layers: per-case actual causation, interventional Shapley credit, and mediation of upstream risk scores. A deterministic wallet-score override carries about 94% of the credit for flags, and a verification gate cancels most of the judge's own flags, whic
s92254a86cf.summary: Researchers audit an agentic LLM pipeline for illicit crypto transaction monitoring on the Elliptic++ dataset, using decision-source attribution to show which component drives decisions.
s92254a86cf.why: Shows that end-to-end accuracy alone hides which pipeline component decides, which matters for auditing compliance systems.

s113c94fa16.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
s113c94fa16.description: arXiv:2611.29847v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an interv
s113c94fa16.summary: MobileGrail is a compact on-device guardrail model that checks mobile GUI agent actions before execution, avoiding sending screens to remote cloud servers.
s113c94fa16.why: On-device safety guardrails can protect private data like payments and messages without exposing every screen to a remote server.

sd9022dd853.title: Semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash on H5N1 One Health questions
sd9022dd853.description: arXiv:2611.29859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) has re-emerged as a One Health concern since 2024, and the public is increasingly consulting large-language-model (LLM) chatbots for health information during outbreaks. Before a chatbot's accuracy can be meaningfully assessed, its consistency must first be understood, so that any single response can be trusted as a fair representative of the model's behavior. We characterized the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 (OpenAI) and Gemini 3 Flash (Google) on 15 H5N1 One Health questions sourced from social media discourse by adopting and extending a centroid-based evaluation framework. Each question was submitted 30 times and reformulated using five Chain-of-Thought (CoT) variants with 30
sd9022dd853.summary: A study measures the semantic repeatability and reproducibility of GPT-5 and Gemini 3 Flash answers to 15 H5N1 One Health questions.
sd9022dd853.why: Shows how consistent chatbot answers are on health topics, a prerequisite for judging accuracy in high-stakes use.

s24ab1d573f.title: Deep Discriminative Feature Fusion of Convolutional and Attention-Based Recurrent Representations for Subject-Independent ECG Stress Recognition
s24ab1d573f.description: arXiv:2611.29870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stress has become a significant concern because of its negative impact on both physical and mental health and therefore drives the need for reliable automated systems to assess stress levels. Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals provide a non-invasive and objective measure of physiological stress responses and have emerged as a promising modality for continuous stress monitoring. While deep learning techniques have achieved encouraging results in ECG-based stress detection, many studies focus only on one type of feature representation, and therefore limit their ability to capture both the morphological patterns and temporal dynamics embedded in ECG signals. To address this limitation, in this paper, we propose three deep learning-based feature fus
s24ab1d573f.summary: Researchers propose a deep model fusing convolutional and attention-based recurrent features for subject-independent stress recognition from ECG signals.

sfda1e5bd5f.title: Weight Averaging at Small Budgets Confounds Formula-Labeled Pretraining in Microstructure-Property Regression: A Pre-Specified Study with Post Hoc Rechecks
sfda1e5bd5f.description: arXiv:2611.29876v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Closed-form physics formulas can label synthetic microstructures at no cost, so supervised pretraining on those labels is an alternative to self-supervised pretraining when labels are scarce. One pre-specified protocol tests this on two public simulated benchmarks, two-phase conductivity and short-fiber stiffness: a ConvNeXt-Small is pretrained on 150,000 synthetic images by formula regression or masked reconstruction and fine-tuned on 100, 400, or 1,600 labels. Five fine-tuning seeds from one formula checkpoint have mean residual correlations of 0.994 (conductivity) and 0.999 (stiffness). On conductivity the formula network compresses its predictions (slope 0.64) and has four times the 400-label error of ImageNet initialization. Two confound
sfda1e5bd5f.summary: A pre-specified study finds weight averaging at small label budgets confounds formula-labeled pretraining for microstructure-property regression with ConvNeXt-Small.
sfda1e5bd5f.why: Highlights that small-budget fine-tuning results can be confounded by seed and averaging effects, relevant to evaluating pretraining claims.

sc3482b3ee8.title: Particle Belief Representations for Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
sc3482b3ee8.description: arXiv:2611.29884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Particle filters flexibly represent complex, multimodal beliefs but expose them as weighted, unordered sets incompatible with conventional fixed-dimensional policies. We study particle-belief encodings as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies while holding belief estimation and policy optimization fixed. We compare statistical summaries, cumulant-generating-function (CGF) features, and permutation-invariant set encoders. Trainable encoders are learned end-to-end or pretrained through belief reconstruction or task-specific prediction.
