Across eight tasks, pooling-based set encoders and gradient CGF features are reliable end-to-end, while the Set Transformer achieves the highest performance with appropriate pretraining. Task-specific pretrai
sc3482b3ee8.summary: Researchers compare particle-filter belief encodings, including statistical summaries and permutation-invariant set encoders, as inputs to reinforcement-learning policies under partial observability.
sc3482b3ee8.why: Offers guidance on how to feed multimodal belief representations into fixed-size RL policies.

s1a0afe0bd5.title: Second-Order Dynamics in Noisy RNNs Produce Exploration and Temporal Compression in Replay
s1a0afe0bd5.description: arXiv:2611.29888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Biological neural networks (like the hippocampus) can internally generate "replay" resembling stimulus-driven activity. Recent computational models of replay use noisy recurrent neural networks (RNNs) trained to path-integrate. Replay in these networks is described as Langevin sampling, but this theory alone fails to capture the environmental exploration and temporal compression observed in real biological replay. To close this gap, we re-examine spontaneous noisy RNN activity ("replay") as Langevin sampling, one timestep at a time, from a time-series distribution resembling lived experiences (unlike previous works which defined sampling as Monte Carlo inference over a static distribution). We provide a normative second-order Langevin samplin
s1a0afe0bd5.summary: Researchers model spontaneous replay in noisy recurrent neural networks as Langevin sampling, explaining exploration and temporal compression seen in biological replay.

s839b709f17.title: From Patterns to Threats: A Deep Learning Model for Anomaly Detection in Cyber-Physical Systems
s839b709f17.description: arXiv:2611.29903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyber-physical systems increasingly rely on interconnected sensing, communication, and control components, creating a need for reliable detection of abnormal behavior. This study proposes a Deep Autoencoder for anomaly detection using the Edge-IIoTset dataset. After preprocessing the full dataset, 2,219,201 observations and 38 numerical features were retained. The proposed model employed a 38-24-12-6-12-24-38 encoder-decoder architecture and was trained exclusively on normal observations to learn representative patterns of expected system behavior. Anomaly decisions were based on reconstruction error, with the classification threshold selected independently from validation data by maximizing the F1-score. To assess model stability, five indep
s839b709f17.summary: A deep autoencoder with a 38-24-12-6-12-24-38 architecture is trained on normal data from the Edge-IIoTset dataset to detect anomalies in cyber-physical systems.
s839b709f17.why: Provides an application of autoencoder anomaly detection for industrial IoT security, though the abstract offers limited detail on results.

s1eba0cd0f6.title: Reward Blindness: A Theoretical Framework for Diagnosing Reinforcement Learning Reward Limitations in Text-to-SQL
s1eba0cd0f6.description: arXiv:2611.29930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems let users without programming expertise query relational databases in natural language. Reinforcement learning has become the dominant way to train such systems, yet progress is still judged by a single number, execution accuracy, which counts correct queries but says nothing about which kinds of semantic error survive training. This paper develops a theoretical framework that examines text-to-SQL from the perspective of reward design. We introduce Reward Error Sensitivity, a measure of how strongly a reward function separates queries that contain a given error type from queries that do not, and prove a Reward Blindness theorem: when this sensitivity is zero, policy-gradient training carries no systematic signal for removi
s1eba0cd0f6.summary: A paper proposes a theoretical framework, Reward Error Sensitivity, to show how reward design in RL-trained text-to-SQL systems lets specific semantic errors survive training.
s1eba0cd0f6.why: Suggests execution accuracy alone hides semantic errors, so teams training text-to-SQL should examine reward design more closely.

sdbfc0ea91a.title: SAEPO: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Credit Assignment for Policy Optimization
sdbfc0ea91a.description: arXiv:2611.29936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has demonstrated strong performance in improving large language model (LLM) reasoning, yet its credit-assignment signal remains coarse. Outcome verifiers provide scalable supervision by judging whether a completed response is correct, but they do not directly indicate which intermediate reasoning tokens contribute to success or failure. As a result, policy optimization can be inefficient, especially when training base models directly from sparse outcome feedback. In this paper, we introduce SAEPO, a Sparse AutoEncoder-guided token-level credit assignment method for outcome-supervised Policy Optimization. Rather than treating correctness only as a rollout-level (sequence-level) signal, SAEP
sdbfc0ea91a.summary: SAEPO uses sparse autoencoder features to guide token-level credit assignment in RLVR for improving LLM reasoning from sparse outcome rewards.
sdbfc0ea91a.why: Offers a way to get finer-grained credit signals than outcome-only verifiers during reinforcement learning for reasoning.

s245a50904e.title: When Learned IDS Model Selection Collapses to a Static Choice: A Measurement Study at the Edge
s245a50904e.description: arXiv:2611.29968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Runtime model selection trades detection quality against energy and latency. However, comparing a selector only with a more costly static detector conflates detector choice with the benefit of adaptation. We present a framework for analysis and physical measurement that combines a pairwise reward criterion, matched static controls, paired blocks, a fixed load-prevalence factorial design, and reporting of actions outside training support. On one Raspberry Pi 4B with four frozen TON-IoT detectors, tabular Q-learning and a deep Q-network (DQN) both select LightLR throughout. A retrospective audit using validation data only rules out preference reversals for MedRF versus LightLR and HeavyMLP versus LightLR. However, TinyDT has a higher reward tha
s245a50904e.summary: On a Raspberry Pi 4B, a measurement study finds learned runtime model selectors for an IDS, tabular Q-learning and DQN, can collapse to a static detector choice.
s245a50904e.why: Shows learned adaptive model selection may offer no benefit over a matched static detector, so edge deployments need controlled comparisons.

s46107334bd.title: CARE-3D: Reinforcement Learning for Evidence Grounded Agentic Reasoning in Situated 3D Scenes
s46107334bd.description: arXiv:2611.29969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Situated 3D reasoning requires embodied agents to interpret objects, scene geometry, and viewpoint dependent spatial relations. Existing methods learn grounded interactions from supervised traces, but largely imitate prescribed evidence acquisition patterns rather than optimizing the support that the returned evidence provides for the correct answer. Moreover, outcome rewards provide limited credit for intermediate tool choices and may leave infrequent tools underexplored. An effective agent should instead adaptively decide what to ground, which tool to invoke, and how to assess the utility of returned evidence. To this end, this paper presents CARE-3D, a reinforcement post-training framework for adaptive grounded reasoning. Supervised fine-t
s46107334bd.summary: Researchers propose CARE-3D, a reinforcement learning method that trains agents to ground evidence for reasoning about situated 3D scenes.
s46107334bd.why: It targets rewarding useful intermediate tool choices rather than only final outcomes, which may inform how engineers train tool-using embodied agents.

sff2b7d1ff2.title: Aligning Judge Models to Be Logically Consistent Multi-Rule Interpreters
sff2b7d1ff2.description: arXiv:2611.29975v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Technical governance of AI models will soon require them to reason over and follow thousands of rules from different jurisdictions. However, as we show in this work, presenting an entire ruleset to a judge model---rather than asking it to judge one rule at a time---changes the way the model interprets the requirements, making it reach conclusions that conflict with its rule-by-rule judgments. We call this challenge multi-rule inconsistency and find that models are more lenient when judging rules embedded within the full ruleset than when judging rules separately. For example, we find that when a safety-critical rule prohibiting a model from pursuing objectives other than those it was given appears in a larger ruleset, all tested judge models
sff2b7d1ff2.summary: Researchers show judge models reach different conclusions when given a full ruleset versus judging rules one at a time, and propose alignment to fix this.
sff2b7d1ff2.why: Teams using LLM judges for compliance across many jurisdictional rules may get inconsistent verdicts depending on how rules are presented.

s40f0d9c5bb.title: Differential Proteomics to XAI Rules: A SHAP-FOL-ILP Modeling for Lung Adenocarcinoma
s40f0d9c5bb.description: arXiv:2611.29989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: We developed an interpretable workflow linking paired differential proteomics, sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and first-order logic (FOL) rule learning in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Methods: We analysed 213 CPTAC-LUAD tissue samples (111 tumour, 102 adjacent-normal) from 111 patients, including 102 matched pairs. Protein effect estimation and testing used the same complete pairs, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Sparse logistic regression used five-fold stratified patient-grouped nested cross-validation. Preprocessing and model selection were confined to training data, with feature selection repeated within inner folds. A separate five-fold patient-grouped evaluation tested SHAP-guided inductive logic programmin
s40f0d9c5bb.summary: Researchers present an interpretable workflow combining proteomics, sparse logistic regression, SHAP attribution, and first-order logic rule learning for lung adenocarcinoma.

sd85410f8f2.title: Categorical Foundations of AI Agents
sd85410f8f2.description: arXiv:2611.29998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We follow the idea of separating intelligence from execution and give the categorical foundations of AI agents: the transformers, the agents, and the orchestrations and choreographies of AI agents are categorized, and which also include their coalgebras and algebras.
sd85410f8f2.summary: A paper gives a categorical foundation for AI agents, classifying transformers, agents, orchestrations, and choreographies with their coalgebras and algebras.
sd85410f8f2.why: Offers a formal mathematical framing of agent composition, but the abstract gives little on practical implications for engineers.

s4e66c4d6ca.title: OWE-Bench: A long-horizon benchmark for measuring real-world engineering
s4e66c4d6ca.description: arXiv:2611.30017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present OWE-Bench (OpenWorldEngineer-Bench), a benchmark of 26 long-horizon engineering tasks written by domain experts in software engineering, physical engineering, machine learning, and scientific computing. Tasks range from optimizing kernels and designing an aircraft, to identifying the faults responsible for an earthquake. Each task requires significant domain knowledge and engineering work, with models averaging hundreds of millions of tokens per task. Solutions are scored on practical measures such as speed, cost and accuracy, both on provided cases the agent could test against and on hidden cases that an engineer would expect from the task description. The best-performing frontier model so far, Claude Fable 5.2, scores 54.6% and a
s4e66c4d6ca.summary: Researchers released OWE-Bench, a benchmark of 26 long-horizon engineering tasks across software, physical engineering, ML, and scientific computing.
s4e66c4d6ca.why: It scores models on speed, cost, and accuracy for realistic multi-hour engineering work, useful for evaluating agent capability beyond short tasks.

s8c557828dd.title: Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA) for Energy Market Settlements: A Machine and Reinforcement Learning-Based Approach
s8c557828dd.description: arXiv:2611.30020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of segmented energy markets into Independent System Operators (ISOs) like CAISO and MISO has increased settlement complexity. Automated transaction processing creates challenges for evaluating accuracy, compliance, and financial integrity. Traditional rule-based manual auditing is inefficient, error-prone, and cannot handle the data volume from automated markets.This research proposes Automated Neural Network Auditing (ANNA), a machine and reinforcement learning framework for settlement auditing via anomaly prioritization. ANNA integrates statistical anomaly detection, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), clustering, and Deep Q-Network (DQN) reinforcement learning to flag potentially anomalous transactions from historical market data. T
s8c557828dd.summary: Researchers propose ANNA, a machine and reinforcement learning framework that audits energy market settlements by prioritizing anomalies.
s8c557828dd.why: Shows automated anomaly prioritization applied to high-volume financial settlement auditing where rule-based manual review is slow and error-prone.

s885c706a70.title: SWAM: State-aware World Action Model for Multi-Agent 3D Environments
s885c706a70.description: arXiv:2611.30042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive world models generate virtual environments autoregressively from player actions and visual history. However, visual history alone cannot reliably capture the evolving states of independently acting non-player characters (NPCs) in real games, particularly when they are outside the camera view. Recent multi-agent world models address this challenge through joint multi-view generation or persistent shared state, but often rely on external observations, like maps or scene geometry, or predefined state transitions. We present SWAM, a State-aware World Action Model that separates agent-state evolution from autoregressive visual generation in interactive 3D environments. A lightweight state model propagates character dynamics from action
s885c706a70.summary: Researchers present SWAM, a state-aware world action model that tracks the evolving states of non-player characters in multi-agent 3D game environments.
s885c706a70.why: Addresses keeping off-screen agent state consistent in interactive world models without relying on external maps or predefined transitions.

se43d28b4ac.title: EVD-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for EEG-to-Image Decoding
se43d28b4ac.description: arXiv:2611.30061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EEG-to-image decoding recovers visual information from non-invasive brain recordings, providing a window into human perception. However, comparisons across systems are confounded by a variable that is rarely reported as such: which participants' data the system was allowed to use. The same Top-1 score on a 200-way gallery may come from a per-participant system, a pooled model over all participants, or a model that never saw the test participant---cases that differ by more than most architectural changes between the methods being compared. We present \bench, a benchmark on THINGS-EEG2 that standardizes the gallery and EEG input, matches training budgets across systems within each regime, and compares three participant-access regimes: within-su
se43d28b4ac.summary: Researchers introduce EVD-Bench, a benchmark for EEG-to-image decoding that separates results by which participants' data systems were allowed to use.
se43d28b4ac.why: Highlights that differing training-data scopes can make cross-system benchmark scores non-comparable, a point relevant to evaluation design.

s262a147d78.title: Context-Grounded Skill Internalization for Vision-Language Agents
s262a147d78.description: arXiv:2611.30075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill internalization offers a way for agents to learn useful behaviors from skills and use them without explicit guidance in context at inference time. A common approach is to generate demonstration trajectories with the skill in context and then fine-tune the same model on its own trajectories with the skill removed. However, this leads to the problem that the model may learn to reference the removed skill, which we named as context misalignment (CoMi). In this work, we first analyze agent behaviors related to CoMi under this common pipeline. Across ALFWorld, WebShop, and ARC-AGI-1, skill-removed fine-tuning consistently results in CoMi: 12.2-46.0% of test trajectories reference the removed skill. To address this problem, we develop Context
s262a147d78.summary: Researchers study context misalignment in skill internalization for vision-language agents, where models learn to reference skills that were removed during fine-tuning.
s262a147d78.why: Identifies a failure mode in a common fine-tuning pipeline for teaching agents skills without in-context guidance.

s7542c7a7c5.title: Correlated by Construction: Endpoint Choice and the Validation of Protein Screening
s7542c7a7c5.description: arXiv:2611.30087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning for protein engineering depends on functional measurements collected at screening scale, but the designs those measurements rank are deployed in processes that run elsewhere. Whether a miniaturized assay remains informative under the conditions of use is usually assumed rather than demonstrated. We describe an automated production and screening platform and test the transfer of its solution-phase metal-affinity measurements to immobilized rare-earth separation. Primary pKd-derived separation factors tracked those measured on covalently immobilized protein across 82 protein-metal-pair measurements from 35 proteins, with pairwise Spearman correlations of 0.878 to 0.923 (pooled Pearson $r$ = 0.836; Spearman $\rho$ = 0.869). Sepa
s7542c7a7c5.summary: Researchers describe an automated protein production and screening platform and test whether miniaturized metal-affinity assays transfer to rare-earth separation.

s0825e1eb78.title: Post-Training Agents for Long-Document Reasoning
s0825e1eb78.description: arXiv:2611.30090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional documents are a long-context workload that retrieval-style benchmarks do not capture. In a ten-domain enterprise collection, a task's evidence is spread across a source document of median length 27 pages (mean 48.8, maximum 873); a third of tasks rest mainly on charts, drawings, and maps; and 70.9% require two or more reasoning hops. We post-train Kimi-K2.7, an open-weight foundation model, at its full context window on 1,465 expert-authored tasks with atomic rubrics from that collection, training rank-32 adapters with one round of privileged-context on-policy self-distillation followed by two rounds of rubric-reward reinforcement learning. We render each PDF as text for training and as extracted text plus selected page images at
s0825e1eb78.summary: Researchers post-trained the open-weight Kimi-K2.7 on 1,465 expert-authored tasks to improve reasoning over long professional documents.
s0825e1eb78.why: Shows a concrete post-training recipe for long-context enterprise document tasks using rank-32 adapters on an open-weight model.

s9ba7922666.title: Small data machine learning: the trilemma of low-sample tabular regimes
s9ba7922666.description: arXiv:2611.30118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small tabular datasets leave few observations for choosing a model and assessing its predictions. We examine these competing demands in controlled simulations and on six public datasets, using SmallGBM and SmallMLP as fixed-configuration case studies. Three results illustrate why the choice of evaluation matters. First, at n = 100, five-fold cross-validation overstated the gain from tuning XGBoost by 0.063 ROC-AUC on random labels, while tuning improved independent-test ROC-AUC by 0.0078 on a Gaussian mixture. Second, when 20% of binary training labels were flipped, the median within-trial ROC-AUC loss was 0.0210 for SmallGBM and 0.0778 for a fixed 200-tree XGBoost configuration. A separate regression experiment showed the sensitivity of squa
s9ba7922666.summary: A paper examines the trade-offs in evaluating and tuning models on small tabular datasets, using SmallGBM and SmallMLP in simulations and six public datasets.
s9ba7922666.why: Shows cross-validation can overstate tuning gains on small datasets, which affects how practitioners should evaluate models.

s67303025cf.title: Could This BE Any More Wrong? Teaching VLMs to Know What They Don't Know in Document Extraction
s67303025cf.description: arXiv:2611.30119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language Models can extract structured fields from scanned financial documents, yet they provide no indication of when a field might be wrong. We derive per-field confidence estimates from the token log-probabilities the model already produces, via a token-to-span alignment procedure that maps logprobs onto each extracted value within the structured JSON output. Evaluated on two benchmarks (CORD v2 receipts, Kleister NDA legal contracts) with three VLM families, the minimum token probability per field achieves Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC) 0.74-0.91 for error detection, far exceeding verbalized confidence (0.53-0.56). The uncertain fields form a natural training curriculum: fine-tuning via Group Relative Policy Optimisation (GRPO) i
s67303025cf.summary: Researchers derive per-field confidence scores for vision-language model document extraction from token log-probabilities on receipts and legal contracts.
s67303025cf.why: Offers a low-cost way to flag likely extraction errors in structured document pipelines without extra model calls.

s86e69b8c30.title: When Does Optical Context Compression Pay Off? A Decode-Aware Cost Analysis of Reasoning VLMs
s86e69b8c30.description: arXiv:2611.30130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rendering long text as images lets a vision-language model (VLM) read a document with fewer input tokens, and evaluations often count mainly these prefill tokens. We show that for reasoning models this accounting is incomplete. Across five models and two long-context benchmarks, reading the rendered document makes the model think longer: decode length grows by 1.5-3.5x on the four general-purpose VLMs tested, and under typical output pricing this decode tax makes image input more expensive than text for two of the five models on QuALITY. Unrecoverable information loss is not sufficient to explain the tax at moderate compression: Qwen's OCR of the same images recovers 98.7% of words, and feeding Kimi-K3 its own transcription as text restores t
s86e69b8c30.summary: A study finds optical context compression makes reasoning VLMs decode 1.5-3.5x longer, which can make image input costlier than text for some models.
s86e69b8c30.why: Engineers evaluating document compression for cost must count decode tokens, not just prefill tokens, when comparing image and text inputs.

s0d507d90ca.title: iFeST: An Iterative Motion Correction Framework for Fetal Brain Diffusion MRI via Frequency-Spatial-Temporal Modeling
s0d507d90ca.description: arXiv:2611.30131v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fetal brain diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) is a pivotal non-invasive tool for assessing the development of brain connectivity and microstructure. However, the prolonged acquisition times and complex sampling requirements render dMRI highly susceptible to unpredictable fetal motion. Existing motion correction methods typically process each dMRI volume independently and focus on inter-slice motion. Such strategies fail to utilize the coherent information between dMRI volumes along different diffusion directions and lack the ability to restore the intra-slice corruption. To address these limitations, we proposed iFeST, an iterative framework that combines frequency (k-space), spatial, and temporal (inter-slice) modeling for fetal br
s0d507d90ca.summary: Researchers present iFeST, an iterative motion correction framework for fetal brain diffusion MRI using frequency-spatial-temporal modeling.

s80de2402b9.title: WASP: Continual Weight Adaptation for Streaming LLM Personalization
s80de2402b9.description: arXiv:2611.30134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Personalized large language models (LLMs) should continually adapt to users' evolving preferences. Yet extracting preference changes from noisy interaction histories while supporting inexpensive updates remains challenging. We introduce WASP (Weight Adaptation for Streaming Personalization), a recurrent framework that captures fine-grained preferences directly from raw user interactions and generates personalized LoRA adapters without expensive per-user optimization. Specifically, WASP achieves this by training a shared hypernetwork that maintains a compact user representation and outputs adapter weights in a single forward pass. As new interactions arrive, WASP updates this representation without reprocessing full interaction history, enabli
s80de2402b9.summary: WASP is a recurrent framework that trains a shared hypernetwork to generate personalized LoRA adapters from raw user interactions, avoiding per-user optimization.
s80de2402b9.why: It offers a way to continually personalize LLMs with cheap adapter updates instead of costly per-user fine-tuning.

s5e0e32f053.title: AutoSECO: Automated Skill Evolution for Cross-Problem Combinatorial Optimization with General-Purpose LLM Agents
s5e0e32f053.description: arXiv:2611.30139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: General-purpose large language model (LLM) agents can develop complete solvers for combinatorial optimization problems. Their specialization, however, often relies on workflows engineered for individual problems, limiting the reuse of development expertise. We propose AutoSECO, an automated skill evolution method that learns reusable solver-development guidance from experience. The challenge is that external evaluation measures the completed solver, while the skill guides decisions during development. AutoSECO connects this feedback to guidance deficiencies by tracing performance shortfalls through solver code and recorded development decisions. Revisions are expressed as general instructions and retained only if a fresh solver developed unde
s5e0e32f053.summary: AutoSECO is an automated method that evolves reusable solver-development skills for general-purpose LLM agents writing combinatorial optimization solvers across problems.
s5e0e32f053.why: It suggests agents can reuse learned development guidance across problems rather than relying on per-problem workflows.

sf20443ddcf.title: ReVAgent: Multi-Agent Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation
sf20443ddcf.description: arXiv:2611.30163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central challenge in generating instructional videos for reasoning-intensive topics is to show how and why the state changes at each step. Even when an animation renders successfully, the depicted object relationships and state transitions can conflict with the explanation, making the reasoning difficult to follow. We present ReVAgent, a multi-agent framework that solves a problem, generates keyframes for its explanation, and synthesizes an instructional video. The agents share the execution record of a solution program, reuse intermediate results and constructions in the scenes, and check rendered keyframes to guide revisions to the solution or the scenes. We also introduce a multidimensional rubric for assessing whether generated videos p
sf20443ddcf.summary: ReVAgent is a multi-agent framework that solves a problem, generates explanatory keyframes, and synthesizes instructional videos showing state changes.

s4b58434527.title: Same Executions, Different Gaps: Judgment Rules in Web-Agent Evaluation
s4b58434527.description: arXiv:2611.30190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Success-rate gains guide the development of web agents. Yet knowing which agent ranks first does not tell us how much confidence to place in its reported advantage. We study the comparison itself: how success is defined, what evidence supports the judgments, and how the difference between agents is estimated. On fixed web-agent executions, changing a judge from predicting likely completion to requiring recorded support can remove most of a reported lead without changing the ranking. This effect persists when unresolved completion is distinguished from supported failure. Controlled source additions explain how missing relations between task requirements, objects and observations can conceal a difference or create an apparent advantage. We also
s4b58434527.summary: A study finds that changing how web-agent judgments define success can remove most of a reported performance lead without changing rankings.
s4b58434527.why: Engineers comparing web agents should check how success is judged, since evaluation rules can overstate confidence in reported gains.

s2f2a3b4e51.title: Adopting AI Technologies without Traps: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework
s2f2a3b4e51.description: arXiv:2611.30200v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI technologies and AI agents play increasingly important roles in human society, including in education, economics, and research. Adopting AI technologies can bring immediate, and sometimes tremendous, rewards such as through productivity boost, but they can also bring negative effects including but not limited to losses of job and training opportunities, and cognitive capability declines. Thus, it is important to investigate the optimal ways of adopting AI technologies without different traps. In this paper, we develop a general multi-agent Markov decision process (MDP) based reinforcement learning (RL or MARL) modeling framework for determining and analyzing optimal adoption of AI technologies. This framework can model the long-term dynami
s2f2a3b4e51.summary: Researchers present a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework to study how to adopt AI technologies while avoiding traps such as job loss and skill decline.

sf49d694dab.title: VeriWorld: A Verifiable Visual SWE-Bench for Spatial Reasoning in 3D Environments
sf49d694dab.description: arXiv:2611.30226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used for spatial tasks such as navigation and manipulation, where they must infer geometry and object relationships from visual input in order to act correctly. Existing benchmarks usually test perception and reasoning in isolation, making it hard to tell whether failures come from visual understanding, downstream reasoning, or the bridge between them. We introduce VeriWorld, a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments with executable actions and deterministic verification. For task families where all three channels are well-defined, we evaluate matched visual, structured, and combined input conditions on the same instance, environment, and verifier; families without a clean
sf49d694dab.summary: VeriWorld is a benchmark for spatial reasoning in interactive 3D environments, with executable actions and deterministic verification for vision-language models.
sf49d694dab.why: It helps separate whether VLM failures come from perception or from reasoning, aiding diagnosis of spatial-task models.

s511c7b1145.title: CLIP-FMoE: Scalable CLIP via Fused Mixture-of-Experts with Enforced Specialization
s511c7b1145.description: arXiv:2611.30233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures have emerged as a promising approach for scaling deep learning models while maintaining computational efficiency. However, existing MoE adaptations for Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) models suffer from significant computational overhead during sequential training and degradation of zero-shot capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose CLIP-FMoE, a novel approach that integrates MoE architecture into CLIP fine-tuning. Our method uses Isolated Constrained Contrastive Learning, a pipeline that trains specialized experts on cluster-based data partitions to accelerate expert specialization. Additionally, we introduce a Fusion Gate mechanism to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of pre
s511c7b1145.summary: CLIP-FMoE integrates a mixture-of-experts architecture into CLIP fine-tuning, using isolated constrained contrastive learning to aim for specialization.
s511c7b1145.why: It targets lower sequential training overhead and preserved zero-shot performance when scaling CLIP-style models with MoE.

s8deca33384.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
s8deca33384.description: arXiv:2611.30281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training large language models routinely pools reasoning trajectories from diverse teachers or algorithms, yet it remains unclear whether standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can learn such heterogeneous strategies without explicit mode conditioning. We study the learnability and local bottlenecks of heterogeneous reasoning through a formal mixture formulation and controlled experiments. We first formalize the representational compatibility of the optimal autoregressive model with latent reasoning mixtures: the target next-token distribution weights modes by their prefix posteriors and concentrates on a single mode once alternative modes assign negligible likelihood to the prefix. In a verifiable symbolic graph-search environment with p
s8deca33384.summary: The paper studies whether standard supervised fine-tuning can learn heterogeneous reasoning mixtures from diverse teachers without explicit mode conditioning.
s8deca33384.why: Teams pooling reasoning traces from multiple sources for fine-tuning may face learnability bottlenecks that this analysis addresses.

sf44b9fb63c.title: A statistical measure of trust in generative AI
sf44b9fb63c.description: arXiv:2611.30286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trustworthiness is a crucial issue for generative AI, as modern models can produce convincing and confident responses even when their outputs are incomplete, unsupported, or wrong. The frequent absence of ground-truth knowledge or labels complicates verification of generative AI outputs. To address this issue, we propose a trustworthiness framework grounded in model-internal confidence calibrated against an external expert reference. We estimate per-token trustworthiness of a student generative model as the statistical typicality of each generated token relative to an expert model's distribution, where the expert is used as a distributional reference rather than as a source of factual verification labels. To this end, we introduce an AI ontol
sf44b9fb63c.summary: Researchers propose a trustworthiness framework that estimates per-token trust in generative AI by comparing model-internal confidence against an external expert reference.
sf44b9fb63c.why: Per-token trust estimates could help flag unsupported outputs where ground-truth labels are scarce.

s981d7d9d52.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
s981d7d9d52.description: arXiv:2611.30287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated
s981d7d9d52.summary: MMMem is a task-aware multimodal memory framework that lets agents consolidate experience from completed tasks rather than only storing and retrieving records.
s981d7d9d52.why: Agents that learn from completed tasks could avoid repeating mistakes across long-term multimodal interactions.

sdb3344dee7.title: MH-RAG-DIVE: Dynamic and Cost-Efficient Multi-Hop RAG Evaluation via Tree-Cached Dialogue Simulation
sdb3344dee7.description: arXiv:2611.30335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quality assessment is essential for determining whether changes to a Retrieval-Augmented Generation system improve or maintain its performance. However, existing evaluation approaches often rely on single-turn or single-hop interactions and therefore do not capture the complexity of multi-hop, multi-turn conversations. We introduce MH-RAG-DIVE, a dynamic interactive user simulation framework designed to evaluate RAG systems in more complex multi-hop and multi-turn settings. The framework extends RAG-DIVE with a Context Discoverer, which identifies documents that can be combined to generate multi-hop questions within an ongoing conversation. To address the high computational cost of dynamic user simulation, we further introduce a Conversation
sdb3344dee7.summary: MH-RAG-DIVE is a dynamic user-simulation framework for evaluating RAG systems in multi-hop, multi-turn conversations using tree-cached dialogue simulation.
sdb3344dee7.why: It offers a more realistic and cost-efficient way to test RAG changes than single-turn evaluation.

s2fcd82f4b5.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks
s2fcd82f4b5.description: arXiv:2611.30353v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Staff pseudonymizing financial data in closed networks must interpret abbreviated column names, identify personal information, and choose processing methods. Local language models can assist, but may give different labels for the same input. PseuDRAGON keeps confirmed judgments and corrections outside a fixed model and reuses them through exact-name lookup and learned rules. For expert review, the workflow searches institutional policy, national privacy law, then international sources. Across 92 columns from one institution, rules increase reuse under the same approval checks from 75 to 83 labels without reuse errors when all training judgments are available. With 25% of the training judgments, withholding non-PII rules for unseen names elimi
s2fcd82f4b5.summary: PseuDRAGON uses local LLMs with confirmed judgments, exact-name lookup, and learned rules to pseudonymize financial data in closed networks, tested on 92 columns.
s2fcd82f4b5.why: It shows how reusing expert corrections can make local models more consistent for sensitive data workflows.

s99da5e6dde.title: mini-psych-agent: Evaluating Human-Like Behavior in LLM Agents through Interactive Psychological Environments
s99da5e6dde.description: arXiv:2611.30365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Large Language Model (LLM), its harness, and the test-time compute budget jointly determine its behavior. Consequently, the same underlying model, embedded in different agentic workflows or allocated different amounts of test-time compute, can exhibit markedly different performance. Psychologists face an analogous challenge when evaluating human performance: the same person may behave differently under different incentives and levels of deliberation. Psychological tasks therefore provide an ideal testbed for studying such behavioral variation. However, when adapted to LLMs, these tasks are typically text-transcribed, replaying fixed, language-rendered experiments as static prompts. This format is ill-suited to agent evaluation, where action
s99da5e6dde.summary: mini-psych-agent is a framework for evaluating human-like behavior in LLM agents using interactive psychological environments under varying compute and incentives.
s99da5e6dde.why: Behavior depends on model, harness, and test-time compute together, so evaluations should vary these factors.

s16c2ff0b08.title: Trustworthy Speech-Based Autism Screening under Class Imbalance with Uncertainty-Aware HuBERT Ensembles
s16c2ff0b08.description: arXiv:2611.30390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Early screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is critical for timely clinical intervention, although establishing reliable speech based screening systems remains problematic due to limited clinical data, class imbalance, and the need for reliable uncertainty estimation. We propose an uncertainty-aware ASD screening framework based on self-supervised HuBERT representations, combining Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) crossvalidation, balanced k-bagging, and Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout. Multiple HuBERT models are fine-tuned on balanced subsets, with predictions combined through probability-based ensemble averaging and aggregated at the subject level. Experiments on the Child Pathological Speech Database (CPSD) show strong performance, achieving 86.
s16c2ff0b08.summary: Researchers propose an uncertainty-aware speech-based autism screening framework using HuBERT ensembles, LOSO cross-validation, balanced bagging, and MC Dropout.

scf87ec87ef.title: Event-Driven Parameter Dynamics for Spatiotemporal Parameter-Update Application in Deep Learning
scf87ec87ef.description: arXiv:2611.30397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard neural network training typically applies optimizer-generated update signals to model parameters at every iteration. This work introduces a spatiotemporal view of parameter updating and proposes Event-Driven Parameter Dynamics (EPD), which separates candidate-update generation from their application through an intermediate state with accumulation, event-triggered release, and reset. In a canonical coordinate-wise instantiation, accumulation produces temporal integration, release imposes a spatial budget, and reset separates successive inter-release intervals, while conventional dense updating is recovered as a boundary case. Across four model--optimizer configurations on CIFAR-100, EPD maintains final performance close to conventiona
scf87ec87ef.summary: Event-Driven Parameter Dynamics (EPD) separates update generation from application using accumulation, event-triggered release, and reset in neural network training.
scf87ec87ef.why: It proposes an alternative to applying optimizer updates every iteration, which could matter for training efficiency research.

s74364fd01d.title: Cost-Sensitive Reversibility of Non-Deterministic Actions
s74364fd01d.description: arXiv:2611.30399v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Determining action reversibility requires checking whether the effects of an action can be undone. Recent work has extended reversibility to fully observable non-deterministic (FOND) planning. It distinguishes weak reversibility, where reversal may succeed, from strong-cyclic reversibility, where reversal is guaranteed under fairness. These notions are qualitative: they say whether reversal is possible, but not how costly it is. We introduce cost-sensitive reversibility for non-deterministic actions. Given positive action costs, we define weak and strong reversal budgets, $k$-bounded reversibility, and a distinction between finite strong reversal and strong-cyclic reversal with unbounded worst-case cost. We relate the resulting notions in a r
s74364fd01d.summary: Researchers introduce cost-sensitive reversibility for non-deterministic actions, extending qualitative weak and strong-cyclic reversibility notions in FOND planning to also measure reversal cost.
s74364fd01d.why: Adds cost measures to action reversibility in planning under non-determinism, useful for engineers building planners that must weigh the price of undoing actions.

s8e8339c434.title: DMC-5: Dual-Model Collaboration with Cache-aware Context Compression for Long-horizon Agents
s8e8339c434.description: arXiv:2611.30412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon agents repeatedly feed an ever-growing interaction trajectory to a specialized agent model. Prefix caching reuses computation over repeated history, but cannot prevent context growth or remove information irrelevant to the current decision. This is especially costly when the specialized agent lacks the cached-input discounts available to general-purpose models, making trajectory compression a natural alternative. However, existing compression methods on selective context risk losing global information, recursively rewriting summary leads to semantic drift, while repeatedly recompressing the full history shifts the growing cost to the compressor. Therefore, we introduce DMC-5 (Dual-Model Collaboration with CaChe-aware Context Comp
s8e8339c434.summary: DMC-5 proposes a dual-model collaboration approach with cache-aware context compression to manage ever-growing interaction trajectories for long-horizon agents.
s8e8339c434.why: Addresses rising context costs in long-running agents where specialized models lack cached-input discounts, a practical concern for agent cost and design.

se7dce42bab.title: TamperCert: A Benchmark for Detecting Text Tampering in Degree Certificates
se7dce42bab.description: arXiv:2611.30419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Degree certificates play a critical role in high-stakes decisions such as university admission, immigration, and hiring. The issuing institution vouches for the holder, so a forged certificate may let its bearer pass these checks. Degree certificate forgery is increasingly prevalent. Yet, many assume that it is easy to spot. Reported cases show otherwise: in 2024, the business school of the University of Hong Kong found that about 30 master's students had enrolled with forged academic credentials. Few studies have looked at how to detect forged degree certificates, partly because public benchmarks are scarce. We present TamperCert, a benchmark built from 400 real degree certificates issued by 38 universities. Each certificate was subjected to
se7dce42bab.summary: TamperCert introduces a benchmark for detecting text tampering in degree certificates, motivated by rising forgery cases in admissions, immigration and hiring.
se7dce42bab.why: Offers a benchmark for document forgery detection, relevant to teams building verification workflows for credentials, though the text gives little on results.

scf313db090.title: HWRE-Bench: Can LLM Agents Understand Hardware They Did Not Design?
scf313db090.description: arXiv:2611.30422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware benchmarks for LLM agents all run the design flow forward, from a specification to RTL, a layout or a bug fix. We ask the reverse question: given an implemented artifact, such as a layout, a gate-level netlist or a protected simulation model, can an agent work out what it does well enough to act on that knowledge? We introduce HWRE-Bench, a benchmark for agentic hardware reverse engineering built on one observation. Each step of the forward flow discards information (names, hierarchy, word-level structure, generator parameters, the programming model), and a reverse-engineering task asks the agent to recover what was lost and to prove it with an executable deliverable that the artifact alone cannot supply. Since layout extraction is n
scf313db090.summary: HWRE-Bench is a benchmark testing whether LLM agents can reverse-engineer implemented hardware artifacts such as layouts, netlists and protected simulation models.
scf313db090.why: Tests agent capability in the reverse direction of hardware design flows, relevant to EDA and hardware teams evaluating agents on unfamiliar artifacts.

sc384061a8b.title: Automated Call for Action: RAG-Based Environmental Law Enforcement Screening System
sc384061a8b.description: arXiv:2611.30423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Environmental law inspectors face a structural issue in identifying potential violations from data: they often do not have the capacity to deal with large volume of data present in the emission events. This paper examines to what extent an LLM-based system can support evidence assembly and permit-based screening of such events, using the coke plants of a steel producer and a regional environmental service as a case. A simple puff-trajectory model aligns air quality measurements, weather and citizen complaints with each emission event. A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline then retrieves facility-specific permit conditions and generates event reports and a period report with an investigation recommendation. Across 74 events from Marc
sc384061a8b.summary: Researchers present a RAG-based LLM system that helps environmental law inspectors screen emission events, using a steel producer's coke plants as a case study.
sc384061a8b.why: Shows a domain-specific RAG pipeline combining sensor data, weather and complaints for regulatory screening, a template for enterprise compliance tooling.

s6533ae596c.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
s6533ae596c.description: arXiv:2611.30494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) are used in more and more new tasks, context engineering becomes a fundamental method to efficiently steer LLMs by constructing instruction prompts or metadata without intensive training. A growing number of LLM context engineering (LCE) approaches automate the task by casting the LLM itself as the engineer that draws generalizable instructions or experiences from offline trials as context. Although these methods resemble how humans learn from experiences, it remains unclear \textbf{when and how} LLMs can engineer effective context from data. To answer the question, we first establish a benchmark composed of datasets with different reasoning patterns. We compared different LCE methods with different LLM familie
s6533ae596c.summary: A paper examines when and how LLMs can act as context engineers, generating instructions or experiences from offline trials to steer themselves without training.
s6533ae596c.why: Clarifies when LLM-driven prompt and context optimization works, informing engineers choosing automated prompt engineering approaches.

s5292c9ad0d.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
s5292c9ad0d.description: arXiv:2611.30545v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In text to image AI models, fixing the prompt and the random seed is widely assumed to fix the image. We show that it does not on GPUs. We evaluate six text-to-image models (diffusion and autoregressive) under four numerical precisions and quantizations on three GPU types (RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada, and H100 NVL), across up to 100 prompts per set for all six models. For each configuration we compare, with the prompt and seed fixed, the image generated alone with the image generated inside a batch, and we also compare across GPUs. Every replay control reported here is bit-exact, so the variation is not random noise: the execution setting, mainly the batch composition and the GPU, decides the output. The effect is large and model dependent. Struc
s5292c9ad0d.summary: Researchers show that fixing prompt and seed does not reproduce text-to-image outputs on GPUs, because results vary with batch composition and GPU type across six models.
s5292c9ad0d.why: Reproducibility of generative image pipelines breaks under batching and hardware changes, which matters for testing, evaluation and audit workflows.

sc5c18c3c32.title: Splitting Belief Bases Conditionally based on Constraints for c-Representations and their Solutions
sc5c18c3c32.description: arXiv:2611.30556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Splitting notions for conditional belief bases aim at localizing reasoning and computation tasks to subbases containing only the relevant parts of the belief base. Among the different reasoning mechanisms, c-representations, a special kind of Spohn's ranking models, have been shown to provide high-quality inferences. c-Representations can be conveniently specified via a constraint satisfaction problem. In this article, we introduce the notion of conditional constraint splittings, extending constraint splittings by also allowing the subbases to share conditionals. Taking inspiration from conditional syntax splittings, we identify the subclasses of safe and fully localized conditional constraint splittings, allowing us to locally and independen
sc5c18c3c32.summary: The paper introduces conditional constraint splittings to localize reasoning over conditional belief bases for c-representations, a form of Spohn ranking models.

se4fe5a4d33.title: Learning What to Change: State-Verified Reinforcement Learning for Educational Agents
se4fe5a4d33.description: arXiv:2611.30559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persistent tutoring agents do more than answer questions: they manage course files, practice records, and learner profiles that govern future lessons. In such stateful settings, knowing what to teach does not guarantee knowing what to change. We identify a pervasive failure mode, content-state decoupling, where agents deliver pedagogically sound responses while silently corrupting workspace state through unwarranted updates, missed prerequisites, or unintended side effects. Text-level judges overlook these state errors, whereas isolated tool-call checks break down because whether a write action is valid depends jointly on the learner request, prior state, and execution order. We propose State-Verified Reinforcement Learning, which supervises
se4fe5a4d33.summary: Researchers propose state-verified reinforcement learning for tutoring agents, targeting cases where agents give sound answers while silently corrupting course and learner state.
se4fe5a4d33.why: Highlights that text-level judging misses state errors in stateful agents, a reliability concern for engineers deploying tool-using agents that modify persistent data.

s04fd5f6b59.title: Interrogation Protocols for AI Control
s04fd5f6b59.description: arXiv:2611.30583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As the intelligence of an AI agent increases relative to a trusted monitor, so does the risk that the monitor will fail to understand the agent's actions or to evaluate them confidently. We introduce interrogation protocols to a high-stakes AI control setting, and allow the monitor to ask the untrusted agent questions about confusing actions. For interrogation to improve safety, a weaker model must be able to distinguish misleading explanations produced by an attack policy from genuine ones produced by an honest policy. We find that on a held-out subset of BashArena, an interrogation protocol improves safety at a 1% audit budget from 72.6% for an actions-only baseline, which does not use interrogations, to 79.5% (+7.0 pp [+0.9, +20.1], 95% pa
s04fd5f6b59.summary: Researchers introduce interrogation protocols in which a weaker trusted monitor asks a untrusted AI agent questions about confusing actions to improve AI control.
s04fd5f6b59.why: Offers a monitoring technique for high-stakes agent oversight, relevant to teams designing safeguards for capable agents against a weaker trusted monitor.

s7de1b79016.title: JaxNaviSim: A GPU-Accelerated, Data-Driven Simulator and Learning Benchmark for Maritime Navigation
s7de1b79016.description: arXiv:2611.30600v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coordinating vessels through the shared waterways of busy ports grows more challenging as vessel traffic increases. Port authorities need realistic simulations to assess how arrival schedules, anchorage assignments, and routes affect vessel throughput and navigation safety. Existing AIS-based trajectory models predict a vessel's track from its past trajectory in an open-loop fashion. They do not simulate step-by-step responses to other ships or test whether a vessel collides or reaches its goal. To address this problem, we introduce JaxNaviSim, a data-driven simulator and learning benchmark coupling Automatic Identification System (AIS) data with fast, controllable traffic simulation, in which learned models steer vessels through recorded tra
s7de1b79016.summary: JaxNaviSim is a GPU-accelerated, data-driven maritime navigation simulator and learning benchmark that simulates step-by-step vessel responses and collisions in ports.

s146a56b516.title: Learning Multimodal Representations from Partially Paired, Small-Scale Data
s146a56b516.description: arXiv:2611.30601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modeling multimodal data from partially paired samples is critical for advancing domains like biomedicine, where vast unimodal datasets and foundation models exist but paired data remains scarce. Existing fusion methods rely on large-scale paired datasets, limiting their use in scenarios with incomplete pairing. We introduce CAMEO, an adversarial learning-based modality fusion framework that integrates modalities from small, partially paired datasets. Combining any pre-trained unimodal encoder with a cross-modal latent alignment mechanism, CAMEO learns shared representations requiring only minimal paired samples. Evaluated on computational pathology tasks such as niche classification and cell type composition prediction, CAMEO achieves superi
s146a56b516.summary: CAMEO is an adversarial learning framework that fuses modalities from small, partially paired datasets by combining pre-trained unimodal encoders with cross-modal latent alignment.
s146a56b516.why: Enables multimodal fusion where paired data is scarce, relevant to biomedical and other teams with large unimodal datasets but few paired samples.

s7825a0826f.title: ActField: Learning Action Effects as Continuous-Time Latent Dynamics
s7825a0826f.description: arXiv:2611.30659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning how actions change visual states is essential for prediction and decision-making in embodied tasks. Existing action-conditioned JEPA world models typically predict future representations at discrete observation intervals, leaving the temporal evolution of action effects implicit. We introduce ActField, a continuous-time JEPA world model that explicitly models latent state evolution through an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time. ActField separates action-independent evolution from action-induced changes, with the latter modulated by the latent context. A reference-conditioned representation and multi-step dynamics loss further support accurate long-horizon prediction. Together, these components provide a str
s7825a0826f.summary: ActField is a continuous-time JEPA world model that learns action effects as an action-conditioned vector field integrated over physical time for embodied tasks.
s7825a0826f.why: Models action effects in continuous time rather than at discrete intervals, relevant to robotics and embodied AI researchers building world models.

s12e44899fe.title: WeMM-Ecom: Advancing Multimodal Content Understanding for WeChat E-Commerce
s12e44899fe.description: arXiv:2611.30662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present WeMM-Ecom, a family of multimodal large language models that deliver frontier e-commerce capabilities while achieving state-of-the-art general-purpose performance at their respective scales. The family spans five sizes, from a 0.8B dense model to a 35B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Our training pipeline begins with two-stage continued pre-training that progressively raises the proportion of e-commerce data within a diverse multimodal data mixture, followed by hybrid-thinking post-training that combines on-policy distillation and reinforcement learning to support both non-thinking and thinking modes. For evaluation, we construct a comprehensive suite of 28 e-commerce benchmarks (23 in-house and five open-source
s12e44899fe.summary: WeMM-Ecom is a family of multimodal LLMs from 0.8B to 35B parameters, a mixture-of-experts model with 3B active, tuned for WeChat e-commerce content understanding.
s12e44899fe.why: Shows a domain-tuned multimodal model family claiming general-purpose performance too, relevant to teams evaluating specialized e-commerce models.

sd7b8b10d87.title: Beyond the Black Box: A Diagnosis-Driven Agent for Interpretable MIP Solver Tuning
sd7b8b10d87.description: arXiv:2611.30670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tuning a mixed-integer programming (MIP) solver is an instance-specific problem, where a poor configuration can increase solving time by orders of magnitude. Existing Bayesian optimization tuners treat solver tuning as a black-box optimization problem: each evaluation returns a single score, allowing the tuner to learn which configuration is faster, but not why. Inspired by the use of profilers in GPU-kernel optimization, we introduce APEC (Agent for Per-instance Explainable Configuration), a log-grounded tuning agent for MIP solvers. APEC has three layers: a deterministic layer that profiles each log, an interpretation layer that guides hypothesis-driven diagnosis, and a system layer that controls evaluation, enabling more reliable and inter
sd7b8b10d87.summary: APEC is a log-grounded agent that tunes mixed-integer programming solvers per instance, using profiler-like diagnosis to explain configuration choices rather than treating tuning as a black box.
sd7b8b10d87.why: Replaces opaque Bayesian tuning with explainable, per-instance diagnosis, useful for teams optimizing solver performance in operations research workloads.

s933f4fa1ad.title: Uncovering Hidden Behaviours in Language Models via Limited-Parameter Finetuning
s933f4fa1ad.description: arXiv:2611.30672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can have behaviours which only arise in hard-to-anticipate contexts. These hidden behaviours pose a challenge to alignment audits, which seek to uncover problematic model behaviour but are limited by the scenarios the auditor can anticipate. To address this challenge, we explore limited-parameter finetuning (LPF) on examples of a target behaviour. While training 3-25% of LoRA parameters, LPF reveals whether the model has a hidden behaviour, even when standard behavioural evaluations cannot. LPF succeeds on a suite of model organisms with hidden behaviours (8-14B parameters), and also surfaces naturally occurring hidden behaviours in open-weight models (27-35B parameters). LPF can thus distinguish between models which app
s933f4fa1ad.summary: Researchers propose limited-parameter finetuning on target-behaviour examples to reveal hidden LLM behaviours that standard behavioural evaluations miss.
s933f4fa1ad.why: Offers auditors a way to surface hidden model behaviours that anticipated test scenarios would not catch, strengthening alignment audits.

s15bca4be51.title: How Many Parameters Does Forecasting Need? A Survey and Code-Level Audit of Lightweight Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
s15bca4be51.description: arXiv:2611.30685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term time series forecasting supports decisions in energy, transportation, weather and finance, where forecasts are produced continuously and often on constrained hardware. Recent work has moved in two directions. One scales Transformers and pre-trained foundation models to millions or hundreds of millions of parameters. The other shows that models with only hundreds to tens of thousands of parameters remain competitive on the standard benchmarks. Existing surveys organize forecasting models by backbone and treat efficiency as a side topic, so the reasons these small models work, and the way their sizes are reported, remain unexamined. This survey focuses on lightweight long-term forecasting. It provides a taxonomy of about thirty-five m
s15bca4be51.summary: A survey and code-level audit examines lightweight long-term time series forecasting models against large Transformer and foundation models.
s15bca4be51.why: Suggests tiny forecasting models can stay competitive on standard benchmarks, relevant for teams forecasting on constrained hardware.

s346ebfabba.title: Skill-Composer: Requirement-Driven Skill Selection from Multiple Marketplaces
s346ebfabba.description: arXiv:2611.30715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills have become the primary vehicle through which agents reuse specialized capabilities, yet public skill marketplaces provide skills with individual items: a query, whether matched through keyword or embedding similarity, returns a list of single skills ordered by relevance or by popularity. Such an interface cannot answer the question a developer actually faces: which set of skills should be installed to cover a task's complete requirement? The highest-ranked skills are often functionally redundant, while capabilities that are genuinely required remain uncovered. In this paper, we argue that skill acquisition should be reframed from ranking to set selection. We propose Skill-Composer, an agent-native framework that selects a non-re
s346ebfabba.summary: Skill-Composer proposes selecting a set of agent skills from multiple marketplaces to cover a task's full requirement, rather than ranking individual skills.
s346ebfabba.why: Addresses redundant top-ranked skills in marketplaces, which matters for developers choosing which agent capabilities to install.

s326218db5d.title: Testing Quantized KV-Cache Maintenance: Encoding Layout and Historical Restoration
s326218db5d.description: arXiv:2611.30720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Repeating rows then selecting originals retains layout-dependent drift despite equal encoding counts. We measure when existing checks fail to establish preservation contracts in fixed quantized KV-cache implementations. In four-bit HQQ axis zero at sixteen cycles, median paired relative-L2 increases over same-shape re-encoding are 7.22 percentage points for Qwen3-1.7B and 11.59 for SmolLM3-3B. Matched encoded states cover sixteen shared questions per model at one and sixteen cycles. Axis one matches the shape-preserving control; lazy reorders preserve the initial state. On one known input, fixed update counts retain the difference; preserving group members removes it. Our prefix-view extension passes current-prefix checks yet changes history
s326218db5d.summary: Researchers test whether fixed quantized KV-cache implementations preserve encoded state, measuring drift from repeated re-encoding in 4-bit HQQ on two small models.
s326218db5d.why: Shows existing checks can miss layout-dependent drift in quantized KV caches, a concern for inference correctness engineers.

s125f73481e.title: Can Cities Have Personalities? Introducing the SCD City Personality Assessment
s125f73481e.description: arXiv:2611.30733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Descriptions of cities are shaped by human experience and institutional narratives. We introduce the SCD City Personality Assessment (SCD-CPA), a method that instantiates document-grounded ChatGPT city personas and interrogates each with an identical 24-statement instrument inspired by the four-pair structure of the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator. Rather than asking a general-purpose model to characterize cities freely, we configure a separate document-grounded conversational agent for each city and use alternative evidence portraits to compare documentary inputs. The resulting four bipolar dimensions and four-letter summaries use independently defined urban concepts and scoring rules. Tokyo, New York, and Paris form the methodological evaluatio
s125f73481e.summary: Researchers introduce SCD City Personality Assessment, which gives document-grounded ChatGPT city personas a Myers-Briggs-inspired 24-statement instrument.

s7e4ba6c668.title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
s7e4ba6c668.description: arXiv:2611.30742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are often ranked by an LLM judge whose error rates are measured once and reused for every agent. The corrected success rates can then be biased when the judge's errors depend on the trajectory and agents differ in the trajectories they produce for successes or failures. We derive the exact asymptotic bias and give a chain of checks from identification to simultaneous ranks. On a four-agent semi-synthetic benchmark, a scalar correction with oracle calibration has maximum bias 0.245 and mean pointwise coverage 0.016, and never recovers the full ranking (0/250 replications). Augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with a uniform or a design-aware random audit keeps the maximum bias below 0.003, with mean
s7e4ba6c668.summary: Researchers show that LLM judge error rates measured once and reused can bias corrected success rates when judge errors depend on agent trajectories.
s7e4ba6c668.why: Warns that reusing a single LLM-judge error calibration across agents can produce biased rankings in agent evaluations.

sb123ca22d2.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
sb123ca22d2.description: arXiv:2611.30745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents turn a user's request and retrieved content into tool calls, and a call can reach the wrong recipient, endpoint, file or participant. Argument-level provenance blocks such values when they come from untrusted content, but accepts a trusted value that the user never requested. IntentFlow, a mediation layer between an unmodified planner and its tools, checks each authority-bearing argument against an intent contract and a provenance policy. On a synthetic benchmark of 200 attacks (oracle intent and injection labels, declared roles), attack success falls from 50.5% with provenance alone to 12.0% [8.2-17.2%]; every remaining success alters a content or payload field. IntentFlow wrongly blocks none of 200 paired benign tasks and 4 of 50
sb123ca22d2.summary: IntentFlow is a mediation layer that checks tool-call arguments against user intent and provenance policy, blocking trusted-but-unauthorized values.
sb123ca22d2.why: Targets a gap where provenance checks accept trusted values the user never requested, relevant for securing tool-using agents.

s92ba36c6d3.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
s92ba36c6d3.description: arXiv:2611.30750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The tools users approve for their AI agents keep changing their JSON input schemas. Of 8 surveyed MCP clients and scanners, none is observed or documented to re-approve a tool whose input schema widens (two not determinable). We define non-amplification over the coordinates visible in the schema (declared arguments and undeclared fields, on effective values) and a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion, trusting no field labels by default and conservative up to its checker and tested case analysis. Evidence: a Coq proof of composition; 48 regression tests; an exact-reference benchmark, where the reviewed version of the rule silently re-bound 27 amplifying changes, now fixed; and a pilot on 604 releases of 39 public MCP servers. There,
s92ba36c6d3.summary: SchemaCaps shows that compatible JSON schema updates to MCP tools can silently widen an AI agent's authority, and none of eight surveyed clients re-approves them.
s92ba36c6d3.why: Highlights that agent tools can gain permissions through routine schema changes without user re-approval, a security risk for agent deployments.

s625953acb7.title: GameDojo: Benchmarking Real-Time Interactive Agents in Video Games
s625953acb7.description: arXiv:2611.30771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Interactive intelligence requires agents to act on observations and adapt to the consequences of actions. Studying these abilities calls for diverse, challenging tasks under controlled conditions. We introduce GameDojo, a controllable interactive gameplay benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games for evaluating model capabilities, learning algorithms, and agent harnesses. Coding agents reconstruct the environments and write gameplay scripts, producing GameDojo-Data with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories. Experiments reveal substantial challenges for frontier models, especially in real-time interaction. Training on GameDojo-Data brings GameDojo-4B to frontier performance, with the strongest real-time performance. We also find joint tra
s625953acb7.summary: GameDojo is a benchmark of 120 boss encounters across 20 games for evaluating real-time interactive agents, with 600 hours of gameplay trajectories.

sdf2c16b3e0.title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI
sdf2c16b3e0.description: arXiv:2611.30816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation fundamentally requires human-centered evaluation, assessing whether explanations align with human reasoning and expert knowledge. However, such evaluations often require expert-driven manual validation and are difficult to scale, leading to the widespread use of alignment-based metrics, where attribution maps are compared against predefined ground-truth (GT) representations. Despite their popularity, alignment evaluations are implicitly bias towards multiple design choices made during the evaluation process, for example GT representations, metric families, metric formulations (soft vs. hard), and thresholding strategies. In this paper, we formalize alignment evaluation as a structured evaluation configuration s
sdf2c16b3e0.summary: Researchers examine how design choices in alignment-based evaluation metrics for explainable AI bias the results when attribution maps are compared to ground truth.
sdf2c16b3e0.why: Shows evaluation configuration can shift XAI alignment scores, so teams should report metric settings when comparing explanations.

sfd44838453.title: AeroJEPA: A Two-Stage Framework for Aerosol Forecasting with Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning
sfd44838453.description: arXiv:2611.30891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aerosol forecasting requires integrating sparse ground observations and modeling meteorologically driven concentration evolution and spatial structure. However, analysis-initialized forecasts make limited explicit use of historical observations, while pointwise regression tends to smooth local variations and provides limited constraints on fine spatial structures. In this work, we propose AeroJEPA, a two-stage joint-embedding predictive framework for regional surface PM$_{2.5}$ forecasting. Specifically, Stage I fuses historical observations, model backgrounds, and meteorological information to predict an initial future state, meteorological conditions, and multi-scale structures. Morphology-guided encoding and joint-embedding predictive supe
sfd44838453.summary: AeroJEPA is a two-stage joint-embedding predictive framework for regional surface PM2.5 aerosol forecasting that fuses sparse observations with meteorological data.

sd4d5ca4430.title: Aggregation Rules Induced by KL-Regularised Preference Dynamics on Networks
sd4d5ca4430.description: arXiv:2611.30941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study agents that each align a model to their own preference data while observing one another, and ask which aggregation rule the resulting policies implement. Each round, an agent takes one KL-regularised step. The step involves a reference that the agent is penalised for leaving and a challenger against which its responses are compared, and each of the two may be the agent's own or an average over the agents it observes; attention need not be reciprocal. Aggregating the reference makes the rule collective. Agent $v$ then has the weight $\pi_v/\beta_v$, its share of the network's long-run attention divided by its temperature. If, in addition, the challenger is fixed, the agents concentrate on the response maximising $\sum_v(\pi_v/\beta_v)
sd4d5ca4430.summary: Researchers study which aggregation rules emerge when agents align models to their own preference data via KL-regularised steps while observing one another on a network.

s7ab15d9780.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
s7ab15d9780.description: arXiv:2611.30962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. Existing benchmarks provide a strong foundation, but fixed difficulty ceilings, limited feature coverage, and coarse aggregate scores progressively weaken their discriminative and diagnostic value. We introduce CUA-SEE, a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence. It disentangles three objectives: benchmark evolution expands evaluation scope through cohort-calibrated difficulty and coverage growth; diagnostic evolution increases resolution through agent-conditional capability-boundary probes; and verifier evolution improves precision by translating changing requirements into state-grounde
s7ab15d9780.summary: CUA-SEE is a closed-loop evaluation environment that co-evolves tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence to keep computer-use agent benchmarks discriminative.
s7ab15d9780.why: Addresses saturating static benchmarks for computer-use agents, useful for teams measuring agent progress more reliably.

s795273a4d1.title: MedUIGym: Evaluating and Training GUI Agents for Clinical Workflows
s795273a4d1.description: arXiv:2611.30983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automating clinical workflows requires vision-language agents that can navigate dense graphical user interfaces (GUIs) in electronic health records (EHRs) and execute precise actions, yet many medical agents still rely on text or structured tool calls. In this work, we introduce MedUIGym, a scalable interactive environment comprising 15,739 tasks from 17 benchmark sources across six clinical task families for training and evaluating clinical GUI agents. In MedUIGym, agents perceive EHR states from screenshots and execute mouse-and-keyboard actions, as well as a paired native-tool interface over identical clinical data. The environment verifies both final answers and required clinical actions, and supports parallel trajectory collection for tr
s795273a4d1.summary: MedUIGym is an interactive environment with 15,739 tasks from 17 benchmark sources for training and evaluating vision-language agents on clinical EHR graphical interfaces.
s795273a4d1.why: Provides a large training and evaluation environment for GUI agents in clinical workflows, relevant to healthcare AI builders.

sc86bedfd75.title: Triage Accuracy of Jev and Open-Weight System One Decision Models and Their Use for Early Emergency Recognition in Symptom-Assessment Applications
sc86bedfd75.description: arXiv:2611.31012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laypeople increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for triage advice, but LLMs answer in variable free text, which makes it hard to evaluate them for use in medical devices. Decision models, which assign a probability to each predefined triage category, may be easier to evaluate. To test their triage accuracy, we evaluated 16 decision models (14 open-weight, 2 proprietary) on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, yielding 163,728 total assessments. The best models triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly and agreed with an existing algorithm in 56.1% of real-world cases. They were more promising for recognising emergencies early: given only demographics, chief complaints, risk factors and red-flag answers, the best model reached a
