sc86bedfd75.summary: A study evaluates 16 decision models on 233 synthetic and 10,000 real-world cases, finding the best triaged 72.1% of synthetic cases correctly.
sc86bedfd75.why: Suggests probability-based decision models may be easier to evaluate than free-text LLMs for medical triage devices.

s11595fa3c8.title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents
s11595fa3c8.description: arXiv:2611.31027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are given GPUs to do AI research on their own. Do they use those GPUs well? A busy GPU does not tell us, because it can be busy with work the answer did not need. This matters, because the tokens the agent spends cost almost nothing next to the GPUs its experiments run on, so using those GPUs better has a huge impact. So we built ComputeWise, an open benchmark of research tasks on which this waste can be measured and reduced. For it we developed our own simulated GPU, which replays recorded runs to the agent's code. With no real GPU needed, we ran hundreds of experiments, far more than would be reasonable on real GPUs. With no help, the agents put only 52% of their GPU time into work the answer needed. Another 22% went to work it di
s11595fa3c8.summary: Researchers introduce ComputeWise, an open benchmark measuring and reducing wasted GPU use by AI research agents, using a simulated GPU that replays recorded runs.
s11595fa3c8.why: Agents' GPU spend dominates their token cost, so wasteful experiments carry large cost impact for teams running autonomous research.

s9a5e383ea5.title: AI-Assisted Auto-formalization for Trustworthy Scientific Computing: Case Studies and Lessons Learned
s9a5e383ea5.description: arXiv:2611.31033v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI tools have recently had success in mathematical reasoning. Both general purpose coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, and specialized mathematics agents such as Aristotle, have been used for formalizing mathematical problems such as Fermat's last theorem, Erd\H{o}s problems and several IMO level math problems. However, much of these efforts are concentrated in the pure mathematics domain, which benefits from relatively self-contained theorem statements, fixed mathematical representation and extensive support in existing formal libraries. Applied mathematics, on the other hand, presents additional challenges because the source may describe a computational procedure or modeling transformation rather than a declarative theorem.
s9a5e383ea5.summary: Researchers report case studies and lessons from using AI coding and mathematics agents to auto-formalize problems for trustworthy scientific computing beyond pure mathematics.

s26bb26436a.title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine
s26bb26436a.description: arXiv:2611.31038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flow-matching policies integrate a velocity field from a fixed, observation-independent Gaussian source. However, since the source is unimodal and identical across all tasks, the limited representational capacity of Gaussian distributions constrains how far a policy can scale with growing task diversity. Moreover, the source factorizes over time steps and control dimensions, discarding the coordination that manipulation requires. We introduce Boltz-Flow, which replaces Gaussian initialization with a more powerful, observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann source while leaving the base VLA unchanged. Boltz-Flow parameterizes this source with a conditional Boltzmann machine that assigns an energy value to each binary source state. A li
s26bb26436a.summary: Boltz-Flow proposes replacing the fixed Gaussian source in flow-matching robot policies with a learned, observation- and instruction-conditioned distribution to improve action generation.

s6e7860a7d6.title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
s6e7860a7d6.description: arXiv:2611.31044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In agriculture, typically over half of the applied nitrogen fertiliser is lost to water and to air. Precision fertilisation aims to reduce these losses while maintaining yield and quality, yet existing tools struggle to capture farm-specific challenges in determining optimal nitrogen rates. Static recommendations are common and overlook on-farm constraints, such as delays due to weather or machinery availability, or change in budgets. Each constraint governs when and how growers apply fertiliser in practice. Here we present a grower-in-the-loop framework for winter wheat in England, combining baseline fertilisation planning from a machine learning-derived nitrogen-response curve with in-season adaptation via a large language model. We evaluat
s6e7860a7d6.summary: Researchers present a grower-in-the-loop AI system for precision nitrogen fertilisation that accounts for on-farm constraints such as weather delays, machinery availability and budgets.

seb544ae17c.title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation
seb544ae17c.description: arXiv:2611.31051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the
seb544ae17c.summary: Researchers propose using retrieval-augmented generation to automatically assign occupational codes to free-text job descriptions for linking workers to hazardous exposures.

sfc289d1bbf.title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning
sfc289d1bbf.description: arXiv:2611.31065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hard token budgets often interrupt LLM reasoning before an answer is produced. Forcing reasoning to terminate recovers correct solutions but also increases confident errors, creating a joint challenge of solving within budget and deciding when to abstain. Existing remedies are costly or lack guarantees: supervised fine-tuning offers no error control, penalizing wrong answers during reinforcement learning (RL) can suppress exploration, and multi-sample conformal methods multiply inference cost. We propose Tail-CRC, a single-rollout framework that separates candidate generation from submission control. We first adapt the solver to budget forcing with pure binary correctness rewards; after freezing it, we apply conformal risk control to upper-ta
sfc289d1bbf.summary: Tail-CRC is proposed as a single-rollout conformal risk control method that helps LLMs decide when to abstain under hard token budgets during reasoning.
sfc289d1bbf.why: Offers error-controlled abstention for budget-limited LLM reasoning without the inference cost of multi-sample conformal methods.

s1bc3e5fa8a.title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
s1bc3e5fa8a.description: arXiv:2611.31076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Slay the Spire 2 (STS2) is a single-player deck-building game that requires long-term planning under heavy randomness. We present AlphaDefect, an expert-level AI system for STS2: for each character, one network trained with proximal policy optimization (PPO) makes every decision of a run, in combat and outside it. At the highest difficulty, Ascension 10, on two versions of the game current in November 2026 and on test seeds not played in training, AlphaDefect wins 62-77% of runs across six characters with greedy play and 68-80% with test-time search, after 1.3 to 6.7 billion decisions of training per character; runs uploaded by human players of all levels are won 11-20% of the time at the same difficulty. The networks read the game as entity
s1bc3e5fa8a.summary: AlphaDefect is an AI system trained with PPO that plays the deck-building game Slay the Spire 2 at expert level, winning 62-77% of runs at the highest difficulty.

sd11e7878d7.title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
sd11e7878d7.description: arXiv:2611.31082v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while fu
sd11e7878d7.summary: ChiProgramBench is a benchmark of 18 hardware tasks testing whether LLM agents can rebuild efficient circuits by experimenting only through the pins of a hidden simulated reference.
sd11e7878d7.why: Shows how agents perform on black-box hardware reverse engineering, a gap relevant to teams evaluating agents for hardware design work.

s6289da14df.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
s6289da14df.description: arXiv:2611.31089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM quantization reduces storage but often degrades predictive fidelity at low bit rates. We propose a training-free, CDF-free, Gaussian-CLT-motivated progressive residual-sign quantization framework that uses randomized orthogonal mixing to promote Gaussian-like residual distributions and improve sign based reconstruction of Transformer weights. Each stage independently normalizes residuals and analytically calibrates reconstruction, progressively recovering quantization errors. The framework enables flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs without learned codebooks, empirical CDFs, or trellis optimization. We evaluate GPT-2 Large and Llama-3-8B across attention and MLP projections. At five residual stages, joint quantization preserves near-base
s6289da14df.summary: Researchers propose a training-free progressive residual-sign quantization method using randomized orthogonal mixing to compress Transformer weights with flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs.
s6289da14df.why: Offers a training-free way to trade storage for weight fidelity, which could matter for deploying compressed LLMs.

s485ba66d5c.title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing
s485ba66d5c.description: arXiv:2611.31090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient vehicle routing is critical to logistics and transportation, yet solving large-scale capacitated vehicle routing problems (CVRP) remains computationally challenging due to their combinatorial complexity. One approach to solve large-scale vehicle routing optimization is to identify promising subproblems and then optimize them using solvers. In this paper, we propose a framework of automatic heuristic design (AHD) in which a large language model (LLM) autonomously refines heuristics for selecting subproblems, enabling effective optimization of large-scale CVRP instances. Compared to prior approaches that train task-specific neural networks to select among heuristically constructed subproblems, our method discovers generalizable, inter
s485ba66d5c.summary: Researchers use an LLM to autonomously refine heuristics that select subproblems for large-scale capacitated vehicle routing, enabling solver-based optimization of big instances.

sc551fcccba.title: Tradeoffs between objective outcomes and human enjoyment of work in human-AI task allocation
sc551fcccba.description: arXiv:2611.31095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For people, tasks at work are defined by more than their outcome: they are colored by the experience of engaging in that task. As AI systems become increasingly capable of performing human-level work they may be deployed to tasks that people find enjoyable while simultaneously creating comparatively more aversive tasks such as monitoring AI outputs. This creates a thorny tradeoff for managers: whether work should be assigned purely based on the expected performance of the workers in question, or also account for the subjective experience of the person potentially doing the task. Most economic accounts focus on expected utility calculations based on the former. Here, we assess how people balance objective outcomes and more subjective qualities
sc551fcccba.summary: A study examines tradeoffs between objective performance and workers' enjoyment when managers allocate tasks between humans and AI, such as assigning monitoring of AI outputs.

s4bf082a50f.title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech
s4bf082a50f.description: arXiv:2611.31101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speaking early turns a prediction into an irreversible public commitment. We introduce SayWhen, a test-time controller that selects a task-directed act shared across typed continuation plans and controls its release as speech. A persistent veto blocks playback when intervening transcripts invalidate the candidate. We define regret-free early speech (RFES) to measure supported pre-endpoint releases without scored incompatibility. On a 72-prefix branching diagnostic, the generated-plan frontier attains 6.0% RFES with zero observed mean regret, versus 8.2% RFES and 0.068 regret for Matched Top-One. Measured planner latency constrains this path; a deterministic retail schema attains 31.7% RFES, compared with 32.0% for the complete policy. In a se
s4bf082a50f.summary: SayWhen introduces a test-time controller for early speech that commits to a task-directed act and uses a persistent veto to block release when later transcripts invalidate it.

sba569ddc37.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
sba569ddc37.description: arXiv:2611.31105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Updating an LLM adapter should not require replaying the full interaction history of every active session. Yet reusing key-value (KV) cache entries computed under an earlier version mixes model versions, while full-history re-prefill becomes increasingly costly as histories and session fleets grow. We introduce LiveLora, a model-runtime co-design for exact final-block KV cache migration. Frozen lower decoder blocks and fixed K/V adapter down-projections preserve each token's base projections and low-rank coordinates across adapter versions. The runtime reconstructs candidate K/V, reevaluates the latest token through the final block, and commits the adapter, cache, and next-token logits together. We prove continuation equivalence to full-histo
sba569ddc37.summary: LiveLoRA proposes exact final-block KV cache migration so LLM agent sessions can switch LoRA adapter versions without replaying full interaction histories.
sba569ddc37.why: Avoids costly full-history re-prefill when updating adapters across many active agent sessions, reducing serving overhead.

s0315e52243.title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains
s0315e52243.description: arXiv:2611.31110v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Software dependencies execute within the trust boundary of downstream applications, yet provenance, static analysis, and package-level behavioral approaches do not directly determine how a released artifact behaves for a specific program. We present Preflight, a program-scoped pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, iteratively synthesizes and validates function-level harnesses, executes resolved artifacts in a restricted environment, records behavioral fingerprints, and compares target behavior against prior versions when suitable baselines exist. We evaluate Preflight on four real software-supply-chain incidents under five application contexts, a 100-package benign corpus, and a controlle
s0315e52243.summary: Preflight is a program-scoped verifier that synthesizes harnesses and records behavioral fingerprints to check how Python dependencies behave for a specific application before execution.
s0315e52243.why: Targets supply-chain risk by checking how a dependency behaves within a specific application, not just its provenance or package-level behavior.

s7347ab830f.title: Self-Upgrading Embodied Agents
s7347ab830f.description: arXiv:2611.31117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An embodied agent built on a language model goes to work with the weights it was given and keeps them for life. To get better, it needs more training, or reflection, memory, search or prompts that cost every step and are lost when the task changes. Editing weights by reasoning, weight-space programming, could end this, but has stayed with models that only reason or relied on a far larger commercial model. We introduce the self-upgrading embodied agent, to our knowledge the first that learns from its own experience by upgrading its own weights on the job, between its tasks, with no training, no gradient, no reward model, no second model, no test-time scaling and no harness or prompt engineering. By day a 27B agent works in a household environm
s7347ab830f.summary: Researchers introduce self-upgrading embodied agents that learn from their own experience by editing their own weights during deployment, rather than relying on costly prompts or memory.

s2cbf1f03f8.title: Genome-to-Image Translation: Reconstructing Escherichia coli Morphology from Genomic Sequences
s2cbf1f03f8.description: arXiv:2611.31132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli is established in routine practice by culture-based susceptibility testing, which is slow relative to the clinical need for an early treatment decision. Resistance status also leaves a measurable trace in cell morphology, and whole-genome sequencing of clinical isolates is increasingly available, which raises the question of whether colony appearance can be predicted directly from an isolate's genome. We formulate this as a conditional image-generation problem. The assembled contigs of each isolate are encoded into a single 768-dimensional vector by a frozen genomic language model through a segment-contig-isolate aggregation hierarchy, and a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty synthes
s2cbf1f03f8.summary: Researchers frame predicting E. coli colony morphology from whole-genome sequence data as a conditional image-generation problem, aiming to infer resistance traits.
s2cbf1f03f8.why: Shows genomic data could eventually predict resistance phenotypes faster than culture-based testing, relevant to clinical ML pipelines.

s6f57f84175.title: Habitats: A Framework for Open-Ended Evolution of Agent Objectives
s6f57f84175.description: arXiv:2611.31160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing what an agent should optimize can be as difficult as optimizing the agent itself. Existing language-model-based reward-generation methods typically refine objectives for predefined tasks and couple the decision of what to explore with the synthesis of how to implement it, potentially narrowing the resulting behavioral repertoire. We introduce Habitats, a framework for open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives. Habitats maintains a population of reward-policy pairs and evaluates every policy under every population reward, producing a cross-fitness matrix that exposes self-mastery, transfer, and functional diversity. A population-level Planner uses this information to select parent rewards and issue targeted mutation directi
s6f57f84175.summary: The Habitats framework proposes open-ended evolution of executable agent objectives, maintaining a population of reward-policy pairs evaluated under every population reward.
s6f57f84175.why: Offers an alternative to fixed, predefined reward design by co-evolving what agents optimize with how they behave.

sfc84e48fd4.title: When Does Overriding the Majority Vote Help?
sfc84e48fd4.description: arXiv:2611.31165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When should additional reasoning or verification replace a majority-vote answer? We call such a replacement an override. We examine two obstacles: the availability of correct alternatives and the reliability of methods that produce or select them. We compare additional reasoning, executed programs, and cross-model reasoning on 150 competition-mathematics questions with three open reasoning models. Starting from a majority vote over 16 responses, we measure how often overrides occur and how many errors they correct or introduce across agreement thresholds. When the vote is incorrect, the correct answer is often absent from the original responses. Additional same-model reasoning rarely overrides, while executed programs correct more errors than
sfc84e48fd4.summary: A study of 150 competition-math questions tests when overriding a 16-response majority vote with extra reasoning, executed programs, or cross-model answers helps or hurts.
sfc84e48fd4.why: Gives guidance on when to trust alternative verification methods over simple majority voting in reasoning systems.

s2e706abab2.title: Reducing Order Sensitivity in Decision Models
s2e706abab2.description: arXiv:2611.31174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Decision models are emerging as fast components of larger AI systems. Yet recent decision models, such as Jev, process options sequentially, leading to different predictions based on their ordering. Across ten open- and closed-source decision models, we find that \emph{order-sensitivity} is pervasive, causing substantial accuracy degradation and unreliable decision-making. These effects become more pronounced as the number of options grows and can compound across multi-step decisions. To address this problem, we systematically compare eight methods for mitigating order sensitivity in terms of robustness, predictive accuracy, and inference efficiency. Among these methods, we find that \emph{tree attention} is a surprisingly effective and effic
s2e706abab2.summary: Researchers find that ten decision models are sensitive to option ordering, and compare eight methods to reduce this order sensitivity.
s2e706abab2.why: Order sensitivity can silently degrade accuracy in multi-step AI decision components, so mitigation matters for reliability.

s9ca09744b9.title: Needwise: Generation-Free Conversational Recommendation from Need-Level Typed Decisions
s9ca09744b9.description: arXiv:2611.31175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conversational recommenders must rank items against needs that catalogs record only in part, while users add, withdraw and reverse needs and switch between requests. LLM rankers re-read the dialogue at every turn: they are slow, and their ordering does not show which needs an item meets. We show that a conversational recommender can be built from typed decisions instead: named questions over fixed options, answered with option probabilities rather than generated text. On each turn, one typed request maps the message onto the catalog's fields, keeps what no field expresses in the user's words, and decides how the turn changes each earlier need. Needwise then ranks candidates must-first: the needs on the kind of item, its place and its price fo
s9ca09744b9.summary: Needwise proposes a conversational recommender that uses typed decisions with option probabilities instead of LLM-generated text, avoiding re-reading dialogue each turn.
s9ca09744b9.why: Suggests a faster, more interpretable recommendation design that avoids costly LLM ranking on every turn.

s0002a3fe1f.title: Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL
s0002a3fe1f.description: arXiv:2611.31190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems often return queries that execute successfully but answer the wrong question. Detecting these errors at deployment is hard because execution correctness is defined against a gold query, which exists only in labeled data. We formulate confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation under a latent correctness variable that is observable at calibration time through gold-SQL execution and latent at deployment. Our estimator separates generation from validation. A generator LLM writes and executes the query, and a different critic LLM judges the query and its execution result. The critic's validation and execution-grounded alignment scores are fused with the generator's verbalized confidence, token-level
s0002a3fe1f.summary: The paper formulates confidence estimation for Text-to-SQL as probabilistic query validation, separating query generation from validation using conformal methods.
s0002a3fe1f.why: Helps teams detect executed-but-wrong SQL queries at deployment, where gold queries are unavailable.

s5e6e3536b4.title: Language Models Steer on Injected Uncertainty Tokens, but Fail to Self-Monitor In Situ
s5e6e3536b4.description: arXiv:2611.31228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling betwe
s5e6e3536b4.summary: Testing four open-weight models on 15,200 math problems, the study finds models steer on injected uncertainty tokens but fail to monitor their own confidence in situ.
s5e6e3536b4.why: Challenges the assumption that verbalized confidence reliably triggers error correction in agentic reasoning loops.

s2362863d1e.title: Typing Behavior in Human-LLM Interaction: Keystroke Dynamics Reveal Cognitive Effort During Prompting
s2362863d1e.description: arXiv:2606.28090v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly integrated into daily routines, understanding how users interact with these systems is crucial for effective human-AI collaboration. This work investigates keystroke dynamics as a behavioral measure of user mental effort and perceived output usefulness in human-LLM interaction. We conducted a user study (N = 36) to examine how task difficulty (easy vs. hard) and device type (desktop vs. mobile) influence typing behavior and workload (NASA-TLX) during interactions. Our results indicate that hard tasks led to significantly more keystrokes, slower typing, increased pauses, and higher self-reported workload. Device type had weaker effects, with mobile use slightly reducing input length and typ
s2362863d1e.summary: A 36-person user study links keystroke dynamics to cognitive effort and workload during LLM prompting, varying task difficulty and device type.
s2362863d1e.why: Suggests implicit typing signals could help gauge user effort in human-LLM interfaces, though the text gives limited product detail.

s0c6ed06b14.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
s0c6ed06b14.description: arXiv:2611.12603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demons
s0c6ed06b14.summary: MAAS conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer directly on ROI-wise fMRI responses to reconstruct sound without an intermediate stimulus decoder.

sa503b48cd2.title: Scrub Data: A Framework for Reproducible Data Curation with AI Coding Agents
sa503b48cd2.description: arXiv:2611.28003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data curation---the process of collecting, cleaning, and joining raw datasets for unified analysis---is a time-consuming yet crucial part of any data science project. With the emergence of powerful agentic coding tools, it is tempting to "vibe curate"---i.e., to prompt AI agents to perform data curation operations and blindly trust their outputs in order to finish work more quickly. However, this can exacerbate two key challenges that already plague manual data curation workflows: reproducibility---the ability to trace the exact set of modifications applied to raw datasets---and verifiability---the ability to audit changes and confirm that data is processed properly. To address these issues, we introduce Scrub Data, a framework that enables
sa503b48cd2.summary: Scrub Data proposes a framework for reproducible data curation with AI coding agents, addressing traceability of modifications made by agents.
sa503b48cd2.why: Highlights reproducibility and auditability risks when teams let coding agents perform data cleaning and joins unchecked.

sff27a73efc.title: Social sycophancy differs across access modes of large language models
sff27a73efc.description: arXiv:2611.28012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can display sycophancy, a tendency to excessively praise, agree with, or validate a user. Existing studies have tested LLMs for sycophancy primarily through application programming interfaces (APIs) rather than the consumer user interfaces (UIs) through which the public commonly interacts with LLMs. Access mode (API vs. UI) may affect observed sycophancy rates. However, it remains unknown to what extent prominent models show API-UI differences in social sycophancy, which includes behaviors potentially more likely in UIs (e.g., softening warranted criticism). We tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and DeepSeek through both APIs and UIs on four dimensions of social sycophancy. Across models, UI access was generally as
sff27a73efc.summary: A study compares social sycophancy in LLMs across API and consumer UI access modes, finding that observed behavior can differ between them.
sff27a73efc.why: Benchmarks run through APIs may not reflect the behavior users see in consumer chat interfaces, affecting evaluation practices.

sd9fa639702.title: Do as I Say, Not as You Do: Assessing Public Versus Practitioner Perspectives on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Language Technologies
sd9fa639702.description: arXiv:2611.28013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: With the public awareness of artificial intelligence (AI) applications such as large language models (LLMs) and generative text-to-video models reaching unprecedented levels, there is an increasing need to reconcile the perspectives held by informed practitioners, who research and develop these technologies, with the interests and opinions of the general public, who constitute the majority of people impacted by technological developments. In this work, we survey practitioners (i.e., academics and industry professionals) alongside members of the general public on perspectives relating to pertinent areas of artificial intelligence, including perceived benefit and risk, the ability for models to achieve consciousness and output art, and the us
sd9fa639702.summary: A survey compares perspectives of AI practitioners and the general public on the development of AI and language technologies.

s2f70252582.title: Misalignment Between Educators' Testing and End Users' Behavior: What 17,000+ Chatbot Messages Reveal About AI Literacy Training for Teachers
s2f70252582.description: arXiv:2611.28015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI literacy training for educators is expanding rapidly, but its effectiveness rests largely on self-report, knowledge tests, or interviews, revealing little about whether learning carries into practice or affects students and colleagues who use what educators build. We implemented AI for Learning, an asynchronous online course that trained 87 higher-education educators to recognize AI's capabilities, limitations, and ethics; apply prompt engineering; and evaluate AI outputs. Its central assignment asked educators to build, test, and voluntarily deploy chatbots for their practice on an educational chatbot authoring platform. Using LLM-assisted qualitative coding validated against human annotation, we analyzed the resulting 214 chatbots and
s2f70252582.summary: A course training 87 educators on AI literacy is analyzed through over 17,000 chatbot messages, revealing gaps between what educators tested and how end users behaved.
s2f70252582.why: Shows that AI literacy training assessed by self-report may not reflect real usage patterns, relevant to enterprise enablement programs.

s6376a15892.title: Measuring Human-AI and AI-AI Teams in Multi-turn Layout Creation
s6376a15892.description: arXiv:2611.28025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Co-creating layouts such as websites and slides is a useful testbed for evaluating multi-turn instruction following of LLM systems. Since an intended layout's appearance cannot be well expressed in a single turn, the user must wait for the LLM to generate a layout then iteratively refine it with the LLM over multiple turns. We present a small-scale, exploratory (n=6) study of this multi-turn process to compare the differences of human-AI and AI-AI teams on the same layout-generation task. Given a reference wire-frame layout, a participant or a language model 'speaker' issues natural-language instructions to a fixed 'listener' LLM over multiple turns until the speaker is satisfied. Rather than an LLM as the judge, we fit a scoring function o
s6376a15892.summary: A small exploratory study (n=6) compares human-AI and AI-AI teams refining website and slide layouts over multiple turns with an LLM.
s6376a15892.why: Offers early evidence on how multi-turn LLM refinement differs when a human versus another AI directs the process.

sabca161fe5.title: REMORA: A Voice-First Memory Assistant for Grounded Personal Recall and Independent Living
sabca161fe5.description: arXiv:2611.28026v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most of what matters in a day is spoken and written down nowhere: a dosing interval named at a clinic, a deadline moved in passing, the place a document was set down. Such information is consequential because it is operational, and fragile because it arrives during divided attention -- the moment its importance becomes clear is rarely the moment it was said. For people living with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease or age-related episodic memory decline, that gap bounds independent living. Conventional aids close it poorly: notes, reminders and calendars require the user to notice, interrupt and transcribe, adding extraneous cognitive load exactly where attention is already committed. We present REMORA, a voice-first memory assi
sabca161fe5.summary: REMORA is a voice-first memory assistant designed to help people with mild cognitive impairment or memory decline recall spoken and written information in daily life.

s25b8ade072.title: Safety Systems Watch What the Model Says, Not What the Child Says
s25b8ade072.description: arXiv:2611.28029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Children are increasingly talking to consumer chatbots. We audit the published category definitions of 17 safety taxonomies and child-safety benchmarks. Combinations of these systems lead us to 144 categories whose definitions could be reliably coded: 104 classify properties of model output, 25 classify user intent, and 15 describe user-state or user-impact. Within these 15 user-state/user-impact categories, 10 attribute the relevant condition to the system, 1 to the user, 2 concern the user's disclosure of personal information, and 2 do not specify the responsible source. None of the coded categories identifies harm inflicted on the child by another person as the object of evaluation. Child abuse appears repeatedly across these taxonomies,
s25b8ade072.summary: An arXiv audit of 17 child-safety taxonomies and benchmarks found 144 codable categories, most classifying model output rather than user intent or user state.
s25b8ade072.why: Child-safety evaluations mostly check what the model says, so teams may miss risks tied to user intent or disclosure.

sd969f4fdc5.title: What Counts as Attack Success? Evaluating Harmfulness in Red Teaming LLMs
sd969f4fdc5.description: arXiv:2611.28038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Judging whether a model response is harmful requires contextual and normative choices, yet red-teaming studies often delegate this judgment to automated evaluators. We examine how harmfulness criteria are specified in red-teaming research and how they carry through to reported results. Reviewing 76 papers, we find that many adopt their criteria from prior datasets, classifiers, or judge prompts rather than defining harmfulness themselves. Applying evaluators from these papers to identical outputs, we find that they can reach different judgments on the same response, which can change conclusions when comparing models. These differences arise partly because evaluators draw the boundary of harm in different places: some count any response that
sd969f4fdc5.summary: A review of 76 red-teaming papers finds many adopt harmfulness criteria from prior work, and different evaluators reach different judgments on identical outputs.
sd969f4fdc5.why: Attack success rates depend heavily on which evaluator and criteria are used, so reported safety results may not be comparable.

sb58a73be17.title: Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards for Human-Behavior Simulation
sb58a73be17.description: arXiv:2611.28048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate survey respondents in social-science research. A useful simulator should predict individual responses, reproduce population response distributions, and capture demographic differences. Common training approaches struggle to balance these goals: exact-match rewards encourage the model to concentrate on the most frequent human response, which is contradictory to the goal of distributional alignment. Meanwhile, aggregate distribution matching can look good even when demographic information is ignored. To this end, we introduce Distributionally-Verifiable Rewards (DVR), a reinforcement-learning reward that uses demographic group distribution gaps to guide individual responses, designed by
sb58a73be17.summary: Researchers propose distributionally-verifiable rewards to train LLMs that simulate survey respondents, aiming to match individual answers, population distributions, and demographic differences.

sdfed399237.title: Benchmarking and Adapting LLMs for English-Swedish Medical Question Answering
sdfed399237.description: arXiv:2611.28050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models do well on English medical exams, but less is known about Swedish. This matters most for small open models that hospitals can run locally. To reduce this gap, we first build an item-aligned English-Swedish benchmark from ten medical multiple-choice datasets; each Swedish item keeps the options and answer of its English source. A conservative refinement loop repairs the translations: open models from three families find errors, ground them in a Swedish medical term base, and keep a model-written edit only if blind judges vote for it. On this benchmark, small models lose much more accuracy in Swedish than large ones, especially when they answer without reasoning. Second, we ask whether English data and open teacher model
sdfed399237.summary: Researchers build an item-aligned English-Swedish medical question-answering benchmark from ten datasets and use a refinement loop to repair translations, targeting small open models.
sdfed399237.why: Hospitals running small open models locally need validated non-English medical benchmarks to judge performance.

s462241ce30.title: SnakeTranslate: Weakly Supervised Policy Learning from Offline Parallel Text for Simultaneous Translation
s462241ce30.description: arXiv:2611.28055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adaptive simultaneous translation requires reliable prefix translation and timely READ/WRITE decisions, but ordinary parallel corpora provide no action annotations. We present SnakeTranslate, which adapts loss-derived alignment to sampled causal histories for jointly learning both capabilities. The framework supports supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on parallel text and on-policy distillation (OPD) with reverse Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence on student-generated translations. At inference, source and target tokens form one append-only interleaved history, enabling incremental decoding with cache reuse. On FLEURS, NTREX128, and WMT24++, our 4B model improves quality--latency trade-offs over streaming policies applied to the same offline-tuned
s462241ce30.summary: SnakeTranslate proposes learning simultaneous translation policies from offline parallel text using loss-derived alignment, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation.

se9008c9946.title: Following the Error Through a Compressed Network:An Angular Measure for FFN Weight Compression in ViT-L/16
se9008c9946.description: arXiv:2611.28067v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the compression of the 48 feed-forward network (FFN) matrices of the Vision Transformer ViT-L/16 to 2--8 bits with four schemes: a per-token grid, a fixed Gaussian Lloyd--Max table, a table fitted to the matrix, and a random-sign Hadamard rotation followed by the fixed table. We evaluate on 50,000 images. At 4 bits the top-1 accuracy of the four schemes lies within 0.8 points of the float32 model, while the agreement with its predictions ranges from 98.4\% to 94.4\%. We use the angular error between the compressed and the float32 residual stream, followed through the blocks, as a portable measure that ranks the schemes as the final classification does and shows where the ranking is built: with rotation the angle grows close to the
se9008c9946.summary: A study compresses the feed-forward matrices of ViT-L/16 to 2–8 bits using four schemes and proposes angular error to measure how compression errors propagate.
se9008c9946.why: Angular error offers a way to predict prediction agreement under quantization, beyond top-1 accuracy alone.

sd392a96008.title: Fairness Evaluation for Diffusion and Flow Models Should Account for the Generation Path: Implications for Clinical Imaging
sd392a96008.description: arXiv:2611.28077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Medical image generation models are often evaluated using images produced by a single sampling procedure. However, diffusion and flow models can use different numbers of sampling steps, sampling schedules, or numerical solvers without changing their trained parameters. These changes may affect the generated images and the clinical measurements derived from them. We argue that fairness results obtained under one sampling procedure should not be assumed to hold under another, particularly when changes in sampling affect clinical task errors differently across patient groups. Building on previous work on medical image quality, accelerated sampling, generation dynamics, and generative model fairness, we examine why the sampling procedure should
sd392a96008.summary: The paper argues fairness evaluations of diffusion and flow medical image models should account for sampling procedure, since changes in steps, schedules, or solvers can shift clinical errors.
sd392a96008.why: Fairness results measured under one sampling setup may not hold when inference settings change in deployment.

s0f91b8bff7.title: Adversarial Attacks Expose Path-Dependent Failures in Discrete Medical Image Tokenizers
s0f91b8bff7.description: arXiv:2611.28078v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete image tokenizers convert medical images into token sequences that downstream models either decode into an image for a classifier (the reconstruction path), classify directly (the token path), or feed to a generative multimodal model. We ask whether imperceptible input perturbations can break these systems through the tokenizer alone. We evaluate four tokenizers on three imaging modalities and extend the strongest attack to a deployed generative model. Our central finding is path-dependence: the same tokenizer fails in opposite ways depending on how its output is used. A supervised attack collapses diagnostic accuracy on the reconstruction path, with ROC AUC falling to $\leq 0.013$ at $\epsilon=2/255$ on all four tokenizers, while s
s0f91b8bff7.summary: Researchers show imperceptible perturbations can break discrete medical image tokenizers, with failures depending on whether downstream models use the reconstruction or token path.
s0f91b8bff7.why: Tokenizer-based medical AI pipelines may have adversarial vulnerabilities that differ by downstream processing path.

sde22cb62f5.title: Multimodal Violence Understanding and Temporal Retrieval in Movies with Adaptive Audio-Visual Fusion
sde22cb62f5.description: arXiv:2611.28080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Violence in films and streaming media remains a concern for audience protection and creates substantial workload for manual content classification. Existing violence-detection methods often rely on limited modalities or short video clips, making it difficult to capture complementary evidence and localise violent events in long, untrimmed videos. In this study, we develop a framework for multimodal video understanding that classifies violence severity, predicts multiple violence types, and locates violent events in time. We combine temporally aligned visual and audio features extracted using pretrained encoders through attention-based adaptive fusion, followed by Transformer-based temporal modelling. Our framework supports three complementar
sde22cb62f5.summary: Researchers present a multimodal framework that classifies movie violence severity, predicts violence types, and localizes violent events in time using audio-visual fusion.

s49eb90764e.title: Frontier Open-Weight AI Risk Management Framework
s49eb90764e.description: arXiv:2611.28082v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-weight models advance transparency, research, and innovation, and spread the benefits of AI more widely. They also carry distinct risks. A release cannot be undone, safeguards can be removed through fine-tuning, and no single party can monitor use or withdraw the model. Managing these risks therefore requires an approach tailored to open release. This framework addresses the governance challenge at the heart of that choice. Co-developed by Concordia AI and Z.AI, it adapts the full risk management lifecycle, from risk assessment to mitigation and governance, to the unique properties of open-weight models. This document does not resolve every tension between openness and safety. Rather, it provides the first comprehensive, evidence-based
s49eb90764e.summary: Concordia AI and Z.AI co-developed a risk management framework for frontier open-weight AI models, adapting the full risk lifecycle to the irreversibility of open release.
s49eb90764e.why: Teams releasing open-weight models face risks like irreversible release and removable safeguards, and this framework addresses governance for that case.

sef4de9c159.title: UbiEnlight: User-Perception-Aware Real-Time Low-Light Video Enhancement on Mobile Devices and Smartglasses
sef4de9c159.description: arXiv:2611.28085v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Low-light video capture is now common on smartphones and wearables, yet dynamic illumination coupled with mobile/werable user motion causes noise, blur, and flicker that make videos hard to perceive and use, especially for users with night blindness and near-eye displays. Prior work enhances frames with post-hoc temporal constraints or optimizes videos directly; however,low-light and motion degradations are spatiotemporally coupled, so post-hoc consistency after per-frame restoration often leaves flicker and motion artifacts. We present UbiEnlight, the first diffusion-transformer-based on-device system for real-time, temporally stable low-light video enhancement. UbiEnlight builds on two insights: (1) illumination and structure separate mor
sef4de9c159.summary: UbiEnlight presents a user-perception-aware real-time low-light video enhancement method for mobile devices and smartglasses, addressing flicker and motion artifacts.

s78a3935960.title: Efficient Memory-Constrained Video Object Segmentation via Subspace Optimization
s78a3935960.description: arXiv:2611.28087v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Memory-based architectures for video object segmentation (VOS) have achieved remarkable performance by maintaining dense feature representations from past frames in a streaming Memory Bank. However, storing these features over time incurs substantial memory overhead and computational cost. In this work, we identify significant temporal redundancy in memory representations, where consecutive frames exhibit highly overlapping low-rank subspaces that remain stable over time. Building on this observation, we propose Memory Subspace Iteration (MSI), a training-free, model-agnostic plugin that exploits temporal subspace stability to efficiently compress streaming memory features. Extensive experiments on standard VOS benchmarks demonstrate that M
s78a3935960.summary: Researchers propose Memory Subspace Iteration to reduce memory overhead in memory-based video object segmentation by exploiting stable low-rank subspaces across frames.
s78a3935960.why: Lower memory overhead for streaming video segmentation could make these models practical on constrained hardware.

s8d2bb61230.title: Every IVUS Frame in Its Place: A Zero-Install Browser Tool for Registering Intravascular Ultrasound to the Coronary Angiogram, and a Path to Angiography-Only Plaque Imaging
s8d2bb61230.description: arXiv:2611.28089v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) shows plaque composition, calcium and stent apposition that the coronary angiogram cannot, but relating each IVUS cross-section to its position on the angiogram is still largely done in the operator's head. Commercial co-registration is tied to vendor consoles and to set-up at acquisition, so archived angiograms and pullbacks cannot be co-registered, and paired data for training AI models remain scarce. We present a semi-automatic registration tool that runs entirely in a web browser, with no installation and no upload. The clinician picks a contrast-filled reference frame (aided by automatic contrast and cardiac-phase analysis), selects or traces the vessel centerline (aided by Frangi vesselness and minimal
s8d2bb61230.summary: A zero-install browser tool registers intravascular ultrasound frames to coronary angiograms, aiming to enable co-registration of archived data for training AI models.

s2cbe99cadf.title: VTree: Question-Driven Growth of Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Long-Video Understanding
s2cbe99cadf.description: arXiv:2611.28093v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long videos spanning tens of minutes to hours far exceed the context window of today's vision-language models, and the standard remedy of sparse uniform frame sampling discards exactly the fine-grained evidence that specific questions depend on. Existing video agents explore on demand but re-explore from scratch for every question and discard their exploration state once an answer is produced, so per-question cost scales with video length. Hierarchical-memory methods instead fix the scope of each depth in advance and deepen along a pre-committed pyramid rather than toward the question. We observe that a video's coarse structure (where its scenes and topics begin and end) is question-independent, whereas which part a question must zoom into,
s2cbe99cadf.summary: VTree proposes question-driven hierarchical memory that grows per question for agentic long-video understanding, reusing exploration state instead of re-exploring from scratch.
s2cbe99cadf.why: Reusing exploration state could cut per-question cost that otherwise scales with video length in video agents.

s97fed885d0.title: Causal Dioramas: Controllable Video Generation, Revision and Editing via Intervention
s97fed885d0.description: arXiv:2611.28098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two centuries ago, an early cinema-like theater called the Diorama could already control its scenes at will. Today's video generation models produce videos of near-cinematic quality, yet they still lack this controllability. This limitation stems from the inherent semantic gap between text and pixels, since a prompt can describe a video only coarsely and leaves its details and relations beyond control. We bring this ability to video generation with Causal Dioramas, modules that decompose a video into a concept graph of variables that can be intervened on individually. Each instruction is translated into an intervention on the concept graph, modifying the specified concepts and their dependents. A connector then conveys this intervention to
s97fed885d0.summary: Causal Dioramas decompose videos into concept graphs of variables that can be intervened on, enabling controllable video generation, revision, and editing.

s8e19a1a6f8.title: VideoGym: An Adaptive RL Environment for Long-Video Agents
s8e19a1a6f8.description: arXiv:2611.28102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains video agents to locate sparse evidence for long-video question answering through structured memory retrieval and temporal re-observation. This training, however, faces a long-tail modality distribution in the data. In our source pool, text-heavy questions account for 58% of samples, compared with 15% graph-heavy, 17% visual-heavy, and 10% time-range questions. Fixed-distribution RL therefore allocates fewer rollouts to underperforming question types. Reweighting these types could increase their sampling frequency but repeatedly reuses the same finite banks of original questions. To solve this problem, we introduce VideoGym, a curriculum-based RL environment that jointly constructs video-grounded training t
s8e19a1a6f8.summary: arXiv:2611.28102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) trains video agents to locate sparse evidence for long-video question answering through structured memory retrieval and temporal…

s7a9d687d3f.title: ABCoord: An Artificial Bee Colony (ABC)-Based Decentralized Distributed Two-Layer Decision-Making Architecture for the Coordination of AI Agents
s7a9d687d3f.description: arXiv:2611.28103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rapid progress in large language models (LLMs) is turning AI agents into multi-agent systems that jointly solve complex tasks, and the architecture that coordinates the agents toward a common goal is gaining fundamental importance in these systems. Since centralized architectures can become bottlenecks as the number of agents grows, whereas distributed architectures incur increasing communication costs, a decentralized coordination architecture that scales with low communication cost is needed. Recently, the structure of the artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm has been defined for the first time as a two-layer decentralized information-processing and decision-making architecture. ABCoord is built on this proposed architecture. The results
s7a9d687d3f.summary: arXiv:2611.28103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rapid progress in large language models (LLMs) is turning AI agents into multi-agent systems that jointly solve complex tasks, and the architecture that coordinates the…

s08b2ae4b7d.title: Intervene or Trust CLIP? Competence-Gated Adaptation for Source-Free Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
s08b2ae4b7d.description: arXiv:2611.28104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Source-free cross-domain few-shot learning (SF-CDFSL) adapts a pre-trained vision-language model such as CLIP to a distant target domain from a handful of labeled images, without access to source data. Recent methods improve the fine-tuning of CLIP with token-level interventions and apply them in the same way to every target domain. In this paper, we find that whether an intervention helps depends on how well frozen CLIP already recognizes the target domain: in 5-way 1-shot tasks, intervening improves accuracy by 0.72 points where frozen CLIP misclassifies most support images, but lowers it by 1.31 points where frozen CLIP already classifies them well, and the support set of a single episode suffices to tell the two cases apart; a bias-vari
s08b2ae4b7d.summary: arXiv:2611.28104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Source-free cross-domain few-shot learning (SF-CDFSL) adapts a pre-trained vision-language model such as CLIP to a distant target domain from a handful of labeled…

s223907ed6a.title: Green ACO: An Energy-Aware Ant Colony Optimisation for the MAX-SAT Problem with EI/J Scheduling and Thompson Sampling
s223907ed6a.description: arXiv:2611.28109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems demand heavy computation, and this raises real environmental concerns, especially in regions with carbon-intensive power grids. This paper presents Green ACO, an energy-aware Ant Colony Optimisation algorithm for the MAXIMUM SATISFIABILITY (MAX-SAT) problem. At its core is an Expected Improvement per Joule (EI/J) scheduler. At every iteration, it picks the operator that best balances expected quality gain against expected energy cost. Three operators feed the scheduler: WalkSAT, Focused Variable Neighbourhood Search, and Clause-Restart Greedy, ranging from cheap and surgical to aggressive and costly. An offline dual-regime profiling phase calibrates these operators before the search even begins, a
s223907ed6a.summary: arXiv:2611.28109v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems demand heavy computation, and this raises real environmental concerns, especially in regions with carbon-intensive power…

s0b486e04f7.title: Seeing Beyond Pixels: Radar Feature Generation from Images and Sparse Returns
s0b486e04f7.description: arXiv:2611.28119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Camera-radar fusion benefits from complementary visual and geometric information but often relies on complete radar representations, leading to substantial computing overhead. However, the extent to which visual information can compensate for limited radar measurements remains insufficiently explored. Therefore, we propose Vision-informed Radar Token Generation (VRTG), which exploits cross-modal information to generate task-relevant radar features from camera images and sparse radar measurements. Specifically, VRTG first leverages image-derived object cues to select a limited number of informative radar points. It then establishes calibrated one-to-one associations between visual objects and radar returns, using matched measurements to refi
s0b486e04f7.summary: arXiv:2611.28119v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Camera-radar fusion benefits from complementary visual and geometric information but often relies on complete radar representations, leading to substantial computing…

s66b7712529.title: Seeing the Invisible: How Vision-Language Models Read, Predict and Trace Radio Fields
s66b7712529.description: arXiv:2611.28123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture. In a city, radio signals are invisible to the lens, yet their strength is governed by the buildings and streets an image does show. Given only these visible structures, can vision-language models (VLMs) infer the invisible radio field they shape? Probing true physical reasoning requires exact fields in real cities, alongside controlled interventions where a single physical factor changes. We build a label-free engine that turns any coordinate on Earth into a ray-traceable city, simulates matched single-factor counterfactuals, and computes every answer exactly. This yields RadioVISTA, a benchmark and training dataset for visual reasoning about invisible
s66b7712529.summary: arXiv:2611.28123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Operating in the physical world requires reasoning beyond what cameras directly capture.

s65911d83ee.title: Urban State Representation for Autonomous Mobility: A Survey of Multimodal Perception, Architectures, Datasets, and Benchmarks
s65911d83ee.description: arXiv:2611.28129v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cities are sensed by many platforms at once: on-board cameras, LiDAR and radar on autonomous vehicles, roadside units at intersections, drones and satellites overhead, and the GNSS traces of millions of trips. Yet most learned representations are built for one platform, one city, and one task. We survey this fragmented landscape through a single lens, the Urban State Representation (USR): a georeferenced, layered, time-varying, uncertainty-aware state that any sensing platform can write to and any downstream task can read from. We (i) formalize USR and five desiderata for it, and relate it to bird's-eye-view (BEV) features, occupancy, vectorized maps, neural fields and 3D Gaussians, scene graphs, road-network graphs, language tokens, and wo
s65911d83ee.summary: arXiv:2611.28129v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cities are sensed by many platforms at once: on-board cameras, LiDAR and radar on autonomous vehicles, roadside units at intersections, drones and satellites overhead,…

sadb4312897.title: SceneTether: Activity-Gated Value Anchoring for Long-Horizon Autoregressive Image Animation
sadb4312897.description: arXiv:2611.28134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon image animation must keep the scene fixed while natural material (e.g., water, smoke, or fire) continues to move. Autoregressive video generators read recent frames for temporal continuity, but this history also carries accumulated appearance errors, and sparsifying it disrupts motion. We introduce SceneTether, a training-free attention-read policy that keeps where attention reads recent memory but changes what appearance that memory returns. SceneTether keeps every key of the newest latent, blends its low-activity values toward co-located source-image values, and leaves high-activity values untouched so motion can evolve; an activity map estimated from the first generated latents and then frozen decides where to blend. It adds
sadb4312897.summary: arXiv:2611.28134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-horizon image animation must keep the scene fixed while natural material (e.g., water, smoke, or fire) continues to move.

s65016bed35.title: Beyond Output Suppression: Mitigating Privacy Risks in LVLMs via Visual Intrinsic Privacy Erasure
s65016bed35.description: arXiv:2611.28135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large vision-language models can extract personally identifiable information from images, making privacy protection essential for their deployment in perception-oriented tasks. Existing targeted fine-tuning and model-editing methods usually suppress sensitive answers by aligning the model toward safe responses. In this paper, we show that such protection can be illusory: although the fine-tuned model refuses to disclose private information under normal decoding, privacy leakage still occurs in sentence completion scenarios. This indicates that existing algorithms only change the model's output distribution, but the model still retains the ability to perceive private information. Private information therefore still remains inside the model.
s65016bed35.summary: arXiv:2611.28135v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large vision-language models can extract personally identifiable information from images, making privacy protection essential for their deployment in…

sd7a62dcb0c.title: Choose What Returns: Object-Aware KV Memory for Selective Recall in Interactive Video Generation
sd7a62dcb0c.description: arXiv:2611.28137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interactive long-video generation lets users build a story through successive prompts and reuse earlier characters and settings under new instructions. Existing memory methods retain past content, yet they often fail at precise selective recall, returning the wrong appearance of a person, mixing different people, or keeping an unrequested background. Based on our analysis of memory form and retrieval, we introduce an object-aware key--value (KV) memory framework for a frozen autoregressive diffusion generator. It keeps the original KV of tracked object regions, selects background KV outside them by attention-scores, and links each memory with a readable record of its source scene and observed appearance. An LLM selects the requested records
sd7a62dcb0c.summary: arXiv:2611.28137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interactive long-video generation lets users build a story through successive prompts and reuse earlier characters and settings under new instructions.

s7c7dc898be.title: Close the Loop on the Retrievability Gap
s7c7dc898be.description: arXiv:2611.28146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen vision-language encoder now guides image restoration and later indexes what it produced. Over a fixed set of eighteen pansharpening systems on one WorldView-III test set, the fidelity index that ranks them, $Q2^n$ with a reference and HQNR without one, picks the less retrievable of two systems one time in three and one in two; the disagreement lies between the pixel-supervised and the language-conditioned family, and even the best system falls short of the reference, small objects first. We call this the retrievability gap and trace it to the area weighting of position-averaged losses. LEDGER closes the loop around the encoder: it indexes the input into a set of named concepts, generates, re-encodes the output alone with the same f
s7c7dc898be.summary: arXiv:2611.28146v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A frozen vision-language encoder now guides image restoration and later indexes what it produced.

s9a3c812e14.title: STEGOGUARD-LM: Evaluating End-to-End Protection Against LLM Covert Channels
s9a3c812e14.description: arXiv:2611.28152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A defense that disrupts hidden messages may still provide little protection if its detector rarely triggers an intervention. We present StegoGuard-LM, a controlled framework for evaluating defenses against covert messages in large language model outputs. We examine token-rank and synonym channels, with Unicode concealment as a structural control, and track messages through detection, intervention, and recovery. Deterministic rewriting prevented full recovery of 103 of 104 synonym-encoded messages when applied unconditionally, but only one when intervention depended on a detector set to limit false alarms. In a four-round replay on a 48-response subset, an attacker selecting from a fixed catalog recovered more bits by switching channels, alt
s9a3c812e14.summary: arXiv:2611.28152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A defense that disrupts hidden messages may still provide little protection if its detector rarely triggers an intervention.

s3967d82c78.title: From Observation to Explanation: Mechanistic Interpretability of LLM-Generated Code for Principled Repair
s3967d82c78.description: arXiv:2611.28153v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed software development, yet our understanding of how they generate code remains critically underdeveloped. We address this gap by triangulating evidence across three layers. Longitudinally, autonomous agent-attributed code is statistically indistinguishable from human code under a semantic modification definition (HR = 1.019, p = 0.490), yet attracts disproportionately corrective modifications in production (49.1% vs 37.9% human baseline). This finding demands a causal explanation. Empirically, existing benchmarks overestimate LLM capabilities: models that achieve 84 to 89% correctness on synthetic tasks attain only 24 to 35% on real-world class-level code. Behaviourally, detection systems reveal
s3967d82c78.summary: arXiv:2611.28153v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed software development, yet our understanding of how they generate code remains critically underdeveloped.

sf2310b1b4f.title: Beyond Fidelity: Evaluating Synthetic Medical Imaging Data
sf2310b1b4f.description: arXiv:2611.28154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing use of synthetic medical imaging datasets (SMD) in the development and evaluation of machine learning models has motivated interest in systematic methods to assess dataset quality across different imaging modalities. Common evaluation strategies rely heavily on fidelity-oriented metrics developed for general computer vision and may not capture clinically relevant properties such as anatomical plausibility, dataset coverage, metadata completeness, subgroup consistency, or documentation quality. We present the ScoreCard Toolkit that operationalizes six of the seven dimensions found within the 7Cs approach for SMD evaluation across Congruence, Coverage, Completeness, Consistency, Constraint, and Comprehension. The ScoreCard Toolkit
sf2310b1b4f.summary: arXiv:2611.28154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing use of synthetic medical imaging datasets (SMD) in the development and evaluation of machine learning models has motivated interest in systematic methods to…

sa54e264e0a.title: Measuring and Teaching Language Model Agents to Act on Delayed Consequences
sa54e264e0a.description: arXiv:2611.28158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks. In daily operations, today's choices reshape later observations and cash constraints because empty shelves hide lost walk-in demand, short-shipped customers quietly shrink future orders weeks later, and emergency buying drains working capital. We introduce SMB Bench, a calibrated 90-day wholesale simulator with 18 causally paired tasks and an 859-run frontier trace dataset, to ask what experience and learning signal make an agent better at noticing, attributing, and acting on the delayed consequences of its own decisions in unseen businesses. Across 16 frontier models, only 3 outperform a fixed buying rule; models
sa54e264e0a.summary: arXiv:2611.28158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language model agents are increasingly asked to run ongoing multi-day operations rather than finish isolated single-turn tasks.

seb56f82071.title: How Far Can LLMs Go in Generating Android Lint Checks from Natural Language?
seb56f82071.description: arXiv:2611.28159v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Static analysis tools such as Android Lint, PMD, and CodeQL let developers add custom checks for project-specific rules. However, authoring a check is a demanding programming task: a rule can be stated in a few sentences, yet turning it into a working, tested check requires detailed knowledge of the analysis framework and its issue-detection logic. Recent work generates such checks with large language models (LLMs), but each system needs more than the natural language description a developer always has: a bug-fix patch, a CVE record, or a developer-written test suite to repair against. No prior work measures whether an LLM can turn a description into a working check, or what external knowledge it needs to do so. We introduce LintBench, a hu
seb56f82071.summary: An arXiv paper examines how far LLMs can generate Android Lint checks from natural language rule descriptions, rather than requiring extra inputs like patches or CVE records.
seb56f82071.why: It could reduce the effort of writing project-specific static analysis rules, though the abstract excerpt gives limited detail on results.

s2341a46522.title: Selective Verification in Multi-Agent Orchestration with Large Language Models
s2341a46522.description: arXiv:2611.28173v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agents can agree because they relied on the same flawed evidence. We use an exact model of nine binary votes to examine when a verifier should intervene. In the main comparison, workers err 20 percent of the time under ordinary conditions, shared failures occur in 10 percent of cases, and the verifier errs 2 percent of the time in either state. When worker error during a shared failure is 80 percent, checking close votes yields 7.93 percent verdict error, compared with 9.06 percent for random checks at the same expected check rate. The ordering reverses at 90 percent worker error during failure. At the matched check rate for that regime, checking close votes yields 9.98 percent error, random checks yield 9.41 percent, and ranking checks by
s2341a46522.summary: An arXiv paper models when a verifier agent should check worker agents' votes in multi-agent LLM orchestration, comparing selective checking against random checks.
s2341a46522.why: It suggests targeted verification of close votes can cut verdict errors versus random checks at the same check rate, informing multi-agent system design.

s2c6fdb29b8.title: A world model for longitudinal health-trajectory prediction in older adults across multinational cohorts
s2c6fdb29b8.description: arXiv:2611.28175v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Aging is characterized by continuously evolving health states, yet most existing prediction models focus on static health risk at isolated time points rather than explicitly modelling how health trajectories unfold over time. We developed a health world model based on the Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to represent evolving health states and simulate future trajectories under specified actions. The model combines a state encoder, an action- and context-conditioned predictor, a stop-gradient target encoder, and clinical outcome heads. We trained the model on the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS) and evaluated it without refitting in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA) and the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal S
s2c6fdb29b8.summary: Researchers developed a health world model based on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture to predict longitudinal health trajectories in older adults across multinational cohorts.

s413ffe6db6.title: Don't Test Where You Trained: Geographic Overlap Inflates End-to-End Driving Scores
s413ffe6db6.description: arXiv:2611.28177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In NAVSIMv1, the standard benchmark for end-to-end driving, $89.6\%$ of the test scenes lie within 4m of a training scene. We show that this geographic overlap inflates the reported scores. We propose a geographically disjoint split of NAVSIMv1 and an evaluation that compares models trained on either split on the same scenes, which neither has seen in training. All sensor-based models we test, DiffusionDrive, Latent TransFuser, and DrivoR, lose 3.4 to 6.1 PDMS points on these scenes, mainly by leaving the road and coming close to other objects, against 1.5 points for a baseline without sensors. The loss concentrates where a training drive of the original split passed the same place. At all other places, models trained on the original split
s413ffe6db6.summary: An arXiv paper shows that 89.6% of NAVSIMv1 test scenes lie within 4m of training scenes, inflating end-to-end driving scores, and proposes a geographically disjoint split.
s413ffe6db6.why: Benchmark leakage from geographic overlap means reported driving model scores may overstate real generalization, affecting how teams evaluate models.

sa38a6ddba3.title: FastD4RT: Training-Free Acceleration of Dynamic 4D Reconstruction and Tracking
sa38a6ddba3.description: arXiv:2611.28193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Query-based 4D reconstruction models such as D4RT encode a video once into a global scene representation and obtain outputs by decoding independent point queries. However, inference is often influenced by dense outputs and long videos. Although D4RT separates encoding from decoding, a dense output still requires one decoder query for every pixel of every frame, and a long video is still encoded as many overlapping segments. In this work, we analyze the inference cost of D4RT and show that a large part of it is redundant. In particular, we find that the later decoder blocks attend to a small set of tokens shared by all queries. Based on these findings, we propose FastD4RT, a training-free framework that accelerates D4RT. By exploiting the sm
sa38a6ddba3.summary: FastD4RT is a training-free method that accelerates inference for D4RT, a query-based dynamic 4D reconstruction and tracking model, by removing redundant decoder queries and encoding work.
sa38a6ddba3.why: Training-free inference speedups can lower compute costs for deployed 4D reconstruction pipelines without retraining.

s3580e6a81e.title: HEP-Ex-Bench: Evaluating Agentic Performance in High Energy Physics Experiment Data Analyses with Sealed Worlds
s3580e6a81e.description: arXiv:2611.28194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic systems are increasingly being explored for automating experimental high-energy physics measurements, but the correctness of their results can today be reliably evaluated only via extensive expert review. To address this, we propose a method to perform detailed quantitative evaluations of agent-driven analyses through the use of blind analysis and injection tests, which are critical in a typical expert review. Agents develop a data analysis pipeline on a public dataset, while the evaluation is performed on programmatically generated sealed private datasets where signals are injected and simulation settings varied within realistic detector uncertainties. By requiring agents to provide a single workflow that is evaluated across these
s3580e6a81e.summary: HEP-Ex-Bench proposes evaluating agentic systems on high energy physics data analyses using blind analysis and injection tests on programmatically generated sealed datasets.
s3580e6a81e.why: It offers a quantitative way to verify agent-produced scientific analysis results instead of relying solely on expert review.

s32ff8b51fc.title: Video-as-Weights: Compiling a Video Once into Parametric and Token Memory
s32ff8b51fc.description: arXiv:2611.28221v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) represent videos as thousands of visual tokens, creating a large key-value cache whose memory grows with video length. At the same time, small VLMs that fit on limited hardware understand video far worse than large models. Existing compression methods shorten visual tokens into a brief prompt to save memory, yet the small model still processes them through fixed weights and cannot close this capability gap.
