To address both challenges, we introduce Video-as-Weights (VaW), which compiles a video once without seeing any question into the parametric and token memory of a frozen interpreter VLM. Specifically, a compiler VLM watches the video, and a single weight decoder jointly generates the interpreter's LoRA weigh
s32ff8b51fc.summary: Video-as-Weights (VaW) compiles a video once into parametric and token memory so small vision-language models can handle video better than with visual tokens alone.
s32ff8b51fc.why: It targets the growing key-value cache cost of long video in VLMs and the capability gap of small models on limited hardware.

scbc2309793.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
scbc2309793.description: arXiv:2611.28231v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Memory benchmarks built on question answering tell an agent which fact to recall. Workplace requests often leave that need implicit: to post an update in the team's channel, an agent must work out which channel from earlier interactions and use it in a tool call. We evaluate Memanto, a memory agent that ranks memories with an information-theoretic relevance score, on DolphinBench, which tests memory through 600 simulated workplace tasks, each validated as requiring memory. Running in the Hermes agent harness with GPT-6-Luna and at most 6 iterations per conversation, Memanto completes 503 tasks (83.83%). The strongest configuration reported by the benchmark's authors, Mem0 with GPT-5.6-Luna and up to 60 iterations, completes 424 (70.67%). Me
scbc2309793.summary: An arXiv paper evaluates the Memanto memory agent on DolphinBench, a set of 600 simulated workplace tasks requiring implicit memory use in tool calls.
scbc2309793.why: Implicit memory retrieval in workplace agent tasks is a practical gap for teams building agents that act on prior interactions.

sc3aa8dbad2.title: A Closed-Form Temporal Readout for Surgical Triplet Recognition
sc3aa8dbad2.description: arXiv:2611.28240v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Surgical triplet recognition requires identifying which instrument performs which action on which anatomical target, and following these interactions as they unfold over time. The task is challenging because several triplets can occur at once, their components span very different durations, and the evidence for an interaction is rarely complete in a single frame. We introduce STRIDE, a post-hoc temporal readout that adds temporal context to any trained recogniser. It averages the recogniser's features and logits over a few fixed temporal windows and combines them with the current frame through ridge regression, solved in closed form on a CPU. Applied as a plug-and-play readout to nine existing methods, STRIDE improves $AP_{IVT}$ in 24 of 27
sc3aa8dbad2.summary: STRIDE is a post-hoc temporal readout that adds temporal context to any trained surgical triplet recognizer by averaging features and logits over fixed temporal windows.
sc3aa8dbad2.why: It adds temporal context to existing recognizers without retraining, a low-cost option for video-based surgical analysis.

sa28d38b012.title: Learning a Rule Bank to Revise 3D CT Reports with Independent Evidence
sa28d38b012.description: arXiv:2611.28281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision--language models can generate fluent radiology reports from 3D chest CT scans, yet they may still omit abnormalities or misstate findings. Independent image analysis using models separate from the report model provides additional observations, but acting on uncertain evidence may introduce new errors. We propose an agent system that learns a revision policy represented as an executable rule bank for each report model. Inspired by experience banks, the agent proposes and refines rules using revision outcomes across development cases. During inference, the retained rules guide local edits using independent classifier predictions and quantitative image measurements without retraining the report model. Unedited sentences are preserved, a
sa28d38b012.summary: An agent system learns an executable rule bank to revise radiology reports generated from 3D chest CT scans using independent image-analysis evidence.

sa8a09442ca.title: HandXFM: Semantic-Structural Distillation for Hand Radiograph Foundation Models
sa8a09442ca.description: arXiv:2611.28283v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hand radiographs support diverse clinical tasks, including skeletal maturity assessment, rheumatoid arthritis scoring, abnormality screening, and anatomical localization, yet existing models are typically trained separately for each task and dataset. We present HandXFM, a domain-specific foundation model that leverages cross-modality knowledge for comprehensive hand X-ray understanding. HandXFM distills semantic priors from BiomedCLIP and structural cues from a chest X-ray Vision Transformer (ViT) through a unified alignment framework, integrating complementary medical knowledge in an interpretable way. After pretraining, HandXFM can be adapted to a range of musculoskeletal tasks, including bone age estimation, SvH score prediction, abnorma
sa8a09442ca.summary: HandXFM is a domain-specific foundation model for hand radiographs that distills semantic priors from BiomedCLIP and structural cues from a chest X-ray ViT.

sd41262e8ed.title: When Video Verifier Scores Mislead: Capability Assessment and Verifier Selection
sd41262e8ed.description: arXiv:2611.28287v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video verifiers judge whether a candidate answer or trajectory agrees with a video, and are themselves chosen by a score. We show that this score depends on two choices in the test, the type of negative and the judgment interface, strongly enough to reverse conclusions about what a model can do and which verifier to deploy. We separate the two with controlled constructions that have exact truth conditions: endpoint-matched negatives, wrong only in their internal states, and a truth-switch test, in which the same two candidates swap correctness between two videos. Under direct judgment, where the verdict is read from answer scores, models that reject a visibly wrong start fall to near chance against endpoint-matched negatives. When the frame
sd41262e8ed.summary: An arXiv paper shows that video verifier scores depend on negative type and judgment interface, strong enough to reverse conclusions about model capability and verifier choice.
sd41262e8ed.why: Verifier benchmark scores may mislead model and verifier selection, so teams should check evaluation design before deploying.

s2fbf3970a1.title: MRI-Driven Dual-Energy CT Synthesis via Conditional Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models for MRI-only Radiotherapy and Protontherapy
s2fbf3970a1.description: arXiv:2611.28294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides excellent soft-tissue contrast without ionizing radiation but lacks the electron-density information needed for radiotherapy dose calculation. Dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) improves tissue characterization and stopping-power ratio (SPR) estimation for proton therapy, but requires additional radiation exposure. We developed a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) to synthesize high- and low-energy CT (sHECT and sLECT) simultaneously from a single MRI scan. Retrospective paired MRI-DECT data from patients receiving head-and-neck proton therapy were used to train and evaluate a multi-decoder DDPM with SwinViT or ResUNet denoisers. Performance was compared with Pix2PixGAN and CycleGAN
s2fbf3970a1.summary: Researchers developed a denoising diffusion model that synthesizes high- and low-energy CT images from a single MRI scan for MRI-only radiotherapy and protontherapy planning.

s4a8621c7d8.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
s4a8621c7d8.description: arXiv:2611.28298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern language models (LMs) are post-trained and deployed as agents inside a "harness", but standard harness designs accumulate context that the neural network is forced to generalize to, making training for long-horizon tasks expensive and time-consuming. We study an alternative emerging path: training inherently neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which externalize and manage context programmatically to compose existing LM capabilities. We hypothesize that training around these harnesses can offer a better return on compute by enabling compositional generalization, as they can learn to decompose complex problems so that every observation their neural LM receives is locally in-distribution, even when the full task is novel. We find that harnesses
s4a8621c7d8.summary: An arXiv paper argues that training neurosymbolic LM harnesses, which programmatically manage context, may offer better compute returns for long-horizon agent training than standard harnesses.
s4a8621c7d8.why: Externalizing context management into programmatic harnesses could make training long-horizon agents cheaper, a design choice worth tracking.

s0044c64533.title: Learning a Food World Model That Predicts the Next State from Production Data
s0044c64533.description: arXiv:2611.28319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Food assembly robots pick ingredients from a pan, and every pick must deliver a target weight. We learn a world model of food picking from 61,773 production picks, labeled automatically by a camera and a scale (self-supervised learning). From the pre-pick heightmap of the pan on a 2.5 mm grid, the commanded pick action, the food and the utensil, the model predicts the post-pick heightmap and the picked mass with uncertainty. We evaluate the mass prediction on 12,294 held-out picks of nine foods. The production controller keeps each pick near its commanded target. The model's root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 10.93 g is 9% lower than that of the commanded target or of a per-food mean. This RMSE is 24% lower than that of the controller's inter
s0044c64533.summary: Researchers trained a food world model on 61,773 self-labeled production picks to predict post-pick pan heightmaps and picked mass with uncertainty for food assembly robots.
s0044c64533.why: Learning from automatically labeled production data shows a route to accurate robotic control in food assembly without manual annotation.

s76ce40f500.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs
s76ce40f500.description: arXiv:2611.28349v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Under structured outputs (JSON schemas, regexes, tool calls), speculative drafters do not see the grammar constraint and repeatedly propose invalid keys, delimiters, and indentation, while the grammar engine already knows which tokens must come next. We present Grammar-as-a-Draft (GaaD), which treats the grammar as a second drafter. Before each verify step, the scheduler merges the drafter's proposal with grammar-forced tokens into one draft row: matching tokens stay as GRAMMAR, the proposal is cut where it leaves the forced path, and forced tokens fill the rest of a row wider than the drafter's proposal. The verify step accepts GRAMMAR drafts without computing their logits, composing with any drafter with no new kernels or compilation on t
s76ce40f500.summary: Researchers propose Grammar-as-a-Draft, which merges grammar-forced tokens with speculative drafter proposals to yield more accepted tokens per step under grammar-constrained structured outputs.
s76ce40f500.why: Engineers serving JSON or tool-call outputs could get faster decoding by letting the grammar engine guide the speculative drafter.

sfc3fb9bddc.title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare
sfc3fb9bddc.description: arXiv:2611.28350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: JEPA world models are trained to predict logged transitions but used to compare counterfactual actions from one state. The logged behavior data show one action per state, and under a local linear approximation we prove the action response is unidentified along any direction the policy never varies within a state. We therefore supplement behavior data with measured outcomes of alternative actions from the same state. Our fork futures execute two actions from one restored state, and their outcome difference cancels the state term, identifying the action response on the sampled span. The resulting model, Fork-JEPA, matches predicted to measured differences, anchors the logged successor with behavior prediction, and adds a lookback head that ke
sfc3fb9bddc.summary: Researchers show JEPA world models cannot compare counterfactual actions from logged data alone and propose fork futures, executing two actions from one restored state.
sfc3fb9bddc.why: Teams training world models for planning need interventional outcome data, since logged single-action data cannot identify action effects.

sabcf4a42d8.title: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks on EEG Models
sabcf4a42d8.description: arXiv:2611.28354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) signals contain sensitive, subject-specific information, making models trained on them potential targets for membership inference attacks (MIAs). Although MIAs have been studied extensively in other domains, their applications to EEG models are relatively scarce, and the factors driving the vulnerability of EEG models to MIAs are not adequately understood. In this paper, we present a systematic empirical analysis of MIAs on EEG models using three datasets, seven model architectures, four attack methods, and two metrics. Results show that poor model generalization (large train-test loss and accuracy gap) is the strongest indicator of MIA vulnerability. Longer training and larger models also increase vulnerability
sabcf4a42d8.summary: A systematic empirical study analyzes membership inference attacks against EEG models across three datasets, seven architectures, and four attack methods.
sabcf4a42d8.why: Teams training models on sensitive neural data should understand which factors make them vulnerable to membership inference.

s70a149324f.title: Cross-Site Transformers Are Robust Heart Rate Estimators
s70a149324f.description: arXiv:2611.28366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Single-site heart-rate estimation from photoplethysmography (PPG) degrades sharply under real-world motion. Multi-site PPG provides a natural solution, but existing models fuse sites as generic sensor channels rather than exploiting their hemodynamic structure: each heartbeat propagates along the arterial tree, appearing across body sites as delayed and transformed copies of the same cardiac event. We propose the Cross-Site Transformer, which introduces a hemodynamically informed inductive bias by restricting multi-sensor fusion to cross-attention between PPG sites. On WildPPG, the largest in-the-wild benchmark available, our model establishes a new single-model state of the art, reducing error by 21% over the previous best and 35% over the
s70a149324f.summary: Researchers introduce the Cross-Site Transformer, which fuses multi-site photoplethysmography signals via cross-attention to estimate heart rate more robustly under motion.
s70a149324f.why: Wearable health engineers may gain more reliable heart-rate estimates during motion by modeling hemodynamic structure across body sites.

s81bce0c619.title: Taking the PULSE of Enterprise Workflows: Evaluating Persistent Project-State Understanding
s81bce0c619.description: arXiv:2611.28374v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Enterprise agents must maintain an up-to-date understanding of work distributed across heterogeneous artifacts, evolving over time, and unevenly visible to different collaborators. We formulate this challenge as persistent project-state understanding (PPSU) and introduce PULSE, a benchmark of 1,573 questions over 30 enterprise project histories. PULSE constructs deterministic, time-indexed project state and documented collaborator views from source-linked records, and evaluates three families of questions: open loops, project evolution, and view gaps. Across retrieval agents, graph- and memory-augmented retrieval, long-context, and oracle conditions, we find substantial headroom for current systems. Retrieval and extraction account for the
s81bce0c619.summary: Researchers introduce PULSE, a benchmark of 1,573 questions over 30 enterprise project histories for evaluating agents' persistent project-state understanding.
s81bce0c619.why: Builders of enterprise agents now have a benchmark for testing whether agents track evolving, unevenly visible project state.

s1ccd38b762.title: Targeted In-Context Poisoning of Tabular Foundation Models: An Empirical Study
s1ccd38b762.description: arXiv:2611.28396v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict the label of a query row conditioned on a context of labelled rows, without training on them. Drawn from operational data, the context becomes an attack surface. We study targeted in-context poisoning in its simplest form: an attacker with write access to the context's source places exact copies of a target row there with the wrong label. On 30 OpenML datasets for binary classification, one such poison row flips on average 53% (TabICL) and 65% (TabPFN) of the predictions correct without attack, and three poison rows flip almost all. The same copy with the true label flips almost none, and performance on the remaining rows hardly changes. Predictions flip by two routes: in TabICL, the target row's emb
s1ccd38b762.summary: An empirical study shows a single copied, wrongly labeled row in the context can flip many predictions of tabular foundation models like TabICL and TabPFN.
s1ccd38b762.why: Teams using in-context tabular models on operational data must treat the context source as an attack surface needing write-access controls.

sea3fafce82.title: When Can an AI Agent Serve as a Model of Human Psychopathology?
sea3fafce82.description: arXiv:2611.28405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models and AI agents are increasingly described in psychiatric terms, such as anxious, depressed, addicted or helpless. A recent study even proposed language models as experimental systems for psychiatry and as a platform for piloting psychological treatments. We ask when an experiment on an AI agent can provide evidence about a specified human psychiatric process. A claim to such evidence has three parts. Something changed in the agent, and the agent's history caused the change. Nothing other than a process shared with people explains that change. The change matches one theory of the human process and not that theory's rivals. Psychiatry and its neighbouring fields have an evidence standard for each part, from the diagnostic manua
sea3fafce82.summary: The paper argues that evidence from experiments on AI agents about human psychopathology requires specific conditions, such as shared processes with people, to be valid.
sea3fafce82.why: It offers little direct engineering guidance, though it cautions against treating agent behavior as evidence about human psychology.

s90a2c95808.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
s90a2c95808.description: arXiv:2611.28411v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-world evaluation of generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites with limited diagnostic coverage. We present ScaleEvals, a scalable reset-free protocol that evaluates policies through continuous physical play across a robot fleet. A VLM AutoPrompter generates scene-grounded tasks with difficulty estimates, language prompts, and skill tags, enabling performance analysis across diverse rollouts. A VLM AutoGrader assesses task progress, achieving 90.7% agreement with human graders. Scores are aggregated via a soft-win Bradley-Terry model, while tag-stratified ANOVA provides interpretable capability diagnostics. Across 3,000+ physical autonomous rollouts on DROID and YAM, ScaleEval
s90a2c95808.summary: ScaleEvals proposes reset-free autonomous play across a robot fleet, with VLM AutoPrompter and AutoGrader components, and reports 90.7% agreement with human graders.
s90a2c95808.why: Robotics teams could evaluate generalist policies at scale with less manual resetting and grading.

sadd625c2c8.title: WingBench: Benchmarking How AI Agents Search for Better Designs
sadd625c2c8.description: arXiv:2611.28418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Design search often uses cheap learned predictions to choose which candidates deserve expensive tests, but these tests can fail, especially on the unusual designs that optimization favors. We introduce WingBench, a multifidelity benchmark in which optimizers and AI agents design transonic wings with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) inside the search. They can query a learned aerodynamic surrogate and spend a fixed budget of sequential CFD evaluations, each returning a score or a failure type. WingBench grades the design each method recommends, reporting separately whether it receives a valid score and how good that score is. Using WingBench, we contribute a study of five baseline optimizers and a comparison of three AI agent methods, whic
sadd625c2c8.summary: WingBench is a multifidelity benchmark where optimizers and AI agents design transonic wings using learned surrogates and a fixed budget of CFD evaluations.
sadd625c2c8.why: It gives engineers a way to compare search methods and agents for design optimization under expensive, failure-prone simulations.

scdfe0186c8.title: Center-Aware Ordinal Learning for Prostate Cancer Grading from Histopathology Images
scdfe0186c8.description: arXiv:2611.28419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Prostate cancer grading from histopathology whole-slide images (WSIs) is complicated by the ordered nature of ISUP grades, class imbalance, and center-dependent variations in staining, tissue preparation, and scanning. Most weakly supervised methods treat grade groups as independent categories and may therefore learn representations that do not transfer reliably across institutions. We propose a center-aware ordinal learning framework that combines a pretrained pathology encoder with attention-based multiple instance learning. The framework uses an Earth Mover's Distance loss to account for ordinal errors, an ordinal supervised contrastive objective to align same-grade slides across centers while separating grades according to disease sever
scdfe0186c8.summary: Researchers propose a center-aware ordinal learning framework for prostate cancer grading from whole-slide images, combining a pathology encoder with attention-based multiple instance learning.

sb4b89dc258.title: When AI Should Not Decide: Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability in Automated Job Interviews
sb4b89dc258.description: arXiv:2611.28426v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to assess employment candidates, yet consistent interview scoring does not establish whether automated recommendations are supported by sufficient evidence. This study introduces the Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability Assessment (ESDSA), which combines criterion-level evidence classification, deterministic quotation traceability and stability checks across linguistic variants assessed as substantively equivalent. We evaluated four approaches (scoring-only, evidence-aware, traceability-based and integrated ESDSA v2) using 540 synthetic interview responses from 60 evaluated scenario families across Software Engineering, Customer Support and Operations. In held-out testing (216 responses),
sb4b89dc258.summary: The ESDSA framework assesses whether automated job interview recommendations are backed by sufficient evidence, combining evidence classification, quotation traceability, and stability checks.
sb4b89dc258.why: HR-tech teams deploying AI scoring need evidence sufficiency and decision stability checks, not just consistent scores.

s4a563d20ed.title: Lean Census: A Distributional Analysis of AI-Generated Lean Code
s4a563d20ed.description: arXiv:2611.28430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries with Mathlib through the distributions of simple statistics of their code. For each library we measure inline claims in proofs, proof length, how often each declaration is used, and design choices such as instances and private declarations, and we read each against the variation among Mathlib's own areas. The AI-generated libraries have more inline claims per theorem, longer proofs, fewer instances, and more private declarations than the human-written ones. We release the code for the analysis as a package, lean-census, at https://github.com/project-numina/lean-census.
s4a563d20ed.summary: A distributional analysis compares two human-written and four AI-generated Lean libraries against Mathlib, finding AI-generated code has more inline claims and longer proofs.
s4a563d20ed.why: Teams using AI to generate formal proofs get concrete code-style differences versus human-written libraries.

s9b70e314be.title: Decoding Frozen Vision Representations for Training-Free Few-Shot Pineapple Detection
s9b70e314be.description: arXiv:2611.28442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Few-shot object detection in agricultural imagery is hampered by dense vegetation, repeated patterns, and scarce annotations. We present a training-free detector that turns dense features from frozen visual foundation models directly into detections, without fine-tuning, a learned head, or external proposals: a whitened foreground-background direction estimated from annotated support images scores every query patch, and the score field is decoded with an adaptive threshold and support-derived geometry. We also test whether predicted relative depth can be fed directly to RGB-pretrained frozen encoders. On aerial pineapple imagery, the detector outperforms PET-DINO and GeCo2 at every evaluated support size; at K=40, predicted depth alone reac
s9b70e314be.summary: A training-free few-shot pineapple detector turns frozen vision foundation model features into detections using a foreground-background direction from annotated support images.
s9b70e314be.why: Agricultural vision teams with scarce annotations may detect objects without fine-tuning or learned detection heads.

sf0b2e951df.title: Guidance-Induced Activation of Score Estimation Errors in Diffusion Models
sf0b2e951df.description: arXiv:2611.28451v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) combines conditional and unconditional score estimates to steer diffusion sampling. The weighted-solenoidal component of each score error has no instantaneous effect on the evolution of its corresponding reference density. Because the guided density in CFG generally differs from both reference densities, the combination of these solenoidal components can affect the evolution of the guided marginals. We call this mechanism guidance-induced error activation. Using a weighted Helmholtz-Hodge decomposition, we identify the activated error field, quantify its magnitude, and characterize when it vanishes. At fixed noise time, the activated error field varies continuously with guidance strength. Its weak first-order
sf0b2e951df.summary: The paper identifies a mechanism, guidance-induced error activation, by which classifier-free guidance can amplify score estimation errors in diffusion sampling.
sf0b2e951df.why: Engineers tuning guidance scales in diffusion models should know that solenoidal score errors can shift guided marginals.

sdc9e7821c6.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series
sdc9e7821c6.description: arXiv:2611.28465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Irregular time series are recorded at nonuniform times and are often queried at other times: between observations, after the last one, or on a regular grid. Continuous-time models answer such queries by integrating latent dynamics, and time-aware attention models answer them by revisiting the observation tokens. We introduce HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that writes an irregular history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates. Masked self-attention first exchanges content among the observations; the updated values are then contracted against kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features and solved through a regularized Gram matrix, so the retained coefficients define a function that is read at any t
sdc9e7821c6.summary: HiPPO-FM is an attention operator that writes irregular time series history into a rank-M function space, enabling queries at arbitrary time coordinates.
sdc9e7821c6.why: Time-series modelers handling irregular sampling can query observations at any time without integrating latent dynamics.

s89d98bdecf.title: Automated Safety Analysis for Agentic Workflows
s89d98bdecf.description: arXiv:2611.28469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM applications are increasingly built as agentic workflows: programs that combine model calls, external tools, and control logic to act autonomously on a user's behalf. Because these workflows execute real-world actions, logical flaws in how a workflow is wired can cause severe harm in deployed systems. Unlike prompt injections or malformed API calls, these workflow bugs stem from defects in the workflow's design, yet no existing tool can statically validate workflow logic across frameworks prior to deployment. We present Apsis, a static safety analyzer that detects workflow bugs before deployment. To operate across frameworks, Apsis lifts framework-specific code into a common intermediate representation (IR). This IR models a workflow as
s89d98bdecf.summary: Researchers present Apsis, a static safety analyzer that checks agentic LLM workflow logic for design flaws across frameworks before deployment.
s89d98bdecf.why: Workflow wiring bugs can cause real-world harm, and this offers a pre-deployment static check that existing tools lack.

scdd18b7367.title: PAMS: Preconditioned Activation-Metric Subspace for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-tuning
scdd18b7367.description: arXiv:2611.28476v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Zeroth-order (ZO) optimization provides a computationally efficient approach to fine-tuning large language models (LLMs), but conventional methods typically rely on isotropic perturbations that ignore the anisotropic structure of neural-network parameter spaces. We introduce Preconditioned Activation-Metric Subspace (PAMS), a ZO optimization framework that uses forward-pass activation statistics to construct structured, layer-wise perturbation geometries without computing gradients or forming dense curvature matrices. PAMS tracks a low-rank approximation of the dominant activation subspace and its associated spectrum online, and uses the spectrum to softly reweight perturbation variance while preserving exploration in directions outside the
scdd18b7367.summary: PAMS is a zeroth-order fine-tuning method for LLMs that uses forward-pass activation statistics to build structured, layer-wise perturbations without computing gradients.
scdd18b7367.why: It proposes a more efficient way to fine-tune large models without backpropagation, though the abstract gives no benchmark results.

sa438f60d92.title: Don't Train It, Write It: An AI Agent Writes New Capabilities into Language Model Weights
sa438f60d92.description: arXiv:2611.28483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that an AI agent can write new capabilities into a pretrained language model by adding gated attention heads and MLP neurons inside its existing layers, without backpropagation and without fitting any weight to the answers of task examples. It has a budget of 50 model passes and sees no validation or test instance. Composed in one model, its modules for six BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) subtasks raise the normalized BBH score of Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct from 19.95 to 41.05 (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: at most 35.01) and that of Gemma-3-1B-it from 10.25 to 32.86. Against the unmodified model at the same precision, both composites leave the next-token distribution on 1,023,000 WikiText tokens unchanged (KL exactly 0), give identical answers on 15,845 it
sa438f60d92.summary: An AI agent adds gated attention heads and MLP neurons to pretrained language models without backpropagation, reporting BBH score gains for Qwen2.5-1.5B and Gemma-3-1B.
sa438f60d92.why: It suggests capabilities can be added to existing model weights with a small budget of model passes, a possible alternative to fine-tuning.

sf6964b43eb.title: Open Vision Banana: An Open Framework for Unified Visual Perception through Generation in RGB Space
sf6964b43eb.description: arXiv:2611.28489v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision Banana showed that a closed image generator, instruction-tuned to paint perception outputs as RGB images, becomes a generalist vision model. Does this carry over to \emph{open} generators, and if not, what fails? We answer with \textbf{Open Vision Banana (OVB)}, an open framework that adapts the 7B diffusion generator of Qwen-Image-2.1 into one instruction-driven model for metric depth, semantic, instance, and referring segmentation, using a single shared low-rank adapter and public data. Each task is a \emph{task contract} whose RGB encoder, instruction, and decoder share one specification and are checked before training. Studying 42 externally evaluated checkpoints from two 100k-update runs, six exact weight-space merges, and eight
sf6964b43eb.summary: Open Vision Banana adapts an open 7B diffusion image generator into one instruction-driven model for depth and segmentation tasks using a shared low-rank adapter.
sf6964b43eb.why: It shows that open image generators can serve as unified perception models, extending a closed-model result to open weights.

sd68c0f3bb7.title: SoK: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning
sd68c0f3bb7.description: arXiv:2611.28491v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distributed backdoor attacks split a trigger among several federated learning clients, so that the backdoor appears only in the aggregated model. Since DBA, a line of work has reported that such attacks are stronger, more persistent, and stealthier than a single attacker with the full trigger. We systematize this literature and test this belief. We code nineteen primary studies and fifteen papers that evaluate against DBA. The reported advantage is rarely measured against a complete trigger delivered by the same attackers, and none of the fifteen evaluations tests whether individual pieces remain effective. We then run 875 paired federated runs that separate adding attackers from splitting the trigger. In our image experiments, adding attac
sd68c0f3bb7.summary: A systematization of distributed backdoor attacks in federated learning finds the reported advantage over single attackers is rarely measured against a full trigger.
sd68c0f3bb7.why: It challenges prior claims about distributed backdoor attacks, which matters for teams assessing federated learning security.

scbee1bbcc9.title: When AI Performance Is Not Enough: Statistical Guardrails for Clinical Development
scbee1bbcc9.description: arXiv:2611.28497v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the operational and inferential landscape of clinical development, yet their adoption frequently outpaces the statistical scrutiny these methods demand. This commentary offers first-principles perspectives across four application domains: anomaly detection in clinical trial data, real-time monitoring and adaptive trial designs, biomarker-based enrichment, and virtual and digital twins. For each domain, we articulate the underlying inferential problem, the contribution of AI and ML relative to established statistical methods, and the risks that statisticians, data scientists, and clinical developers must actively manage. Across these domains, a unifying theme emerges: AI an
scbee1bbcc9.summary: A commentary argues that AI and ML adoption in clinical development outpaces needed statistical scrutiny, covering anomaly detection, adaptive trials, biomarkers, and digital twins.
scbee1bbcc9.why: It highlights statistical rigor requirements for deploying AI in clinical trials, though it offers no technical implementation details.

s783fbd0ef6.title: A generative framework for unified representations bridging electrophysiological and haemodynamic brain activity
s783fbd0ef6.description: arXiv:2611.28507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Electrophysiological and haemodynamic recordings resolve brain activity at complementary temporal and spatial scales, yet paired acquisition remains difficult to scale. We propose a generative framework that aligns paired multimodal recordings in a unified representation space and generates modality-specific haemodynamic responses from EEG. In paired cohorts, the framework generated fMRI BOLD and fNIRS haemoglobin responses that reproduced regional dynamics, cortical maps, functional connectivity and task structure. Generated BOLD followed Real BOLD time courses and cortical patterns, while Generated haemoglobin responses tracked task-evoked HbO and HbR dynamics. The framework enabled decoding across visual, motor-imagery and mental-arithme
s783fbd0ef6.summary: A generative framework aligns paired EEG and haemodynamic recordings in a shared representation and generates fMRI BOLD and fNIRS responses from EEG.

sbacd9595cd.title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
sbacd9595cd.description: arXiv:2611.28508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Understanding naturalistic brain activity requires going beyond the stimulus alone, as external inputs continuously interact with an individual's evolving brain state. A world model captures such dynamics in a latent state by inferring it from neural observations, predicting stimulus-driven evolution, and updating with new observations. However, existing brain world models fail to maintain a persistent latent state over time, and standard metrics of neural prediction accuracy cannot tell whether a model tracks an individual's brain state or relies solely on the stimulus. To directly test state inference, prediction, and updating, we introduce BrainStateBench, which evaluates a model's latent state through a frozen linear probe on whole-cort
sbacd9595cd.summary: Researchers propose learning world models of naturalistic brain dynamics that maintain a persistent latent brain state, and introduce evaluation metrics beyond standard neural prediction accuracy.

s1b3e6b7391.title: Digital Twins for Multi-Agent Systems: When to Trust, What to Change
s1b3e6b7391.description: arXiv:2611.28517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Digital twins of agent networks need to flag unreliable forecasts and help users choose interventions. Both decisions depend on what happens over several steps: an error can spread through the network, and an edit whose trajectory is easy to predict may still yield a poor collective outcome. We ask when information about error propagation improves failure detection and whether a learned twin can select effective network edits despite imperfect forecasts. We propose Propagation-Aware Validation for Networked Digital Twins (PAV-Twin). Its monitor combines Jacobian-based propagation features with recent errors and ensemble disagreement to estimate the risk that a forecast exceeds an error threshold. Its planner simulates each candidate edit an
s1b3e6b7391.summary: PAV-Twin is proposed as a propagation-aware digital twin for agent networks that flags unreliable forecasts and selects network edits.
s1b3e6b7391.why: It addresses monitoring and intervention in multi-agent systems where errors can spread across network steps.

s6fa2578958.title: General-purpose language models are neurosymbolic reasoners able to annotate proteins from sequence
s6fa2578958.description: arXiv:2611.28529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining the function of genes across the tree of life is one of the major challenges in biology. Generative AI approaches to this problem generally fall into two categories: language models trained on biological sequences that are able to predict structure and function from signals in those sequences; and generalist language models trained on text, that are able to reason about biological function symbolically. A default operating assumption is that protein language models do not perform well on symbolic tasks, and that generalist language models do not perform well on sequence tasks. However, a recent report showed that frontier generalist models perform surprisingly well on next-residue prediction tasks. We set out to explore whether
s6fa2578958.summary: The paper argues general-purpose language models can reason symbolically about protein function and annotate proteins from sequence, challenging the assumption that protein language models lack symbolic skill.

s692eff3601.title: From Reward Engineering to Data-Centric Reinforcement Learning for Effective Agentic Visual Tool Use
s692eff3601.description: arXiv:2611.28558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) increasingly use external visual tools to acquire evidence during reasoning, yet learning when to invoke these tools remains challenging. Existing tool-use reinforcement learning (RL) methods often rely on call-contingent rewards to encourage beneficial tool use, but such reward engineering can distort the task objective and lead to degenerate calling behaviors. We argue that effective tool-use learning requires identifying not merely which questions are difficult, but which failures are attributable to missing visual evidence and can therefore be corrected through tool observations. We propose AOVO, a data-centric framework that enables MLLMs to learn effective tool use through perception attributio
s692eff3601.summary: The paper proposes data-centric reinforcement learning for multimodal LLM visual tool use, targeting which failures are attributable to tool use instead of reward engineering.
s692eff3601.why: It offers an alternative to call-contingent rewards that can distort task objectives and cause degenerate tool-calling behavior.

sb9db19965f.title: SAFE-DRIFT: Data Selection for Supervised Fine-tuning with Controllable Off-Target Drifts
sb9db19965f.description: arXiv:2611.28560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose SAFE-DRIFT, a data-selection framework for supervised fine-tuning that improves a target capability while controlling unwanted drift in the model's other behaviors. We formalize this as a constrained optimization problem that maximizes alignment with the target gradient, subject to a budget on off-target drift which we quantify using the Fisher information of a reference distribution. Under this objective, the optimal, closed-form update is a damped natural-gradient step that downweights reference-sensitive directions. To estimate these high-dimensional gradients and work within the right geometry, we further derive a scalable algorithm that approximates the Fisher information and the target gradient in a shared low-dimensional s
sb9db19965f.summary: SAFE-DRIFT is a data-selection framework for supervised fine-tuning that improves a target capability while constraining off-target behavior drift using Fisher information.
sb9db19965f.why: It gives teams a way to limit unwanted regressions in other model behaviors during fine-tuning.

sca555569cf.title: Tool-to-Self: Internalizing Visual Tool Capabilities via Scaffolded Reinforcement Learning
sca555569cf.description: arXiv:2611.28564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly rely on external visual tools to access fine-grained visual evidence, but repeated tool execution incurs substantial inference overhead and deployment dependencies. Moreover, conventional tool-use RL can improve visual-task performance, yet the resulting tool gains are often unstable. Motivated by this, we propose Tool-to-Self (T2S), a tool-scaffolded reinforcement learning framework that turns external visual tools into temporary training scaffolds. T2S cold-starts tool-use ability and observation prediction from tool-repairable examples, then progressively anneals tool execution on a per-tool basis during RL. By combining answer-correctness and observation-consistency rewards with privileged on-p
sca555569cf.summary: Tool-to-Self proposes using external visual tools as temporary training scaffolds so vision-language models internalize tool capabilities and avoid repeated tool execution at inference.
sca555569cf.why: It aims to reduce inference overhead and deployment dependencies of visual tool use in VLMs.

s72ee28b093.title: MACE: Memory-Augmented Crop-Disease Evaluation of Frozen Vision-Language Models
s72ee28b093.description: arXiv:2611.28573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In plant phenotyping, crop disease diagnosis has traditionally relied on expert assessment of visible symptoms and on models tailored to specific crops or diseases, and both are difficult to scale across field conditions. Recent methods provide frozen vision-language models with source-grounded knowledge bases that summarize the typical symptoms of each disease but describe little of how symptoms vary across individual cases. We introduce MACE (Memory-Augmented Crop-Disease Evaluation), a training-free method that supplements the knowledge base with a memory of symptom descriptions paired with known disease labels. MACE matches a description of the query image against this memory and retrieves only text descriptions and disease labels, so t
s72ee28b093.summary: MACE is a training-free method that augments frozen vision-language models with memory to improve crop-disease evaluation across field conditions.

s9186ad877d.title: CLASP: Deciding Structure and Claims Before Decoding for Whole-Slide Pathology Report Generation
s9186ad877d.description: arXiv:2611.28576v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Whole-slide pathology report generation has advanced through stronger slide encoders, retrieved knowledge, and, recently, slide-level multimodal LLMs. However, these generators leave every report-level choice to the decoder: how long the report is, how it is organised, and which findings it states and where. On the standard PathText-BRCA benchmark, we find that these choices dominate n-gram overlap, as reports from the query's hospital selected without learning approach the state of the art, while decoders under-generate and fall back to the most frequent findings. We present CLASP, a decide-then-decode generator that makes these choices explicitly, once per slide. Before decoding, an Exemplar Structure Prior (ESP) takes the sentence plan a
s9186ad877d.summary: CLASP decides report structure, length, and claims before decoding to improve whole-slide pathology report generation on the PathText-BRCA benchmark.
s9186ad877d.why: It shows that report-level choices, not just decoding, drive quality in multimodal medical report generation.

s5b74a9f5e1.title: Right Verdict, Right Reason? An Execution-Grounded Study of Whether LLM Vulnerability Detectors Understand Vulnerabilities
s5b74a9f5e1.description: arXiv:2611.28584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to detect vulnerabilities, and their benchmark scores are often read as evidence that they understand the vulnerabilities they report. We test this reading against program execution. For 515 C and C++ functions from BigVul and PrimeVul whose vulnerability we reproduce with a proof of concept, we identify the line at which the fault occurs and the statements on which the faulting run depended. These facts ground a ladder of five tests, from telling a vulnerable function from its fixed version, through locating the fault and reacting to its removal, to judging execution-confirmed edits and predicting the outcome of a concrete run. Each test is paired with a baseline that needs no understandin
s5b74a9f5e1.summary: arXiv:2611.28584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to detect vulnerabilities, and their benchmark scores are often read as evidence that they understand the…

se648a24f01.title: AsyncMixVLA: Runtime Asynchronous Robot Policy Switching for Adaptation to Dynamic Environments
se648a24f01.description: arXiv:2611.28585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, enabling general-purpose robotic control. However, environmental perturbations, such as objects moving during execution, can undermine their reliability. Different policies exhibit complementary failures under mid-rollout perturbations, motivating selective switching between policies for recovery. Such switching can stall the robot during inference of the newly invoked policy or, if performed asynchronously, act on stale observations. We present AsyncMixVLA, an adaptive inference framework for proactive, asynchronous switching across heterogeneous VLA policies. A learned trigger balances recovery potential against intervention har
se648a24f01.summary: arXiv:2611.28585v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate visual observations and language instructions into robot actions, enabling general-purpose robotic control.

s5aec5d12ba.title: MedCoast: Semantic Abstraction of Reasoning Trajectories for Test-Time Biomedical Question Answering
s5aec5d12ba.description: arXiv:2611.28586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires multi-step reasoning under limited inference budgets. While test-time search methods such as Tree-of-Thought can improve reasoning performance, directly searching over free-form language is computationally expensive and highly redundant, as many reasoning trajectories contain semantically equivalent intermediate steps expressed in different surface forms. We introduce MedCoast, an offline-to-online reasoning framework that converts sampled chain-of-thought trajectories into a compact space for structured process supervision. Offline, we recursively cluster semantically similar reasoning steps under shared prefixes to construct an abstract reasoning tree that captures recurring clinical reasoning
s5aec5d12ba.summary: arXiv:2611.28586v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Biomedical question answering often requires multi-step reasoning under limited inference budgets.

sb64f6715e5.title: Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation
sb64f6715e5.description: arXiv:2611.28603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students. Recent studies report diminishing or even negative returns from teacher scaling. We hypothesize that these limitations arise in part from insufficient student capacity to absorb the teacher's knowledge. We therefore investigate loop and recurrent computation as a way to expand the student's effective capacity by modifying its computation graph while keeping the backbone parameter count fixed. Under teacher-forced KD during pretraining, weight-shared looping improves performance but retains teacher-size saturation, whereas cross-token recurrence avoids the observed reversal with larger teach
sb64f6715e5.summary: arXiv:2611.28603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students.

s542edbe6b6.title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage
s542edbe6b6.description: arXiv:2611.28607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost. Group-wise integer quantization stores every weight of a group at the same precision, although the input channels of a group differ in sensitivity. We present BITSHARE, a codebook-free weight format that keeps the integer grid and the dequantizer of group-wise quantization but varies precision within each group. Sensitivity-aware binning places the channels of each group into three bins at fixed positions, and static bit sharing with optimal bit-value allocation lets the less sensitive weights share their lower bits, each stored once per group or once per pair of weights. A sharing-aware version of GPT
s542edbe6b6.summary: arXiv:2611.28607v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost.

s2df3e11fde.title: Action-Conditioned Transition Irreversibility for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Reinforcement Learning
s2df3e11fde.description: arXiv:2611.28611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement-learning agents shape the observations they encounter; consequently, detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) states requires analysing action-conditioned trajectories rather than treating inputs as independent samples. We propose Action-Conditioned Transition Irreversibility (ACTI), a detector that evaluates forward and backward transition likelihoods, calibrates this comparison against the in-distribution profile at each timestep, and smooths the score over a short window, using no future information. We tested ACTI across six environments and fifteen detectors within OOD-RL-Bench, using the four anomaly mechanisms that qualified in every environment, with ten policy replicates per environment. All primary metrics are matched-tim
s2df3e11fde.summary: arXiv:2611.28611v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement-learning agents shape the observations they encounter; consequently, detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) states requires analysing action-conditioned…

saedb0e6310.title: Fast World Planner: Advantage-Aware Action-Chunk Policy for Online Planning
saedb0e6310.description: arXiv:2611.28616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is central to online planning for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL), but its iterative refinement incurs planning latency. Reducing refinement iterations often degrades performance, motivating stronger policy guidance learned from the planner. However, existing methods typically learn from the planner through action-level alignment, which does not directly capture the complete $H$-step planner proposal. Moreover, planner imitation leaves further target improvement to online refinement. To address these limitations, we propose FaSt World PlANner (SWAN), an advantage-aware MPPI-based MBRL framework that explicitly represents and improves the complete $H$-step planner proposal to improve po
saedb0e6310.summary: arXiv:2611.28616v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is central to online planning for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL), but its iterative refinement incurs planning…

s361e5c9579.title: LoopSeek: Decoupling System One Search from System Two Answering for Long Video Understanding
s361e5c9579.description: arXiv:2611.28635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long video question answering requires finding relevant evidence before reasoning over it. With a limited frame budget, single-pass frame selection can miss critical evidence, while adaptive search often relies on repeated text generation to decide where to look. We introduce LoopSeek, a framework that decouples evidence search from answer generation through a division of labor between a non-thinking System I and a generative System II. Our key insight is that search can be expressed as a sequence of small, typed decisions, allowing System I to find the evidence that System II needs. Four System I role agents navigate a tree of video windows and coordinate through probability outputs to select frames, assess evidence, and revise the search
s361e5c9579.summary: arXiv:2611.28635v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long video question answering requires finding relevant evidence before reasoning over it.

s184a4b645b.title: Make Position Uninformative: Exchangeable Self-Distillation Flattens the Lost-in-the-Middle Curve
s184a4b645b.description: arXiv:2611.28638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented language models answer well when the relevant document comes first or last and poorly when it sits in the middle. Some fine-tuning recipes lift the middle by lowering the start. We show how training contexts teach positional bias. With a uniform answer slot and shuffled distractors, the optimal reader ignores position. Building on this result, Exchangeable Self-Distillation (ExSD) trains a small adapter on shuffled contexts to reproduce the model's answer when it reads the answer document alone. It needs no gold answers and only a few thousand examples. On six models from 1.5B to 32B parameters, ExSD raises both average and worst-position accuracy against the frozen model, including on a held-out test split. In controlle
s184a4b645b.summary: arXiv:2611.28638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Retrieval-augmented language models answer well when the relevant document comes first or last and poorly when it sits in the middle.

sf73a5ed171.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
sf73a5ed171.description: arXiv:2611.28671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. MASSys executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, using five workload families spanning software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, and diagram generation. It records task qu
sf73a5ed171.summary: arXiv:2611.28671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation.

s6894f63443.title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation
s6894f63443.description: arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible research in music generation. We present PopMelodyGen, a copyright-aware platform for controllable pop-melody generation that combines rule-based synthesis with neural generation. Our approach first uses an expert synthesizer to produce large-scale labeled synthetic melodies from explicit musical knowledge and templates, providing scalable pretraining data with auditable provenance. A neural model is then pretrained on this corpus and adapted with a small licensed real-pop corpus to improve melodic naturalness while preserving controllability. The platform supports interactive
s6894f63443.summary: arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible…

s9368bf0ac1.title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills
s9368bf0ac1.description: arXiv:2611.28706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes. Existing workflows fragment evidence across versions, evaluation cases, and execution traces. We present SkillLens, an interactive human-LLM system for diagnosing and refining agent skills. A formative study with five developers and researchers identified challenges in prioritizing failures, reconstructing case-level evidence, and preserving context across revisions. SkillLens links performance changes, case transitions, skill diffs, invocation sequences, traces, and outputs in a recoverable workflow, while keeping model-generated explanations and refinements under human review. Through a
s9368bf0ac1.summary: arXiv:2611.28706v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on reusable skills, yet maintaining them requires developers to connect revisions with changes in behavior and task outcomes.

se2fcf3c27d.title: KMed-31B Technical Report
se2fcf3c27d.description: arXiv:2611.28719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics. We therefore divide medical training tasks into four categories by these two properties, train one specialist per category with a reward that its feedback supports, and integrate the specialists into a single student with M
se2fcf3c27d.summary: arXiv:2611.28719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware.

s5fd56e1839.title: AERIN: Aerial Instance Navigation with a Visual World Model
s5fd56e1839.description: arXiv:2611.28723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searching from high altitude and navigating to a target instance specified by a reference image is a common application for UAVs. In such tasks, high-altitude observations provide broad ground coverage for efficient search, but targets occupy fewer pixels, making instance verification and action selection more difficult. We present AERIN, a visual world model that uses action-conditioned prediction to guide the UAV toward the target while adjusting its viewpoint to obtain higherquality observations for subsequent instance verification. Highaltitude navigation requires fine-grained target details and scene context relevant to visibility, but repeatedly predicting dense visual representations of this information is computationally expensive.
s5fd56e1839.summary: arXiv:2611.28723v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Searching from high altitude and navigating to a target instance specified by a reference image is a common application for UAVs.

s7c3b944c2e.title: Seeing Is Not Planning: Spatiotemporal Planning and Plan Repair in Multimodal LLMs
s7c3b944c2e.description: arXiv:2611.28726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planning in a visual world means reading the layout, foreseeing how the state will change, and following the task rules all at once. When a plan fails, a model should also use what went wrong to fix it. We call these two abilities spatiotemporal planning and plan repair, and test them with Railbound-Bench. A model sees a railway puzzle, adds tracks under a budget, and submits one complete layout; a simulator then moves all cars at once and decides whether the layout works. After a failure, the model sees what happened and may submit a new layout, up to five attempts in total. On the 200-puzzle main set, the best of nine models solves 59.5% within five attempts, the next 39.5%, and the other seven at most 10.0%; a 1,000-puzzle extended set w
s7c3b944c2e.summary: arXiv:2611.28726v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Planning in a visual world means reading the layout, foreseeing how the state will change, and following the task rules all at once.

sc1c847998c.title: Entangle: Scaling Human-Video In-Context World-Action Models across Unseen Tasks and Contexts
sc1c847998c.description: arXiv:2611.28732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables foundation models to perform unseen tasks from context without parameter updates. In robotic manipulation, a human video provides the context that specifies how a task should be performed. However, scaling human-video ICL on world-action models (WAMs) faces two challenges: task-level human-robot pairs are not temporally aligned with robot actions, and standard action losses allow policies to rely on initial-scene or task-identity shortcuts rather than tracking the context. We present Entangle, an in-context world-action model that maps a single human video and current robot observations to future visual states and executable actions. To scale temporally aligned training data, we convert recorded robot video
sc1c847998c.summary: Researchers present Entangle, an in-context world-action model for scaling human-video context to robot manipulation on unseen tasks.
sc1c847998c.why: Shows a route to teaching robots new tasks from human demo videos without retraining, though the abstract alone gives limited detail on results.

s107d0734a7.title: Multimodal LLMs Know the Game but Assume the Real World
s107d0734a7.description: arXiv:2611.28745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models can state the rules of a video game, but do they apply them when they only see the game? We introduce RuleCraft, 1,240 image questions over 155 Minecraft rules with outcomes verified in the game engine, each asked in text, on the image with the game named, and on the bare image. Six widely used models know the rules and recognize the game, yet answer the bare image by real-world physics: naming the game raises their accuracy on rules where the game departs from reality by 8.2-19.8 points on a main set and by 33.8-52.7 on a hard stress-test set. Their errors pick the real-world outcome, the gap is largest where the game leaves a scene unchanged, and reasoning traces state the game's rule, then answer by reali
s107d0734a7.summary: Researchers introduce RuleCraft, a benchmark showing multimodal LLMs know Minecraft rules but default to real-world physics when shown only the game image.
s107d0734a7.why: Highlights that multimodal models may fail to apply domain-specific rules from images, a risk for visual agents operating in non-realistic environments.

s0e46118066.title: Pretraining Representation Lottery Determines Fine-tuning Generalization
s0e46118066.description: arXiv:2611.28777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large scale pretraining (PT) followed by fine-tuning (FT) is the central paradigm of modern deep learning, yet how PT shapes FT generalization remains poorly understood. We use a synthetic setup in which the ground-truth concept geometry of entities is known, as a controlled testbed to study how representational geometry affects model behavior and how PT representations determine FT generalization. We first show that models differing only in training seed can closely match in PT loss yet vary substantially in FT generalization. We hypothesize that a representational lottery underlies this phenomenon: the random seed dependent geometry formed during PT determines what FT can reach. We confirm this causally. First, injecting the ground-truth
s0e46118066.summary: A paper argues that pretraining representation differences, even from seed alone, largely determine how well models generalize after fine-tuning, using a synthetic testbed.
s0e46118066.why: Suggests fine-tuning outcomes can vary substantially between runs with similar pretraining loss, complicating reproducibility and model selection.

s4c9ef3f78b.title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding
s4c9ef3f78b.description: arXiv:2611.28800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages. Meanwhile, current datasets focus primarily on highway pavement defects, falling short of real-world inspection across diverse infrastructure components such as highway pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the Highway Infrastructure Inspection Progression Chain (HIIP-Chain), spanning Anomaly Detection, Anomaly Recognition, Condition Analysis, and Maintenance Resolution, and introduce
s4c9ef3f78b.summary: Researchers release HighwayVerse, a benchmark testing multimodal LLMs on sequential highway inspection tasks across pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage.
s4c9ef3f78b.why: Offers a multi-stage evaluation for applying MLLMs to infrastructure inspection, though the abstract gives no performance findings.

s2336b28038.title: Not All Directions Are Flat: Decomposed-Gradient Flatness for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting
s2336b28038.description: arXiv:2611.28802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many applications of novel view synthesis, such as augmented reality and robotics, can afford only a few input views, since dense capture is costly. With such sparse views, however, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) overfits the training views and degrades at unseen viewpoints. Among the approaches to this problem, flat-minima optimization treats the Gaussians as trainable parameters and steers training toward flat minima, which generalize better, by perturbing the Gaussians with random noise or along the training gradient. However, these perturbations ignore their direction relative to the other training views. Interestingly, we find that the direction of the perturbation determines whether it improves generalization. Specifically, we decompose
s2336b28038.summary: A paper proposes decomposed-gradient flatness to improve sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting, reducing overfitting to training views.
s2336b28038.why: Targets a practical limitation for AR and robotics where only a few input views are available, but the abstract gives limited detail.

s97ac85659a.title: PointNeXt Adapter Improved Model for BIM Component Defect Association under Construction Images and Design Model Attributes
s97ac85659a.description: arXiv:2611.28820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Construction site defect analysis increasingly requires linking field evidence to the correct BIM object, because a crack, spalling area, missing sleeve or misaligned support is useful for quality control only when it is connected with component identity, location, responsibility and design intent. This paper proposes a PointNeXt Adapter improved model for BIM component defect association under construction images and design model attributes. The method aligns site image crops, local point cloud patches, BIM component identifiers, geometry attributes, material categories, installation stage, inspection distance, viewpoint quality and source reliability tags into component level inspection windows. PointNeXt learns local geometry and deviati
s97ac85659a.summary: Researchers propose a PointNeXt Adapter model that links construction site images and point cloud patches to BIM components for defect association.
s97ac85659a.why: Could help construction tech teams tie field defects to the correct BIM objects for quality control, based on a research prototype.

sc95e0c5698.title: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design
sc95e0c5698.description: arXiv:2611.28823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large audio-language models (LALMs) have recently been shown to bypass audio CAPTCHAs designed around limitations of automatic speech recognition. To address this threat, we introduce reverse-capability verification, a general CAPTCHA framework that reverses the conventional human-easy, machine-hard relationship with respect to the physical ground truth. It selects challenges in which stable human perceptual limitations cause the human-reference answer to differ from the physical ground truth, while machine analysis tends toward that truth. Because the verifier accepts the human-reference answer, advanced solver capabilities and resulting improved recovery of the physical ground truth may instead strengthen the human-machine separation. We
sc95e0c5698.summary: Researchers propose reverse-capability audio CAPTCHAs that exploit human perceptual limits so that humans answer differently from physical ground truth while machines do not.
sc95e0c5698.why: Offers a defense against large audio-language models bypassing audio CAPTCHAs, relevant to teams running bot protection.

sfcc2512e40.title: Hidden Sensitivity in LLM Pre-training: A Dynamic System View
sfcc2512e40.description: arXiv:2611.28830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Large Language Model (LLM) pre-training, loss curves can conceal substantial instability, i.e., even small perturbations may lead to dramatically different predictions while leaving loss nearly unchanged. To investigate this phenomenon and reveal the underlying mechanisms, we first formulate LLM pre-training as a non-autonomous dynamical system that jointly evolves model weights and Adam optimizer states. Based on this formulation, we introduce a normalized sensitivity score in optimizer-relative coordinates to identify sensitive training checkpoints. sfcc2512e40.summary: A paper frames LLM pretraining as a dynamical system and introduces a sensitivity score showing small perturbations can change predictions while loss barely moves.
sfcc2512e40.why: Reveals hidden training instability that loss curves miss, which matters for teams monitoring large pretraining runs.

s0e0564f762.title: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems under Governance Opacity
s0e0564f762.description: arXiv:2611.28834v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the contemporary artificial intelligence ecosystem, foundation models are increasingly deployed under AI-as-a-Service (AIaaS) schemes characterized by high technical opacity, technological concentration, and limited external auditing capability over governance, training, and internal operational processes. Under these conditions, traditional ethical oversight approaches that focus exclusively on corporate governance or on internal model inspection become insufficient to ensure effective control over AI systems deployed in real-world contexts. This work proposes a pragmatic operational assurance framework inspired by Zero-Trust principles from cybersecurity, which shifts effective auditing efforts toward the application layer, where risk
s0e0564f762.summary: A paper proposes operational assurance methods for LLM-based systems deployed as AI-as-a-Service, where governance and training are opaque and external auditing is limited.
s0e0564f762.why: Addresses oversight of third-party foundation models that enterprises deploy without visibility into internal processes.

sbf287b64aa.title: KineState-SWAM: A Surgical World Action Model with Explicit Kinematics and Causal Interaction Dynamics
sbf287b64aa.description: arXiv:2611.28871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing surgical world models often leave implicit how instrument motion drives localized tissue responses and how interaction history informs subsequent actions. We introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model coupling action prediction and video generation through a persistent interaction state, separating kinematically determined instrument motion from learned scene evolution. A flow-matching policy predicts joint trajectories conditioned on interaction state, robot configuration, and task instruction. Kinematic Geometry Conditioning converts these trajectories into surface-motion tokens and spatially aligned instrument renderings using calibrated URDF kinematics. sbf287b64aa.summary: Researchers introduce KineState-SWAM, a surgical world-action model that couples kinematic instrument motion with video generation through a persistent interaction state.
sbf287b64aa.why: Suggests more structured surgical robotics world models, though the abstract provides no benchmark outcomes.

s4d6451c050.title: NAT: Scaling Causal Neural Action Tokenizers Across Embodiments
s4d6451c050.description: arXiv:2611.28873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Action tokenizers let robot policies treat control as autoregressive next-token prediction. As these policies are trained on larger and more diverse datasets, they will need a universal tokenizer that can encode actions from many embodiments and data sources, including ones it has not seen. We study action tokenization at scale, training on 49k hours of action data from real-world robots, handheld grippers, simulation, and humans. We introduce Neural Action Tokenizer (NAT), a causal tokenizer whose decoder lets actions be executed as their tokens are generated. Across four simulation benchmarks, NAT outperforms FAST and prior neural action tokenizers when tokenizing unseen robot embodiments, and in vision-language-action models it outperfor
s4d6451c050.summary: Researchers present NAT, a causal neural action tokenizer trained on 49k hours of action data across robots, grippers, simulation, and humans to handle many embodiments.
s4d6451c050.why: A universal action tokenizer could simplify training robot policies across heterogeneous hardware and data sources.

s7e0c27b696.title: Topological Neural Collapse
s7e0c27b696.description: arXiv:2611.28894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural collapse (NC) predicts that, late in training, last-layer class features concentrate at their means and the means form a simplex equiangular tight frame (ETF). We ask whether NC also leaves a signature in the functional connectome of each layer: the graph of Pearson correlations between hidden-unit activations, built per class and summarized by persistent graph homology. Using deep MLPs, we observe two topological phenomena that co-occur with the well-studied geometric NC in the final layers during the terminal phase. Contrary to NC1, the split-half variability of a class connectome increases (TNC1).
