s7e0c27b696.summary: A paper reports topological signatures in the functional connectome of deep MLP layers that co-occur with neural collapse in final layers.
s7e0c27b696.why: Offers an analytical lens on internal network structure during training, with limited direct implications for engineering practice.

s5da93a4b8f.title: Can Open LLMs Clear Sanctions-Screening Alerts? A Pre-registered Test on Public Sanctions Lists with Turkish Name Variants
s5da93a4b8f.description: arXiv:2611.28914v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sanctions screening raises name-based alerts that are mostly false positives, and level-1 analysts clear them by checking the customer's date of birth and name against a written policy. We test whether open-weight language models that a bank can run on its own premises can perform this level-1 disposition. From the UK and EU sanctions lists (7,103 natural persons) we built 12,200 synthetic customers: listed persons under six name conditions, including Turkish spellings of Arabic-origin names and Turkish romanisations of Cyrillic names, and two date-of-birth conditions, plus namesakes, near-name customers and a general population. A deterministic fuzzy and embedding screen raised 7,383 alerts, which three open models served on domestic infra
s5da93a4b8f.summary: A pre-registered study tests whether open-weight LLMs can clear sanctions-screening alerts using UK and EU lists with Turkish name variants.
s5da93a4b8f.why: Bears on whether banks can run compliance screening on-premises with open models, though the abstract does not report final results.

saa2e5088fa.title: Definition-Guided In-Context Learning for Zero-Shot Spoken Language Understanding
saa2e5088fa.description: arXiv:2611.28929v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Adapting spoken language understanding (SLU) systems to novel or revised label taxonomies conventionally requires additional labeled data and retraining, creating a bottleneck for real world deployment. While in-context learning with few-shot demonstrations offers an alternative, multi-modal generalization and scaling has been challenging. In this work, we investigate whether natural-language definitions alone can guide zero-shot SLU without demonstration exemplars, finding that symbolic definitions serve as the primary supervisory driver for adapting speech-text models. We operationalize this principle as Definition-Guided In-Context Learning (DG-ICL), a fine-tuning framework that decouples semantic categories from fixed lexical names. By
saa2e5088fa.summary: Researchers show natural-language label definitions alone can guide zero-shot spoken language understanding without demonstration examples.
saa2e5088fa.why: Suggests taxonomy changes in voice systems might be handled by updating definitions rather than collecting labeled data and retraining.

sde695f61a0.title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation
sde695f61a0.description: arXiv:2611.28940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-criterion LLM judges often evaluate responses without specifying how conflicting criteria resolve, leaving the winner undetermined even under exact criterion scores. Issuing a strict verdict without declaring the required trade-off premise constitutes silent value completion. We introduce TradeoffBench to isolate this failure by separating rule execution from response scoring. On authoritative criterion vectors, six open-weight non-reasoning judges pass all dominance and equality controls yet pick unsupported winners on 9%-81% of 1,345 conflicts. sde695f61a0.summary: TradeoffBench is introduced to show multi-criterion LLM judges often pick winners on conflicting criteria without declaring the trade-off rule, with error rates from 9% to 81%.
sde695f61a0.why: Warns that LLM-as-judge evaluations can silently make unstated trade-off decisions, affecting the reliability of automated evaluation pipelines.

s10785db4cf.title: Micro Operational Robustness of LLMs on Code Generation
s10785db4cf.description: arXiv:2611.28957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is now common practice in software development for large language models (LLMs) to be used to generate program code. It is desirable to evaluate the robustness of LLMs for this usage. This paper is concerned in particular with how sensitive LLMs are to variations in descriptions of the coding tasks. However, existing techniques for evaluating this robustness are unsuitable for code generation because the input data space of natural language (NL) descriptions is discrete and sparse. To address this problem, we propose a robustness evaluation method called scenario domain analysis, which aims to find the expected minimal change in the NL descriptions of coding tasks that would cause the LLMs to produce incorrect outputs. We have formally p
s10785db4cf.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a robustness evaluation method for how sensitive LLMs are to variations in natural-language descriptions of coding tasks.
s10785db4cf.why: Shows code-generation output can shift with small wording changes in task descriptions, which matters for relying on LLMs in development workflows.

sd95b3c0e0a.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
sd95b3c0e0a.description: arXiv:2611.28963v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A world model should tell us not only what will happen, but what would happen under a different action. Learned Earth models now forecast remarkably well, yet forecast skill says little about what their state means or how it responds to a changed driver. We build LandWM, a world model of land-surface water in which rain is the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS observations: physical observation operators tie its latent state to soil water, and a mass-conserving balance governs how that state responds to rain. Over the U.S. Southern Great Plains, the model, never shown a soil-moisture value, tracks 28 in-situ probes as well as the operational SMAP Level-4 product, even from CYGNSS alone, and a storm added to the forcing of
sd95b3c0e0a.summary: Researchers built LandWM, a land-surface water world model trained on seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS satellite observations, where rain is the action.

se1ca59684c.title: MolReJev: Decision Models Are In-Context Molecular Predictors
se1ca59684c.description: arXiv:2611.28965v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular prediction helps prioritize compounds for screening. Specialized predictors are trained for a fixed set of tasks, limiting cross-task generalization. Language models can condition on task descriptions and have recently shown promise in molecular prediction. However, generating answers token by token adds inference cost, and general-purpose models often lack task-specific molecular knowledge. We thus propose MolReJev, which combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning (ICL) on a language model. MolReJev retrieves similar labeled examples from existing task data and scores candidate labels jointly in one forward pass. ICL improves predictions from the released general-purpose Kev checkpoint and the separately traine
se1ca59684c.summary: MolReJev is a proposed method that combines Jev-style candidate scoring with in-context learning on a language model for molecular prediction.
se1ca59684c.why: Offers a way to get task-general molecular predictions from a language model without per-task training, though the summary gives limited detail on results.

s3df20780fb.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
s3df20780fb.description: arXiv:2611.28968v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. Work on safe model updates assumes fixed inputs and so ignores patients who lack the new data. The update has no new measurements for them, yet their rank can change, and a sick patient not yet tested can drop off an alert list. We split rank-based compatibility by data availability and pair it with error correction and alert-list effects. We compared each update with ordinary retraining on the old inputs, predicting ICU admission or death and hospital admission, on 78,475 emergency department visits from MC-MED and, in a pre-registered replication, 100,000 stays from MIMIC-IV-ED at a second hospital. Radiograph re
s3df20780fb.summary: A paper studies how adding a new data source, such as lab results available for only some patients, can reorder patient risk rankings in a deployed clinical model.
s3df20780fb.why: Highlights that safe model updates with partially available inputs can change alert lists for patients who lack the new data, a risk for deployed systems.

s20deb7627a.title: A Design Space for Data Agents: Insights from KDD Cup 2026
s20deb7627a.description: arXiv:2611.28970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data agents interpret analytical requests, gather evidence from heterogeneous sources, and compute results within finite resource budgets. We analyze the final code submissions of the ten highest-ranked teams in the KDD Cup 2026 Data Agents for Complex Data Analysis competition. We organize the observed design choices into three interacting layers, covering workflow orchestration, analytical functions, and working state. The comparison reveals recurring patterns for allocating computation in response to task progress, structuring evidence for computation and assessment, and preserving reusable artifacts with their provenance. Candidates that rely on the same evidence can inherit the same error, so interpreting their agreement requires traci
s20deb7627a.summary: An arXiv analysis of the final code submissions from the ten top KDD Cup 2026 teams identifies design patterns for data agents across three layers.
s20deb7627a.why: Gives engineers concrete architecture patterns for orchestrating data agents under compute budgets, drawn from competition-winning systems.

s7566f19924.title: World Models for Ocean Engineering: A Critical Review of Maritime Autonomy, Adaptive Latent Prediction, Digital Twins, and Biodiversity Monitoring
s7566f19924.description: arXiv:2611.28978v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Marine robots face partial observability, non-stationary dynamics, and sparse communication, motivating WMs that learn compact predictive states for planning. This review develops a functional taxonomy of WMs for ocean engineering, focusing on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and AdaJEPA's test-time adaptation within model predictive control, mapping them to navigation, adaptive sampling, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring, and separating demonstrated evidence from prospective applications. The synthesis identifies key Gaps: benchmarks, uncertainty calibration, safe adaptation and proposes a research agenda for physics-informed, deployment-adaptive marine WMs validated through simulation and field missions.
s7566f19924.summary: A review surveys world models for ocean engineering, covering JEPA-based approaches, AdaJEPA test-time adaptation, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring.

s1f2aa2a52a.title: CLASP: Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling for Zero-Shot OOD Detection using Vision-Language Models
s1f2aa2a52a.description: arXiv:2611.28986v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) enable zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) detection in medical imaging, yet existing approaches often rely on final-layer confidence or entropy-based layer selection, potentially missing complementary information. We show that low in-distribution (ID) confidence entropy does not reliably predict OOD discrimination. We introduce CLASP (Complementary Layer Selection and Profiling), an ID-only framework that jointly models layer--prompt responses and visual features. CLASP ranks visual encoder layers using Gaussian conditional mutual information and selects a compact subset through anchored spectral selection, without fixing the number of layers. It then combines the selected layer--prompt profiles with PCA-compr
s1f2aa2a52a.summary: CLASP is a proposed ID-only framework that selects and profiles vision-encoder layers to improve zero-shot out-of-distribution detection in medical imaging with VLMs.
s1f2aa2a52a.why: Suggests intermediate layers, not just final-layer confidence, can improve OOD detection in vision-language models used for medical imaging.

sde69d04cf8.title: Demystifying Classifier-Free Guidance for Auto-Regressive Image Generation
sde69d04cf8.description: arXiv:2611.29002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) has been widely adopted in autoregressive (AR) models for high-quality image generation. Despite its strong empirical performance, its mechanism in AR models remains unclear. This paper demystifies the mechanism of CFG through both empirical and theoretical studies. By examining the top-ranked semantics of different components in CFG, we show that texture information is primarily encoded in the difference between the conditional and unconditional logits, whereas both logits share previous-token repetition as their leading semantics. This strong repetition semantics obscures the desired texture information, causing greedy decoding from the conditional logits alone to produce nearly pure-color images. Through a
sde69d04cf8.summary: A paper examines how classifier-free guidance works in autoregressive image generation, finding texture information is encoded mainly in the difference between conditional and unconditional logits.
sde69d04cf8.why: Clarifies the mechanism behind CFG in autoregressive image models, which can inform tuning of guidance in generation pipelines.

s6fcbacc428.title: DoC: Learning to Defer or Commit for Timely, Accurate, and Stable Conversational Diagnosis Prediction
s6fcbacc428.description: arXiv:2611.29003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conversational diagnosis prediction requires accurate, early, and stable predictions from ongoing clinical dialogue, yet dialogue-level labels do not specify when to commit. We propose a two-phase framework for learning deferral and diagnosis decisions. First, iterative commitment-boundary estimation constructs Defer/diagnosis supervision without annotated commitment times. Second, Defer-aware supervised fine-tuning initializes a policy, refined through reinforcement learning with trajectory-level rewards for timeliness, first-commit accuracy, and post-commit stability. On EMSDialog and MediTOD, DoC commits early, achieving the highest first-commit accuracy among post-trained methods (76.7%/51.2%) and the lowest post-commit error overall (1
s6fcbacc428.summary: DoC is a two-phase framework that trains models to decide when to defer or commit to a diagnosis during conversational clinical dialogue, using reinforcement learning.

sa35c91a123.title: Consumer-Time Validity in Stateful AI Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State and Deferred Authority
sa35c91a123.description: arXiv:2611.29004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes reuse execution state and deferred permissions across components and sessions. A cancellation, rollback, or approval is recorded by one component and relied on by another, and recording it does not make the later use valid: a downstream consumer may read state or dispatch an action whose identity, production status, allocation, or target revision has since changed. We call the missing check consumer-time validity and separate two forms. State validity governs what a consumer reads. On vLLM with LMCache, an interrupted KV load leaves unwritten blocks indexed, and a host-only counter rewind desynchronizes the GPU position, so a second tenant generates a schema-valid tool call naming the wrong te
sa35c91a123.summary: A paper introduces consumer-time validity, a check that verifies recovered state and deferred permissions are still valid when used by downstream components in stateful LLM serving and agent runtimes.
sa35c91a123.why: Identifies a correctness gap where cancellations or approvals recorded by one component may be stale when another acts on them, relevant to agent runtime design.

sa0ea29b2ff.title: NoHairCache: Calibrate-Once KV Cache Eviction with One Power-Law Exponent
sa0ea29b2ff.description: arXiv:2611.29006v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The decay exponent $\alpha$ in KV-cache eviction is an intrinsic property of the model: calibrated once on a single corpus, it transfers directly across domains. Attention-based accumulation (H2O) and recency-based sliding windows (StreamingLLM) are two dominant eviction frameworks, often treated as unrelated, but we show that they are the two endpoints of a single power-law family: by scoring each token as $s_i = A_i \cdot (t-i)^{-\alpha}$, where $A_i$ is cumulative attention and $\alpha$ controls the age penalty, H2O and StreamingLLM correspond to $\alpha=0$ and $\alpha\to\infty$, respectively (with StreamingLLM additionally hard-coding an attention-sink patch). The no-hair mechanism of \citet{xiang2026nohair} bounds the admissible range
sa0ea29b2ff.summary: NoHairCache proposes a KV-cache eviction method using a single power-law exponent that unifies H2O and StreamingLLM as endpoints and is calibrated once per model.
sa0ea29b2ff.why: Offers a single calibrated parameter for KV-cache eviction that claims to transfer across domains, relevant to inference memory optimization.

s0a90c99471.title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks
s0a90c99471.description: arXiv:2611.29009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems built on large language models (LLMs) often aggregate over one-to-many and many-to-many joins, a classic trap: when the joined rows repeat an entity, a SUM or COUNT counts it more than once, yet the query runs and returns a plausible number. We characterize these fan-out errors by one condition on the relation an aggregate reads, which depends on two facts a schema does not show: each measure's grain, and how many rows a join on each key repeats. An audit that tests the condition on the data finds distorted gold answers for 4.2% of the dev questions of BIRD, a widely used benchmark, and BIRD's later, independent revision changed 44% of the answers the audit flags as definite fan-out, against 16% of unflagged ones. We rel
s0a90c99471.summary: A paper addresses fan-out errors in LLM-generated text-to-SQL, where aggregates over one-to-many joins double-count rows, and proposes grain-aware guards and audited benchmarks.
s0a90c99471.why: Silent double-counting in aggregates produces plausible wrong numbers, a real risk for LLM-driven analytics and BI query generation.

s93e7a0d01b.title: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM
s93e7a0d01b.description: arXiv:2611.29018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can we tell whether an LLM is watermarked without knowing its secret key? Published black-box tests suggest that carefully designed prompts can reveal the statistical footprint of a watermark. This paper examines what happens when those tests move from controlled reference implementations to a deployed model whose watermarking parameters are undisclosed. We present an audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude. Across ten initial configurations, the published test never rejects on a model the provider states is watermarked, despite detecting a local reference at comparable sample sizes. Controlled experiments expose a failure mode: including the prompt in the watermark's repeated-context history suppresses marking exactly wher
s93e7a0d01b.summary: An audit of the Red-Green watermark presence test on Claude found the published test never rejected on a model the provider states is watermarked, across ten configurations.
s93e7a0d01b.why: Shows black-box watermark detection tests may fail on deployed models, relevant to anyone relying on provenance claims for LLM outputs.

sf3f6304a8c.title: Introducing the Amazon Bedrock Trusted Access API with Anthropic’s Enterprise Frontier Safeguards and Enterprise Data Controls
sf3f6304a8c.description: Amazon Bedrock now offers a trusted access program API: one place to discover, request, and enroll in model provider programs. The first two offerings, in public preview, are Anthropic's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC), which give you control over your data when you use Claude Fable models.
sf3f6304a8c.summary: Amazon Bedrock launched a Trusted Access API to discover, request, and enroll in model provider programs, with Anthropic's EFS and EDC offerings in public preview.
sf3f6304a8c.why: Engineers using Claude models on Bedrock gain a single path to request data controls and safeguards, though the text gives no detail on terms or availability.
